text_fidelity_a:
Googly Eyes Game — Family Drawing Game with Crazy, Vision-Altering Glasses This game is FUN!
But may not be for kids that are perfectionist when art is involved.
The goggles have different settings - easy, medium, hard which makes it nice for the kids to start out with easy and adults to start at hard if your kids don't like losing.
The rules are easy.
This game is a fun "charades type" spin on a game.
The goggles make you look silly and is fun too!
This game is best for kids that are already pretty good artists, basically if they draw a lot with sidewalk chalk and you can really tell what they are drawing - then this will be good for them.
However, if your kids are still drawing stick people, then this is not the game for them, they will most likely leave the game crying.
I would consider 7 year olds as the very minimum, but I would base it more on the ability and less on age.
The kid should also be able to know how to read the simple instructions, which from my experience - 7 years is appropriate.
I think this game would be most fun for a group of kids the same age with the same artistic ability to really level the playing field. There is a possibility for cheating if you try looking at the end of the frame where the lense and frame meet. Hopefully nobody on your team decides to try that.
Keep an eye out for drawing with a head at an unexpected angle!
text_fidelity_b: Googly Eyes Game — Family Drawing Game with Crazy, Vision-Altering Glasses

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Natural Play: Play, Draw, Create Reusable Drawing & Magnet Kit – Ocean (42 Magnets, 5 Dry-Erase Markers) I wanted to LOVE this set.
I really like it. But I don’t love it.

1st - I don’t know why companies create toys for kids 3+ that include markers that aren’t washable!!

2nd - the main (black) dry erase maker is the only one that is a complete handled marker with an eraser lid. The other 4 markers have a 1.5” handle area to hold onto. The markers work and erase well.
The markers are hard to get back into their elastic straps. It’s difficult to do as an adult- let alone a 3+yo. An additional 1/4” of elastic would have been helpful.

3rd - the activity pages have a spiral binding. The way it is set up the last page is attached to the back of the kit - I like this. But the spiral is too small to allow the pages to tuck behind the kit and the top of the pages lift up from the back of the bottom.
The pages are sometimes used together for a project but not always.

4th - there isn’t a bag or something to store the magnets that aren’t being used.
The magnets are all on 2 sheets and are very strong. You can easily layer these magnets to get different looks. There are 54 magnets so it would be nice if there was an area built in to store the magnets while they aren’t being used.

5th - This activity pad takes a lot of space and is larger than a child’s lap - it’s 23” wide. It would be nice if the pad could be opened and folded in half.

6th - the velcro closure is nice and strong but the cardboard tab is weaker than it needs to be. I worry that after much use this tab will be ripped off.

All that being said - this activity pad is nice.
It’s a good quiet time activity that has a lot of fun included.
My daughter takes this to restaurants and plane rides to keep her busy!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Natural Play: Play, Draw, Create Reusable Drawing & Magnet Kit – Ocean (42 Magnets, 5 Dry-Erase Markers)

Melissa & Doug Mine to Love Travel Time Play Set for Dolls with Diaper Bag, Bottle, Sunscreen, More (17 pcs) - Baby Doll Accessories, For Kids Ages 3+ Lots of things to keep track of - just like having a real baby!
This travel set has everything you would need for a baby on the go.
I like that the diaper is adjustable but I wish the elastic was a little stronger.
The banana purée label starts to crinkle instantly with each squeeze. For these reasons I deducted 1 star.
As you can see the diaper fits our cabbage patch doll pretty good - the bottoms is a little wider than it needs to be - but I’m not worried about leaks!
The wash cloth is just a microfiber cloth - I wish it had a design on it and felt more like a real wash cloth.
The wipes feel like cut up interfacing.
The travel check list is plastic and bendable and a little stiff - which I like.
It feels like you could use a washable marker on it - if you trust your kids with a washable marker.
The lid to the sunscreen can be removed and the tube is inviting to be filled with water or other liquids - my daughter loves to put water, soap, who knows what else in items like this. I wish the bottle had a hole in the top and was closed like the banana purée.
The bag has a divider down the middle. I wish the bottom would open up more.
The one sided velcro on the sun label is weak and you will likely loose this after a week it hard use.
The side of the bags has bottle holders which is great.

Pinkfong Baby Shark - Doodle Me Doll - Baby Shark - Preschool Plush - by WowWee This shark stuffy is 100% polyester cloth, stuffing and thread.
I appreciate that the wash instructions are on the tag attached to the shark.
The shark measured about 12” from fin to tail.
The shark is well sewn and packaged.
The shark comes with 2 washable markers - purple and green.
It says that the markers may stain furniture, paint and clothing.
It’s not recommended to use any other markers besides the ones provided. It would be nice if 4 or more markers were provided and not just 2.
To wash - put the shark in a pillow case and then machine wash on gentle cycle using mild detergent. Do not prewash or use bleach.
It’s recommended to air dry and not to tumble dry.
For best results wash within 48 hours of scribbling.
If left after 48 hours multiple washes may be needed.
I agree with the age rating of 3+ as your kid will be less likely to draw on other things. 4+ might be an even better option.

Draw Into Crime Game -- A Game Created for Kids, by A Kid! I love that this is created by a kid for kids.
The instructions are simple and easy to understand.
The age is 6+ which I feel is fair - any younger and the kids will have a hard time drawing the suspect.
My concerns with this game is that -

text_fidelity_a:
Schleich Horse Club 70-Piece Lakeside Country Dollhouse and Horse Stable Playset for Kids Ages 5-12 This box was heavy!
The quality of the pieces is exceptional.
The house and barn come together quickly and easily. They click together and they can easily be separated by pushing on the tabs if you wanted to take it apart.
I cannot attest to the durability of the horses legs, which were packaged with cardboard between them, which worried me that they might be fragile. Time will tell on that.
But the structure itself is very stable. There are SO MANY accessories. The house has specific locations where the picture sticker is added to the wall and the ribbons get added to the wall, etc.
I was surprised by the amount of details.
I love the attic hatch in the floor and the telescope in the attic. The only thing I think it is missing is a third person. The family photo that comes with it has four people in the family. The bedrooms can fit four people. Also, I do wish that all the people could ride the horses and not just the one person.
It would be nice if two people were included that could ride a horse so it would be easier to have so siblings or friends play together. The saddle is elaborate.
My 10 year old niece thought this was really neat and was excited to play with it.
My almost 5 year old nephews were excited to play with it also, they like to play with the farm set that is at a 1:64th scale, I was kind of expecting these to be at that scale, but it is much bigger.
Schleich is very high quality brand for miniatures and has a good reputation for that reason.
I guess I'll have to buy a few more kits to get a rider and another kid for the family.
text_fidelity_b: Schleich Horse Club 70-Piece Lakeside Country Dollhouse and Horse Stable Playset for Kids Ages 5-12

Baby Einstein Magic Touch Ukulele Wooden Musical Toy, Ages 12 months+, Red When I read that this ukulele was wooden I expected the whole instrument to be wooden.

The ukulele goes from off to volume low to volume high.

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for $80.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is large enough to make it feel like a nice machine, but small enough, especially when folded, to port around, which is nice because it lends itself to easy travel. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards seemed kind of flimsy, and didn’t stay on well, so I flew without them. The drone handled test crashes well. The propellers held up well, with only some minor scrapes after hitting the ground and nearby trees. The copter simply hit the ground and the arms folded in on impact.

Quiet - The drone has a relatively quiet sound, and isn't too loud. I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. When executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward or backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button at the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Tuning - This was easy to do, and I liked the tactility of the joystick buttons. I found it worked well.

Camera usability- The quality is good, and it is fun to use. However, I’m kind of in the middle on this, which is why the camera is in both the pros and cons. It does provide an accurate view of what the drone sees, and I didn’t have almost any lag. The picture resolution was nice. It’s not super easy to use, but I was able to figure out most of the controls while flying.

Battery: This had a nice battery life, with about 22 minutes of battery life to 1.5 hours charging time. I didn’t stream video, which I would imagine uses a bit more battery, bt for my medium intensity flight, I was very happy with the flight time, especially considering that they give you two batteries, which could give you about 45 minutes of flight time.

Cons:
Unstable/Jerky Camera - Because the camera is hard-mounted to the drone body, the video is very twitchy and jerky as the drone flies around and tilts, particularly when descending. The video became very shaky. I found myself more inclined to use the photo option over the video though, because of how unstable it was. I also found the field of view to be frustratingly narrow, and wanted a more upwards view from the drone.

Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as set up the camera, one of the main selling points with this drone. I’ve found this is a common issue with Syma instructions, and it just makes the products a lot harder to use. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark and the DJI Tello, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for 35 dollars. Compared to other drones, I would say that there are certain improvements that could be made but those drones are much, much more expensive.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is quite small, which is nice because it lends itself to indoor flight and easy travel. It is about 4.5 inches by 4.5 inches for a length and width, and the diagonal rotor distance is about 5 inches, while to entire copter stands at about 1.25 inches. This, as I said, is nice for indoor flight and you don't have to worry too much about hitting someone. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards proved themselves quite useful, as I bumped it into walls several times, and the guards did their job. The copter simply bounced off the wall and continued flying. Additionally, when I was testing it, the drone died while flying. I knew this was coming, as I could feel the responsiveness beginning to slow and the flip function would no longer work. The drone fell from about 12 feet in the air onto the blacktop. I didn't notice and dings, dents, or scar=tches, and once it was charged, it flew fine.

Quiet - The drone has a shrill high pitched sound as it flies. It isn't too loud, and I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. Executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward of backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button a the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Cons:
Disproportionate flight to charge time ratio - According to the user manual, this charge time is about 70 minutes, while the flight time is around 5 minutes while hovering. I, however, found that it took about 35 minutes (charging for a wall outlet) for a full charge from dropping out of the sky dead. The flight time that I got was about 6 minutes, doing maneuvers, flips, climbing, falling, accelerating and decelerating. Still, I think this could be improved, and, as there are no removable batteries you can plug in once another is dead, I make using the drone for more than 10 minutes hard.
Poor wind resistance - This thing blows outside with the slightest breeze. Inside, the flight trim is hard to adjust, and outside, it is not worth it. I found myself constantly adjusting to compensate for any wind.
Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as find things within the manual. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
Joysticks don't articulate much - This is actually somewhat annoying. there isn't much height to the sticks, and they don't move around much, making any more precise movements difficult. Additionally, the other buttons on the controller are somewhat difficult to press.

There were scratches in the paint finish, and the worst were on the header with "Fire Station" painted on it, just where it will be the most visible. The paint seems very thin, and flaked areas look like they'll easily spread with use. In many places, the paint came off when I peeled the part-number stickers off. I deducted the second star because the accessories were not as advertised in the listing or the video. Missing were the doghouse; one of the basketball standards (two were shown; only one was included); the bathroom sink; and one firefighter (two were included; the description promises three). The firefighter's helmet makes it nearly impossible for him to fit through the holes to slide down the pole. The Dalmatian dog pictured was replaced by a brown dog, with a dog bed that he does not fit into, instead of the doghouse. The TV/bookcase console was replaced by a freestanding TV on a pole that is very unrealistic looking. The included accessories match the parts-list in the instruction booklet, so I know the omissions were not accidental.

text_fidelity_a:
Anbalulu Magnetic Tiles for Kids, Stacking Blocks, Preschool Stem Construction Building Set 100 Pcs These building elements are a lot of fun! They'll be easy to play with even for the littler kids, and they're colorful, sturdy and simple. Magnets are just perfect - strong enough to hold blocks securely, while not so strong that they'd pinch little fingers, though really small kids might need help with initial separation and pulling of the blocks out of the box. Even a taller construction held up solidly and didn't distort. The set comes with two wheeled bases as well, and as a bonus those can be connected into a train. The wheels move freely, and everything has a quality feel to it.

There's also a little booklet with some basic shapes to build that go gradually from the baby simple to the more complex shapes. A kid could figure them out on their own easily and learn along the way.

The box came chock-full of building elements. I'm not kidding, it's like a puzzle in there - don't expect to be able to figure out how to get it all back in after you take them out. (This is actually kinda nice, because it makes the set very easy to transport without worry of anything shaking up and breaking. Just be aware that it's heavier than expected... I'm taking this to nieces kids by plane, and will have to throw out another thing to stay under the weight limit. That's a lot of magnets.)

The stained glass effect of colors is so pretty, I'm really tempted to get another set for my inner kid, to build a lamp shade with. :-)

UPDATE: The 5 year old I gave this to is still completely in love with it, months later. I had to buy another set for his little cousin who was very upset he didn't get one too.
text_fidelity_b: Anbalulu Magnetic Tiles for Kids, Stacking Blocks, Preschool Stem Construction Building Set 100 Pcs

Intex Inflatable Jump-O-Lene Playhouse Trampoline Bounce House for Kids Ages 3-6 Pool Red/Yellow, 68-1/2" L x 68-1/2" W x 44" H Like many busy parents who are struggling to work from home during the pandemic while caring for our young kids, I was looking for a toy that would keep my 3-year-old entertained for a few minutes and since he loves jumping and bouncy houses this seemed like a great idea.
This took about 45-60 minutes to inflate and we had to use a blow dryer for the widest opening in addition to an electric pump. It inflated nicely and it did take quite a bit of space in my living room. However, when my son came to try it he became instantly frustrated because the material is very stiff and isn’t bouncy. This is more like an inflatable pool kind of material, only stronger and stiffer. We tried using this several times but my son simply doesn’t enjoy it. Then I tried to return it and they made me a) fit the darn thing in the tiny original box (which of course was impossible) or I wouldn’t get a refund and b) pay for shipping myself. I would’ve had more fun burning $70 something bucks for this piece of junk. I certainly don’t have the time or energy to go through their cumbersome and senseless return process. I don’t recommend it to any parent. I ended up buying a trampoline and my son and I are much happier with that.

text_fidelity_a:
Prime Climb Great game for helping kids understand factors and learn their multiplication/division (and addition/subtraction) facts, plus it's FUN! The part that initially drew me in for where my kids are was the color coding of the basic primes, and by extension the use of those colors to represent factors in the products. Then, it arrived and the gameplay was really fun--there are two ten sided dice and you can add, subtract, multiply or divide the number you are on by each die in turn to move. If you land on a prime you get to draw a Prime Card, which you can either use right away or save for later to benefit yourself or target an opponent, depending on whether the card is an Action card or Keeper. The first person to move both pawns to 101 wins. If you get tired of the standard rules, though, they apparently have some variations here: [...] but I have not yet tried any--looking forward to doing so after we've played through a few more times.

Oh and keep in mind that it takes longer the more players there are--folks with younger kids might want to keep it to 2 or 3 players so it doesn't go so long, or modify the rules so people don't get sent back to start so often. I'm sure there are cooperative ways to play too if that's more up someone's alley, like it was for us when the kids were younger.
text_fidelity_b: Prime Climb

text_fidelity_a:
Testors Decal Paper, Clear, Pack of 6 (9201) I'm giving this product 4-stars partly because what was in the envelope was not what I ordered (white not clear), and because the sheets are small and there are only 6 of them for the price. Having found a work-around so I could use white substrate, I find this decal material relatively easy to use and can say the end result is quite suitable.

Here's what produced the best results:
1) Printed the images (inkjet Epson ET) and let them dry at least over night.
2) Sprayed them with one coat Krylon Crystal Clear Acrylic Coating, and let that dry for an hour or so. Acrylic clear coat is essential to getting a high quality finished result.
3) Applied a second coat of the Krylon and let is dry for about an hour.
4) Cut the images very close to remove as much of the white backing as possible.
5) Placed the decal in water with the backing side in the water. The edges curled up and I had to hold them flat for a few seconds to get the decals to lay flat in the water.
6) When the edges of the decal substrate (what the image is printed on) began to curl away from the backing sheet, I removed the backing sheet with the now loosened decal from the water and gently slid the decal off the backing sheet and onto my project surface.
7) Patted the decal gently with tissue to remove excess water from under and around the decal.
8) Set the project aside and allowed all moisture to dry. This assures the decal is set onto the piece.
9) Sprayed the project with two top coats of Krylon, with about two hours between spraying. This assures the decal is not easily scratched or marred.

What DID NOT WORK was floating the decal design side down in the water. This wets the Krylon coat too much and when you slide the decal off the backing and onto the project, some ink leeches out into the water and moist Krylon creating a slimy, grayish muck and tends to ruin the graphic.

I also searching for another brand that offers more and larger sheets for just a little more money.
text_fidelity_b: Testors Decal Paper, Clear, Pack of 6 (9201)

They aren't very loud so if you need to hear them from across a home they might not work for you.

I bought these for my 3 dogs, mostly for my geriatric Fox Terrier who asks for everything the same way -one scratch on the front door. And that scratch could mean he needs to go out into the back yard, or he wants me to open the front door so he can gaze out through the screen door, or his water is unacceptably dirty, or... You get the picture. I started with just one of the buttons and recorded my voice easily. The playback was clear, I really am impressed.

The problem is, our home is a bit older, about 130 years, it's not large but we have a closed floor plan with wonderfully thick walls. Unfortunately that means no matter how loud I shouted when recording you can't hear the playback if you aren't in the same room as the button. I guess my dog figured the front door is central enough that you can hear him scratch it from most areas in our home. Go figure.

Replogle Aragon 12" Desktop World Globe, Raised Relief, Up-to-Date Cartography, Made in USA (Blue Ocean) The review always asks: What did you use this product for?
Well, when we watch the network news at night, I never know, exactly, where the places are that are in the news.
When I'm introduced to a new person who has an accent I just can't place, and when I ask them where they're from and they answer with the the name of a country, that I'm not familiar with, let alone the continent it resides on, I feel like an ass.
And admit it, when you play Jeopardy (and 90% of the world plays Jeopardy) your palms start to sweat when the category is Capitals Of The World.
And you go into overdrive when the Final Answer is: What peninsula (peninsula?) is where the historic treaty of peace (what?) was signed in 2001 between the United States and the Republic of Whatever (OMG).
This replogle globe, which is Made in the United States, is not only beautiful but it holds lots of information. The Legend denotes swamps from canals and shipping routes. You just can't believe what you can "read" on a globe. If you want to know where they are and you are in this world, buy a globe. Buy this one.
Can you name at least three countries that survive Ukraine?
I rest my case.

TAOZI&LIZHI Christmas Puzzles for Adults 1000 Pieces, Christmas Harbour Holiday Cheer, Xmas Vacation, Jigsaw Puzzle Gifts for Women Men Families, Nightmare Before Christmas Decorations(27×20in) I rediscovered my love of puzzles when COVID hit, and I was doing a traveling job, so I was stuck in a corporate apartment in a shut down city knowing NO ONE. When I wasn't at work, I was cooking, doing movie marathons, and puzzles.

I love the puzzles that require a true strategy, rather than the obvious "let's get the edges first" or "oh, all the purple stuff is in this corner". This puzzle begged for a solid strategy, because the drawing is complicated, and there's some duplication. You can't take anything for granted with this jumble! As well, the poster that comes with it does NOT include the added glow-in-the-dark ink pressed on top, so you have a guide, but it's also got surprising additions to trip you up.

My last pic shows how vivid the glow-in-the-dark ink is. I took this at dusk, with a lot of light still spilling in, and those teeth are GREEN.

All in all, this puzzle is a head scratcher and a definite win.
text_fidelity_b: TAOZI&LIZHI Christmas Puzzles for Adults 1000 Pieces, Christmas Harbour Holiday Cheer, Xmas Vacation, Jigsaw Puzzle Gifts for Women Men Families, Nightmare Before Christmas Decorations(27×20in)

text_fidelity_a:
Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model I bought this model for my 7 year old grandson who recently started riding and currently aspires to be a Vet. The model is small and some of the bits are tiny but manageable if one has reasonable dexterity. It is not for the easily frustrated as it requires patience and a thought to put together. The documentation is marginally helpful, and we used the picture on the cover more that we did the provided sheet for guidance. I also bought "Horse Anatomy (Dover Nature Coloring Book)" which proved a useful addition.
I worked with my grandson to put the model together for the first time. One of the small pieces had molding flash still attached which prevented it from fitting properly until the excess material was removed. The pieces will all fit together properly, but the final assembly is not terribly robust.
To reiterate, it was a bit of a problem solving exercise to fit the pieces into the correct spots, but we found the feeling of accomplishment worth the effort. I do not recommend this as a quick-assembly toy. There are better choices for that purpose. However, I do recommend it as a learning exercise for the curious child. It was fun to see my grandson made associations with his dog and human anatomy during the process. The finished product is suitable for display in a safe spot and can be disassembled and reassembled as long as one keeps track of all the pieces (you wouldn't want to lose his pancreas, would you?). I deducted a star for the less than great documentation.
text_fidelity_b: Tedco 4D Vision Horse Model

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Winning Moves No Stress Chess, Natural (1091) for 2 players My daughter (8 years) really took an interest in a chess a few years ago. We played regular chess, but it wasn't that engaging. This levels the playing field and is really fun, even if you understand play chess a lot. The game focuses on drawing cards that tell you want piece to move. Based on the card, it poses different scenarios that either level the playing field or draws the game a bit longer. For example, being in check and not drawing a king card to move out or not drawing a card to neutralize the check. My daughter had made some gear combos with the pieces in her hand. There are really three modes

(1) each player draws one card and that is the card to move. (Easiest)
(2) each player has 3 cards and plays a piece from that
(3) each player has 5 cards and plays a piece from one of those cards

I'm surprised this hasn't been invented before. It is great if you've never played chess or have played chess and want to teach someone new.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Winning Moves No Stress Chess, Natural (1091) for 2 players

The only other problem I see is that the glitter tubes should have a shaker end since younger kids have real problems shaking anything out of an open tube.

I have a feeling we will be going get more paint (and paper) really soon because it was a hit with my daughters and we taped their art work to the computer cabinet.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist Electronic Scrabble Twist is a great idea and it more like an electronic version of Boggle in which players can make as many three, four, or five letter words as possible from a random group of letters before time runs out. Simply press the buttons on the unit to spell the words and “twist” to save the word - the bigger the word, the more points you receive for that word. Unfortunately, I love the idea more than the execution. There are both good and bad features of the game, which I’ve summarized below.

Good:
• Games are quick and rules are basic
• The game can be played by anywhere from 1 to 8 players, depending on the game mode
• There are different games that can be played and different levels of difficulty with varying lengths of the time players are given to find words
• The game quickly shuts off automatically if not in use
• The letters will automatically display in the right direction even if the unit is turned, which is good for the party mode in which the unit is passed and also means it works well for both left and right handed players
• The Turbo mode, for head-to-head play between two or more players is fun
• The sound can be turned off for quieter play

Not So Good:

• The worst part of the game is that the letters are hard to read and is a strain on your eyes after playing for a while. People in my family of all age groups said the same thing.
• Three AA batteries are required, but they’re not included
• The instructions on using the game unit aren’t clear (I was able to figure out how to use it by playing the game a few times.)
• The solo mode tracks high scores, but not by name. It doesn’t feel like you’re working toward anything since you can’t really compare scores from game to game since it depends on the letters you had for each game.
• When the sound is on, it’s loud, even at the lowest level. Different sounds do alert you that you’ve played a valid word. A second sound plays if the word you’ve played is invalid or a duplicate. Sounds also let you know if time is about to run out, but I found that this distracted me from finding my final words
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Scrabble Twist

text_fidelity_a:
Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome This is a fun ride-on toy for kids. I like that it sits close to the ground, which makes it better for younger kids, but the design is still “cool” enough that older kids will still like it. The dune buggy has a lot of good features. First, the blue color will appeal to both girls and boys. The vehicle has two speeds, which is nice. However, the parent lock-out needs to be removed to access the higher speed. The lock-out is a screw that’s fairly difficult to remove because of its location. The higher speed is definitely needed to easily ride in the wet grass, even on flat ground. It’s fairly easy to steer the vehicle and is a lot of fun for kids to drive.

To stop the vehicle, take your foot off the gas pedal. It will still slide a little on pavement, possibly because of the plastic wheels. It also will continue to slowly roll going downhill, even on a small incline. That’s why even though the guidelines say ages 3 to 7, I would use caution for younger kids unless you have a large, flat area with no nearby hills. Older kids, up to 11 or 12, will like it, too. However, with the position of the steering wheel, their height will determine how well they’ll comfortably fit in the dune buggy and be able to easily steer.

Be sure to charge the battery the night before using the first time. The battery only lasted about 15 minutes right out of the box after being putting the car together. I also learned the hard way that the dune buggy is heavy to push if it does bog down or if the battery dies. (The battery is rechargeable battery, but there isn’t a battery indicator, so I wasn’t expecting it to go dead so quickly.)

Once the dune buggy is assembled and the battery is charged, it’s a lot of fun for kids. The assembly is a chore for adults, though. I took almost an hour and a half to assemble. Most of that time was spent putting on the wheels. The directions aren’t clear and some of the screws are hard to get to and there isn’t room to use an electric screwdriver. As long as you allow enough time for assembly and charging the battery, this dune buggy will be a hit.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Dune Racer, Chrome

text_fidelity_a:
Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone This is an easy-to-learn game with minimal set-up. It’s fast-paced and the rounds and the games go quickly. The circular game board has letters from which to select and a 10-second time. A player draws a card and picks one of two categories to play, such as “Pizza Toppings”. The first player thinks of something that fits that category, such as “Cheese”, and presses the “C” on the board. The next player now needs to think of a pizza topping, but can’t use the letter “C”. Play continues until only one player remains. Then, the round is over and the next player chooses a card.

The game requires 2 “AA” batteries that are not included. There is a storage place on the bottom of the game board for the cards. If the timer wasn’t so loud, it would be a great game for the car. It would be good to bring on a trip to play once you arrived, since it’s compact with self-contained storage for the cards. This is a great game for families because the cards are double-sides with different difficulty levels on each side.

It was harder than it seems to come up with things that fit the category beginning with one of the available letters, within the time-limit. Younger kids may get bored after a few rounds, but great game for passing a short amount of time. It would be nice if it came with more cards, because if it did become a family favorite, it wouldn’t take long to go through the cards. Still, it’s a fun family game.
text_fidelity_b: Tapple - Fast Word Fun For Everyone

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Party Board Game "Logo Party" gives players the chance to guess famous logos in a variety of ways. Depending on what type of card you draw, you will try to have other players guess the logo by drawing the clues (like Pictionary), acting out the item (as in Charades), or describing the brand (like the old game show "Pyramid".) Players have twenty seconds to guess the brand from the clues provided. Each team has a token to move around the board and try to get to the end first by guessing more brands than the other team. The game includes a tablet for the drawing clues and a box to hold the cards during play and for storage. Unfortunately, the box is too small and the cards don't fit well.

The game is designed for four or more players divided into two teams. The recommended ages are listed as eight and up, but most eight-year-olds would be unfamiliar with many of the brands featured in the game. In fact, even older teens and adults won't know some of these brands. Also, I would call some of the items products and not brands. For example, one of the "brands" is Chicken McNuggets (as opposed to McDonald's.)

The game is somewhat fun, but would be much better with a large group of people. My family found it almost impossible to act out most of the brands, but it was funny to see people try to act things out like "Tupperware". With more people, I'm sure it would be even funnier.

Throughout the boards, there are spaces called, "Reveal It". When landing on this space, players from both teams try to guess a brand by looking at the logo. This is also how the winner is ultimately determined when teams reach the end of the game board. The timer that comes with the game doubles as a holder for these cards. The card starts out fully covered and then parts of the brand are slowly revealed. This is a clever idea, but it's hard to place the card in the holder without looking at. Also, it makes an annoying buzzing sound (like the sound of a small wind-up toy.) Because of the sound, we used a different timer during regular play and saved the timer for the "Reveal It" cards.

The game would be more fun for a large group of people. My family had some fun playing "Logo Party", but got bored after a while since some of the brands were unknown to some of the players and it was hard to act out the brands and actually get someone to guess them.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Party Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Board Game The Classic Edition, 2-8 players I have many fond memories of playing "Monopoly" with siblings, cousins, and parents when I was child and then with my own family as an adult. This version is very close to the version I remember playing in the 70s. The game board and tokens are sturdy, and my favorite tokens from when I played as a kid are included - the dog, the horse, and the race car, along with the shoe, hat, thimble, iron, wheelbarrow. Two others are included that I don't remember at all - a cannon and a ship.

The game comes with rules for the standard, full length game. Players choose a token and go around the board purchasing property and building houses and hotels, hoping to force their opponents into bankruptcy. This game can be played by two or more players.

The property title deeds are still made of thin cardboard, but may be a little more flimsy than older versions. The money tray is even better than it used to be. It's made of plastic and seems like it will hold up much better than the old flat tray with the flimsy dividers that used to quickly fall apart. The only thing that is off for me is the color of the Community Chest cards. They are a yellow-orange color instead of the yellow I am used to. I don't know if the very first version of the game had cards this color or not, but this is the first time I've seen this.

If you're looking to replace your old game or haven't played the original version, you can't go wrong with this classic game.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Board Game The Classic Edition, 2-8 players

text_fidelity_a:
Educational Insights Pass The Peas This game has a cute, creative format unlike anything I've seen for a word game. Everything about the game from the container, to the letter trays, and the letters themselves is related to peas. The cardboard trays are made to look like pea pods and the letters look like peas.

The container is a cylinder made of sturdy cardboard in which all the game pieces fit. The letters come in individual, green drawstring bag. If the game was played often, I'm not sure how long the letter trays would hold up, but other than that, everything does seem fairly durable.

Unfortunately, the game itself doesn't live up to the clever concept. Each player draws 10 letters from their bag of letters and has 30 seconds to make a word. Then all players "pass the peas" to the next player, who tries to use as many of their own letters to make a new word out of the original word passed to them. The only requirement is at least one of the original letters must be left remaining. For example, you can add an "S" to the beginning and an "S" to the end to make the word "TOP" into a new word "STOPS" or you can change "DUST" into "LINT" by replacing the "DUS" with "LIN".

The game sounds like it could be fun, but it is frustrating. I play online word games often, but still found it hard to think of a word using my letters and get them arranged on the tray within 30 seconds. It was also hard to make a new word when one of your opponent's trays was passed to you. I first played the game with just one other player and thought maybe adding another player would make the game more fun, but the main problem was the difficulty in making words and not the pace of the game, it wasn't any better with three players. After repeated games full of frustration, it became boring and nobody wanted to play any longer, which is a shame since the pea theme is so clever. An elementary school child might have fun ignoring the timer and the rules and just using the letters to make words since the game pieces are so cute.
text_fidelity_b: Educational Insights Pass The Peas

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game "Monopoly Empire" is like a simplified version of the traditional game of Monopoly. The colors and layout of the board are very similar to the traditional game, but each has a famous logo, such as Hasbro or EA Sports, instead of street names. The object of the game is to add tiles with various brands to your Times Square type "billboard tower" before the other players. The more brands you add to your billboard, the more money you get when passing Go, which allows you to buy more brands. The game tokens are representative of the brands in the game, such as a bottle of Coca-Cola and an Xbox controller. The board is a bit smaller than the traditional board, because it doesn't have railroads.

The game is easy to learn, in part because of an excellent, full-color instruction guide that includes a very clear diagram of how to set up the board. The way the items are priced make it easy to pay for purchased tiles. Although the game is lacking the excitement and strategy of trading properties and building houses as in the original version of Monopoly, it is good for a quick game. It would be easy for kids to learn and play. The game is most fun when it's a close race between the players to complete their towers. If one player takes a large, early lead, it's hard for the other person to come from behind.

Note: The logoed tiles have various sizes, which is part of the game. However, the sometimes the positioning of the stickers with the logo make it confusing to put them into the tower correctly.

All in all, this is a good game that is easy to play and goes by quickly.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player I looked forward to playing this game, but was very disappointed. It sounds fun - each player rolls five dice and adds their roll to the roll of a common die. I thought it would be more like Yahtzee, but it was not nearly as fun as that classic game. The common die gives the chance for each player to double their score, which helps someone come from behind and catch up with the player that is leading. However, when rolling only 5 dice, the odds of getting a decent roll were slim. It was almost impossible to get anything more than a three of a kind, and that was hard to do. This made the game more frustrating than fun. I've never played the original Farkle, and we had to make some house rules because many portions of the instructions were unclear, which added to my frustration. The instructions referred to online video directions being available, but I didn't think it was worth having to watch a video to learn to play what should have been a very simple dice game.

For those familiar with Farkle, the common die may add an interesting twist, but the bubble-popper and dice risers are unnecessary. The bubble-popper for the common die does not roll the die well and seems like it would break after a few uses. We took the die out and rolled it by hand. This was much easier and kept the game moving more quickly. (On a side note, when we removed the die from the bubble-popper, it looked dirty!) The dice risers are rickety and make the play of the game more confusing. Since you can't combine the numbers you get on individual rolls, it's necessary to keep track of what you got on each roll within a round. It was impossible to do this on the risers, so we just started putting the dice aside from each roll and not using the risers at all.

The dice themselves are sturdy, even though the white coloring started coming off the numbers after only a couple of uses. I like that there are four sets in different colors so each player can have their own color. However, the red and orange were too similar in color and it was hard to tell them apart.

Overall, I think the dice risers and bubble-popper are flimsy and just a gimmick to make more out of the game than there is. It's not an exciting game and became very boring when it became clear it was too hard to get a decent score from an individual roll.
text_fidelity_b: PlayMonster Farkle Frenzy Multi/None, 2 - 4 Player

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Princess Design Activity Kit - 9 Double-Sided Plates, 4 Colored Pencils, Rubbing Crayon The fashion design activity kit is nicely made and comes in nice, bright pink and purple colors. The plates can be placed in the tray in different combinations to create outfits and then rubbed to see the result of your design. It's easy to use; however, the drawings aren't crisp. They come out a bit blurry, and details like buttons or stripes don't come through.

It is made perfectly for travel. It has a handle to make it easy to carry and a locking tray to securely hold the tracing plates and colored pencils. text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Model Magic Jewelry Studio This isn't the usual jewelry-making kit with beads and other accessories. While the kit does include those items, the best part about it is that it comes with Model Magic to actually make your own beads. There are special tools included to help shape the beads and a plastic rack/tray to dry your creations overnight. The resulting beads are spiral-shaped and can be made to be multi-colored.

The manufacturer lists the recommended ages as 6 to 15. I would agree, although younger children will need some assistance from someone older. I thought it was interesting that the box pictured only girls around age 13, all wearing heavy make-up. The jewelry accessories for pendants and bracelets would appeal more to younger girls, but teens will like the chance to make their own beads, which isn't possible with most jewelry kits. There are a couple of different themed add-on kits available with additional Model Magic and jewelry accessories.

Overall, I think this is a unique kit for a variety of age groups.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Model Magic Jewelry Studio

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin My family has really enjoyed playing this updated version of an old favorite. The basic rules are the same as in the original Sorry! Each player has four pawns to move around the board from Start to Home. You draw a card to find out how many spaces you can move your game piece. Landing on another player's pawn sends them back to start as does the Sorry! card, just as in the classic version.

What's different about Sorry Spin is the spinning board. The center circle is the main board, with connecting circles for each color's home which fit together like gears. The challenge of the spinning board is your home is contantly changing position in relation to the main board. You may be just a few spaces away from reaching your home track when the board will spin and you will end up all the way across the board from your home.

It took about 5 minutes to assemble the game board, which seems very sturdy. We had some trouble spinning the board on a slick surface (wood table, counter top), but when we placed it on a placemat, it worked fine. A nice addition is a box that can be assembled and used to store the cards.

This is a great family game which is faster paced than the original version of the game due to the spinning board and a shorter path between start and home. Also any number gets a pawn out of start. (unlike the original which requires a 1 or 2). Older kids and adults will enjoy the suggested variation of the two-player game in which each person selects two different colors instead of only one.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin

The Game of Life Twists & Turns I used to love the original Game of Life when I was younger. I had bought the updated version for my family, but it was very hard keeping track of the money in the new version with higher values and life points.

This new game is more interesting because you can choose your own path and cards take the place of pre-printed spaces on the board so each game is different. The electronic money-tracking makes the game go so much faster. You can also choose how many turns you want each player to get so you can control the length of the game.

Fun for adults, teens, and pre-teens.

KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+ It really is all it's cracked up to be! I have been eyeing it for almost two years and I got lucky and found it in November for $120. I waited to put it together until the night Santa stopped by our house. It did take a few hours to assemble but my husband never left his recliner. I only needed an extra set of hands once or twice and my mom easily did the job.

The top is tricky to attach because the freezer and microwave doors have a tendency to want to leap off the kitchen. I definitely recommend assembling on carpet--the freezer door fell off while I were attaching the top (it's totally stable after the top is attached) and my hardwood floors dinged the corner when the door landed.

If I had to put the kitchen together again, I would definitely get an Allen wrench drill-bit for my drill. The two types of Allen screws in the box have the same head so you can take one of them to the hardware store to ensure the proper drill bit fit. Using a low-power drill makes furniture assembly fast and SO much more pleasant. :)

My son loves it!!! He was only 18 months at Christmas so I was worried he wouldn't know what to do with a kitchen. To my surprise, he ran right to the stove and started turning knobs. He tested the sink handles to make sure they turned and then he started cooking! I totally recommend the utensils and stainless pots & pans from Ikea (they fit the burners perfect). The Melissa & Doug wooden pantry and fridge foods are awesome, as well. Very, very cute.

All-in-all, I am completely delighted with the quality and playtime potential this kitchen offers. My baby might not have any idea what I am talking about when we play "Iron Chef", but he knows how to stir, flip, move things to the sink and move food from the fridge to the microwave to the oven...

Oh, also, my big little guy is 33" already and he has to stand on his tip-toes to see inside his stock pot. He will be cooking for many years to come.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Deluxe Let's Cook Kitchen, Gift for Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
JOY FOR ALL - Orange Tabby Cat - Interactive Companion Pets - Realistic & Lifelike My 75-year-old sister almost died from acute kidney failure following a major flare of autoimmune vasculitis. When I spoke with the doctors, they said she would not be able to keep her pets (two little dogs, two cats) because it would not be safe. She'll be on immunosuppressants from here on out, and exposure to live pets will be too dangerous.

I didn't realize there was such a thing as a robotic companion animal for adults, but a friend of ours said she was looking into a robotic dog from Japan. (Yeah, one of those really expensive futuristic plastic ones.)

I started researching and watching videos on YouTube, and I thought this Joy For All cat would be perfect for her. Her cats have always climbed up on the desk between her iMac monitor and her keyboard drawer and been a constant presence. Joy For All also has a dog version of this companion pet, but knowing my sister, it will be the cats she misses the most. This kitty can lie on her desk and be responsive to her when she needs it but go to sleep when she's embroiled in work.

I just got word my sister's new kitty has been delivered to her home and is waiting for her on the dining room table. She won't be out of rehab for at least a few weeks, but I'm so glad to know she won't be completely alone when she gets back home. I mean, hey, she refers to her Roomba as "My manservant, Raul" and talks to him, so I know she'll be really tickled with this robotic cat. I just thank goodness that these are available. I was really worried that my sister, who has had cats her whole life, was at risk of sinking into a bad depression after all she has been through. But what a great kitty this is! I want one, too!
text_fidelity_b: JOY FOR ALL - Orange Tabby Cat - Interactive Companion Pets - Realistic & Lifelike

text_fidelity_a:

They are a little too small for that, but the noodles themselves are great. I like the black color. I will probably try to press them into service for building floating pond islands and the like.

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf Super Soaker Zipfire 3-Pack(Discontinued by manufacturer) UPDATE: Man, these things get the job done! It only took a few reminders, but now the dogs are not barking, either inside or when we go out (even if I don't have a squirt gun with me). All I have to do is pick one up and they immediately run off and cower QUIETLY in the bedroom! I think what makes these work better than dog whistles or scolding or time outs is that they can be targeted at the instigator, not both dogs. So if one dog is quiet, he doesn't get shot; just the offender gets blasted. They figured it out really quickly. They do NOT like to be blasted! LOL! And I think they actually compete to see which one can stay the quietest.

Got these to blast the dogs when they won't stop barking. They don't blast a targeted enough stream unless you are standing closer to the dog, like maybe six feet away, but they seem to work for their intended purpose. The chiweenie Bingo's the really rotten one, and the first time I used one of these pistols, I shot him once, he turned around and defiantly barked at me; I shot him again, same thing; then I shot him in the face with it, and he ran off into another room and stopped barking. The first time I used it with Doobie, a Jack Chi, he responded right away. (These dogs hate getting wet...but a dog who loves water would react differently. Still might quit barking, though.) So I'm hopeful these are going to get the job done. Only time will tell, but so far they see the brightly colored gun in my hand and quit barking.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf Super Soaker Zipfire 3-Pack(Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig UPDATE: Oh, the poor little Bandit! Bandit has been Bingo's security blanket, humping companion, BFF, and "only other dog in the house" until we got a real-live lifewire little dog, Doobie, who is a Jack Chi. Doobie is one high-energy chewing fool. Doobie has gotten up inside of Bandit and pulled his guts out of his butt and also chewed his eyes out, leaving holes. Bingo is not happy and so is trying to tug his dear Bandit away from Doobie, so I knew Bandit was not going to be long for the world. I ordered a new Bandit for Bingo, and he is thrilled, but I'm going to have to put him up until Doobie is over his puppy stage. But this Bandit racoon puppet is a fantastic purchase for a little dog.

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Move over Gator. Hit the box, Fox. Bandit has arrived.

Our 10-week-old Chiweenie puppy wants to bite-shake play, and even though he's careful not to be too vicious with DH's hand, he was breaking the skin. I got this puppet as a way to protect us from those sharp little puppy teeth.

Bingo went nuts for Bandit, and we did, too. On my hand, I don't like the fit on my thumb, which tends to slide out of the arm, but it seems to be fine on DH's larger hand. I just lift Bandit by the back and march him up and down, and the puppet is floppy enough, but also firm enough, to seem like a living critter.

I can't emphasize enough how nice the contrast between his nose and white snout is. When we say "bite his nose," he goes right for that little black nose. The nose and the eyes are sewn in very well so I don't worry so much about our dog pulling them off and choking them. Another thing really nice about this puppet is that it has some movement to it even when we are not assisting him in playing with it. He will pick it up and shake it, carry it around like it's his prize possession (which is funny, because it's bigger than he is), and put it in his "room" (a small rug) with his collection of squirrels and such.

UPDATE: Oh, Bandit is such a hit! Bingo sleeps with Bandit, pees on Bandit, madly humps Bandit, chases him all over the house when we throw him, carries him proudly to show "Bingo too" in the mirror, jumps up into the back of the loveseat in the living room with Bandit so Bandit can look out the window with Bingo at the neighbors passing by. Bandit has had to go in the washing machine quite a few times now, and with vicious chiweenie tug-of-war play, poor Bandit's scalp is starting to come unsewn. I can sew him up by hand and he'll be fine, but I'm already thinking I'd better get another Bandit to have on hand for when Bingo's BFF is in complete shreds! Bandit has shrunk some with washing, so it's hard to get a large adult hand into him, but he's still more than doing his job. He and Bingo now are about the same size. Bingo's eight months old and seven pounds.
text_fidelity_b: Aurora World 11" Pinky The Pig

text_fidelity_a: Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up Me and my brothers have been buying board games for a while now. But no other board game takes as much dedication to play, store, and maintain, as this one. Aside from maybe pen and paper D&D. You get a box around the size of a family dog crammed with game. There's a reason there are YouTube videos dedicated to various ways to store this game's pieces. LMAO Along with various storage solutions sold on the internet. It's a beast to store. A beast to set up. But for all the work you put up with, is the actual game worth the hefty price tag? Hell yes. The ongoing campaign really gives you a sense of accomplishment as you trudge through one dungeon after another in your pursuit to fill your map with markers. Oh, and that map. We hung ours in a frame and laminated the countless stickers and markers so that they could be stuck to the frame glass with mounting strips. We proudly hang it on the wall showing everything we've done. Our band of mercenaries, Duke's Coinpurse, have opened up a LOT of content with hours and hours of gameplay. And we're not done with it by a long shot. Not even counting the expansion we bought for it. Now there are a few things that are kind of annoying. Like some of the personal quests that you may get that will want to complete content you already completed, or character classes you've already unlocked. Making your character's personal quest pointless or do some back tracking to complete. So there is kind of a miss-step in the order of reveals for some things. Your group is going to argue about rules in the rulebook. I can almost guarantee it. LOL Not that the rules are hard to understand, but there are so many that you're going to be dragging it out to double check something if you're anything like my group. LOL But it's about as close to an actual D&D campaign as you can get. The character classes you play aren't all that fleshed out aside from a backstory on the back of their card, and the game has city events and road events that play out with a scenario that the group chooses from a multiple choice outcome. But the immersion is a little lacking in that you don't actually "role play" per say as you do just dungeon crawl. But it's still a Hell of a lot of fun. Just prepare to work for that fun. Because it's a huge, long game. Scoundrel4Life
text_fidelity_b: Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up

text_fidelity_a:
Marvel Guardians of the Galaxy Dancing Groot This is a simple toy. It's not something to entertain a modern child with for more than a few minutes, not even enough time to go through the demo batteries. He isn't all that interactive and stays in music detect mode less than 3 minutes. Getting it out of the the box will take longer by far. But. I'm not a kid. And apparently easily entertained.

The sound is reasonable and there are a few song bites from the soundtrack. I have had no problems getting him to pick up sound even from some distance. He dances to my terrible singing. Gotta love that. His arms are poseable, moving like most action figures, up, down and some lateral movement. The eyes light up and he speaks. He has a shutoff switch to save battery life.The bottom half of the body slides across surfaces and will eventually find the edge. Something to watch for since I doubt he bounces well.

All that being said...

I think this little guy is absolutely adorable. He is now Guardian of the Residence and shows up all over the house, much like that little Christmas elf. I may even end up making him clothes. And every Baby Groot needs his own mini teddy bear from the craft store.

This has been goofy and fun for me and well worth having around.

I AM GROOT!

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Oil Pastels Portfolio Series, Water Soluble, Colors may vary, 12 Count (52-3612) I tried the Crayola neon pastels first and then decided to get a bigger set so I bought the portfolio crayolas set and have included a picture of all 24 colors.
They are bright with a variety of colors including black and white. Crayola has never come across as a high-end brand, but in oil pastels they are highly regarded as some of the best, and I agree. If you watch some of the videos on YouTube about how to use oil pastels you will realize how great these are. You can also see comparison videos, and the crayola brand gets very high marks. Oil pastels don't make a mess unless you use your finger to blend them, and then your finger will be a big mess. But you can clean it with baby wipes or soap and water or lotion to get down into your skin if it's dry. You can use traditional rolled paper sticks for blending also. These come packaged neatly so you can keep them in their original slots in that packaging. Besides coloring with them you can also use a wet brush to blend them, and you can layer them on top of each other or blend them together with your finger. I have also seen them covered with a clear acrylic paint and then used again on top of that paint. You can see that on YouTube. These are an inexpensive way to enjoy yourself artistically and produce beautiful results just like painting when you add the water or vodka or a blender like turpenoid.

text_fidelity_a: Crayola Oil Pastels, Assorted Neon Colors, Gift for Kids & Adults, 12 Count I bought these and used them in my first attempt at oil pastels which I have included in my photo along with samples of each color. This set provides all three values... cool, warm, and neutral, so you can produce good work without having every color you would like to have or you can just buy more because they don't cost much especially the Crayola brand. I bought the bigger set and also their portfolio set. If you choose to smudge them using your finger you will get a colored finger. You can clean your fingers with baby wipes or soap, and even lotion is helpful at removing stains. Also you could use a blender tool like a paper tortillon. I used my finger. -- charge your LiPo's rapidly
-- balance charge your LiPo's so each cell has the same voltage
-- discharge your LiPo's if they're fully charged but you want to store them
-- charge your LiPo's to storage voltage levels for long term storage
-- plug your charger into AC wall power

The adapter cable fits a large variety of cell terminal plugs.

There is a balance port that receives the included balance plug adapter that can connect to anything up to 8S batteries.

This particular kit comes with an AC power supply like those that come with computers. The charger is really designed to hook to a car battery or other 12VDC high amperage source. This AC supply lets you plug it in at home easily and reliably. It comes with the right plug to fit perfectly.

The only things that could be added are extension cables on the balance connector to make it easier to charge the cells by making all the wires about the same length. text_fidelity_a:
Holy Stone HS720 Foldable GPS Drone with 4K UHD Camera for Adults, Quadcopter with Brushless Motor, Auto Return Home, Follow Me, 52 Minutes Flight Time, Long Control Range, Includes Carrying Bag [[VIDEOID:61f52fe954b9387d0799a4276217dbef]] Great Beginner or Experienced Drone operators with camera and video that pivots downward a full 90 degrees give the pilot great views and options, one fault is it's not on a gimbal but at this price point it can be expected. Super quiet brushless motors, 1 battery and usb charger, nice controller. Comes with decent quality carrying case that stores everything perfectly, along with a zippered compartment area, where you can keep the manuals and spare props, yes you get a set free with the drone!

Flies well in the wind I put it up in winds that were around 15-18 mph and it handled them well, of course the advertised battery life suffered and was only about 17 minutes but it was fighting the wind the whole time. On a less windy day it was almost 24 minutes of total flight time!

If your looking for a drone to learn on at a decent price point this is a good one and it's the right size, this is my 3rd Holy stone drone and I'm pleased with the product, I own the 700d, 270, and now this bad boy. All the features like follow me and point of interest work as expected I have yet too use way points on any of my birds, but the WiFi connection and FPV work well too.

I bought this one too go on Vacation with us in April to florida, mostly because of its footprint and portability, it is a little smaller than the 270.

Eventually I will be spending a ton on a DJI Mavic pro as I want to have a drone with autonomous flight and obstacle avoidance, but these drones have definitely exceeded my expectations and well worth the $$$ spent and are a great addition too my 7 other flying machines I have! So I highly recommend this unit!
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS720 Foldable GPS Drone with 4K UHD Camera for Adults, Quadcopter with Brushless Motor, Auto Return Home, Follow Me, 52 Minutes Flight Time, Long Control Range, Includes Carrying Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover [[VIDEOID:bf921d7e8b73b1b75b44b485dab75323]] So after a week of having this unit I had 9 flights and was pleased to fly it! Although I had an issue once don't know if that was just the bird or that was me, I'm leaning toward me as I might have not turned the drone in the right direction and had a failure to calibrate or that could been just the area I was in and its inability to gain GPS, with that said it was pretty much a problem free week of flying the 270. Now dealing with the single battery was an issue, I do think they should offer a package or drone deal with 2 batteries standard. 😁.

I will say it is a great beginner drone for young teens are adults that want to get into flying. From the moment I unboxed it it felt great in my hands it didn't feel cheap most of the construction was plastic but with that said it is very consistent with some of the quality that I've become accustomed to with the hs700 the hs190 and a hs720. The controller is smaller then what I'm used to. It felt good in the hand but a lil small for my liking as I used my Galaxy Note 9 which is the limit as far as the holder, every other feature like the FPV, follow me mode and plotting way points , and circle point of interest on a map and it's going there and coming back worked pretty well. The Return too home when low on Battery functioned well as I flew the bird too that point almost everytime, there was an issue with the follow me I should have had it up a little higher it did hit a branch on a tree which was my fault because these drones do not come with obstacle avoidance and it took a fall to the ground no worse for wear I stopped the motors flipped back over unlock the motors and she went right back up no issues. Photo quality really really love the camera and take some great pictures even out that 400 ft. I really like the 4K camera and the quality of the video and pictures ( all photos post are unedited) and this unit also allows you to record record audio which is pretty good for bloggers , though my one gripe is I wish the 270 came with a gimbal to really make exceptional video, but at this price point it's a trade off!

The HS270 is very very wind resistant I flew this in pretty high winds somewhere between 15 to maybe 18 miles an hour and some strong gusts I thought for sure it going to blow over the pond or even into some of the trees. The GPS worked awesome as it kept the unit in its place and even though in my video it was shaky because you could see the wind is blowing it all over the place I was thoroughly impressed and this bird should not fly away from you unless you accidentally turn off the GPS in which case you really need to know how to fly this thing or any drones in the wind with the GPS off. It has a 3-speed future from low medium to high I enjoyed that it seemed like when it was windy I kicked it in high speed and it flew alot better keeping in medium most of the other times I enjoy a quick flights back and forth but was able to enjoy the roughly 21 minutes of flying time at the most and less on that really windy day it was only about 16 minutes most of the time it was fighting the wind. It takes pretty good pictures fpv to the cell phone like 720pvideo and 2K photo But the quality really comes to life when you have a SD card in the unit.

I think overall this unit does exactly as it's advertised to do and being able to fold up you can actually take this thing with you on vacation put in your suitcase carry out with you when you go on a hike and have something with you besides your camera that you can put up into the air and taking it up sectional a different view all of your vacation or a picture of you and your family or significant other standing by a Mountain or even the Grand Canyon with a drone from a distance and capture something that cant be done with a selfie stick. So I recommend this unit, but make sure you get extra batteries cuz it does take a while with the USB plug to charge the battery, most times it took 2-3 hours till fully charged. I grabbed a case on Amazon which I believe it was a case setup for a DJI mavic I did a little modifying on the sides of the hard foam and it was able to sit down in the case well which I showed the picture in the reviews it was the soyan case for like 22 bucks or something like that. All in all a great deal, I'm totally satisfied!
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS270 GPS 2.7K Drone with FHD FPV Camera Live Video for Adults, Portable Selfie Quadcopter with 2 Batteries for Beginners with Auto Return Home, Custom Flight Path, Follow Me, Auto Hover

text_fidelity_a:
Holy Stone HS700D FPV Drone with 4K HD Camera Live Video and GPS Return Home, RC Quadcopter for Adults Beginners with Brushless Motor, Follow Me, 5G WiFi Transmission, Modular Battery, Advanced Selfie I really thought over a couple times before buying this what may be purchased this in the first place was watching the many videos of people online can I belong to an RC blog site and there were probably about 25 or 30 owners that have these could have done different modifications from antennas to figure props more powerful Motors taking the antennas and extending them and so on and so forth are some that even put 3-axis gimbal with their GoPros on and these were very versatile Hardy quadcopters. Also being that this was my first purchase for any drone over $150 I did quite a bit of research to make sure this was a decent purchase.

Needless to say I can't be any happier with 21 minutes of Twilight time per battery charge and just somewhere over a half mile of radius I can say I'm very pleased with the purchase and I would recommend this quadcopter to any beginners and somewhat moderates operators if you want a drone just to around have some fun and it's really really fast 36 miles an hour I was keeping up with my son's car. I have some future modifications in the works already with higher DB antenna for the transmitter 3-axis Gimbal and a GoPro.

I would recommend this again to anyone looking to go in the medium area as far as quality drone but this build quality is quite good it feels and looks like a quality unit. There are those in my RC clubs that have some of these drones and have crashed them nothing more than maybe a propeller or some rotor guards now two of these people have the Meijer model previous mine DHS 700 and they fly them all the time one guy had like 10 batteries for the thing.

Owning this unit has renewed my desire and my love for the hobby and I'm looking forward to continuing exploring further with my hs700d great Job Holy Stone!
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS700D FPV Drone with 4K HD Camera Live Video and GPS Return Home, RC Quadcopter for Adults Beginners with Brushless Motor, Follow Me, 5G WiFi Transmission, Modular Battery, Advanced Selfie

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Deluxe Wooden Magnetic Responsibility Chart With 90 Magnets This is an ok chart but with some issues. I really really wanted to love it because I've never been disappointed with Melissa & Doug products. For those wondering, it has the exact same tasks and pictures as the other Melissa & Doug Responsibility chart. It just does not have a spot for the child's name.

The good:
It's got a decent selection of tasks that. The visuals are great and easy to understand for my non-reader. The reward smileys are fun to pick out and have a rainbow selection of colors. It can easily hang (though it's a bit heavy).

The bad:
My board was warped, so the magnets don't fully stick. In addition, it was shipped with a plastic covering over the white boards. Unfortunately the magnets stuck to this plastic and peeled plastic off when trying to use it. This makes the magnets less sticky (see picture for example). This happened to more magnets than were good ones. There are only 26 choices of tasks, which make it pretty minimal. They are geared toward much younger kids, so my five year old won't use most of the magnets as he's already consistently doing these things. I wish there was a larger selection as the children age. There's not enough room for all of the extra magnets to be stored on the bottom half when not in use. One task does not fit if you have all of the smileys and all of the excess tasks down below.

Overall, I'm happy with the product but sure wish it didn't arrive with the above stated damage.
