text_fidelity_a:
Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 + I had a light bright as a kid, it wasn't a favorite toy of mine but it was pretty invigorating - I might've used it only a couple of times. That thing seemed like a tank. I guess it had to be to protect the bulb. You could even buy a replacement bulb if it broke.

This one sadly feels a bit cold and inexpensively made. No glowing filament bulb to keep things warm. Nice, new energy efficient electronics that are powered by 3 AAA batteries - hopefully you have some rechargeable ones to use.

The kickstand is terrible. You either have to hold it or lay it flat to put the pegs in but even then it rocks side to side easily. When you use the kickstand a slight bump to the top of the unit could knock it over.

The bezel is also too wide and I also don't understand the reason for the extended parts of the black plastic on the side. With such a wide bezel you don't need them and it would like nicer as a square.

My unit does not glow evenly. I opened it to see if something wasn't working. Everything was but there just weren't enough lights, one more and a little adjustment would've helped. The unit is also on a timer. As it runs on batteries having it lit all the time would likely drain them. They should have added a USB port and just not included the cable. You're not able to keep it powered on 24/7. It's maybe a 10 minute timer. Pressing the button multiple times changes the light mode: lit, 3 section rotating flashing light show, full on off blink and the last one turns the 4 LEDs on 1 at a time and then off 1 at a time.

I made one of the provided examples and I had just enough pegs of a few colors. a few extras would been nice.

The sticker on mine was very crooked and out of place.

However, where the LEDs do light the unit right, it does look cool. I think, way better than the OG, they're more neon glow, the colors are much better, instead of a yellow glow the LEDs are bright white which allows you to have yellow, pink, orange, blue and white pegs. These colors on the dark background are nice.
The pegs stay in nicely. I've only made one picture but not one has fallen out. It may not hold up to repeated removing and placing of the pegs but I plan on leaving it with a certain design for a while.

This would be awesome if it just had a few improvements. I'd probably buy another

Hasbro, you can do better than this. For an MSRP of $19.99 it's not worth it. Even Amazon's marked down price is too high. This is something I'd expect to see at 5 and below.
text_fidelity_b: Lite-Brite Peg and Template Refill Pack, Light Up Drawing Board Accessories, LED Pegs with Colors, Toys for Creative Play, Light Toys for Kids Aged 4 +

Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in Does a perfect globe exist? Probably it does, but I couldn’t afford it. I’m happy with this one although it isn’t perfect.
The good stuff: it came in a super sturdy box that held the globe stable during transport. (The manufacturer ships it, not Amazon.) The stand seems strong and sturdy, and of course I’m grateful for the 720° rotation. The colors are attractive. I even like the raised texture where there are mountain ranges. I’m glad that the United States is divided into states. Finally, although I’m not 100% educated on geography, I can say this globe is up-to-date enough for my purposes; for example, Sudan is divided into Sudan and South Sudan.
The less-good stuff: I’m surprised to see that Canada’s provinces are named, but not outlined! Unless the lines are just so fine that I can’t see them, you have to guess their boundaries. Some cities are identified in the US states, but I was really surprised to see that state capitals are not identified! I suppose some state capitals are named, but Austin Texas (where we live), Tallahassee Florida, and other states I’m familiar with have various cities but not their capitals identified! I also think that city placement is close, but not 100% accurate. Nevertheless, this globe will get a lot of use in homeschooling, and will serve our purposes. I would buy the same globe again if I needed to for some reason.
text_fidelity_b: Advantus 12 Inch Desktop World Globe with Blue Oceans (30502),13 W x 12 D x 15 H in

text_fidelity_a: Hasbro Games Mashin Max My son was gifted this game for Christmas and he LOVES it. He's 5, and any game that includes Hulk like smashing is perfect for him, add the collecting of tokens & cute woodland creatures and it's the perfect game for a 5 year old. text_fidelity_a:
Mega Puzzles Save-a-Puzzle Glue, 8 Oz I have been glueing puzzles together for YEARS. I have tried heaps of other glues, and trust me not all puzzle glues are equal. This glue is the best glue by far that I have used. I will never go back to other glues. It dries uber clear and gives a glossy shine to the puzzel that makes the puzzle 'POP' if you use it on the face of the puzzel.(my son's diary of a wimpy kid puzzle looks awesome with the added shine!)

It comes with 2 different applicatiors! One is similar to a rubber cooking spatula minus the handle that helps you get the glue into all those nooks and crannies, and one inside the bottle to get it out without dumping the glue into a bowl which wates so much glue! No more gummy brushes for me!

The clean up is so easy! Soap and water and it's gone! No nasty residue left on your skin. It's a great value! I have an 8 oz bottle and I did one 19"w x 14"L puzzle with 2 coats and there is enough glue left over for another puzzle! I know this product is at Walmart for purchase also, I paid $5 for mine.

text_fidelity_a:
Little Tikes Backyard Barbeque Get Out 'N Grill Little Tykes = Shoddy

1) you cannot push the red 'igniter' button without pushing over the whole grill, it's so stiff. My toddle certainly can't do it at all.

2) the pieces don't fit together properly, as usual with Little Tykes toys. Ugh. The side panels (the sink and burner pieces) don't mate properly, so the result is very slanted and everything slowly slides off.

3) incredibly light weight. Topples very easily.

4) the doors won't open or shut completely without an adult assisting. My two year old is very particular, and get frustrated that he can't close the doors all the way.

5) the two grilling areas are very small. The slippery food provided falls off incredibly easily. That is not conducive to toddlers enjoying themselves. I would rather have a large flat grilling area that kiddies could enjoy instead of two poorly placed small ones.

6) the faucet handle doesn't move. It really looks like it could. How much more difficult could it be to make that happen? Apparently- for a company that gets everything else wrong- it's far tough.

TL,DR: if you like spending money on cheap products, get it.
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Backyard Barbeque Get Out 'N Grill

text_fidelity_a:
Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith The Journey Girls dolls are 18" dolls. Clothing-wise, they appear to be compatible with other 18" dolls such as American Girl, Playtime by Eimmie, the Our Generation dolls, or even the 18" Adora dolls. At this price point, they are definitely an affordable play option for younger girls. Like the Adora dolls, they have plastic shoulder and upper torso area and the lower torso is cloth. (The AG, Playtime by Eimmie, and Our Generation dolls all have completely cloth torsos). The Journey Girls dolls do not turn their head well, but their face sculpts are all unique to each doll (again, similar to the Adora dolls, as the Playtime by Eimmie seem to all have the same face sculpt with different skin shades and paint jobs). I personally find the Adora dolls to be my favorite 18" alternative to the American Girl dolls, but they are still at a high enough price point that I would not want to hand one over to my 5 year old for unsupervised play. The Playtime by Eimmie dolls have a full cloth body, making them softer and more huggable than the Journey Girls dolls (and probably more appealing for younger girls), and they are about the same price point. The style of clothing the Journey Girls have, as well as their sculpted plastic upper torsos, they give the impression of teenagers rather than younger girls, which makes them very appealing to the 8-10 year old set.

Meredith is absolutely beautiful and my daughters love her glamorous clothing and hairstyle. An affordable 18" doll option that doesn't make me cringe to give to impulsive young girls for play.
text_fidelity_b: Journey Girls 18" Doll, Meredith

The body composition also has a difference over the American Girl or Playtime by Eimmie dolls. There’s a neck joint and the neck, shoulder, and upper torso area is plastic while the lower torso is cloth. This allows for a greater range of neck & head motion over other dolls of this size, which have completely cloth torsos and limited, if any, neck motion.

Her clothing is designed with play in mind, making it easy for an older child to take on and off, but the quality is such that she would make an excellent addition to a collector’s display as well.

Her pink streak in her hair and quirky expression make Lucy my daughter’s favorite. There’s something about her smile that reminds me of my best friend growing up and that makes her so special.

text_fidelity_a:
Classic Game Collection 6-Deck Automatic Card Shuffler There are two vendors on Amazon for this product with slightly different pricing. A group of us have purchased half a dozen from the other vendor over a period of about 2 years - 2 failed and had to be replaced within the 30-day period, one failed a month later. Some work better than others - 2 still work very well. The picture on this one looked different and the reviews read better, so I ordered one thinking it was made by a different manufacturer. Wrong - it's the same manufacturer. So far, so good, but it's not been quite 30 days yet.

We need to shuffle between 5 and 6 decks - the hints in the reviews have helped: Shuffle maybe 3 decks at a time rather than all 6 decks; tap the cards together so the edges are even; be sure the clear plastic plate is held firmly against the outside... Most of the hints are to help guide the cards so the leading edges are even and parallel.

We'd still like to find a shuffler of better quality...but it sure beats shuffling 6 decks by hand!

NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Break Open 15 Premium Geodes - With Goggles, Detailed Learning Guide, 3 Display Stands, Great STEM Science Toy & Educational Gift I recently received this geode kit. I was eager to bring it to a young friend of mine, a ten year old boy with an eye for science and a curious mind. The package and its photo of a young girl smashing rocks open promises at least a mild adventure, and what young man doesn't enjoy carte blanche to hit things with a hammer?

While my youthful pal did have a good time, I can chalk that more up to a willing sense of adventure than to the kit itself. First, a small gripe. The package depicts a little girl giving the rock her level best with a hammer and wearing safety goggles in the process. No hammer is included, but that's reasonable enough. (If you don't have a hammer, most likely geodes are low on your list of priorities.)

Still, the product seems designed as a dangerous source of fun for latchkey children, as only a single pair of safety goggles are included. Unless NatGeo assumes adults are down with little shards of rock storming their aqua vitreous, they really should have included a second pair. Unlike a hammer, I don't think safety goggles are a household staple.

The bigger issue with the product is the difficulty level in cracking the geodes. A giant Ziploc bag of small-to-medium size rocks is included, as well as some of the trinket-iest "display tables" I've ever seen, pieces of plastic that look to be pilfered from a Playmobil t-ball set. That's beside the point, though. Unless your child is sneaking steroids, these geodes are going to prove a most formidable foe. I cracked and whacked with all my (decent, adult) might and we only managed to get a couple open. If we had kept at it, we surely would have ended up with cartoonishly large dominant arms.

So it is good exercise, and hitting things with a hammer is usually a solid albeit not entirely safe source of fun for a kid. It would be disingenuous to say we had a bad time, but I can't give the product any real recommendation, either. If you do check it out, or get it as a gift, invest in that second pair of safety goggles to avoid giving your eyeballs that hipstery studded look, and don't let any kid hit these rocks by their lonesome if you value their fingers.
text_fidelity_b: NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Break Open 15 Premium Geodes - With Goggles, Detailed Learning Guide, 3 Display Stands, Great STEM Science Toy & Educational Gift

NERF Laser Strike 4 Player Lazer Tag Pack - Indoor or Outdoor Game for Girls, Boys, Families, and Adults - Includes 4 Blasters with 300 ft Range, 4 Vests, and 4 Holsters These are super cool and fun. And I like playing as an adult, too, although only if the kids want to play. I love that there are so many slight adjustments you can make - with or without the chest plates, changing ammo types, etc., and especially that it takes more than one shot to kill, since it really sucks when you get out right away and have to wait for the next round.

I know other people have said this, but the battery thing just kills me. I mean, any down time makes me see all those batteries draining prematurely. Yeah, you could get external rechargeables, but those Ni-MH or other nickel types really aren't quite the right type for something where you want to recharge them every time. I know it would cost more, but if these all had a li-ion internal and a docking station for the set, it would be perfect. I mean, it's already a fairly expensive toy, so why not offer the option at least. I mean, I have a lot of batteries around, but 24 at once is a lot. And then if just one guy dies, you have all kinds of sadness going around.

Even so, great set when everything is up and running.

It's sort of like campervanning to the extreme. The bus is even designed like a big RV, but with plenty of room for...friends. Oh yeah, and a sliding board. I guess any campervan-type bus needs one of those.

Totally cool set. Really for girls, although boys would probably secretly like it too...I guess they can just replace the teenage girl figures with LEGO The Punisher if he exists (if not, he should). My nieces love it.

text_fidelity_a:
Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday The car itself is pretty cool. I like the way it moves its entire axels to do its stunts. You can get a pretty good idea of hwo this moves if you look at the pictures. Simple, but effective. Seems like kids younger than 8 would like this; odd because they show small kids crawling on the floor using this, but say it is for ages 8 and up. Just watch they don't try to eat the batteries, I guess. It's not super fast, either, so older kids might get bored.

Anyway, they totally cheaped out on the battery setup. 400mAh?!?! Are you kidding me? Even the cheap, "included" versions of decent brands are 1100mAh, with good ones getting 2500mAh or more. And why the goofy charging setup? You have to take it out and then hook it to an oddball USB cable (so now you can't just use any USB cable you have laying around, you have to have this one on hand). They should just wire a higher capacity battery inside and add a micro-USB port like everybody else. And maybe similar functionality for the controller, which, oddly, uses two batteries...more than the car itself.

Pretty fun. Not well thought out overall, but on the other hand, if your kids falls out of love with toys quickly, maybe it's better not to spend more for the battery setup that could have been...
text_fidelity_b: Minsk Remote Control Stunt Car Toy, 4WD RC Cars Double Sided Rotating Vehicles 360° Flips to Bloom, 2.4GHz High Speed Rechargeable Toy Presents for 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 Year Old Boy Birthday

LeapFrog LeapTV Dance and Learn Educational, Active Video Game I received this game through the Amazon Vine Program, although the usual green writing may not be written above.

This game is pretty good if your kid is young enough to get excited over "dancing" to burn off energy. There are a bunch of mini games to do alone or with friends that require body movement to excel at.

The deal with the lighting is this, and it applies to all the camera based games: if you have low light, the camera may not register your hand is moving in front of something that is dark, and therefore will not pick up on the movement. So, for example, when I am using ambient light and the living room is not bright, my red couch looks almost black on the screen, so if you have to touch something that is in that area, it won't pick up on it. Similarly, if you turn on the lights, those items will be picked up automatically. Add light or put a white sheet on the couch, in that case.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapTV Dance and Learn Educational, Active Video Game

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Island in Hordaland, Norway 1500 Piece Puzzle To paraphrase my reviews on other Ravensburger puzzles, this is a surprisingly high quality puzzle. I always thought it was silly to claim quality in a puzzle, but you can notice it in the way the pieces fit (or don't) and by the fact that there is much less "puzzle dust" (small bits of paper) in the box afterward.

This one is actually better than it looks on Amazon; there is more detail on the island than it looks like from the picture. It is a good picture to do as a puzzle because of the many shades of blue and green with other colors spotted throughout. Plus, it's a big, serious puzzle at 1500 pieces. Definitely recommend putting it on a board or something to move it out of the way when not under construction.

I definitely recommend it as a puzzle, especially if you like the picture.

text_fidelity_a:
Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball I love geography and travel, and putting this together is both fun in a puzzle sort of way and great for reminiscing about past travels and dreaming about places yet to be seen in person. It's really cool - even cooler that it comes with a stand and you have a globe of your own afterward.

It is very up to date - it includes S. Sudan. And a warning to independence haters: Kosovo is shown as its own country. It is quite small and not labeled, but it has its own color.

We did the first half (the bottom) in the first night, but used the numbered backs as a guide as shown on the instruction sheet. It was fun, but left something to be desired. I wished they didn't have the numbers, and thought they would be impossible to ignore. After this, this was going to be the first Ravensburger puzzle I would have given less than five stars.

BUT the second night we finished it, but without the numbers. Turns out they were easy to ignore, and this allowed it to be what it should have been all along.

It might be overwhelming to not look at the numbers at first, but I suggest you do it that way. I suspect you still will have it done in 3-4 nights (assuming a few hours each night - it is addicting).

The pieces are plenty durable for snapping together, but many pieces are alike, so you could conceivably put the whole thing together as a sphere, but have it still be wrong. Anyone with any sense of geography would be able to catch a mistake like that. And when in doubt, the backs are numbered.

And when you're done, you have a nice little globe, textured to show it was a puzzle, and with a reasonably good looking stand. Very neat.
text_fidelity_b: Globe 540 Piece 3D Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Krypt Silver 654 Piece Blank Jigsaw Puzzle Challenge for Adults – Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly I love the Krypt. Oddly, I had passed it up in favor of a standard puzzle once before, thinking I might be disappointed when it actually came down to doing the puzzle. That was not at all the case: the Krypt has all the addictiveness of a standard puzzle, while offering the user the chance to think with a slightly different part of their brain. One can see that there are slight patterns to the way the puzzle is laid out, so it's not just a hunt-and-peck experience.

It actually went faster for me, but that might be because the piece count is a bit lower than other Ravensburger puzzles of this physical size. Or it might just be because my mind works better at making out the slight patterns and differences in the pieces. Either way, it is a lot of fun for puzzlers.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Krypt Silver 654 Piece Blank Jigsaw Puzzle Challenge for Adults – Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Harbor in Portofino, Italy 1000 Piece Puzzle I cannot help but parrot the reviews I've done for my other two Ravensburger puzzles because each one has impressed me the same, and got me somewhat addicted to puzzles (something I used to love as a kid, in smaller form):

Basically, I originally thought Ravensburger's claim to "outstanding quality" sounded ridiculous - it's a puzzle right? But it really is outstanding quality. The pieces are crisp and you barely ever get a false positive. Meanwhile, there is very little dust and paper shavings in the box compared to other puzzles I've done.

As for this puzzle in particular, it's a beautiful picture that has lots of similar shades of colors, making for an excellent challenge, without being absurdly frustrating.

Arrange to do this on a proper sized backer board so you can move it out of the way; it may take longer than you think.

An excellent puzzle, indeed.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Harbor in Portofino, Italy 1000 Piece Puzzle

You get a baseball that has bluetooth tracking and with the use of a free app, you track your progress, receive scores and encouragement, and can compete against your friends or against anyone around the world. The baseball is official size and weight (I weighed and measured then compared it to a real baseball), but it has an opening to insert a battery-operated tracker. The battery is included. It’s important to note that the baseball is not meant for batting.
There aren’t a lot of instructions included with the package, but more instructions come when you download the app (App store or Google Play).
My star rating at this time is based on the premise of the game and the quality of the baseball itself. A more thorough review will come after Christmas when my ball player gets his hands on this baseball game :) I’m eager to try it out!
text_fidelity_b: Playfinity Gaming Baseball - Perfect Baseball Gift: Real Ball+Free App with Games. Immersive Sound. Lots of Fun and Skill-Building!

text_fidelity_a: Thames & Kosmos | Robotics Smart Machines: Tracks & Treads | for Kids 8+ | STEM Kit Builds 8 Robots | Color Manual to Help with Assembly | Requires Tablet or Smartphone | Parents' Choice Silver Award For a 10 yr old, getting started with the kit was tough - understanding that this is not a programming-first robot like a competitor product but more geared towards understanding how various parametes influence balance (in various robot configurations). text_fidelity_a: Nerf Rival Charger MXX-1200 Motorized Blaster -- 12-Round Capacity, 100 FPS Velocity -- Includes 24 Official Nerf Rival Rounds -- Team Blue This deserves a ZERO rating.  This junky motor last exactly ONE time.  After that, you can switch batteries, try to keep guessing  if the rounds are stuck somewhere and keep checking etc... but absolutely nothing will work.  Other than now owning a few 1.5V C batteries, this thing is going to be disassembled and going to recycle and/or trash.  What a waste of resources to make something this junky.  Not worth the $35 listed;  If the batteries are included, this thing is worth about 4 bucks.  Better yet, dont waste the plastic or the packaging and shipment.  Do not consider this.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf Rival Charger MXX-1200 Motorized Blaster -- 12-Round Capacity, 100 FPS Velocity -- Includes 24 Official Nerf Rival Rounds -- Team Blue

text_fidelity_a: LEGO Speed Champions Lamborghini Urus ST-X and Lamborghini Huracán Super Trofeo EVO 76899 Building Kit (663 Pieces) Typical of Lego, this is a fun set to build - a 9 year old boy had immense fun building the set in a 2-3 hours.  For a set of this size, the level of details is good, though the reliance on stickers is a bit too heavy.  The main drawbacks  of this set that prevents it from getting a full endorsement are (i) all the action is imagination-driven - there is no motor/pullback mechanism that could have at least moved the built piece a few inches! (ii) the amount of customization via stickers can get a bit cumbersome, especially for younger builders  (iii) the finish line was best avoided - it serves no real purpose and looks tacky for a Lego set.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Speed Champions Lamborghini Urus ST-X and Lamborghini Huracán Super Trofeo EVO 76899 Building Kit (663 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: NERF Fortnite TS-R Blaster & Llama Targets - Pump Action Blaster, 3 Llama Targets, 8 Official Mega Darts - for Youth, Teens, Adults (Amazon Exclusive) For a 8 year old, finally caved in for a "gun" toy.. this became an instant favorite...but also a source of some frustration.  While somewhat oversized, the bigger issue is the frequent jamming. Though it is easy to unstuck, the experience gets degraded pretty dramatically when that happens.  But being a huge Fortnite fan, he still sticks to this Blaster.  With goggles and constant reminders to aim right, this is a safe way to get exposure to this genre which seems to be so difficult to avoid!
text_fidelity_b: NERF Fortnite TS-R Blaster & Llama Targets - Pump Action Blaster, 3 Llama Targets, 8 Official Mega Darts - for Youth, Teens, Adults (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a: LEGO Stranger Things The Upside Down 75810 Building Kit (2,287 Pieces) For a 14 yr old who is a fan of the show, this set was a huge hit - not only did it give her the unique house, she had a blast coaching a 8 yr old brother to build the piece.  Typical of the larger sets, this too has multiple printed instruction books and separate plastic bags.  Other than the occasional trouble with assembling the "roof", the set was easy to build - a couple of hours each over a long weekend.  The assembled piece is sturdy enough for a younger child to play with.  Overall, a good value for a complicated piece with a very unique design.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Stranger Things The Upside Down 75810 Building Kit (2,287 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: LEGO City Space Deep Space Rocket and Launch Control 60228 Model Rocket Building Kit with Toy Monorail, Control Tower and Astronaut Minifigures, Fun STEM Toy for Creative Play (837 Pieces) For a very enthusiastic 8 year old boy who already owns 60226 and 60227, this new set gives him a more complete space-themed playtime.  Approximately 7 hours to build spread across a weekend, this wasnt a difficult build at all.  Even an adult can marvel at the sheer clarity of the instructions and the thought that goes into designing such a set; all neatly captured in  7 separate instruction books.  The Explorers app is a nice touch but it is hard to say that it is well integrated; perhaps its value is dependent on the imagination .  Overall, the same excellent standards of any Lego set, realistic designs, great instructions and a good attempt in integrating a "screen" for more imaginative play.  A wonderful addition for the space-themed Lego sets.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Space Deep Space Rocket and Launch Control 60228 Model Rocket Building Kit with Toy Monorail, Control Tower and Astronaut Minifigures, Fun STEM Toy for Creative Play (837 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: LEGO City Downtown Fire Brigade 60216 Building Kit (943 Pieces) Unlike in the video of the product description, the fire engine is not motorized and is not capable of independent motion - that was a big let down.  The flashing lights and sound is great, but with Lego already having an excellent motorized collection, a motorized fire truck would have been great (especially when the video suggests that).  Other than that, the set is an excellent addition to any City fan, the fire flames and stickers are a bit silly looking - but the 6 yr old didnt mind and the 8 yr old didnt care.  The disadvantage of attention to detail is that you get to deal with a lot of tiny accessories that can get "misplaced" very quickly.  The minifigures are a hit... overall, a decent, very detailed set - wish at least the engine was motorized.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Downtown Fire Brigade 60216 Building Kit (943 Pieces)

text_fidelity_a: Thames & Kosmos Step-by-Step Magic Show Introductory Magic Kit This is a good intro set to some concepts in magic that a 7-9 year old may enjoy - even though they may not be able to master it themselves.  The instructions are better than other kits we've tried - but the material seems like it will not last for more than a few months, thankfully, these materials are easy to replace.  For the 25$+, pricepoint one will expect a better quality set.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Step-by-Step Magic Show Introductory Magic Kit

text_fidelity_a: K'NEX K'Nex Imagine – 4WD Demolition Truck Building Set – 212Piece – Ages 7+ – Engineering Educational Toy Building Set Apart from the misleading number of pieces in the title (it has 212 pieces not the 400+ as indicated in the title), this is a good intro for the Knex sets that include a motor.  (competing with the Technique line of Lego, perhaps)  The three variations in this set  are not much to crow about, but for the sheer value of watching a child follow detailed instructions is just immense.  This household already is a huge fan of K'nex sets offering multiple modeling options such as [[ASIN:B00VYAFTEM K'NEX 100 Model Building Set - 863 Pieces - Ages 7+ Engineering Educational Toy]],  the motor adds an extra delight.  The pieces from various sets can be mixed - giving endless opportunities for imagination to run wild.  This set can be easily built by 7-8 year old with minimal support - may be a tad boring for the upper range indicated for the set.
text_fidelity_b: K'NEX K'Nex Imagine – 4WD Demolition Truck Building Set – 212Piece – Ages 7+ – Engineering Educational Toy Building Set

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO City Heavy Cargo Transport 60183 Toy Truck Building Kit with Trailer, Toy Helicopter and Construction Minifigures for Creative Play (310 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) With the two cute minifigures and a very realistic looking truck, the helicopter will find it hard to be the star of the set. This is one of the sets that provides a good amount of building (300+ pieces) at a relatively less cost (at the time of review, much less than the 8-10c/piece I typically see).
The sturdiness and durability of Lego is well-established..so, no comments on that per se. This is, however, a great set where the whole set provides a spectacular visual and somewhat surprising functionality. There is no single star in the set - a wonderful 5* ensemble.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO City Heavy Cargo Transport 60183 Toy Truck Building Kit with Trailer, Toy Helicopter and Construction Minifigures for Creative Play (310 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a: Thames & Kosmos Remote-Control Machines: Construction Vehicles | Science & Engineering Experiment Stem Kit | Build 8 Real Working Models | Parents' Choice Silver Award Winner |Astra Best Toys for Kids This is a great investment - for building patience, understanding assembly, teaching opportunity on engineering concepts, and just time away from screens clicking away to oblivion.  With the sheer number of pieces to assemble, a large number of options to build, and a somewhat difficult set of instructions (because this requires patience; not because one cannot understand), this is probably the best building-blocks based set we have purchased (that includes all kinds of motorized sets in K'nex and fairly involved sets from Lego).  Overall, the sturdy construction and the general challenge this set offers will be a hit for any kid in the 6-12 range, though a 6-7 yr old is not likely to stick with it by themselves.  With this set, Thames has become our go-to brand for STEM-like toys that doesnt scream "school"
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Remote-Control Machines: Construction Vehicles | Science & Engineering Experiment Stem Kit | Build 8 Real Working Models | Parents' Choice Silver Award Winner |Astra Best Toys for Kids

text_fidelity_a: K'NEX Education STEM EXPLORATIONS: Vehicles Building Set Building Kit One of the core skills in STEM is to be able to understand the impact of various factors and how to determine them.  This set is a fun way to introduce the concept of experiments and factors and how to measure each factor's impact.  Though the number of models that can be built with the fairly small set of pieces (125 or so), the emphasis on experiments make this set stand apart from the traditional K'NEX collections.  (Expect to pay 10-15 c/ piece to see if you are getting a reasonable deal)..
text_fidelity_b: K'NEX Education STEM EXPLORATIONS: Vehicles Building Set Building Kit

text_fidelity_a: K'NEX Imagine Power and Play Motorized Building Set 529 Pieces Ages 7 and Up Construction Educational Toy With the sturdy pieces, excellent design options, and fun colors, this is an excellent addition to any K'NEX fan.  The 529 pieces give not only great options from the included designs and available online also allows for creative imaginative play.  The look of pride and accomplishment on my 6 year old (with some help from big sister) in assembling a moving, basketball contraption was priceless.  Like all other sets, this one also is well built and if past experience is any indication - built to last.  Absolutely entertaining and educational, builds not only spatial skills for kids, but also patience, building concepts such as modularity, and hours of fun post-assembly.
text_fidelity_b: K'NEX Imagine Power and Play Motorized Building Set 529 Pieces Ages 7 and Up Construction Educational Toy

text_fidelity_a: KID K’NEX – Budding Builders Building Set – 100 Pieces – Ages 3 and Up – Preschool Educational Toy This is an excellent introduction to the K'Nex brand for a 3-5 year old (this review is based on a 4 yr old);  With the ability to let imagination (and silliness) run wild, the box comes with enough pieces to create one's own imaginary whimsical creatures or take a somewhat structured approach to go through the building ideas the set provides (not all of them are interesting or capable of sustaining the interest for more than a few minutes).  Role playing with the imaginary creatures seemed to get most attention, at least for this test pre-schooler.  Overall, with sturdy yet flexible pieces (didnt notice any brittleness as some others have experienced) and ease of use for a fairly active 4 yr old, this is a great intro to the K'nex that will prep them for years of fun with the brand...
text_fidelity_b: KID K’NEX – Budding Builders Building Set – 100 Pieces – Ages 3 and Up – Preschool Educational Toy

text_fidelity_a: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle T. S. Shure had a temporary design lapse with this product; probably, the worst coming out of this brand.  Excellent idea coupled with poor execution only increases the frustration one would feel about the product.  The idea of 'magnetic' pieces to help discover countries and continents is great; so is the use of some cutesy imagery that often is often ascribed to a particular country (the dragon shaped like the Great Wall of China is a clear standout).  But trying to cramp all kinds of information in a tiny board proved disastrous.  The pieces are cut with no logic - the sub-continent looks from another planet; the font size for the capitals is so tiny, the target audience will barely notice it;  there are random airplanes and ships distracting the overall map and adding no value.  The tiny pieces are clearly not to be allowed anywhere near babies (it is rated for 6-15 years, to be fair; though it will be a miracle if anyone in that age group will use this for more than a day).  On the positive, with the weak magnetic pull and cardboard-feeling tiny pieces are bound to be lost sooner or later. And then you could create a new game - "which country is missing?".  That may be a better use of this playboard;
text_fidelity_b: T.S. Shure Map of the World Magnetic Playboard and Puzzle

text_fidelity_a: VTech Switch and Go Dinos Turbo Bronco The RC Triceratops Vehicle My 3.5 year old has named this the "dad" triceratops to the smaller versions he already had ([[ASIN:B007XVYSZW VTech Switch & Go Dinos - Horns the Triceratops Dinosaur]]  and [[ASIN:B007XVYT1A VTech Switch & Go Dinos - T-Don the Pteranodon Dinosaur]]).  The remote option to transform between the two modes and the impressive size is what you are really getting by upgrading to this version.  The remote+toy needs 8 AA batteries. The volume and sound effects are not too annoying for the parents and the wide variety of phrases the dino talks makes it less repetitive.  Overall, a fun toy for a 2-5 year old, I doubt the older kids in the 3-8 years range in the description will be continuously attracted to the limited play options.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Switch and Go Dinos Turbo Bronco The RC Triceratops Vehicle

text_fidelity_a: Hot Wheels Marvel Avengers Assemble Avengers 5-Pack [Amazon Exclusive] This made-in-Thailand collection of die-cast Avengers has proven to be a great hit for my 3.5 year old.  His familiarity with Avengers is not very strong, but hours pass by with his role playing aided by this collection.  A well-made set typical of the Hot Wheels brand; appealing construction, Subtleties on whether the set is a true reflection of Avengers and whether cars are the right representations for Hulk and Thor may be lost on the target audience - overall, an excellent set.
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Marvel Avengers Assemble Avengers 5-Pack [Amazon Exclusive]

text_fidelity_a: Green Toys Rocket, Red/Blue - 4 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Kids Toy Vehicle Playset. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA. While the brand deserves kudos for making toys from recycled plastic - that alone is not sufficient for a loyal brand following if the product is not that great.  Luckily, this particular toy doesn't disappoint.  For the target audience of 2 yrs and above (most likely 2-4 yr old will find this interesting for a while), the use of primary colors, very simple mechanical parts (just two 'doors' that can be easily maneuvered by a 2 yr old) and the relative size will prove to be attractive.  For the parent - the absence of any annoying sounds, lack of small components, and the ability afforded for pure imaginative play is welcome.  However, for the 'features' this toy provides, it is of 'fair' value at this price point only if you value the "green" credentials and "leave-it-to-imagination" nature of the toy to be much more valuable than any other electronic gizmo.
text_fidelity_b: Green Toys Rocket, Red/Blue - 4 Piece Pretend Play, Motor Skills, Kids Toy Vehicle Playset. No BPA, phthalates, PVC. Dishwasher Safe, Recycled Plastic, Made in USA.

text_fidelity_a:
World Series of Yahtzee Board Games The gaudy noisy console alone may drive adults away from this variant of Yahtzee..while the digital aspect may enhance appeal to kids, the increased requirement of speed/response may make this game too "hyper" and noisy pretty soon. The subtle changes in the rules may also limit the interest of those already familiar with the original game.
The game pieces look "casino-like" but the board itself is quite flimsy and not likely to withstand repeated use. Overall, an OK twist to the original game, but probably not enough to keep the kids gravitating towards "Temple Runs"...
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

text_fidelity_a: Maisto R/C 1:24 Scale 1967 Ford Mustang GT Radio Control Vehicle (Colors/ Mhz May Vary) This is a good value for the advertised price - stylish design, good details, light (its plastic) and a very entertaining "entry-level" R/C toy.  Not sure who the target audience is, but my 8 year old has a blast entertaining my 2 year old with it. Neither one couldn't care less whether it is a 67 Mustang (a red one at that).  But now, I own a classic car and it runs on batteries (not included).  Finally a classic car I can afford the insurance and upkeep....  Combined with hours of fun for the kids, this is a good value.  Part of the fun comes from the fact that the wheels don't seem aligned, the steering wheel mostly works on a prayer and direction changes can be random and the speed is (too low to print).  With screws to hold the remote and the car, the packaging is more robust than what my smartphones came in... Overall, a good value.
text_fidelity_b: Maisto R/C 1:24 Scale 1967 Ford Mustang GT Radio Control Vehicle (Colors/ Mhz May Vary)

text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price TRIO Hot Wheels Stunt Ramp Builder After over 3 months of observing how a 6.5 yr old has been treating this set, it seems like the most fun was derived during the building than actual playing. Big sis had fun trying to build different ramps to entertain a 15 month old lil bro (not recommended for play for children less than 3 according to the specs).  The pieces seem quite strong and the structures when put together do not tip over or seem unstable. Overall, very sturdy pieces that are easy to build with.  This is a decent start for evaluating a child's interest in building - before graduating to even more creative sets from Lego ([[ASIN:B000NO9GT4 LEGO Ultimate Building Set - 405 Pieces (6166)]][[ASIN:B004GUMGK2 LEGO Community Miniature Figure Set - Contains 256 Pieces]] are favorites in this house).  The limitations of this set is that creativity is limited to ramps and very limited structures and there are not many logical complementary sets.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price TRIO Hot Wheels Stunt Ramp Builder

text_fidelity_a: Tonka Chuck and Friends Fold and Go Tumble Tower The best part of this tumble tower is the cute little truck that comes with it - both "testers" of the toy (2 yrs and a very young 7 months - not recommended  age) preferred to play "freestyle" with the truck than use the tumble tower - they lost interest in the "tumbling" very quickly.  The younger one actually liked the voice responses when he touched the tower - and was smiling with a 1000 Watt smile..and would intently watch along the older kid play with the truck...  (Luckily, there is a OFF button to power off the voice - but no volume control).  The highly repetitive and non-creative elements of the toy is not likely to sustain a kid's interest for long - encouraging freestyle play - mixing with other playsets, etc is a far better option to get value from this playset.
text_fidelity_b: Tonka Chuck and Friends Fold and Go Tumble Tower

text_fidelity_a: Boley Unicorn Toy, Toy Unicorn with Sound and Music, Unicorn Toy with Wings for Girls and Boys, Ages 3+ My daughter really likes this unicorn toy. It has a brush that comes with it, makes noises and plays music, and is easily integrated into her small herd of fantastical beasts. She loves the brightly colored wings, although I think the toy would have been fine with or without the wings. She plays with this unicorn for hours, and it has become one of her favorite toys. I would order this again.
text_fidelity_b: Boley Unicorn Toy, Toy Unicorn with Sound and Music, Unicorn Toy with Wings for Girls and Boys, Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a: Sooez Heavy Duty MTG Deck Card Box with Dice Storage, 100+ Deck Case Boulder, Perfect Deck Holder for MTG Commander/YuGiOh/Pokemon/TCG and Sports Cards (Black) This deck box has so many features that people who play trading card games will like. The bottom portion easily holds dice and counters. The top portion is great for two small decks or one commander deck, at least for MTG. Everything came together nicely, and the storage deck box is perfect for travel. My son got this for Christmas, and he was very excited about it. All the rest of our family players were a bit green with envy about this deck storage. Definitely a winner.
text_fidelity_b: Sooez Heavy Duty MTG Deck Card Box with Dice Storage, 100+ Deck Case Boulder, Perfect Deck Holder for MTG Commander/YuGiOh/Pokemon/TCG and Sports Cards (Black)

text_fidelity_a: 400 Pockets Trading Card Binder with Sleeves, 4-Pockets Zipper Card Binder Collect Holder Storage Carrying Games Case Compatible for Pokemon Cards, Red I like this binder for keeping my MTG collection in an easy to find, easy to retrieve, easy to put back state. The zipper keeps the cards secure. The outer flaps are somewhat rigid, but do have a certain amount of give and flex. I would have rather the outside flaps be sturdier than they are, but with the cards inserted, it does give it more structure. It isn't a bad choice in general.

After multiple readings of directions and many try outs we think we kind of have a handle on the basics but doing any tricks are an accidental result only.  Batteries are already in this.  Everything for power is concentrated in the center of this orb.  It comes w/USB to charge through our computer.  There is a tiny, tiny white slide tab in center by batteries that you move to turn this on.  Immediately (if charged) the center ball light will come on and flash colors.  When charging or a problem, the ball light will flash red only.  This is a fairly fragile  plastic caged flyer.  It doesn't weigh a lot because it has to keep it's self flying + hovering with 4 little sets of plastic blades that rotate (think fan blades).  Four extra blades come with this. Inside the orb besides the power center and the blades are sensors that will cause the orb to change directions when they are blocked in any way. To start, you have it on and slowly let it drop out of yr hands, it will drop and start hovering before it actually hits the floor(the sensors realize there is something in the way). After it starts hovering low over floor you get a hand(s) underneath and just start raising it and moving it all over the place by using yr hands to block the sensors...All the while, center light is flashing colors and the orb is making this noise..lol, between a whine & buzz and you find yrself almost running around the room trying to control this thing!  It will go up to the ceiling and then you have to figure out how to get a hand up to control it!  We don't dare take it outside to do, afraid it wouldn't come back! Reading info for Major Arcana cards- general meaning and interpretation (upright), love and relationships (upright), money and career (upright), general meaning and interpretation (reversed), love and relationships (reversed) & money and career (reversed)

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.

LEGO NINJAGO Temple of Resurrection 70643 Building Kit (765 Piece) What I like with this LEGO set is that it does come with 7 mini figures. Makes it so much easier for me because I didn't have to run out to try to find some type of figures so the kids were able to play with this once they got it all built.
I let the older grandchildren go ahead and build this by themselves. It's getting hard for Paps to see all those smaller pieces anymore.
What was cute is that once they had it about 1/2 way built, they let the smaller kids pretend that the "warriors" were in command on getting their temple built. Because of that, they really helped keep the younger ones occupied for at least 3 days.
This is what I love about toys like this. Kids aren't glued to the tv, and kids aren't glued to their phones. They are using their brains and their hands to build something. Then they are using their brains to come up with a new adventure each time they play with it.
And, it's not set for just one age group. Yes, to build it the child has to be a certain age to understand the concept of putting it all together and reading the instructions. But, once it's all built the younger children (once they know not to put small items in their mouths or destroy what's built) can join in and play. Right now we have kids ranging from 4 1/2 to 12 playing with it. And when they grow older and lose interest in it, we pack up the entire set in zip baggies, add the instructions, and repack it into the box to save for the next generation of kids in the future.
I have always liked how well LEGOS are made. Parts are nice and sturdy and the colors on the blocks seem to last for years on end.

Fisher-Price Imaginext DC Super Friends, R/C Transforming Batbot Not only do my grand kids love transformer type toys but, my grown children also love them!

It does require 6 AA batteries for the Batbot. 2 AAA batteries for the remote. A LOT of batteries so I'm hoping they last for more than a day.
With this toy I might consider rechargeable batteries depending on how long regular batteries last.

The remote control is in the shape of the "batman" bat. Not only too cute but it fits in the childs hand so nicely.
Also comes with a small batman doll that fits into the belly part of the Batbot.
I am really hoping this toy is made as well as it looks. This is something all the kids will playing with for a very long time.

This transforming Batbot is just too nice of a toy to pass up. A little pricey but, so well worth every cent.

text_fidelity_a:
Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd Comes packed in a nice sturdy box. Inside the play yard is in a nice nylon bag.
Just pull the 2 velcro straps open, take off the wrap around/bottom part of play yard, pop the play yard open, insert bottom pad.
It wasn't until I was packing this back up that I found the instructions. They are in a small pocket that's on the wrap around/bottom pad part of play pen. With that said, we had a little trouble getting this set up but, finally got it figured out without instructions.
When opening, before you push the middle part of the bottom down, straighten and lock the side rails up. If you open it up all the way, the two smaller sides won't lock into place. Pull the red strap back up a bit then click them and push the bottom back down.

The bottom pad is a bit thin and it's a little shorter than the play yard is. Nothing that I would take a star away for.
Once set up, it seems sturdy enough to keep a small child safe.
There is nice padding around the entire top. Even the release buttons are under the padded top rail so there's no chance of child pinching any fingers.
Has nice plastic wheels on one side so you can easily lift one side and roll it to another location.
The top arching top attachment is cute with 2 small monsters attached to it. It just snaps onto the side rails and is nice and flexible. Not sure how much abuse that can withstand. And not sure what a bigger child would do to it if they were jumping in it.
Packing it back up was just a little difficult. Have to make sure the side rails are completely released so it closes up nicely to be packed. Nothing to complain about. Do it a few times and it will be a breeze.
The bottom pad wraps around the play yard. Put velcro straps through opening, pull tight, and push the velcro into place.
Slips back easily into nylon packing bag.
Nylon bag also has a couple handles for easy carrying and I can slip it onto a bike hook and hang it in the garage so it doesn't take up floor space.
This is a great play pen/play yard for a young child. Can toss it into the car and bring it anywhere you might need it.
I think the price is a great price for what you're getting.
I really don't have any complaints with this.
text_fidelity_b: Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd

It's a nice Smartwatch for children 4+. I think it would be better for an older child. On the plus side, the sprinkle packet stayed closed in the vanilla kit box (it broke open in the chocolate kit box and there were sprinkles everywhere). The frosting packet is inside the main pouch with loose flour, so it's a messy proposition to get the frosting packet out -- flour spills easily. Lastly, the silicone molds are quite flimsy. Putting them into something supportive, such as a muffin tin, is highly recommended prior to filling and baking.

The vanilla donuts have a much better flavor than the chocolate, especially when additional vanilla extract is added. The assembly process is simple and, while kids will need supervision (especially when dealing with the silicone molds) it's a fun activity.

Taking all the pros and cons into consideration puts my score at 3.5 stars. It's a great idea, but some of the kinks need to be ironed out to make it a kit that is worth the price charged.

PLANET BAKE Donut Baking Kit - Vegan Chocolate Donuts with Pre-Measured Ingredients and No Added Sugar- Complete Chef Kit Idea for Boys and Girls ages 4-12 I'm not at all pleased with this donut kit. I like the idea -- a kit that includes everything needed to make baked, frosted donuts that kids (with supervision) can take on as a fun project. Unfortunately, the execution of the idea was not done well.

The items come in a flimsy cardboard box that is easily dented up in transit. It makes for a poor presentation should this be a gift item sent to child. Inside the box is a set of cheap silicone molds for the donuts, a packet of sprinkles and a sealed packet with the mixes. The sprinkle packet opened up in transit so there were sprinkles everywhere. Two stars for the overall concept of a donut kit as a fun kid project (both making and decorating) but everything else is a fail.

text_fidelity_a:
JOY FOR ALL - Freckled Pup - Brown and White Soft-Touch Coat - Realistic and Lifelike Interactive Companion Pets A few years ago I purchased a similar “robo pet” (a cat) for my elderly Mom. It was cute and somewhat entertaining, but the motions were jerky and robotic, and the audio was rather poor. I was looking forward to trying this dog version out since I thought the tech would have improved over the past few years.

Sadly, no. The motions are still rather jerky and accompanied with a lot of mechanical noise. The range of motions exhibited is quite limited. The audio is of poor quality – it sounds like it is coming from a ten cent speaker. It performs about the same as the robo cat I purchased a few years ago for less then half the cost of this puppy. Given the price point, the performance was pretty disappointing.

On the plus side, the overall build quality shows some good attention to detail. The tongue and foot pads are rubbery plastic with a much nicer feel than you would expect. The fur is very well attached. On the downside, the fur feels fake and artificial.

This is not what I would call a “cuddly” pet due to the artificial fur feel plus the fact that it is pretty hard under the fur.

It runs on 4 C batteries, which come already installed. The battery compartment has a three position switch: on, off and mute. It is a little challenging finding the battery compartment – you have to really hunt for a seam on the underside which comes apart via Velcro.

Most of the feedback from the puppy is cute – it moves its head and barks/cries/pants when you scratch its ears. It also responds to sound so you can talk to it. The only routine it has that I didn’t care for is the heart beat. If you scratch its back, you’ll hear a heart sound. To be frank, I found that rather creepy – it sounded like something out of the Tell-tale Heart. On the plus side, once the heart sound was heard, the pup got the name Edgar.

While there have been some incremental improvements in the tech for these “robo pets” over the past few years, it’s still pretty crude. It might hold some fun for a small child, but the non-cuddly nature of it makes it a poor substitute for a plush animal that can be hugged (even if it doesn’t bark or cry). Two stars, since the performance does not come close to justifying the cost.
text_fidelity_b: JOY FOR ALL - Freckled Pup - Brown and White Soft-Touch Coat - Realistic and Lifelike Interactive Companion Pets

EZ BioResearch Bacteria Science Kit (I) : Pre-poured LB Agar Plates and Cotton Swabs, E-Book for Science Fair Project with Award Winning Experiments I used to work in Microbiology and one job in particular pertained to streaking for bacteria and viruses on various types of agar plates. We used to mix up and pour our own plates for most of our plating and only used pre-made blood agar plates for growth isolation. That said, these EZ BioResearch Pre-poured Agar plates worked great for my child's science experiment. Though they were poured on the thin side, they were thick enough to show growth from water that had been filtered using various filtering devices. I was worried that they might dry out while being stored in the refrigerator until we were ready to use them, but they seemed fresh and clear of any contamination. The sterile swabs worked great for our purposes. The 10 plates and swabs gave us enough plates for two runs of our experiment plus controls.

I would definitely use these again. The nutrient agar was just what our bacteria wanted and these plates made it clear to us which filtering device was the best, and which one was the worst. Very good plates!
text_fidelity_b: EZ BioResearch Bacteria Science Kit (I) : Pre-poured LB Agar Plates and Cotton Swabs, E-Book for Science Fair Project with Award Winning Experiments

text_fidelity_a:
Thames and Kosmos Remote-Control Machines DLX My nearly 12 year old daughter was super thrilled to see this box sitting on the counter when she got home from school. She immediately tore into it and with mom (me) helping her for awhile she began to build the robotic arm. I eventually bowed out since she was obviously fine building it without parental supervision. I was amazed at all the various parts. 3 motors, a remote control and lots of plastic parts that somehow come together into various machine creations. She had the robotic arm completely built that evening and it was picking up things like doggie toys, socks and iPods then rotating around and releasing them into a box. The robotic arm tended to want to fall over when it raised up too high but she figured out how to build onto the base to stabilize it.

The instruction booklet is very detailed, but it only has pictures. the pictures are full color and you must carefully study it a bit to understand what connectors you need to what parts, and exactly how they're connected together. She said she would have liked a few written instruction but the pictures were fine. So it would seem that no particular language is required to build the various machines in the box. The pictures are not simple and they take some time to study, but they are very well done. She also said it's a great set and she will be disassembling the robotic arm to build other ideas given in the book. After a few are built, I expect her to come up with some original designs of her own. I think the book is superb at showing how to build and should plant seeds to stimulate an interested person into building some of their own creations.

The parts included will only build what is given in the book. If you or your child want to build even more exotic machines, then a second kit might need to be purchased. I think this is a great starter kit to get someone interested in building machines/robots but it is limited by the amount of parts included. And it doesn't include batteries. She used 5 AA batteries to get her robotic arm to work. But it was pretty cool watching her manipulate it via remote control. I personally feel girls should be given such gifts and encouraged to build these things. It is superb in helping them understand how things work in relation to each other. My daughter told me she understood how it functioned and even took the time to describe to me in detail how this part turns this part which causes this part to do this and so on.... I was extremely pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Thames and Kosmos Remote-Control Machines DLX

Barbie Dream House Arrived yesterday in a big box. Parts loosely tossed inside, some in plastic bags. The included instructions are so BAD that we didn't/couldn't even use them to assemble the Dream House. We relied mainly on the pictures on the front of the box to guide us.

Pieces are initially hard to snap together. Some of the white columns go in very specific places so I had to take some out and replace them with others. Luckily, I had 2 kids and another adult helping me assemble this thing. The main elevator gets stuck at the second level and I need to work on that some more to get it functioning properly, if possible. The plastic parts are durable enough, I still felt I had to be extra careful to avoid breaking any of them. After we had it mostly assembled I was able to finally snap all the columns in place whereas before no matter how hard I tried I couldn't get them to snap firmly into the bases.

A LOT of accessories are included from silverware to bathroom fixtures, jewelry, etc...so there are LOT of small parts to suck up in the vacuum cleaner or for a pet (like ours) to chew up. We will have to be extra careful about those but they are nice to have to complete the Dream House environment. A sticker page is included that you peel and stick to various areas of the house to make it seem more realistic - fireplace, etc...

Although I had a hard time assembling it (don't try to assemble it on an empty stomach), I didn't for once lose my cool and toss it out the window. We got it assembled, it looks pretty cool to be honest. And my 9 year old daughter absolutely went nuts over it. She loves Barbie and this Dream House is like a parallel Universe to her which she can escape into make-believe land instead of watching TV. Even her tomboy sister likes to play with it. I don't know if it will maintain it's appeal after a while, but despite it's difficulty in assembly, and the horrible instructions (just small black and white pictures, no words whatsoever), you can assemble it if you are patient and keep trying different parts and studying the pictures on the box.

And it's pretty tall....at least 4 feet high. The barbie dolls fit nicely inside of it and overall it's a pretty cool thing to look at when it's completely assembled and all the furniture and stuff is placed inside it. I would have loved to have had one of these when I was a kid. Is it worth $159.00? I don't know. I might would have paid at least a hundred for it.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Dream House

Ravensburger Dad's Shed - 500 Pieces Large Format Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly I bought this puzzle for my 86 year old mother. The pieces are larger-sized which is one of the reasons I bought this particular puzzle, and the fact I thought the picture would be one she would have an interest it.

However, though she worked very little on it, it gave us something to do while we were over at her house visiting. She would try to put some pieces together but they were almost always the wrong ones. But we still had fun.

This puzzle was really hard to work and took us about 3 visits to finally finish. There are so many items in the picture that took extra time to figure out where what piece went where. Each deck is separated from the others with marked tabs. Each deck has 1 card that explains how best to use the cards to teach the concepts that relate to the math skills that they seek to teach and has suggestions for games and activities.

The Time cards show analog clocks on one side and the time in digital format on the other. The money cards show US currency, combinations of bills and coins, on one side and the value in numbers and words on the other. The fraction cards show circles divided into portions on one side and the value written in fraction format on the other side. The function cards have large numbers showing a problem and in smaller type the problem that is on the other side of the card, which makes it easier to quiz the child.

The flash cards themselves are each approximately twice the size of a regular deck of cards, but each set is still small enough to bring along.

It hadn't registered when I'd ordered the figure, but it is over a foot wide and nearly 2.5 feet tall. While it's strong hard plastic, there are many moving parts, so it's best to transport it in its original box. It arrived via FedEx in a plastic sheath and the toy's original box. The moving parts are held down with plastic ties. I can see how unpacking/releasing the robot from the ties can be part of the fun for a kid. As I had planned to bring it to my nephew, I'm disappointed that it's too big to pack in carry on luggage.

The eyes light up when you move the robot's head. The hands can open and close their grip. The legs have secret compartments that open up to release rockets or that can serve as hiding places. There are 2 figurines that have perches - one on the shoulder and the other by the leg. The figure can move its torso but I haven't figured out how to make it walk yet.

I can imagine that it'll get my nephew excited and it's something that will interest his older sister as well.

text_fidelity_a:
eeBoo French Flash Cards I had the great fortune of parents who made sure I learned three other languages as a kid. They started very early with me and I distinctly remember them making their own flashcards. It's too bad that they didn't have access to these beautiful, affordable, and very easy to use flashcards to aid them! Now, as a parent, teacher, and a nanny, I work hard to teach my kids the basics of French and Spanish, and I stumbled across these. They have been well worth the price and they were highly affordable. Best of all, my kids that I teach love the cards and enjoy using them too. I would recommend them to both the beginner and the advanced speaker as they embark on teaching others.

There are a few times that the cards use outdated pronunciations or word choices, but it's actually a plus in my book because it aids further in teaching. When I see a card with a different context of pronunciation or word choice than what is currently popular or commonly used, then I can supplement by saying "Or you could say it like this ..." Anyways, the cards are really lovely and sturdy. They seem sort of indestructible because one of the kids I nanny is 18 months old and a total "rip things to shreds" sort and he wasn't even able to destroy one! They also wipe off nicely with a damp cloth.

Do consider using these for your own kids! You wont be sorry!
text_fidelity_b: eeBoo French Flash Cards

The game is cute and has mostly functional listening software. My son cant probounce r’s and the software recognizes it 99% of the time. This is a huge game but you can do a respectable amount with the first four books. You can only get more books with a subscription which makes sense i am assuming this product is a loss leader, year of monthly sets of 4 books is 250$. The only thing that really doesnt work if that theres four mini games outside of the main storyline and the ‘story stone’ game basically scrolls text up whether you are reading or not preventing us from actually reading the text. The other games work very well. The wand concept and the reflector. Are great concepts and work well. It does not follow tiny steps of progression like Bob’s books or a proper school curriculum, lots of things like multi syllable words and vowel combos, hard vowels etc are introduced randomly so needs some parent engagement. Overall i am impressed and signed up for a limited subscription. My son loves it.

HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 I am a solid intermediate (I hesitate to call myself advanced). Put a plane in my hands and I can probably fly it pretty well.

I have had a Night Vapor that I absolutely love to fly when I am too lazy to carry all the gear out to a park. I can fly the Night Vapor around the yard. I wanted something just a little bigger to fly in the small field behind my house. After seeing some videos on YT I could tell this plane can fly nice and slow. I made the mistake of thinking this was a 4 channel airplane when I bought it. I got it home and was a little disappointed when I pulled it out and realized there where no ailerons...until I flew it.

I have to say, this little plane is an excellent little flyer. It literally flies itself. Ultra stable in fast and slow flight. Docile stall tendencies and if you just stop touching the sticks it will roll itself over and be flying straight and level within a second or two. Take off roll is only about 5 or 6 feet if you jump of the power. Landings can be done in about 10-15 feet of concrete if you are good at spot landing. Just remember THIS IS NOT A PLANE FOR WINDY DAYS. As much as it sucks to get a RTF home and not fly it, be patient and wait. Even 5 mph is probably a bit much for this featherweight little plane. Experienced flyers will be able to handle this plane up to 5-8 mph but new guys should wait for calm winds. Since this plane is so light it doesn't really break easy, it just bounces off things. Being inherently dumb I like to do things I probably shouldn't. The result of this is my Champ being bounced off roofs, trees, rocks and pretty much any other object I just can't resist buzzing as close as I can. So far only little scuffs on the foam are the evidence of my wild flying. This little bugger is hard to break!

My Dad is new to RC and as soon as they get another Champ in at the hobby store I am buying him one to learn to fly.

As an experienced flyer I would HIGHLY recommend this for a new flyer or an experienced flyer that wants to have fun in a very big back yard or a small field.

By the way, I still wanted a 4 channel so I went straight back to the hobby store and got a Parkzone T-28 (the ultra micro version that is roughly the same size as the Champ). It is fun and the ailerons allow for more aerobatics but I have to admit the Champ is much more fun in a small field because it is so easy to fly.

I have a lot of airplanes and helis. I can't think of a better plane to learn to fly with. The Night Vapor I mentioned is also super easy to fly but the Champ flies more like the bigger planes so it will make a much better trainer.
text_fidelity_b: HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Aroma Putty, Silly Putty Alternative, Gift, 4 Count I am so glad I waited a few weeks to review this product -- When it first arrived, my reactions was little more than, "Hmm, that's interesting." I had the hardest time figuring out how to open the containers (they twist open), and the first few I opened had a very chemically, medicinal, almost artificial scent. Plus, I no longer subscribe to a daily newspaper, so the silly putty fun of my childhood -- copying pictures from the funny pages onto the putty -- was not really an option. Meh. It's okay. Kind of novel but not particularly useful.

I was headed to a funeral the next day, and I brought one of these along, thinking it might be a harmless diversion if I needed a little stress relief. I started with the peppermint. It smelled nice enough. Minty, a little bit chemical, but nice. Then I started to play with it, kneading it in my hand. At first, it was pretty hard, and I had to dig it out of the container. In no time, it became softer, just the right texture for kneading, stretching, twisting, wrapping around my finger, collapsing, kneading. It was kind of fun. I put it back in the container. My daughter opened each of the containers, stamping designs into the putty. The designs remained until the next time I opened the containers.

Since the funeral, I have had several IVs and blood draws. I brought along a little container of putty to the hospital, and found it worked just perfectly for the "make a fist and squeeze" stage. It was fun and distracting to play with while the IV was going. I keep a container in my purse, and find it fun to play with while riding the bus or subway, and when I need a whiff of something pleasant (as can happen when taking public transportation), I just hold the putty up to my nose. I can smell it, but the smell is not so strong or overwhelming as to bother others sitting nearby. And, as my husband discovered when he found a local high school newspaper, you can still copy comics from newsprint.

The containers are small and easily slip into a purse or backpack. So far, I haven't had any issues with the lids coming off when I don't want them to -- which often happens to things in my crowded purse. Occasionally, the putty becomes a little too warm and starts sticking to things. I was vigorously kneading it for some time and the putty started to stick under my rings. When that happened, I just put it away -- and it was back to its original texture in short course.

Overall, I'm really glad I discovered these little treats. They are an adult alternative to fidget spinners, and have provided more hours of -- I'm not sure if I'd call it pleasure or relief or what -- let's just say they have been used for many more hours than I ever expected I would use them, and the seem to be holding up well, staying good as new.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Aroma Putty, Silly Putty Alternative, Gift, 4 Count

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

text_fidelity_a:
Marbleocity Triple Play Archimedes Screw Marble Machine Kit I like the idea of this toy/project more than I enjoyed the toy/project itself. It might provide an hour of entertainment to someone who liked to build models or tinker, and it is mildly educational, but it wasn't that much fun to put together, it was VERY SMALL, and it took a few tries to get it to work well. I would like to give it more stars because it's such a neat idea, but somehow it did not live up to expectations.

WHAT I LIKED: Learning about Archimedes screws and how they are used to move sewage and water. The project comes with a booklet that includes instructions and a comic showing how the device works and how it is used in application. I wish there were more explanation of the principles involved. It would have been nice to have a little bit more information about the function of various parts and pieces when putting things together.

I DISLIKED: It's small. Some of the parts are really small and difficult to handle. It requires white glue and ideally, a piece of waxed paper to use as a work surface. Would have been nice if those items were included. It really didn't work so well. On of the pieces of wood in the model I made was insufficiently sloped so the ball bearing wouldn't roll off properly. It worked okay with a little cajoling -- but who wants to cajole?

I did this project with another person. It was fun to work together, but I think this is probably better suited to a solo effort, as the parts are small and you really do need to look at the instruction book closely to figure out what goes where. Also, the project suggests that you purchase a motor -- why not just include the motor in the kit?

Overall, this provided a half hour or so of amusement and I learned something. But it wasn't as much fun as it looked like it might be. Perhaps if I were a twelve-year-old who liked to tinker, I might have a more positive review.
text_fidelity_b: Marbleocity Triple Play Archimedes Screw Marble Machine Kit

text_fidelity_a: Kamigami Scarrax Robot - Discontinued by Manufacturer This box weighs next to nothing, and the contents are not particularly impressive when you open the box -- causing me to raise an eyebrow at what seems like a high price.  But after putting this toy together, you realize that you are not paying for the physical materials that make the toy, but rather for the programming that makes the toy fun.  In the box, you will find a flat plastic sheet stamped with eight parts, a bag of teeny-tinyplastic rivets for assembly, a USB charger cable, and some electronic body parts.  It takes a little bit of patience (and steady fingers) to put this the Scarrax together, but it is not particularly difficult, and no special tools are required.  It's mostly a matter of folding the pieces from the plastic sheet and snapping them together with the rivets.  I would allow an hour, at least, for getting everything together.  Once assembled, you can download the app on an apple or android device, and program your robot to do whatever.  Scarrax can really more -- you'd be surprised at his speed and dancing ability, particularly considering he's made from a single flat sheet of plastic.  I would say this is appropriate for late tweens and teens, although some younger children might be able to use it (1) if they're super geniuses or (2) with adult help.
