Mattel Games Pictionary: Frame Game I was really excited about this product, as Pictionary is one of my all-time favorite party games. This was a disappointment on so many levels.

First, there is no storage box. It comes with a frame, a frame stand, a timer, and a marker. And a dice, which got lost in no time. The "frame" itself is about the size of a sheet of paper (8" by 10"), and it is clear, so you can see through it. The small size makes it ideal for travel or a backpack, but the fact that it is clear makes it difficult to see when holding it on your lap. And forget about using it on the black coffee table. It works much better when used flat, on a light background surface. I like that you can use the frame as a window, so the see-through feature may be useful one at a time. It's pretty much impossible for two people to write on opposite sides of the board at the same time. Honestly it is pretty much for anyone to write on the board when it is in the stand, which keeps the board vertical.

We like to use large dry-erase boards when we pay Pictionary. I would recommend that rather than this game. The frame might be fun to draw on once in a while -- but shy not get a small whiteboard, which is much better suited for the purpose?

My Little Pony Equestria Girls Pinkie Pie Doll For the past few months, every trip we made to the big-box store involved a determined march through the toy section, looking to see if the Equestria Girls dolls were yet available. My 9 year old, who watched My Little Pony endlessly, and has already watched Equestria Girls more times that I want to count, was thrilled when the dolls were finally available! Her favorite doll, by far, is the Deluxe version of Rainbow Dash [[ASIN:B00CANI9RQ My Little Pony Equestria Girls Rainbow Dash Hairstyling Doll]] -- because of all that multi-colored hair. I think Pinkie Pie comes in a close second place -- again, because of all that hair. The other Equestria Girl dolls have smooth, straight hair, so Pinkie Pie's masses of pink curls are a little different and fun to play with. And her pink skin tone is a little less eerie than the purple and blue of some of the other dolls.

Pinkamena Diane Pie has sparkly eyeshadow and a "cutie mark" on her cheek, reflective of her virtue. Pinkie Pie's cutie mark consists of three balloons, and reflects her virtue of laughter. Her happy, chaotic spirit is reflected in her curly hair. There's not much in the way of accessories -- a plastic headband to tame all those curls, and a little pink hairbrush. There is only one item of clothing -- the skirt -- so I don't think that these dolls will be dressed and undressed much -- that real appeal is the hair. The boots are interchangeable, so we have switched the boots around on several of the dolls. I find the boots a little disturbing -- well actually the legs, because the doll legs end at the ankle, and the boots pop on to the ankle. Without the boots, the dolls are footless. Kind of creepy, but I guess it's better than having those teeny weeny little Barbie high heels all over the place. Pinkie Pie has a small hole in her upper back -- it's pretty well hidden under all of that hair -- but some of the other dolls come with butterfly (or angel??) wings that pop into the hole, so Pinkie Pie can borrow those wings if she's so inclined, since she too has a hole for attaching the wings. Each Equestria Girl doll also comes with a sheet of stickers and a little pamphlet -- but my daughter hasn't even looked at those, and I expect they'll end up in the trash soon. The long piece of hair is supposed to be the horse-tail, but it is odd that it has a different texture than the rest of Pinkie Pie's hair. As a mom, I thought that the hair could have been better done -- the plugs are sparse and separated, so if you don't pull Pinkie Pie's hair back just right, she looks like she just visited Hair Plugs for Men -- not pretty.

Pinkie Pie is a cute doll with a big pouf of brushable hair. Is she super high quality? Probably not. Will she be a cherished heirloom to pass down over the years? Who knows. But is she a fun plaything for an Equestria Girls fan? You bet.
text_fidelity_b: My Little Pony Equestria Girls Pinkie Pie Doll

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner This toy is plenty entertaining for a short while. It is great fun to make the art, and the paint colors are bright and contemporary (neon green, yellow, coral, blue, and purple). The spinner is seemingly durable, powered by one C-cell battery (which is not included).

But, consider --

The bottles of ink are teeny-weeny -- .6 fl oz each -- about the size of a small hotel shampoo bottle. The jars of glitter are even tinier. Although the kit contains glitter, there is no glue to apply it. The glitter seems like a bit of an afterthought. And for some reason, even though there are five colors of paint, spinner device contains only three holes to hold the paint.

The cards to paint on are tiny as well -- there are ten cards that are about 4"x 4" each, and another ten cards that are about 3" x 3". Half are black and half are white. You may be able to make "beautiful art" (says so right on the box) but at 3" x 3", it's hard to make much of a statement.

The kit contains a clear plastic "splash guard" That is labeled in tiny font as such, along with a "do not discard" warning. If you happened to overlook the label, you would likely discard the splash guard, as it is indistinguishable from much packaging.

I have a similar spin-art painter from Crayola, the color spinner -- hard to say which one of these two items would be preferable. This Alex spinner is battery-operated, the Crayola one is not. This Alex spinner definitely has cooler paint colors. The Crayola spinner has circular pieces of cardboard to paint on. They are much larger and the shape is more interesting. Either kit would be fun for kids. Once or twice.

This would be a fun toy to play with once or twice, but I wouldn't expect it to be something you will return to again and again. And if you purchase it, don't forget to get a C-cell battery.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Toys Artist Studio My Art Spinner

text_fidelity_a:
Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs We've been making potholders at home and it seemed like we were always running out of the colors we wanted, so we ordered replacements from several different sources to see what worked best. Although these are not the easiest to use, they by far make the best finished product. This is a great big bag of loops with very vibrant colors. The colors are great -- teal, cobalt, lime green, kelly green, pink, red, reddish-purple, yellow, orange -- enough to make some beautiful combinations. Compared to the other loops we've used, these are very thick and less stretchy. Because they are bulkier, they are a little harder to work with. I haven't found any that don't fit, though. On the flip side, the finished potholder is larger and holds its shape better. I've found that the stretchier brands seem to have a lot of nylon, and it doesn't seem like they'd hold up as well to hot dishes. These loops are kind of scraggly, with loose threads hanging off of them, but when you weave them together the loose threads aren't really a problem.

Someone commented that her daughter wasn't able to weave the edges with these because they were less stretchy. My daughter hasn't been able to weave the edges with these either, but she's very, very proud of the finished product as it is larger, more vibrant, and more even in shape than the potholders made with the stretchier loops.

If you want something that's really easy to use, you might check for the loops made by klutz or others, as these might not be the best bet. If you want to make cool potholders, though, these are a good choice.

UPDATE: I'm back a year later to buy more. Glad that I was able to find the good loops again. And now that my daughter is 8, she no longer has difficulty weaving the edges -- most of the time. Also, these are much easier to weave off the edges when you use the metal loom, rather than the plastic ones.

UPDATE #2: Almost two years later, and my daughter is back making potholders, this time trying to create her own designs. Need more loops!
text_fidelity_b: Friendly Loom Lotta Loops 7" Traditional Size Bright Cotton Loops Makes 8 Potholders, Weaving, Crafts for Kids and Adults by Harrisville Designs

TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese) This tank model is superlative with a lot of details to glue on. ( it has no unnecessary steps that one hates and all the details are easy to glue on and there is no awkward steps that will make one curse while doing it) It take more than the time you expected which for an experienced modeler that is a joy t o add one after another small piece to the model and make it looks very real. After it is done it looks like from a $40 dollar kit than a 16 doller kit.
I have always learned something from other people's comment about how a model is made. Here I am going to recommend using epoxy glue for small parts of plastic details. The epoxy glue gives you more time than CA glue for small detail pieces. And the epoxy glue also have thicker substance than CA glue for small pieces so it will stay in place when the small pieces are glued on. The epoxy glue also becomes thicker as time goes on so you can adjust your timing to chose the right time to glue the pieces on to the model. The smaller the pieces the faster you need to glue on the model and the larger piece you can wait until is becomes very thick before using it. Another trick about dealing with those shining drops left unintentionally on the models; I usually drop some power ( you can use fine grain white pepper dust) onto the drop of glue before it is dried. This will eliminate those ugly sheen of glue and later the glued dust can be painted as rust for weathering.
All in all this little model (about 6 inches long) is well worth your money. It looks far better than other 16 dollar model kits and i can guarantee it.
text_fidelity_b: TAMIYA Models Chi Ha Type 97 Tank (Japanese)

Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red Pandemic has become a favorite on game nights in my circle of friends, and the On the Brink Expansion improves the experience in several ways. There are new game modes, new roles, new events, and all of them work well. On the most basic level, the ability to have five players is a big improvement. You have to relearn the board setup some to compensate for how many new events are included to keep from unbalancing the game, but none of the changes are so drastic as to be overwhelming.

Aside from this, most of the new material boils down to making the game more difficult. The most basic form of this is the addition of an additional Epidemic card to enable "Legendary" difficulty (I think we lost in ten minutes the first time we tried that mode). The Virulent Strain variation to the rules increases the power of one of the diseases. The Mutation variation adds a fifth disease. All of these are good for the increased challenge, but don't really change the core gameplay too much.

The one exceptionally different mode is the Bio-Terrorist variation, which makes one player an enemy to the rest of the group. I, like many of the other reviewers, love this mode. My friends and roommates don't all agree. It is the type of game mode that certainly has the potential to ruin friendships if you play it too often, but I think it injects some welcome variety into the game. That said, it's totally optional and the expansion has plenty of other improvements to justify buying it even if this game mode doesn't prove to be a hit with your crowd.

As a last, wonderful feature, the game box comes packaged with a tray that is capable of holding the materials not only for the expansion, but for the original game as well. This way you can actually store the original game and the expansion in a single box. It sounds like a small thing, but little touches and details like that are what separate the good game publishers from the great.
text_fidelity_b: Pandemic on the Brink Board Game EXPANSION | Family /Strategy /Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ |2 to 5 players | Average Playtime 45 minutes | Made by Z-Man Games , Red

Ravensburger Cozy Retreat 500 Piece Large Format Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 14967 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly I have not done puzzles for years, but recently thought I might like to start again. My first puzzle was 1000 piece and to be honest with you, it was a little frustrating. My eyes aren’t what they used to be and the size of the puzzle was hard for me to work because of the table it was on. I had to stand up a lot to get to the top of the puzzle to work so it just wasn’t relaxing, this time I decided on the 500 piece and I bought this one without realizing the pieces were larger. I am working this on a puzzle mat and it is actually working out the size of 1000 piece puzzle because of the larger pieces. Just be aware of that if you have a smaller place to work your puzzles. So far I am finding this puzzle to be very relaxing and enjoyable there are enough objects in the puzzle so you can get a pretty good idea of where the pieces are going to go in the general area of the puzzle. The pieces are going together very nicely, and there was absolutely no puzzle dust whatsoever in the box.
I would definitely recommend this puzzle especially if you are just getting into puzzles or don’t want one that is very hard. This wouldn’t be considered extremely easy I don’t think but if you are looking for a challenge, I think this one might be a little too casual but for me just getting back into puzzles after years it’s been a very good choice. I’ve been working on it for a few hours today and I have a nice amount completed.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Cozy Retreat 500 Piece Large Format Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 14967 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

Harrisville Designs Lap Loom Kit, Hand Weaving for Kids and Adults (Style B) I used to make wall hangings as a child with homemade looms. I recently met someone who weaves huge items and after seeing photos of her work my interest in weaving was renewed. I like the simplicity of these looms but do have some comments. Firstly, the frame is wood with plastic pegs. A screw in each corner holds the frame together but mine is a bit loose. I may need to tighten later. Instruction booklet is well written, read all the way through before starting because there are tips later on in the booklet. Parents please note that every other row you must insert a second flat shed stick into the loom. It's not complicated, just takes time so be aware if your child may not have patience to do this.
My only complaint is I ordered the bigger size B loom and in the photo on Amazon it showed yarn in orange, yellow and reds so I bought a refill yarn kit called Sierra because it was black and red and I thought it would be nice to have both but when my loom arrived I see the size B comes with the black and red yarn and the smaller sized A has the oranges. So now I'll have two black and red items :( I don't know where the photo came from but it should be corrected!
The manufacturers website shows the correct colors but I didn't go there until after I got my loom. I would also recommend spending $10 more to get the Wonderloom. It helps push the yarn down evenly.
This loom is a good size for making place mats.
text_fidelity_b: Harrisville Designs Lap Loom Kit, Hand Weaving for Kids and Adults (Style B)

If you have a backyard and want something for a younger kid to play around with and you won't lose a ton if it breaks, then this is it.

text_fidelity_a: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Pounding Bench Wooden Toy With Mallet - STEAM Toddler Toy I have two toddlers and really love the idea of Melissa and Doug's wooden, no battery products and I am willing to pay an extra few dollars for high quality items - assuming they last. However, I am now seeing quality issues in multiple M&D products and they just aren't lasting. This bench was the first casualty when it fell apart (into multiple pieces) only a few weeks after purchasing. I have had it in my "fix up" box, but so far I am not having any luck putting it back together so my boys just use the hammer on our other workbench (which is now coming loose as well). Other products are proving to be less than solid as well - the trains in our M&D train set are chipping paint everywhere, our paint brushes are shedding their bristles, and our wooden train stacking toy lost its wheels. Seems like there has been a definite decrease in quality over the past year and I am much more wary of purchasing Melissa and Doug products from here on out. I have found a few new wood products at Land of Nod and the quality has been superior thus far.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Pounding Bench Wooden Toy With Mallet - STEAM Toddler Toy

text_fidelity_a:
NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Break Open 2 Geodes Science Kit – Includes Goggles, Detailed Learning Guide and Display Stand - Great STEM Science gift for Mineralogy and Geology enthusiasts of any age If you have a child that is into science and searching for "pretty rocks", this is a cool gift to give. However, after opening it you'll find that this isn't a child-friendly operation any longer.

You will need (at minimum) a hammer and a punch (or you can put the geode in an old sock and bash it on the ground).... You'll make an absolute mess with them.... these geodes don't open easily or cleanly. They will shatter into thousands of pieces and you will have a broken and mutilated looking geode after all is said and done.

If you want to make the most of this kit, you will need to get a diamond saw blade and carefully cut them open.

In our kit we received a selection of geodes. One or two that were small but decent sized. The rest got much smaller. For the cost, I have to admit, I was expecting a little bit more. However, after receiving the kit and feeling the weight of it, I understand why they can't provide larger geodes. This kit is heavy.

Again, this is an interesting gift for kids. Don't expect too much. It is work to open the geodes (if you want them to look nice) and they are somewhat small in size. However, economically, from a business stand-point.... this is a good value for what they are delivering to you. Weight equals money these days when it comes to shipping.....

text_fidelity_a:
NSI Smithsonian Giant Volcano Kit Small When my 4th child, my 6 yr old daughter, decided she wanted to do a volcano for her science fair project, I inwardly groaned. Having gone the modeling clay and salt dough methods in the past with my older children, I really wasn't up for doing this project again. So, I decided to make life easier and buy a kit from the local craft store. I brought it home, THEN decided to read the reviews on it before we started, as there are often good hints in them. Unfortunately I found this volcano had horrible reviews. No one seemed to have any success with them. I almost took it back, but decided to take a peak at the contents. They were completely different from what had been described by previous viewers, so we took a chance at it. It seems that Smithsonian has paid attention to the reviews and the new contents avoid all the previous problems. Instead of a poorly fitting plastic mold that you have to quickly pour uncooperative gray cement into, there are now 2 large cardboard circles that you use embroidery floss to weave a lava tube to. Sounds complicated, I know, but with an extra hand (I actually used my chin) to hold the lava tube in place during the first half, it really isn't difficult. (Use a knife to ensure the slits in the cardboard are all open before you start. Some of the pegs will have more than one string looped over them- just keep the strings all going vertical.) I then taped the structure down onto a larger piece of foamboard. (Not included.) Then, 2 rolls of plaster impregnated mesh tape are cut into 6 inch strips. You then dip the strips into warm water and drape and smooth them around the structure, overlapping them slightly until the entire volcano is covered. My 6 yr old was able to do this part completely without assistance. The plaster was completely dry by the following day. The result was nice and lightweight. The string structure resulted in vertical groove lines that we liked, because they gave the feel of lava flow lines. In fact, I kinda wish we had intentionally made the grooves a little more prominent. The old kit had no paint and was gray. The new contents include brown and green paints with a little sponge to apply them with. My 6 yr old used a paintbrush instead, and needed additional paint because she also painted the foam board base. The kit also includes a small vial of lava "glow" paint that we have yet to add. There are no longer non-working eruption tablets, either. Instead, you are expected to provide your own coloring, vinegar and baking powder (creates a longer eruption than baking soda, according to the directions). But, we have those on hand and specific amounts and instructions are given, so we expect success when we try it tonight. I don't usually write reviews, but felt I had to so people would know that this kit is no longer such a bust. It's been the easy experience I had hoped for! It's too bad Smithsonian doesn't get a fresh review slate to go with the new and improved contents. (Note: I don't know if the old kits are still out on the market. The box our kit came in looked exactly like the one above, except with a sticker touting the glow paint that it came with.)

Edited to add: We added the glow paint. It isn't much, but is pretty impressive looking when the lights are turned off. The recommended amounts of baking powder and vinegar aren't really enough. It's more of a bubbling effect. The baking powder makes bubbles for a longer period of time, but baking soda has a quicker, more dramatic reaction. The best volcano effect is with a reaction called "elephant toothpaste" using yeast. A google search should get you the amounts needed. Anyways, the kit was great. She had the most beautiful volcano at the science fair. : )

Update: It's 4 yrs later and my youngest child also decided he wanted to do a volcano for the science fair. Remembering this kit, we went ahead and got another one. He's 8 and my 15 yr old assembled the cardboard structure for him. We duct taped it down to a foam board and he plastered the strips on, then painted it and the foam board with his 10 yr old sister and 7 yr old friend. You definitely need more paint and a paint brushes in addition to what is in the kit. They now require a scientific method experiment at the science fair, so we tested a variety of volcano eruption recipes: vinegar+baking soda, vinegar+baking powder, peroxide+yeast+dish soap, mentos+coke, and ketchup+dish soap+baking soda to see what was the best. Based on our results, we created our own recipe: 50 ml dish soap+150ml vinegar+1 T baking soda. Baking soda makes the biggest reaction and is dramatically fast, while the dish soap makes bubbles that last. Note: the above recipe is too big for the volcano which holds only 1/4 c liquid. We'll have to size it down.
text_fidelity_b: NSI Smithsonian Giant Volcano Kit Small

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Forces & Interactions: Middle School Classroom Kit | NGSS-Aligned for Physics & Engineering Classes| Teacher Guide & Lesson Plans | Durable, Timed for Classroom Use, Includes Storage I generally love Thames and Kosovo’s products. This is a classroom physics kit. There are enough pieces to build several cars at once, but some experiments can only be done one at a time. For me that is fine since I am using this with homeschooling several kids, but for a small classroom, I can see students wanting to make their own. I am also not sure there are enough pieces to build more than one ramp. The snap pieces can be hard to remove especially for smaller finger, there is one connector puller included. For bigger groups of students I would have liked more of the pullers (looks a bit like the Lego splitter tool) You will need to provide weights for one experiment and batteries for the power module. I used slightly stronger nylon cord for my bucket pulls. It comes with magnets, wires, cord, nails, a cheep compass, and paper clips. Most of the odds and ends I just used my own and left the nails etc in the bucket.
There is a nice top divided tray to store the tinier pieces, and the bottom bin I left filled with the large pieces. The top of the storage box is dimpled to allow connecting the (not Lego) plastic building blocks to it. My kids had fun and easily figured out how to build onto any experiment we tried.
My one and biggest complaint with the kit is the magnet and iron filing board. None of the magnets work. They appear to have either been super heated or smacked around enough to unalign or weaken the magnet. I have a collection of bar magnets and rare earth magnets so I replaced the included magnets with my own. Most science teachers I know have collections of magnets so overall not a big issue. The clear iron filing board designed to show magnetic fields was a bust though. It’s not that the filings didn’t align, but that there were so few filings inside to show anything to begin with. I have a board I bought from a science teaching supply store and it has enough filings to demonstrate the magnetic field. This one was meh at best.
Because it does allow for multiple fun interactive classroom experiments I am rating this four stars. The spiral teaching book was great with Detailed instructions for building, and alignment guides (this assumes a knowledge of the material on the teacher’s part). The plastic technic like pieces were easy to use and fun for the kids. It was in the magnetism and wires and accessories that fell short of expectation. My Dad was a physicist (and MD) and I have a background in Physics as well, I had no trouble explaining what was going on to my kids, but this does not have answers to the questions because it assumes teacher knows answers, and how to relate NGSS Standards. Booklet includes lesson plan with target student age, time to teach, and any any materials needed. It is a great classroom kit, or group science instruction kit. Just keep in mind it’s target is classroom supplementary instruction, not home so kit is not designed to be a done by a kid on their own following a visually interesting book. (The spiral is pretty standard for teacher lesson books)
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Forces & Interactions: Middle School Classroom Kit | NGSS-Aligned for Physics & Engineering Classes| Teacher Guide & Lesson Plans | Durable, Timed for Classroom Use, Includes Storage

text_fidelity_a:
TEAM MAGNUS 18ft XL Slip and Slide - Heavy Duty Inflatable Slide with Central Sprinkler and XL Crash Pad I’ve used the slide on a slight slope and almost a flat surface. PRO’s: width and length of slide (twice as long as other slides in target audience), easy setup/operate/put away, splash zone (pool at end) works to stop toddlers. CON’s: the streaming water that “wets” the slide is too wide near the end of the slide and hardly existing at the start of the slide. The splash zone edges (inflated) nearest to the slide don’t ensure participant won’t slide over and miss splash zone.
A simple design improvement would be to have far less watering holes for the slip and slide near the splash zone and progressively more as you near the starting point. This to be is the largest flaw in the slide.
There are ways to “work around” the lack of water on the slide (the lack of slipperiness) but the product should fix this vs the customer having workarounds.
text_fidelity_b: TEAM MAGNUS 18ft XL Slip and Slide - Heavy Duty Inflatable Slide with Central Sprinkler and XL Crash Pad

text_fidelity_a: Holy Stone GPS Drone with 1080P HD Camera FPV Live Video for Adults and Kids, Quadcopter HS110G Upgraded Version, 2 Batteries, Altitude Hold, Follow Me and Auto Return, Easy to Use for Beginner [[VIDEOID:3c39acadb44f7af0c1ae7316aabdb717]] A Holy Stone Masterpiece! This is the first controller I have with also a USB rechargeable battery battery. The downloadable app installed on my iPhone with no issues and quickly and easily connected to the drone. The flight times are very good with the supplied battery as I got around 12 minutes of flight time. As an overall package, this is a very high quality, solid built, stable and beautiful looking drone that is easy and fun to fly. Highly recommended for both the beginner and advanced pilot.

text_fidelity_a: Monterey LG8510 Lady Bug Lure, Pack of 3 I buy these lures each year ever since I learned that ladybugs like to cluster in small hollow space in houses. One year I had 1 exterior wall with over 1000 ladybugs crawling on it in the sunshine, a day later they were all gone and over the following weeks they started falling out of the cracks inside my house. Every morning as soon as the sun rose I would start finding them everywhere. I checked the internet and found the Ladybuglady who told me that ladybugs cluster in the late fall to stay warm through the winter. If they find a space like a house and a way in they will literally take over the sun side wall of the house. The way to avoid this was to build ladybug houses (similar to bird house but with smaller holes) and place them in your garden and orchards where the Ladybugs will benefit your plants (they eat aphids) and get these lures to draw them to the houses. Well for 2 years it has worked like a charm. No ladybugs in my houses and the trees in my orchard are doing very well.
text_fidelity_b: Monterey LG8510 Lady Bug Lure, Pack of 3

I bought this kit because the loom was metal, and I'd read reviews and seen videos where the person's PLASTIC loom would break. So, what's the problem?
I really don't like how the loops slip off this loom, especially when you're getting towards completing the project. Pop, pop, pop go the loops - OFF the loom! This might be the nature of pot-holder looming, but I think the problem is the little spokes (hooks) are straight, so there's nothing to keep the loops from slipping off. They should be curved and WIDER at the top so the loops can't slide off. Towards the end, when you're crocheting the edges together, the last side can get completely unraveled.
THAT IS frustrating.
I'm going to try to find another loom.
Unfortunately, I looked at a lot looms before I bought this one, and they ALL seem to have the same design flaw.

Afterthought:
On a positive note: the loops are NOT polyester, but cotton, so the potholders came out nice 'n thick and heavy.
I can see why posters said they lasted a long time. They probably will.

text_fidelity_a:
Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 120" X 72" X 22", for Ages 6+ We purchased this pool together with the following products:

- Intex The Wet Set Rectangular Pool Cover
- Intex 120V AC Quickfill Pump
- 10'X12' HD Tarp
- Associated pool toys

Set up was made quick and easy by matching the large opening on the pump with each of the three large intake openings on the pool to get all three levels quickly filled with air, starting at the bottom as per the directions. After laying out the tarp the pool unfolded quickly and we centered it over the tarp prior to inflating. We followed the suggestions of other reviewers to use the smaller tip on the pump with the smaller valve openings on the pool to finalize the air fill so as not to over inflate. The entire setup process couldn't have taken more than 15-20 minutes. Very easy.

It took another 20-25 minutes to fill the pool with a garden hose to the fill line clearly marked inside the pool. With a 90 degree day outside in the sun we could have done without adding any hot water but we did put in a couple pots anyway. We also added a cup of household bleach to the pool as one reviewer suggested. Undoubtedly there are better ways of keeping the water clean and we'll research those as we go along. We simply wanted to get up and running quickly the first time as our 5 year old couldn't wait.

Wouldn't have set this pool up any other way. The electric air pump made inflation of the three levels very quick and easy. I would recommend a tarp (they're quite inexpensive at Lowes or Home Depot), and while you could use a bed sheet as a pool cover we're quite satisfied with the Intex product.

Just a reminder - there's a single drain valve in the bottom corner of the pool. Remember to close that prior to filling. I forgot to do it and as I began filling the pool I thought it had arrived with a leak. Doh!

Keep in mind that this is a day 1 review. Cleaning, etc., may dampen our enthusiasm but if this pool lasts through the summer it will have been well worth the investment.

The only complaint we have after our first really fun day with this pool is that Amazon lowered the price by $5 the day after ours arrived. That's the second time this has happened to us with an Amazon purchase. While it's only $5 it is irksome.
text_fidelity_b: Intex Swim Center Family Inflatable Pool, 120" X 72" X 22", for Ages 6+

Kelsyus Premium Floating Lounger XL with Fast Inflation, Inflatable Recliner Chair, Lake & Pool Float for Adults with Cup Holder, Amazon Exclusive I bought this item and, for the most part, enjoyed its design, but...
1. It's just about impossible to inflate or deflate because of the valves; standard foot pumps do not work with these valves and doing it by mouth (which is what I ended up doing) is extremely tedious, because there is not enough length to hold it in your mouth to pinch it for opening the valve. Deflating the main air chamber is likewise nearly impossible, this time because that chamber is composed of both the main ring and the air pillow -- it would have been a lot smarter to use three chambers. (The second, tiny air chamber to float the footholder, does not hold much air and so is not as much of a problem.)
2. the netting that serves as seat is very flimsy, yet too closed and acts a magnet collecting every floating insect; cleaning that is not as simple as it seems, because the fully inflated, wet lounger is something of a handful and the netting does not want to let go.
The position in which one floats, however, is excellent -- I just wish the manufacturer (or another manufacturer) would make a version that is easy to inflate and deflate and does not trap everything that floats.

Step2 Cascading Cove Sand & Water Table with Umbrella | Kids Sand & Water Play Table with Umbrella | 6-pc Accessory Set Included, Blue I looked at different types water tables and sand tables and combos and finally decided on this one. Price was unbeatable (purchased during prime day and got a great deal). I based my finally decision on the following factors:

1) Feedback: based on the feedback this seemed to be the best product out there regarding hour long entertainment, durability, quality, and price
2) Quality: It comes with a cover lid that is fastened via cords on each side allowing it to stay put during storms and it is such a tight fit that it may not let any critters in to access the water or sand
3) It is a combo: meaning it allows for versatility. You can either fill both sides with sand or water, sand and water, or rice (as per feedback when moving it indoors to keep the mess at bay and allow indoor fun during the winter months)
4) It has two drain plugs (one each side) to allow the water and/or sand to drain easily
5) Easy clean up
6) Light enough to move
7) It came with the umbrella for the times the deck has no shade. This is great to allow a little protection from the sun
8) Value and price. If you would get a water table and sandbox separate from each other you would ultimately pay more unless you are lucky and get it used or hand me down or have time to build your own sand box.

Only down side I found so far: My 17 months old son has discovered how fun it is to transfer the sand from his sand side to the water side to make mud (Thank you hubby lol). Either way it can get messy and a bit more cumbersome to clean the water side after his fun. Suggestion: drain the water and let the sun dry out the side and grab the vacuum. Simple and quickest method.

Recommendation I like to pass one from a feedback I read on another sand table product: Add a bit of cinnamon to your play sand to deter critters (in case they find a way in with the cover). It works.
text_fidelity_b: Step2 Cascading Cove Sand & Water Table with Umbrella | Kids Sand & Water Play Table with Umbrella | 6-pc Accessory Set Included, Blue

text_fidelity_a:
My Critter Catcher - Spider and Insect Catcher So I know that spiders are generally good, in that they eat other bugs. But they are also terrifying because they are FAST and HIDE BEHIND THINGS, just waiting to attack! Trying to remove them with a cup and piece of paper is perilous at best (what if it GETS OUT and gets on my hand?? I would flail in terror and then who knows where it would land?). So, to defend myself from these miniature terrors, I bought this.

I knew my time had come when my cats were staring at the floor. It was my nemesis, a spider. I tore the catcher out of the packaging and - with only a little shrieking - successfully subdued the spider! It was caught in the bristles, unable to escape! And I was at a safe distance, unlike the cup method where I'd be practically touching the spider. I darted outside and released it. I told the spider he was evicted and to eat bugs outside, never inside. If it ever does venture inside aagin, I know my cat sentries would alert me to its presence and - with minimal shrieking - I could safely evict it again.
text_fidelity_b: My Critter Catcher - Spider and Insect Catcher

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) The resistance is a fantastic game with a great price and superb components. The rules are very simple also so the game can be picked up by nearly anyone in a matter of minutes. A sample round will remove any doubt about the rules and is often the best way I have found to teach the game.

So what is this about? The Resistance is a game of guessing and deduction that is rules light and fun heavy. In the basic game 5 to 10 players take on the role of either good guys or bad guys by being dealt cards that depict their character. Good guys or the resistance are blue and spies are red. The ratio of spies to resistance is driven by the number of players in a game. The spies always have fewer allies in the game than do the resistance players.

Once the players have secretly looked at their role card, everyone closes their eyes. The first player commands everyone to close their eyes, he then commands the spies and only the spies to open their eyes and look around to identify each other, he then commands them to close their eyes and lastly commands everyone to open their eyes.

So now the spies know who each other are but the allies have no idea.

The game is then played as 5 simple 'missions'. A mission consists of the first player choosing a number
of players to 'go on the mission'. The number is dependent on how many total players are playing. The more players, the more involved in each mission. Each mission from 1 to 5 will have gradually more players involved.

Everyone votes to allow or disallow the chosen players to go on the mission. Each player will have two cards to vote
with each round. These cards are marked clearly with symbols to indicate if you do or do not agree to allow the chosen players to play.

Here is where the game gets going. If the vote fails to allow the chosen players to go on the mission twice in a row, the spies win automatically.

If the players allow the mission to go forward, those players involved get to either make the mission successful or to sabotage the mission. This is done my dealing each player involved in the mission two cards. One of each success and sabotage. They secretly place their cards into two piles. The mission result and the dead pile.

Spies can sabotage or succeed a mission and the resistance players MUST succeed the mission.

The majority of succeed of sabotage rules the mission.

Rounds continue like this until the spies or the resistance have a best 3 out of 5 missions won by their side.

Up until this point your first game might seem kinda boring. But just wait, almost immediately you will figure
out who your junior sleuths are! Finger pointing and accusations will begin to fly out of the most timid players
mouths!

You will find players who are just 100% certain they know who is who and are almost always wrong! You will find out that some of your friends are REALLY GREAT LIARS and some are REALLY POOR LIARS!

The compound the fun there is also a plot deck. The plot deck is simply a deck of cards that each round, one is dealt by the first player and he can give it to someone else or keep it.
These cards are things like 'look at someone else role card' or 'veto a vote'.

I initially thought the plot deck would be horrible but I was very wrong. The first time we pulled a card that let one player look at another players role card the player looked and claimed the other player was a spy. The player accused immediately did a double take and denied the allegation fervently!

We were back at square one but now had two more people we couldn't trust! FUN! FUN! FUN!

You cannot go wrong with this game unless you live in a convent full of people with ZERO personality who have had all their fun genes removed.

So if you are looking for an excellent game, with super components, short playing time, and an immeasurable amount of fun, look no further than this gem!
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

69 Holes Bubble Bazooka Gun with Colorful Lights, Super Rocket Bubble Machine Bubble Gun for Kids Adults Gift, Rocket Boom Bubble Blower Bubble Maker Toys for Indoor Outdoor Birthday Party Wedding The ONE problem with this great Bubble Toy is running out of the proper mix. I thought my nieces boy would totally get a kick out of this and had to surprise him with it.

Who know it would be his grandfather who would be wasting all those wonderful bubbles when Luca wasn't around????

The cool thing is using this at dusk because it has some crazy light effects. It is really rapid fire. My brother was playing with a mix that made the bubbles more stiffer or rubbery so they would last longer.

I don't expect this to last very long as the kids were rough playing with it. My niece thought maybe to just start adding some colorful duct taping to it to make the plastic parts more resilient. Especially the part that snaps together.

I'm not saying it isn't made really good. The kids have been play fighting with it and it has been dropped or tossed several times. On the lawn it is safe from breaking. If they take it to the driveway were worried.
They are only allowed to play with it on the lawn. When they first used it in the patio, they made a mess!

it was a fun mess and i totally loved it because, hey.. That is what a great kids toy is for!

This toy was much better received than when I got the nieces and nephew a case of Silly String! It actually can stain a light colored surface. LOL... but it was FUN! Of course it was the Adults who made the worst mess!

Consider getting TWO so that the kids can have more fun. Heck... get four! The mess can be rinsed off easy with a garden hose. Oh, Google Bubble Soap Mix. You will be surprised how much fun this can be when you have an endless supply of Bubble mix!

Oh, when you order this, order Bubble mix too. That way the first time out won't be a dud because you ran out immediately!

Fortunately, Amazon protects this purchase - thanks, Amazon. Returned.

text_fidelity_a: Aquabeads Disney Princess Character Set This kit was really fun for my 4 year old! I definitely think we'll get the pen to help her with getting the beads in the holes but you can drop them in with your fingers if you're careful. I wish the colors had been labeled more clearly. We did Tiana after Ariel and my daughter used the dark brown beads for her skin. She looked great and things were fine until we went to do Jasmine and realized that Jasmines skin is supposed to be orange not light brown. We ended up having to use a mix of colors for Belle's hair since the dark brown is supposed to be for that. But we had fun anyway and plan to get more to make the princesses again. The description says you can peel these after 10 minutes and you definitely can't! The directions say to wait an hour. We did 30 minutes on Ariel and her tail came off at the bottom but waited an hour for all the others and had zero issues. My daughter loves playing with them now that they are dry and hard. This is a great gift and a wonderful quiet time project for kids. It's also really small so it can travel easily or store easily if needed!
text_fidelity_b: Aquabeads Disney Princess Character Set

text_fidelity_a: Potensic A20 Mini Drone for Kids and Beginners RC Nano Quadcopter 2.4G 6 Axis, Altitude Hold, Headless Mode Safe and Stable Flight, 3 Batteries, Great Gift Toy for Boys and Girls -Red I am no drone expert by a long shot but I do have a Mavic Air. I bought the A20 Mini to play around with. The best part about it is how durable it is. I let some kids play with it and it crashed multiple times and seems to have had no negative effect. The irregular shape of the pieces, the non-standard design, the pieces that do not snap together, and the heavier pieces were stress-inducing. The pleasure of solving a puzzle was replaced with a difficult challenge that was too much work to enjoy.

If the person solving this puzzle is more up for a challenge, then this might be ok. If the person is older, does not like things that are different, has anxiety, and does not like challenges, then this would not be a good gift.

The difficulty level is high even though the number of pieces is low. This puzzle is not suitable for kids.

The price is much higher than a typical puzzle. The higher price point is understandable based on the quality, but it does not translate to a more enjoyable activity when solving this. Being 5x the price of a regular puzzle does not translate to 5x the level of enjoyment. At the higher price, this would be something to buy as a gift for someone, just be careful of who you give it to.
text_fidelity_b: LEOGOR XL Whimsical Wooden Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults with Shaped Animal Pieces (Lion Puzzle - 339 pcs - 19.7" x 12.4" in) - Laser Cut and Challenging for a Unique Puzzle Experience

As with many puzzles, the printed photo is at a lower resolution or a lower color depth than the actual photo, so the details are washed out in some of the darker areas. text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

You can also get magnetic wooden blocks (Tegu) but those are really expensive so I haven't bought any.

The magformers are one of those toys that both kids and adults can sit and play with for an hour or longer. What I've noticed with three young grandkids together is that they each have their favorite pieces and styles of construction. One always creates vehicles, one creates houses, and the third makes towers. The colors and feel of the pieces are both soothing and exciting to work with.

Update: I had five kids and two adults playing with these recently and the person that seemed the most focused on building things is an MIT Neuroscientist. Once he built things following the guide, the kids quickly caught on and followed suit. I recommend that an adult work with the kids to begin with.

Regarding complaints about the magnets not working, if you snap together two piles of similarly shaped objects and then try to put the two piles together, sometimes the piles will reject each other. If you take one pile and start adding it to the other one at a time, all the pieces hold to each other. It seems as though the magnets must change polarity inside the plastic. I'd love a proper explanation.

I only recommend getting sets of 40 or more to have enough pieces to be creative. Wait for them to go on sale unless money is no object. Since all the grandkids took their sets home with them, I've bought a fourth set to keep at my house.

Addendum per request: I first chose these toys because of the brightly colored plastic material but soon discovered that having the pieces snap together and hold their shape is quite satisfying. While they don't take away from the joy of plain wooden blocks, they are different and allow you to vary how you play with them.

This particular kit is right for me because I'll have a crowd of five young children and many adults (thankfully two engineers) for two weeks over Christmas and I'll put this out on a large sofa table in the living room near the tree. That way the kids will feel like they have toys and waiting won't be so hard. It also incorporates many of the other kits you can buy separately so the kids can see specific types of builds.

Go to youtube and type in magformers to see how they are used. Construction is really that easy.
text_fidelity_b: Magformers Magnets in Motion Set - Engineering Magnet Toys for Brain Development - 300 Pc Set

I got both the Matchbox Aqua Cannon Swamp Blaster and this Fire Truck Rig for 5 and 6 year old grandkids. Until I showed them how to use the toys, they didn't show much interest in them. I think these toys are best suited for ages five and under.

1 year followup: This toy spent the winter outside by the pool and it still works like new. I have to keep it out of the hands of adults who delight in shooting water far outside the pool area (violating house rules).

text_fidelity_a:
Magic The Gathering 300 Assorted MTG Basic Lands Cards Firstly, this claims a "good mix" of the basic lands. Mine had the following distribution:
Plains - 4.33%
Island - **73.66%**
Swamp - 20.0%
Mountain - 0.66% !!!
Forest - 1.33% !!

So of 300 lands, 2 mountains and 4 forests make this somehow a "good mix?" This is almost unusable for any purpose - it's just a lottery of what one type of basic land you're going to be stuck with over 200 of.

Secondly, it claims "almost all cards are in NM/M condition". Mine included cards with writing on them (one of my islands was a Sengir Vampire - cute...), severe punctures, edge wear, grime, etc. By my count only about 80% of them would approach the Near Mint mark, and almost none were mint. Almost 25% of them would be unplayable without sleeves because the wear makes them clearly marked.

Stay away.
text_fidelity_b: Magic The Gathering 300 Assorted MTG Basic Lands Cards

text_fidelity_a:
WB Games Lego Marvel's Avengers - Playstation Vita Compared to other Vita Lego games, it is disappointing. Those who played other games on consoles are probably happy, since it sounds closer to a console in terms of content, but, honestly, it is disappointing, and a bit broken.

First of all, I hate the city hub. It is too big. While it does come into play a bit during the main gameplay, having to navigate it during cleanup is a pain. Trying to find all the collectibles that are scattered throughout the city is annoying, even with a guide. Half of them are in such obscure places that you would never think to look for them there, let alone be able to see them from the distance (if they even render if you just pass by). The missions in the city are just painful; while the smash challenges are easy enough but rely more on luck than anything, the ground and jumping time trials are manageable, but the flying ones are utterly impossible. Precision flying controls with constant change in altitude are ridiculously broken, particularly when you can't see where you are supposed to go. I easily plat any other Vita Lego games, as they are easy and relaxing. And in this game, I have everything else done, but these flying challenges, I just give up on them.

Speaking of the trophies, several of them are glitched; even if you complete everything they still do not show up. And the game is glitched too; I had to restart the game at least twice because it froze and I could not move at all.

The main mission was on the shorter side. Apparently, the console had extra missions about Cap 2 and Thor movies. Rather than having Manhattan hub, I honestly would have preferred a few extra levels. Also, they did have many cutscenes from the movies, but they cut out the punchlines of most of those scenes, which was also pretty disappointing,
text_fidelity_b: WB Games Lego Marvel's Avengers - Playstation Vita

text_fidelity_a: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up This version of Monopoly does not use money! Genius idea for very little children! Even my 4-year-old loved playing. It can be very quick (which was perfect!). I was out before I ever passed Go, haha. Instead of money, this game uses green circles called HP. You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. My kids have already played this 5 times in 2 days. Great buy! I rate this board game A+.

text_fidelity_a:
ELEGOO Building Block Car Kit, Intelligent and Educational Building Block Toy Car Robot Kit 3 in 1 for Fun and STEM Learning Toy This review was written by my 11 year old son, Nathaniel.

----------

I’m an avid LEGO builder, and I’ve participated in the FIRST LEGO League as well as LEGO robotics competitions. I’ve built kits at home as large as 1000 pieces. But although some of these had moving parts, like wheels, doors, gears and suspension, I’ve never built a fully robotic kit that I owned myself. Besides, LEGO robotics is way too expensive for a kid like me… So, for a long time serious robot-making felt like an impossible goal. But then imagine my surprise when I got my first Elegoo kit!

The Elegoo kit: The Elegoo Building Block Car Kit is an attractive package and comes in a neat and reclosable plastic container. I really liked the container design as it wouldn’t rip as easily as the standard LEGO kit cardboard box would. All the parts are bagged by type. There are MANY connectors in the box as well as wheels. This is not an official LEGO kit, so all of the parts are LEGO clones, however, they fit just as well as the official product. The robotics-specific parts are nonstandard LEGOs, however they have similar connections to a normal LEGO and have magnets that snap them to one another. The kit has a large flat paper instruction sheet that folds out to cover an entire table. It's large enough to literally build the entire project on. However, it only contains startup instructions for the project. You’ll need to visit an android or ios app store to download the “Colego app” in order to find building instructions and the programming tools for the car.

The Colego app (co-LEGO?): This is where things go downhill. The user interface is so-so, so I will split it into 3 parts: The manual, the coding, and the coding lessons.

In the manual the part colors aren’t always accurate so there is some confusion during assembly. For instance, a gray part shown in the manual is actually black in real life. You also can’t zoom into small spaces, making examining details difficult. Also, a suggestion, double-tapping on a part should zoom in on it to show you how many studs or technic holes it has. This will definitely help with differentiating parts.

In the coding section of the app some elements take up almost the whole screen so you can’t edit your code. There is just not enough space at all. You also can’t change what the blocks are auto-set to when they first pop up. There is no redo, undo, copy or paste (for example the SCRATCH coding app has all these features). This makes it very hard to make long code strings. Also the blocks don’t fully fit together in the user interface leaving gaps. This doesn’t affect your code, but looks very sloppy. Basically, the coding interface and layout is the absolute worst I’ve seen for any robotics kit. It needs to be fixed. Other issues I have with the app are that there is only one “when start button pressed” block and the bluetooth power saving settings are pretty aggressive and turn off the connections very quickly. As far as the robotics hardware goes, most of it is pretty well built, but I think the ultrasonic sensor is not the best. They are rather closely set together and seem to get confused by many typical household objects (like my mother’s sneakers).

Lastly there are the coding lessons. They aren’t bad, but they go by type (movement, sound, etc). You can’t see the next type of lesson or skip/scroll through lessons you’ve already done. This is a good kit for kids who have done complex LEGO kit building and know how to plug things in using cables and ports, but are new to programming. Especially if they will only make very simple programs as the user interface of the app falls apart with larger blocks of code. Arduino use or knowledge would also help but if you’re already using Arduino this kit will be too simple for you.

Good overall and I had fun with it, but not a real LEGO Robotics replacement. If it worked with Buzzwizz or BrickController 2 it would be a LOT more useful. But it is not recognized by those apps. The most fun I'm having with it is using it like a little remote control car with the app's control function on the home page under kit.
text_fidelity_b: ELEGOO Building Block Car Kit, Intelligent and Educational Building Block Toy Car Robot Kit 3 in 1 for Fun and STEM Learning Toy

text_fidelity_a:
WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White This is a four star product in many ways. But I'm giving it three due to the following factors...

Excellent build quality and hardware features. However, without some additional software and accessories this you won't see lasting use.

Hardware: you WILL need a phone or tablet to unlock the limited potential of this toy. The included gesture and sound functionality is too rudimentary (and yet also hard to acess consistently) for lasting interest. If you don't plan to provide access to a tablet or phone, get WowWee's robotic dog product instead. Although it is easy to set up an obstacle course or seesaw on your own, purpose-built accessories would go a long way towards providing a "fiction" for the toy to inhabit, as well as proven fun activities.

Software: the existing apps are very well made and provide a significant boost to the toys functionality. I'd say about 75%. However, most are of limited scope and soon become repetitive. The best feature is the ability to remotely drive the robot and also record its adventures. I'd like to see a feature that allows kids to rudimentarily program the robot (perhaps to interact with purpose built accessories) not just activate sounds and colored lights... I'd also like to see the toolset opened to adults (Lua scripting?) so that they can extend the functionality for Pre-K through K STEM learning.

I understand trying to hit price points is important. But this is either a $75 toy with a few $25 accessory kits, or a $125 toy all in. The existing package (while decent) is limiting the potential of the product.
text_fidelity_b: WowWee - MiP the Toy Robot - White

Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - The Roundabout - Quality Time Playing Together Wooden Safe Play - Smart Play for Smart Families I was so glad I found this brand of marble maze. We have bought a few plastic versions but they have all been flimsy and not very engaging.

This marble maze series made by Hape is tremendous. We have had so much fun building with this. Not only does each set come with a book and great step by step directions with photos for making multiple mazes the color coded-functionality of the transporting blocks help kids work out marble flow and direction when building on their own. Some blocks allow marbles to flow one or two directions or alternating directions as well as some being travel though pieces while others are drop into pieces.

Although the wood pieces fit together they do not lock so it can be knocked over which may be an issue for younger children who get really excited like my four year old grandson but my seven year old son builds and maintains his mazes with no problems.

It also comes with a bag full or marbles so never having a marble should never be an issue. We use a funnel and just load the maze up and it can have a marble flow continuously for as long as someone collects and loads. It's a bundle of excitement and engages the kids for HOURS!
text_fidelity_b: Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - The Roundabout - Quality Time Playing Together Wooden Safe Play - Smart Play for Smart Families

text_fidelity_a: Award Winning Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - The Xcellerator This was a Christmas gift for my 7 year old son who absolutely loves it. This Quadrilla marble maze made by Hape is fantastic. Sturdy wooden pieces with various openings, functions, and tracks have provided hours of marble fun. Fairly sturdy although it can be knocked over but doesn't fall apart just because of a bump. It came with a book with various maze set ups with easy step by step instructions that my son was able to do with just a little help. Great way to get the mind thinking in engineering cause and effect ways. Love this and will be purchasing the additional tracks and add-ons. We bought the Xcellerator and Round About to start. My four year old grandson loved it also. He stood in front of it for hours and kept feeding it marbles as fast as we could get them back to him. We had to take turns being the marble gatherer. Will definitely be investing in the marble return tray as well.
text_fidelity_b: Award Winning Hape Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - The Xcellerator

I read all of the different reviews for all of the different products like this. I watched all of the youtube reviews of every product like this, including the Nerf one. This is the only one that had a quiet motor. All the rest had a motor that is super loud which can get annoying and distracting fast. Then I looked at how high the air blew the balls. This product was the only one that had air that blew the balls pretty high from the product. It also looked like an easy assembly. I bought this for a gift for my 9 year old nephew who likes shooting Nerf guns. I wanted to test it out first before wrapping it up. It was easy to assemble. All you have to do is place the orange ball holders into the product. Thats it. Then you place the balls on top and turn it on. The air lifts them at the height that you are wanting. Not close to the product where you would think "This kind of sucks". The motor really was nice and quiet. You can barely hear it. If youre looking to buy one of these air lifting ball target toys, this is the one you want. There is another product by the same company that is black in color, but the reviews for that one didnt look so good. So buy this one, the grey and orange one. Our test run went great. Everything worked as I was hoping. The balls stay floating. They dont lift and fall over time. They stay floating in the air. It comes with a gun but that gun is a single load gun, so you have to stop and reload it every time. So I would either purchase a separate Nerf gun if the person youre giving it to doesnt have one or if you already have one, use that instead. This is the one you want. I hope this helps!

text_fidelity_a: Nature Gift Store Kids Worm Farm Observation Kit Shipped with Live Worms I ordered this as a Christmas gift for my young daughter who is into all things worms, gardening, and composting. It estimated it would arrive December 5th, but it arrived a lot earlier. I think earlier shipping is always fine with the exception of live creatures. Being more than a month away, I was worried the worms wouldn't make it for the holidays. I contacted the seller right away to get tips on how to keep the worms alive and they were not helpful at all. I think I got a one or two sentence reply with no information. So I decided to do some research myself and I was able to keep them all alive without having to transfer them until the farm was opened on Christmas day. I kept them in the dark and a cool area of my house. I would take the cup out once a week to check on them. I'd water the soil a little every other week (just moist, not wet). I also set a couple carrot shavings, a torn up spinach leaf, and a broken egg shell on the top.  The worms did really well.  We transferred them as soon as she opened the farm.  The farm itself was disappointing in size and much smaller than I was expecting. It's more like the size of holding your two hands side by side. We plan to transfer them from the farm to her vermicompost bin in a few weeks.  She seems happy with the purchase, but overall I would not recommend this farm and would suggest creating your own with a little more research.
text_fidelity_b: Nature Gift Store Kids Worm Farm Observation Kit Shipped with Live Worms

The RC has no data connection so you cannot see live maps unless you're fortunate enough to have mobile hotspot on your cellphone so you can link the RC to it. The fly more plus has the extended batteries but that's the end of the usefulness of spending $249. text_fidelity_a: Holy Stone HS340 Mini FPV Drones with Camera for Kids 8-12 RC Quadcopter for Adults Beginners with One Key Take Off/Landing, Gravity Sensor, Headless Mode, Waypoint Fly, Throw to Go, Indoor & Outdoor I purchased this mini drone because I purchased a HD175D and wanted to learn how to use a drone before trying a more expensive one. So I read the instructions and got the HS340 working  (hoovering) without too much hassle. I tried using the cell phone and camera portion but that would not work so I just settled with the remote control by itself. This worked fine so I began trying to learn to steer I kept it very basic, no tricks or anything that a kid might want to try indoors. After about 5 minutes of getting used to this tiny drone it hit the wall (4 feet up in the air) and slid down to the floor. I turned it off and redid the start up procedure to get more practice controlling the drone. OH NO!!! all it does now is goes side ways and immediately lunges towards the floor. I can not believe how simple it is to destroy this plastic drone. I am a very cautious adult, thus buying this HS340 so that I would have experience under my belt before using a $150 dollar HS175D ( much better than the HS175) drone. I wanted to buy my HD175D from amazon but the D version was on e-xxx  dot com website for less money (after making an offer) and better camera plus better bearings. Now I see that the return window is closed so I will simply throw this $35 (sale price) dollar paper weight in the trash. I guess I can not in good conscience recommend this drone unless you are prepared to use it only in a space that can not hit a wall at 4 foot height. So not very likely. I am quite disappointed with Holy Stone products overall.
text_fidelity_b: Holy Stone HS340 Mini FPV Drones with Camera for Kids 8-12 RC Quadcopter for Adults Beginners with One Key Take Off/Landing, Gravity Sensor, Headless Mode, Waypoint Fly, Throw to Go, Indoor & Outdoor

Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud This is a completely different kind of game and the idea of stars and lanterns is abstract. It says it is easy to learn, but to be honest, don't bring your friends together to learn the game. You should set it up, read through the directions and pretend to have two friends with you to understand what is going on. THEN you can explain the game to your friends. The reason is because you can tell this game was not designed in America, there are a few minor English mistakes. The directions have interesting choice of words. So I'm going to try my best by using parentheses to show the words they used in the directions.

The goal of the game is when a word card is revealed, you try to figure out which dixit (picture) cards match that word--by the picture itself, the color(s), inspiration, characters, etc. Then you mark an X (cross) for each dixit card you feel matches that word. At the same time, you want to choose cards you think your friends will choose. If your friends chose that card too, both of you earn stars (sparks) and so on. If they didn't, then you lose (fall) and stop there. If you marked X for too many dixit cards (hoping to get a lot of points), more likely your friends won't have that same card marked and that will make you lose. You have to work like a team, trying to figure out what your friends will choose and win. (This is what they mean by the word, greedy.) This is a good way to teach kids how to perceive the pictures and THINK of others and what they could be thinking, again a "teamwork." This is where it is supposed to be fun. My daughter liked it, but my son didn't like it.

I have one suggestion for you as parents or caregiver of a child age 8 or over. (Ages for the game is for 8+.) I suggest you form the first few turns, you handpick the words you feel your child will be able to "match" then go from there. You handpicking and seeing a few cards in advance honestly does not change the game. The game actually entirely relies on the other players' dixit card choices.

There is one rule that seems pointless. Of course you need to read the directions first to understand what I"m talking about. Here I go anyway--suppose you "fall" then at the end of the game when everyone is ready to score. If you have some sparks and a super-spark from one of your dixit cards that you marked off (crosses), you wipe away one star (but not the super-spark star) then count the remaining stars (sparks). The super-spark star has the same point value as the other sparks so I'm not sure why it makes a difference to wipe off a star or a super-spark star.

This game is Made in China and being sold by a Chinese company on Amazon. It's also created in China and I don't know that it's going to be that great, at least for some U.S. audiences.
text_fidelity_b: Dixit Board Game 2021 Refresh | Storytelling Game for Kids and Adults | Fun Family Party Game | Creative Kids Game | Ages 8+ | 3-8 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Libellud

If you are the type of person who likes participating in an escape room, or think you might like to participate in an escape room, then this might be for you. But this is not a game of chance. There is no luck. You do not roll the dice, or pick a card. You must complete each task before continuing. You either get the task right, or wrong. If you get it wrong, then there are hints to help, if you choose to use them.

It takes about 2 hours to complete. It could take you more time if you don’t use the hints, and perhaps less time if you do use the hints. It’s played with between one and 6 players. Honestly, I think 6 players would be too many. If you had 6, I think four would be playing the game and two would be making sure the drinks and snacks keep flowing. ;-)

Once you complete this game, you will not play it again, because you already know how to complete all of the tasks. But you certainly could give it to friends who have not played it. Or, perhaps you could invite other friends over who had not played it before and you could assist them with it.

Once you remove the lid, you will find the different pieces. But do NOT open the box that is inside until you are given instructions to do so. There are tasks which must be completed before you open the box that is inside.

If you want to have an idea of how to get started, then I highly recommend that you do an online search for “Unfiltered Gamer Break In Alcatraz”. These are a couple of guys who will walk you through about the first 20 minutes. If you don’t want to go that far then you can simply watch until they have completed the 1st task so you know exactly what you need to do. Yes, this can be a little complicated, but if you at least watch them complete the 1st task, you’ll know how to get started.

text_fidelity_a: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad The power wheels kawasaki lil' quad is a great toy for a toddler. You will want to make sure that your little one has enough flat space to drive around because the turning radius is extremely wide. You will need a very large space to make a complete circle. Also, there is no reverse button. You should not ride this near hills, slopes, pools, roads, cars, or anywhere else that could increase the chances of an accident. You should also note that even if the "go" button is not being pressed the quad can reach high speeds if on a steep incline.  It comes with a rechargeable 6v 4Ah battery and charging cord that is to be plugged into a wall outlet (not a ceiling outlet!). Before using for the first time the battery must be charged for 18 hours, and 14 hours after each use. You are warned not to leave the battery charging for longer than 30 hours or it may cause the battery to degrade. The biggest downside is that there is no light to denote the battery is charging or completely charged. You just have to assume it is charging and that the battery is completely charged after you unplug it. It requires about 10 minutes of assembly time (excluding the sticker time). The quad does not come with the stickers already placed, so you will need to place the stickers on yourself. You will need a philips head and a flat head screw driver, all other parts are included. The only problem that I noted was one of the connections would not completely engage. There is a wire that is used to connect the battery one end and then the electrical supply from the "go" but on the handlebar. For some reason I could not get the handlebar connection to completely snap into place. Even though it did not completely connect it was enough for everything to work, so I left it as is. I was afraid to force it to completely connect and potentially breaking the plastic connector. It is listed to be for 12-36 months, and up to 40 pounds. Personally, I think 12 months is a little young to be riding this, especially if your child is on the small side and not completely steady on their feet when walking. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Power Wheels Kawasaki Lil' Quad

It has a spinning flower, an abacus, spinning eyes, different size blocks (circles, squares, triangle), and a white fluffy tail. The colors are beautiful, simple, and eye catching.  I could see this as a family keep-sake. Solid construction, fantastic design, and a great learning toy.  It’s Made in China.
