This is a single horse, which is more for display than anything else. It’s nice enough if you have a collection and want to add this one to it. I’m not sure that that apples and beets really add anything to it. Overall it’s ok, but really nothing special. Kind of expensive for Made in China plastic.

[[ASIN:B00TV9J9KI Schleich Horse Feeding Play Set]]
text_fidelity_b: Schleich North America Horse Club Arabian Mare Playset

text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Nickelodeon Blaze & The Monster Machines, Flip & Race Speedway This is a very short / small race car set.  Unless the child is older, an adult will need to put the track together.  It’s simple enough though, and can be put together in just a few minutes.  Though it’s colorful, and there is the aspect of flipping the car. . . . as you can see from the video. . . it only takes a second or two for the car to go around, and then you’re done.  There is simply not enough “excitement” to keep a child engaged for very long.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Nickelodeon Blaze & The Monster Machines, Flip & Race Speedway

text_fidelity_a: Toy State Caterpillar CAT Junior Operator Dump Truck Construction Vehicle This listing is for the Junior Operator Dump Truck, though currently other models are also shown.  I really like this dump truck for several reasons.  One of the main ones is that you actually have to put it together.  That’s a great idea.  It’s easy enough to put together, but it’s a great learning toy, in that respect.  It’s well-made, and is suitable for kids 36-months and older.  FYI, this also comes in a different model which has a hand drill, instead of a screwdriver, but I really prefer this one.  You can also add the excavator and bulldozer, which is sold separately.  It comes disassembled, in a “bucket” just as it shows in the pictures.  The bucket measures approximately 8.5” X 7” X 5”.
text_fidelity_b: Toy State Caterpillar CAT Junior Operator Dump Truck Construction Vehicle

text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Disney Minnie, Sparkle 'n Spin Fashion Bow-tique This is a cute, albeit expensive, dress-up set.  Note that three AAA batteries are required and included, but you’ll always need to have extra on-hand.  When closed, it’s fairly compact.  There are not a lot of pieces to it, but you can always add other items / playmates from other toys you already have. . . or. . . . you can purchase additional from Fisher-Price as they offer several other sets.  There are a few lights and sounds.  The one “issue” I have, and this might sound kind of silly, but is the name.  I don’t like it when companies try to be cute and change the name form “Boutique” to “Bowtique”.  Kids have enough problems trying to remember how to spell words correctly as it is.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Disney Minnie, Sparkle 'n Spin Fashion Bow-tique

text_fidelity_a:
LeapFrog Fridge Numbers Magnetic Set This is a fun game / set to learn numbers. There are ten number tiles, and ten food item tiles matching the numbers. Note that this is the number version, but there is also an alphabet version. Note that three AAA batteries are required. Though they are included, you’ll need more rather soon, as they are “demo” batteries only. The tiles are large. Though the set is called “Fridge Numbers” you can attach it to any metal surface. It not only helps with numbers, but also colors and food groups. Overall a really great item.

[[ASIN:B00JLHVX36 LeapFrog Fridge Phonics Magnetic Letter Set]]
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog Fridge Numbers Magnetic Set

text_fidelity_a:
LeapFrog Count and Crawl Number Kitty This toy has a lot going for it. It’s certainly cute. But it is a fun and easy way to learn numbers from one to twenty. There is music. . . and of course it talks. This is kind of like a “companion” to the LeapFrog “AlphaPup” toy for letters. Both are really great to have. They make great gifts. My one suggestion to LeapFrog is on the packaging. They should have put it in a fully-enclosed box with a window. Because of the way it’s packaged, you hear it if you shake the shipping box. Not a big deal, but kind of annoying. Hahahaha Don’t forget the batteries! Three AAA batteries are required, and included, but you will certainly need more.

[[ASIN:B00GTCKOCM LeapFrog AlphaPup Toy, Green]]
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog Count and Crawl Number Kitty

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher Price Think & Learn Code-a-Pillar Toy, 3 - 6 years What an incredible toy. It’s so much more than just your “generic” moving toy. You don’t have to use all of the connections. .. but you certainly can. You can also purchase additional connections separately, like ones which will cause the “code-a-pillar” to turn all the way around 360 degrees.

I think that this is the type of toy best played with along with an adult, at least at first, to explain to the child exactly what’s going to happen when each connection is added. Great sort of parent/child item.

This works best on a flat floor. . . and with plenty of space. So like an open basement, garage, and such.

I will admit that it’s not inexpensive, but for this sort of toy, and type of learning / thinking it causes. . . I really like it.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher Price Think & Learn Code-a-Pillar Toy, 3 - 6 years

text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Soft Sport Hoops Set - Batman This is the Batman set, though Franklin Sports also offers a Superman set and perhaps others.  Overall it looks nice.  Certainly not something that’s “high quality”, but for what it is, it works.  Note that the “ball” is soft and squishy.  It’s not like a “real” basketball which would bounce.  The ball itself is kind of nice to just toss around.  Note that it’s not a foam ball, meaning that it has enough “oomph” to it to knock over a lamp, were you to hit it.  As fifteen bucks, this sent is not cheap for Made in China, but nonetheless, I still like it.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Soft Sport Hoops Set - Batman

text_fidelity_a: Janod Story Box Circus - 19 Piece Set - Ages 3+ - J08520 This is a fun all-wood set.  The pieces all fit nicely into the box, and you can also use the box as part of your “set” to play with.  The box itself is cardboard.  Each piece is nicely painted.  Very colorful.  It’s great to take on trips as well as playing at home.  There are nineteen pieces total.  It’s also priced about right too.  Overall I’m in love with this set.  Note that the same company, Janod, also make other such themed sets.
text_fidelity_b: Janod Story Box Circus - 19 Piece Set - Ages 3+ - J08520

text_fidelity_a:
Maui Toys 09316 Girl Combo 3Pack Toy First of all, at the current price of nineteen bucks. . . this reaches the level of spectacularly crazy expensive. You have three, very cheap (and I don’t mean inexpensive) toys which are Made in China and only cost pennies each to make. If this set were five bucks, then it would be reasonable.

The “Glitter Skyball” is a small ball, about 1.5 the size of a softball. I’m unsure why it shows “Jumbo”. . . I guess it’s “Jumbo” if you compare it to a ping pong ball.

The jacks, on the other hand, are large than normal jacks.

The jump rope is colorful. That’s nice.
text_fidelity_b: Maui Toys 09316 Girl Combo 3Pack Toy

text_fidelity_a: Lil Lockitz Sweets Set There are a plethora of these sets offered.  All with a different theme.  Some, like this one, are a little “crazy” to me.  Sweets? They are very simple. .  .quick. . . and easy.  You can put all of them together within minutes.  The most challenging part is deciding which items you would like to enclose.  Unfortunately they do not “stick” inside, and simply bounce around.  You can certainly wear them, but also attach them to things like backpacks.
text_fidelity_b: Lil Lockitz Sweets Set

text_fidelity_a: Lil Lockitz Pets Set Alex Toys makes a ton of these sets with different themes for each set.  This is the “Pets” set.  They are super quick. . . super simple. . . . You can zip right through them in no time.  There are wristbands. . . lockets. . . you can attach them to backpacks. .  .and so on.  Let’s be honest. . . They are super “cheap”, and I’m not talking inexpensive.  The trinkets you put inside are very tiny, and just “flop around”.  Not super exciting, but it’s something to do.
text_fidelity_b: Lil Lockitz Pets Set

text_fidelity_a: Faber-Castell Do Art Paint with Marbles - Abstract Art Painting Set for Kids If you have a budding Jackson Pollock in your house, then this might be an item for you.  This is really one of those “odd” items, that I really don’t “get”. . . but. . . I’m certainly not judging what kids might enjoy.  Nonetheless, I think that most kids will use mostly the other parts of the kit.  It might be nice to have some extra brushes on hand.  You can also use the paints as finger paints.  The set is neatly packaged.  I like that there is a tray included, which means less mess.  The kit is Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Faber-Castell Do Art Paint with Marbles - Abstract Art Painting Set for Kids

text_fidelity_a: Alex Little Hands String and Beep Kids Toddler Art and Craft Activity They call these “beads” . . . but they are indeed vehicles. .  .  I find it amazing that the set comes in a wooden frame.  I have no idea why that’s the case.  I would have been happy to pay less, and come in cardboard.  Nonetheless, it’ a cute set.  You can certainly string them together, but you can also simply play with them separately.  They are quite colorful.  At the current price, it’s also affordable.  The same company makes a variety of these sets with different teamed “beads” in each set.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Little Hands String and Beep Kids Toddler Art and Craft Activity

text_fidelity_a: Creativity for Kids Fashion Headbands Craft Kit, Makes 10 Unique Hair Accessories This is a different type of craft set that I haven’t seen before.  You can make four “Flower Crowns” with the set.  Everything you need is included.  Included is:  Paper Flowers, Fabric Leaf Garland, Bud Branches, Berry Bunches, Gold Glitter Accent Paint.  All of the pieces look quite nice.  You might also use them to adorn a hat.  Overall, better than expected.  I also think that the current price is very reasonable for such an item.  Great for after school activity. . .  Grandparents house. . .  Camping trip or travel.  .. . etc.
text_fidelity_b: Creativity for Kids Fashion Headbands Craft Kit, Makes 10 Unique Hair Accessories

text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Moonlight Meadow Activity Set, 5 Pack [Amazon Exclusive] This is a very colorful five-piece set.  Granted, once you open it, the “pieces” will just become part of all your other toys!  Hahaha  It makes for a nice gift for a new mom (or grandparent).  There is nothing super exciting about any of the items, though the hedgehog is rather cute.  For same price, you could probably put a few (more interesting) toys together. . . but the current price isn’t too bad for a set of five as well.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Moonlight Meadow Activity Set, 5 Pack [Amazon Exclusive]

text_fidelity_a: Lil Lockitz Rockstar Set These are bracelets which look similar to a watch, but don’t have a watch inside.  You simply put small trinkets inside. . . close it up.  . . and the trinkets move around when you move your hand.  This is the “Rock star” set, though you will see that Lil Lockitz makes a variety of different sets.  It’s very simple and easy to put together.  There are three bracelets included.  It’s very quick and colorful.  Not really worth the current price of ten bucks for Made in China, but not really crazy expensive either.
text_fidelity_b: Lil Lockitz Rockstar Set

text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Baby's Bandstand Play Gym The colors are nice and bright.  That it makes sounds is a plus.  It’s also nice that the arch can be removed, and play can continue as baby grows.  The matt itself is washable.  Two AA batteries are required. . . So you’ll want to stock-up on those, if you don’t already have a bunch.  This is a simple / fun / cute item.  . .. . but. . . I think it’s quite expensive at the current rate of over forty bucks, especially for Made in China.  Granted, you’re also paying for the Fisher-Price name.  But if Grandma wants to buy it. . .  Go For It!  ;-)
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Baby's Bandstand Play Gym

text_fidelity_a: Play-Doh Create N' Store Big Bucket It’s very important to note that this “bucket” does NOT include Play-Doh.  It’s just the bucket, along with some cutters, molds, etc.  The actual Play-Doh has to be purchased separately.  It hold 12 5oz tubs of Play-Dough.  Once you have the actual Play-Doh, it’s a nice set to play with.  The molds and cutters are all small in size.  Only a couple of inches (at most) across.  This set is just molded plastic, Made in China, so it’s a little expensive, but not too bad. It’s nice to have a place to store Play-Doh all in one place.
text_fidelity_b: Play-Doh Create N' Store Big Bucket

text_fidelity_a: Mega Bloks Call of Duty Wraith Attack Vehicle If you’re the recommended age, as shown on Amazon, of 12 – 15. . . sounds about fight. . . or just someone who enjoys putting together models. . . then this one is an interesting one.  Note the on the box it shows for 10 and up, but unless they are really into such models, I think older is probably better.  There are 351 pieces to this model, so it’s certainly going to take some time to put together.  Great for a rainy day, perhaps.  Mega Bloks makes several Call of Duty sets.  This is NOT Lego, meaning that there are lots of pieces and it takes time to put together.  Certainly not recommended for younger children.  Mega Bloks makes great “First Builder” sets for small kids as well.
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Call of Duty Wraith Attack Vehicle

text_fidelity_a: Kulipari enemy -“BATTALTIONS” Scorpion Ranger figure with gloved fist and deadly spear! If you’re a collector of this series, then of course you’ll want to have this one too.  The arms move some, and the spear is removable.  Though these are really the quality of a toy you would find in the bag of a fast food restaurant for your kids meal. . .  .since Amazon has dropped the price a lot, they are now affordable.  They come in a specific character box, and I like that part.
text_fidelity_b: Kulipari enemy -“BATTALTIONS” Scorpion Ranger figure with gloved fist and deadly spear!

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco DKN81 Halo Covenant Needler Blaster Toy This is a cool, albeit expensive toy. The “odd” shape certainly catches your attention. The lights give it an added cool feature. It comes with sixteen darts. More can be purchased separately.

Overall I really like it. . but again. . I think it’s a bit expensive. This came company makes other models which are a lot less expensive. Also, two AA batteries are not included.

If you would like to add additional darts, see the link to the listing below.

[[ASIN:B00TUVMNDC BOOMco. HALO Covenant Darts & Targets Pack]]
text_fidelity_b: BOOMco DKN81 Halo Covenant Needler Blaster Toy

text_fidelity_a:
Barbie Doll & Horse “Riding Barbie”, as I will call her, comes in a few different designs. This one gives her a more “realistic” riding look as compared to some of the others that I’ve seen.

Overall it’s a nice enough set. The only real “issue” I have is the fact that she can’t actually ride the horse! That’s just crazy to me that a doll and horse set was created, but you can’t actually put Barbie on the horse to go riding! For that reason, I can’t give it more than four-stars.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Doll & Horse

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Laugh & Learn Sis' Smart Stages Push Car This toy reminds me of the old “popper” toy kids would push around and balls would pop inside of it. But there was no “learning” with the “popper” toy. . . . . and there is with this one. . . .at least a little bit.

This little car is cute. . . colorful. . . and “talks” to keep the kids interested. There are two “styles” . . . one more for girls and one more for boys. It would have been nice to have just one and let it be “gender neutral”. Nonetheless, it’s still a nice toy overall.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Laugh & Learn Sis' Smart Stages Push Car

text_fidelity_a: Kulipari Hero -“BATTALIONS” Strawberry Frog Ranger figure with deadly slingshot! This small figure is Made in China and not great quality.  Having said that, if you’re a fan of Kulipari, and you’re collecting all of the figures then it’s certainly one you’ll want to add to your collection.  At the current price it’s still expensive.  Honestly, this almost looks like something kids would get in their lunch from a fast-food restaurant.
text_fidelity_b: Kulipari Hero -“BATTALIONS” Strawberry Frog Ranger figure with deadly slingshot!

text_fidelity_a: Yummy Nummies Mini Kitchen Playset - Soda Shoppe(Discontinued by manufacturer) This is the craziest toy ever. . . .and not in a good way. . . . No matter how you get to the “end result” (making a teeny-tiny soda) it tastes HORRIBLE.  So telling you how bad it is from start-to-finish really doesn’t matter, because the end result is awful.  If you want to make your own soda, then you might as well get a SodaStream and be done with it.  Granted, it doesn’t have the “cute” factor of this toy. . . but at least you’ll have something that you can actually swallow.
text_fidelity_b: Yummy Nummies Mini Kitchen Playset - Soda Shoppe(Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Jr. Jungle Fun Activity Cart This is a very cute “walking” type of toy. I really like the fact that it’s wood. It’s also easy to put together. There are lots of little things for the youngest of kids to play with. It’s very bright, colorful and inviting.

The only “negative” about such a toy is depending upon where you use it… . it can “ding” furniture / walls. But as long as that’s not an issue, then it’s really a great item. The “list price” was crazy expensive, but the current price of quite reasonable.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Jr. Jungle Fun Activity Cart

text_fidelity_a:
Lamaze Gardenbug - Baby Foot Finder Socks & Wrist Rattle Set - Sensory Development Toys - Newborn Baby Essentials Very cute. . . .Very bright and colorful. . . . The “rattle” part has virtually no sound. The “wings” are crinkly, like the material which is used in so many items these days.

Overall, I like it. . . but. . . I wish the socks were made like socks. . . and. . . I wish that the price wes a bit lower as these are Made in China and could not have cost very much to make.

As a “side note”. I think the company really should have put a different (smiling / giggling) baby on the box. They would be selling more of these. The baby shown looks like they really have no interest at all.
text_fidelity_b: Lamaze Gardenbug - Baby Foot Finder Socks & Wrist Rattle Set - Sensory Development Toys - Newborn Baby Essentials

text_fidelity_a:
Kulipari enemy -“BATTALIONS” Scorpion Enforcer figure with massive claws! The figure that I received is not glossy, as it shows in the pictures, but it has a matte finish. It’s pink and kind of a darker mustard color.

Only the two “main” arms, attached at the shoulder, move up-and-down. The legs, “other” arms, tail do not move.

Overall it’s not a bad price for a molded piece of plastic Made in China. Originally they were not discounted, so they were crazy expensive. But the current price is “affordable”.
text_fidelity_b: Kulipari enemy -“BATTALIONS” Scorpion Enforcer figure with massive claws!

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming-Pie Face! This is a new take on Russian Roulette. . .. using whipped cream (not included). Depending upon how much whipped cream you use. . . will determine the size of the “SPLAT”. I highly recommend you wear clothing you don’t mind getting splattered with whipped cream. Again, it all depends upon how much whipped cream you use, but I’d recommend being on the safe side.

This is especially fun when both kids and adults play. The only thing I have against it is that it’s crazy expensive for a Made in China toy at the current prices.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming-Pie Face!

text_fidelity_a:
Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game This is a fun game for the youngest of kids. It’s very simple and easy. A few things to keep in mind. . . .

#1. It’s Made in China. It’s not worth the crazy expensive prices currently being charged. If you can get it for ten bucks, or less, then it would certainly be worth it.

#2. Two AA batteries are not included. . . and they should be for the current price.

#3. An adult will need to apply stickers to the ducks. Again. . . they should have been applied in China.
text_fidelity_b: Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game

text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Ice Age Creator Kit This is fun hands-on item. Granted, it’s a one-time sort of thing. Nonetheless, it’s a lot of fun to put together. This is an item where adult supervision is really required.

The kit includes not only instructions but information and questions for kids as well. Makes it a little more educational.

This item really makes a great kids gift (with parent approval, as they will need to help).
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Ice Age Creator Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Play-Doh Star Wars Luke Skywalker vs. Darth Vader Can-Heads I don’t know anyone who doesn’t like Play-Doh. . . Put it together with Star Wars. . . . and a very reasonable price. . . . and you have Winner! I will say that this is the type of toy you have to create your own fun, and use your imagination. There’s no soundtrack. . . There are no “rules” . . . . No flashing lights. But it’s still a lot of fun.

Note that there are several small pieces. . . .and. . . the Play-Doh contains wheat, as it shows on the back of the box.

Cool Baker Chocolate Treats Maker This is a fun set. . . BUT. . . it is not really the easiest thing in the world to do. It really takes some “experimentation” and practice. Sometimes that doesn’t work so well with kids. It also takes adult supervision from beginning to end. You’ll want to either have an apron, or clothes you don’t mind getting dirty. But it’s chocolate, so most kids love chocolate, no matter what!

This is a “simple” item that uses hot water to melt the chocolate. That’s not always going to work. It can depend upon the type / brand of chocolate you use. The chocolate is not included. Again, this is all part of the “experimentation” process. Make sure your hot water is really hot. Fill the melting container. . . Shake it around for a couple of minutes. . . Empty the container. . . then fill it back up with hot water again. . . before placing the chocolate into the container.

The current cost isn’t “crazy expensive” for a Made in China set. . . And it can give you an afternoon of fun with your children, so, in the end, I think it’s worth it.

text_fidelity_a:
Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink Let’s just say. . . I’m not “squealing with laughter” as it shows on the listing in several places.

First of all. . . This is NOT a pretty pig. It’s kind of “odd” because the color is different in the pictures (the picture of the girl holding it makes it look white with a little tan and black splotches. . . which it is not). The one that I received looks like different shades of tan with some dark splotches. Not the least bit pink. . . not the least bit attractive. I understand that not all pigs are pink in real life. . . and not all pings are “pretty”. . . but when you’re making a toy, then the majority of the time they are pink. . . and they should be at least “not-ugly”, which this one is. . . ugly.

The pictures show the pig standing. This pig does not stand. It lays flat down, with the legs forward. There is nothing stiff in the legs so that it can stand, and it’s obviously made to lay flat.

The “puppet part”. There is a “slit” in the bellow where you put four fingers. You have to find the holes for the fingers for the two front legs. Then you use two fingers to move the mouth up-and-down. Not the easiest thing to do.

The pig “grunts” when you squeeze the “rump” part of the pig. Again, not the best design, in my opinion.

There is a tag that shows that this pig won the 2014 “plush toy” award, which I find very hard to believe.

Finally. . . This is a Made in China toy. . . At the current price it’s WAY too expensive for Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Folkmanis Grunting Pig Hand Puppet, Standard Packaging, Pink

I scrolled down the page and saw Super Mario Bros 2, Punch Out and, my absolute favorite, The Legend of Zelda so I figured why not? With games like those there will be a ton of others I’ll enjoy and I’ll have days of nostalgia to look forward to.  Well, I will tell you why not. Those games aren’t on here. I saw this giant version and just had to have it. What a fun twist on classic game. The wooden blocks are all perfectly made. There are no splinters or rough spots and they’re all identical. The case is great and makes it possible to carry all those blocks easily. Set up takes a little longer than the original since there isn’t a plastic case lining them all up for you but it’s fun and the kids enjoy stacking them. If you’re careful, you can get this tower pretty tall. And when you aren’t careful enough they come crashing down. If you play this inside, do NOT set it up on hardwood unless you’re ok with occasional divots in your floor. We play on a large area rug and it works well. It’s been a blast playing with this and we’ll be enjoying it for years. I highly recommend this to fans of the original or anyone looking for a fun, challenging game.
text_fidelity_b: Jenga Official Giant JS6 - Extra Large Size Stacks to Over 4 feet, Includes Heavy-Duty Carry Bag, Premium Hardwood Blocks, Splinter Resistant, Precision-Crafted Known Brand Game

Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626 I wear a silicone ring and truly like it. Perhaps prefer it because I don't worry about it like I do gold or silver, nor do I tend to hook it (sometimes painfully) on things. I recently noticed the Enso Rings Collections and liked much of what I saw, so when I spotted this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection available I grabbed it. In this case, for my wife. I am a Disney fan as well, but Stitch is one of her favorites, and honestly, I was not a big fan of the red - I prefer blue or black in silicone and the traditional silvers and golds. So... how would we like this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection?

1. It arrived in a nice little packaging making great for protecting the ring, displaying the ring, and a nice presentation for gifting. Great all around.

2. Sizing. Honestly, this was the hardest part. Sizing your finger is never the easiest of tasks as we have discovered. But in this case they wanted the inside of a ring rather than your finger. We have a flexible, cloth type measuring tape, but still, trying to get that in there and with the metal end and lined up and staying in place as you pull it out.. not fun. They do have their sizes to the rounded whole - I feel like I remember others with in between sizes, which would make this harder. In the end we went with the one we got consistently and hoped. Turned out great - fits my wife's middle finger as she wanted and my ring finger.

3. The red is actually pretty cool. Again, not my favorite on the spectrum of ring colors, but my wife loves it and I like it. And for the Lilo and Stitch option, it works. There is a sparkle to it - both nice and not overwhelming.

4. The in-print on the ring feels "subtle," but present; something you can see, but at a glance it's more like a light-shadow affect. Upon closer examination you spot the little Lilo (not a fave character for either of us), but the Stitch rocks. And the little flower brings out the Polynesian flavor, while giving the whole thing a sweet nod to Disney. For a Disney fan, it's a great find.

5. This is my wife's first silicone, but like me, she's liking it. It is comfortable, easy to wear, does not catch on things in the same way (but all rings do catch), and it has that silicone flexibility that makes wearing it more comfortable in many situations.

6. I have found in wearing silicone I have to be more careful when washing my hands. Soap can build up behind and/or keep up the wetness between ring and finger, and can come off easier when drying. I warned her and sure enough, same thing. So do be careful. Additionally, she finds there is a (slight) risk of stuff like soap building up in the little grooves. No worries, what little she thinks she saw (it's tiny) washed out easily. And so far, after two weeks, it continues to look like new.

In the end she really likes this Enso Rings Disney Lilo and Stitch Silicone Ring Collection and is so happy to have this Stitch ring. I've seen a few others on their pages I'd consider, so yes, we'd get another Enso ring. Always fun to wear an ode to something that makes you smile.
text_fidelity_b: Enso Rings Disney Lilo & Stitch Silicone Ring Collection - Comfortable and Flexible Design - Ohana and Experiment 626

It is intended for ages eight and up. The large cards are easy to hold and the things you're supposed to memorize on each card are clear to see. There are 25 suspect cards which include variations in color, clothing, and animals. You place three to six of these cards out (depending on the difficulty level you desire) and memorize each card before turning them upside down. There are six number cards that you place above each suspect so that you know which suspect to talk about when you roll the dice. The dice roll tells you which suspect to talk about and which feature (color, clothing, or animal) that you need to remember correctly for that suspect. If the player is able to correctly remember that feature, they keep the card and score a point, but if they remember wrong, the rest of the players each have a chance to guess until someone gets it right or no one does. That suspect card is replaced with a new one, and everyone has a chance to look at the new card. Thus, you are constantly having to remember new information for each position. This can be a fun way to train your brain to remember better, but some people might find it too frustrating.

The set includes 120 magnetic sticks, 40 steel balls, and a gray bag with a drawstring to hold the set if you don't want to use the original packaging. The magnets hold together strong enough to basically stay where you put them but not so strong that it's difficult to pull things apart. The set also came with pictures of a number of projects. The pictures show only the finished building projects, but they were not always clear about what went where when the lines overlapped in the picture. Still, I've been able to do most of the projects, and of course you can come up with your own ideas. AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card [[VIDEOID:3ab25a1fe74e640fbb16d3764ecc8aea]] This Kid's Action Camera was better than I expected. The camera (not in the waterproof case) measures 2.5" tall x 2.25" wide x 7/8" thick. The full color screen on the back measures 1.5" tall x 1.25" wide. The photographs can be up to 5M (you select can 5M, 3M, 2M, or 1M), and the photographs actually look pretty good (good color balance, no distortion, in focus). You can record just audio, and this came out clear when the camera was held within a foot distance of my mouth. I didn't test any further. The video can be selected at 1080P, 720P, or VGA quality. The 1080P looked good but it doesn't appear to be the normal HD proportions but rather closer to a square than a long rectangle. Some of the recordings also had mysterious sounds in addition to the expected ones--maybe like something tapped against the case during the recording. Also, I haven't found a way to remove the automatic time stamp placed on the video and photos. You can playback the videos, etc. on the camera if desired and also delete them off if the take was a bad one.

I found the camera very easy to use once I read the instructions. One rechargeable Li-ion battery is included. You charge the battery using the included USB cord connected to a computer or using a USB charging adapter. There's a red LED light when charging which turns off when it's full. Charging didn't take long, and they estimate that a full charge from near empty will take about 2.5 hours. I did notice that, even with the camera switched off in addition to being turned off, the battery tends to drain. We used the camera a bit, then left it sitting for a few weeks, only to discover that it needed to be fully recharged before we could use it again. So just charge it periodically so it'll always have enough of a charge.

They estimate that you can take about 90 minutes of 1080P video on the included 32 GB micro SD card (probably limited by the battery as I think 32GB can hold twice that). You need to format the micro SD card before use. You can do this by inserting the card into the camera, going to the settings menu, and selecting the option to format the card. You can download the images, audio, and video from the camera either through the USB cable (turn the camera on before connecting to your computer) or by removing the micro SD card and inserting it in the destination computer.

The set includes connectors that allow you to connect the camera to connectors that attach to a helmet, a bike, and so on. In the instructions, they show how the various connectors can be used for different situations. The set also comes in a very nice storage / carrying case so the unused connectors and such don't get lost. There is a holder for the camera that is a waterproof shell (good up to 30m or 98 feet underwater) and this can also be connected to all these other connectors.

I tried to film a sunset, and it did look pretty accurate when the lens was pointed directly at the sun/brightest area. If I dropped the focus of the camera to the ground, the camera Auto changed things so that it looked like a bright daylight scene. I tried some video of moving objects (like a flag on a windy day) or with me moving the camera, and it came out good.

The 3 games were pretty simple and may bore kids used to touchscreens. For example, the puzzle game would be pretty quick to work except you have to select a piece, use the arrow to move it one square, then select a piece, etc. Lots of clicking the buttons. Still, fun if there aren't other options around.
text_fidelity_b: AKAMATE Kids Action Camera Waterproof Video Digital Children Cam 1080P HD Sports Camera Camcorder for Boys Girls, Build-in 4Games, 32GB SD Card

UPDATE 9/18/18: I received the replacement toy, and it works perfectly. The toy is so fun and a good price for what you get. I wouldn't hesitate to buy one as a present in the future.

UPDATE 9/10/18: Yesterday (Sunday), I sent an e-mail to customer support about the malfunction. I received a reply early this morning. It was a real person who communicated clearly and actually addressed my problem. They're sending a replacement that has been tested to make sure it works fine. They're also sending a pre-paid return label for the return of the malfunctioning toy so their engineers can look at the unit. I'm super impressed.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (3 stars): This is generally such a fun, nice toy that I almost gave it 4 stars even though I would have returned this toy if I'd actually bought it. The remote is fairly simple: hold down the left button to turn left, hold down the right button to go right, hold both down to go forward. These button work great. But one of the transform buttons had a glitch from the beginning. The vehicle starts out as a race car when you turn it (and the remote) on. When you hit the bulldozer button, that transforms the race car into a bulldozer just fine every time. However, if the user likes to frequently switch back and forth between the two, the race car transform button will malfunction once out of every two or three times you hit it. When it malfunctions, instead of transforming into a race car, the bulldozer goes straight backward until it runs into something. Since there is no stop button, there is no way to stop the crash. You're no longer in control. At this point, the remote control commands do nothing, and you have to lift the vehicle to access the on/off switch to turn it off and on before it will work again. So far, it hasn't damaged the RC vehicle or anything else. However, this malfunction is a bother at the very least and will damage something eventually.

Intended for ages 3+. It certainly works well for the 5 year old boy who mainly plays with it. Made in China.

Crayola Sticker Design Studio, Paint & Print Art Activity, Repositionable Stickers, Decorate Gear, School Supplies & More (74-7217) If your kids primarily want this kit because, "cool, I made my own stickers!" then they probably will enjoy it. If, like me, they liked the look of the stickers in the advertising, be warned that's more difficult to achieve. I included some pictures of my finished stickers to give an idea of the type of stickers included.

Update: In the end, I've found it easiest to put the drops of paint directly on the sticker sheet, with the desired colors in the right spots (including a red and yellow drop together to make orange, or two red and one blue to make purple, or two yellow and one blue to make green. The blue is very strong and tends to overwhelm the other colors, so use less of it). THEN I use the roller (included) or a sponge brush (not included) to mix the colors directly on the sticker. The problem with using the mat as directed is that too much paint made the roller not mix well, but too little paint meant that the stickers didn't evenly coat with the paint. There would be bare spots (even if paint was under that area) or the paint was thin in spots.

Original review: The first thing I did when I got this set was open it and read the directions. Knowing that practice makes perfect, I tried my first efforts on some white card stock. I followed the directions about the amount of paint to drop on the mat and how many times to run the roller over those drops. The roller started skidding instead of rotating after two passes, so the paint wasn't mixing in the cool, tie-dye-look way. As I used all three colors, the paint quickly turned into a muddy, grayed color. I put the card stock down on the paint, rubbed on the card stock to transfer the paint, turned it over and used the Pattern Design Tool to scratch some lines into the solid color. Some paint came off, some didn't, so it wasn't a clean plaid-pattern type look. Hmm. I looked at the pictures more closely and realized you use the pattern tool on the paint BEFORE you transfer the paint to the paper. The transfer mat looked so much like the finished notebook that this wasn't as clear as it could have been, and the text didn't mention this information. Ok, so that worked, though it's a little hit-or-miss how nice it'll look.

Next attempt: The paint pattern turned into a variety of greens again rather than a tie-dye look, but I loaded the roller (like the cover of the directions shows) and rolled it over the stencil of the dots. Not one bit of paint got on the card stock below the stencil. I used a sponge-brush to pick up paint and dab it on the card stock through the stencil. That worked, but the sponge brush isn't included in this set. I mixed more paint and I used the roller on the zebra stripes stencil, and just a little got through in the larger portions of the design. I tried flipping the paint-covered stencil and rubbing the paint on the stencil onto the card. That worked pretty well, but it's not quite as nice of a design. Then I realized I'd mixed up the directions. You either press the stencil into the paint on the transfer mat and transfer that to the card stock OR put the stencil on the transfer mat, put the paint on the stencil, then roll it down through the holes in the stencil onto the transfer mat, and finally transfer it to the card stock. The roller is only for mixing the paint.

Next try: I only used yellow and red paint and less of it, and I finally got a pretty yellow, orange, and red tie-dye look. If I put a sticker from the sticker sheet down on the paint and rubbed to transfer the paint, that would be a decent success. But I put the card stock on the paint and rubbed the paint onto the card stock. It looked pretty good, but some spots had less paint than others.

So (1) practice a bit before you do your stickers, (2) use only two colors at a time if you wish to create brighter colors (less gray or brownish areas), and (3) you may be able to use 6-9 drops of paint, but this made the roller just skid for me; fewer drops resulted in better blending. Putting the drops in groups (several drops of the same color next to each other) rather than alternately (blue, then yellow, then red) also resulted in more colorful mixes.

Clean up is easy--simply run the mat and tools under warm water in your sink, then dry with a paper towel. All materials are nontoxic. The paints may stain clothing or furniture, though, so wear protective clothing when working with the paint, cover the work surface while painting, and wash up immediately with warm water when finished.

Loopdedoo – DIY Friendship Bracelet Maker Kit – Make Bracelets in Minutes – Award-Winning Craft Kit - Ages 8+ It's suggested for ages 8 and older, and I'd agree with that age range. I think younger kids could successfully use it if an older, experience person was nearby to help. Basically, you loop embroidery thread around the two hooks to create the desired core thickness, then twist a knob to spin the core while you lay down an outer design over that core. You tie on the finished piece using the end loops. The bracelet should withstand normal wear if tied according to the directions.

The distance from one hook to the other is 11", but longer items can be made by linking finished 11" pieces or by a somewhat trickier shifting of the piece after you have 11" of it's length finished. You can, of course, make lengths shorter than 11". The instructional book was easy to follow and was all I needed to create a nice bracelet with no frustration involved. They also have good instructional videos on their website: annwilliamsgroup. com/instructional-videos

Included in the kit is the main Loopdedoo tool (with a push-out drawer for storing the thread and clips); instructional booklet; 18 skeins of embroidery thread (100% cotton, 8.7 yards) in a variety of colors including reds through purples, black, brown, and cream; and 2 alligator clips (which are used with the tool to hold threads in place when making the longer items). The thread is Made in China, but I think the loop Loopdedoo is made in the USA.

The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games The Wolves is a quick game that looks easy to play, but it sure is not that.

The basic mechanic of the game is to manipulate your terrain tiles to perform actions, each of which can influence how fast the game accelerates, and how you manage to score points. Everything is controlled by these terrain tiles, and so you might choose a move actions specifically so that you can flip a tile that will allow you to use a Howl action. Or you may be lucky enough to flip three matches to Dominate an opponent's wolf, but that would require a lot of luck...or is it skill?

I would compare this game to 5 Tribes. None of the mechanics are similar in any way, but if you've played 5 Tribes, you might know that on your turn, you can likely identify ten different moves you could do, but it's mathematically impossible to always choose the correct action. In this game, you have a similar conundrum. What is the best move? Is it to howl at a wolf to put an extra marker on the board, or build a den that helps me establish area majority? There are turns where you legitimately have to decide between 5 different, equally powerful moves you can make, and then live with those consequences.

I do have one problem with the game, though, and that is that there are a lot of little rules to remember. Two pieces per space, you cannot be moved if you share a spot with a den, you have to re-move if someone "pushes" your pack wolves with an alpha, and alphas are the only ones who can howl. Dens can be upgraded to lairs if your den is next to water, but some spaces have rivers on them that look like water sources, but they aren't. Also, alphas have to be on the space to build a den, but can be adjacent to upgrade it. You get a reference card for some of this, and some is on the board, but it can be tricky to remember all of the specific placement rules for each different action.

This game is a lot thinkier than you might expect, and so it won't be for everyone. Everyone will want to play it though - the production quality of the game, from the art to the unique wolf meeples, is really quite excellent, and the game is rife with possibilities for expansions. The box insert is well-designed, and the maps are modular, which is great for replayability. Overall, our heavy gaming family liked our two plays of the game, and will come back to it often, because not too many games of this depth can be played this quickly.
text_fidelity_b: The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games

Challengers Card Game | Strategy/Interactive Deck Management Game | Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 10+ | 1-8 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Z-Man Games For this game, you really need to know what you're getting.

This is a strategy deckbuilding game with a lot of silly, and a little stupid. And if you're OK with a lot of silly and a little stupid, you will probably love Challengers! if you have a even number of players.

In Challengers, you are deckbuilding in preparation for a game of War. Yes, that game of War where you mindlessly turn over cards and hope for high numbers, even knowing that there are a bunch of low numbers in your deck.

The only player choice is made during the deckbuilding phase, and then you get to sit back and watch the chaos.

And if you're OK with a chaotic game like this, where choices are limited and it's all down to luck, then you've found a winner with Challengers! If you think this sounds like a waste of time, then for you, it probably is. We had a few stand up and cheer come-from-behind moments and a lot of inglorious losses.

This is a great deckbuilding intro for kids, and for the grownups with the right tastes, this will be a hit, but I think a lot of people will absolutely hate it also.

I get the feeling that these are well-known characters in that universe, and I think that if you know who they are, that might add an extra layer of fun to the game. The actions are largely mechanical, but it is fun the first few times you work to add a barracks to your castle or help a damsel in distress.

I will say that the best element of the game is the production value. This is the only version of this game (that I know of) and it feels like what you'd get from a $100+ Kickstarter campaign, with wooden everything and quality cards.

I think if the characters provided a bit more personality to the story, or if I knew something more about the world, I might really like this game, but I found it rather mechanical and slow moving, and the campaign didn't hook me as well as I'd hoped. It's not a bad game, but it wasn't for me.

The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.

Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers I absolutely love the concept of this little worker placement game, but the execution is not great.

You spend each turn doing basic worker placement stuff - go here, get resources, then convert those resources somewhere else, all while building a cell wall around your plant cell in an effort to turn your stuff into points. There is real science here - you use different cell components according to the actual chemical formulas of 6 water + 6CO2 to do photosynthesis, and cards are named after actual scientific stuff. There's also an area control segment of the board where you can earn some minor points and bonuses. The highlight, though, is that when you play this game, you'll know more about real-life science than when you started, and that's a pretty cool thing.

The game suffers though, because there just isn't much to do at the end of the game, and catching up is extremely difficult given that so few actions lead to points, and so many of the things you can collect are useful for only one or two functions. It's a little bit like saying that the science got in the way of the fun. When one person does the action to trigger the end of the game, there is usually a rush to do the singular action left that can generate points, and if you don't have it, you just stockpile some useless resources. That's a poor endgame, and on second or third playthoughs, you'll find that there are really only one or two viable strategies for winning at all.

Ultimately, this is an awesome game for teaching a small group of teenage scientists more about cell structures, but at the price of a hobby board game, it's tough to put in the hands of teachers for classroom use, and harder still to spend valuable class time to educate non-gamers about the intricacies of worker placement prior to their first play. And that play will run the course of a class period, more or less, so that has it's benefits, and it's detriments.

As a gamer's game, we found the concept extremely interesting, but the execution needed a little work. It won't hit the table often, because every other worker placement game we have is more exciting at the endgame, and offers us a greater variety of strategies for winning.

Do note that the addition of the "Mangrove" board, which was a kickstarter stretch goal, is essential to me keeping this one in our collection. The normal board is not nearly as good.
text_fidelity_b: Cellulose: A Plant Cell Biology Game | MENSA Recommended Strategic & Entertaining Game to Learn Photosynthesis, DNA & Biochemistry | Educational STEM Board Game for Families, Students & Teachers

The Adventures of Robin Hood | A Kosmos Game | Family-Friendly, Cooperative, Role-Player, Story-Driven Game for 2 to 4 Players, Ages 10 and up I think I'm just a bit too spoiled by the Pandemic Legacy games, Kings Dilemma, Crusoe Crew, Above and Below, and the like.

The Adventures of Robin Hood is a fine game that is meant to be a legacy-like experience - you play a pretty straightforward move-around-the-board style game, trying to stay inside the shadows printed on the board, until you need to pop out to land on one of a few dozen removable/flippable cardboard cutout pieces that populate the boards. Once you land there to complete objectives, you read a few lines from a book based on the mission at hand, and sometimes you need to perform well at a little combat or make a decision on what to say.

The game is easy to learn and offers a very different gaming experience for those who are unfamiliar with the aforementioned legacy games. Unfortunately, if you've played those, this one is likely just a bit too juvenile. Reading from the book is fun at first, until you find yourself going through the motions and making very similar decisions about completely uninteresting plot points as you progress. Characters largely say the same things, all lead you more or less directly to where you need to go, and when you get there and succeed, you get a "congratulations" rather than a different gaming experience (like in Pandemic), new challenges (like Kings Dilemma) or even a remarkable story experience (like Above and Below). Everything just kind of plays out on it's own.

If you have an impatient bunch, the "pick the next player" from the bag thing could leave people waiting quite a while between turns.

The other thing I don't like is that the rules are a bit interpretive in terms of how movement and the shadows rules affect players. If you want to play this "by the rules" and you have someone who wants to argue over a millimeter, the rules will allow the fudger to make pretty much any interpretation they wish. Most missions are also very much on the easy side.

As this is aimed at a younger audience (I think - the box says 10+ age), some of this is quite forgivable, but for the mature gamer, you have far better options, even if you're enamored with the theme, as I am, or the legacy style game, as my family is. The little one was bored by the long missions, Mom and Dad were thinking there should just be a little more punch to the story. We found this to be a 2/5 experience, but I think most would find it to be a 3/5 or so.

Pandasaurus Games Sonora - Unique Family-Friendly Board Games, for Adults, Teens & Kids (2-4 Players) , Orange This is a simple "flick-and-write" game with good production values, a questionable rulebook, simple and fast gameplay, and a box that is just ridiculously large for what it is.

Gameplay is fast and straightforward, involving a Crokinole style mechanism for shooting your disc into a recessed game board with a central hole in the middle. This board has a plastic shelf with corner sections for "shooting" pieces, and they'll fall into a central area divided into four main sections. My central board easily comes loose from the shelving piece, and needs to be adjusted prior to gameplay almost all the time. Once you shoot, you'll be making marks onto your player board with the included markers, which are of average quality for a game like this. The boards are easily erasable - a major plus to the production aspect of the game.

The rules are not that hard, but they are explained in a way that makes learning the game quite a bit more difficult than it needs to be. Few examples are covered, and there will be a number of times that you run into situations where you aren't sure how to interpret the rule as written. Once you get it though, play is not too hard, and Sonora is something you can play with the kids after you've worked out the kinks. And they'll want to play this - it's colorful, with kid-friendly artwork, and the gameplay looks like a kid's game, but has enough meat to interest an adult for at least a little while. I don't know that I'd play this game too often, but it is certainly different and a good family game that will keep kids interested. You can play a few games back to back, as they'll run 20 minutes or so once you know the general flow of the game. For a family game night, this will be a good alternative to a more traditional strategy or roll-and-move board game.

The biggest downfall of this one is that the box is so large. As a gamer with a large collection, it's disappointing to see a 12x12 "Ticket to Ride" sized box for a game that could have opted for a foldable game board and fit into a very small game box. They would have lost nothing in doing this, and in fact, they might have fixed the issue I have with the main board. Even if they must have a one-piece board, dropping the molded plastic insert that holds a handful of discs and pens could have reduced the size by a few inches in depth. In reality, there's not much here in the box, and the components can be entirely stored in the recessed game board area alone. That would be about 3/4" in depth, not 3".

All in all, it's OK.

AniBlock Puzzle Challenger Lite I Brain Game and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 4 and 5 This was delivered to my house about an hour ago, and my 6 year old daughter is about to put it away. She's just now finishing up the hardest puzzle included in the kit.

I'm torn on how to review this. It's clearly a nice toy for a lot of kids. The pieces are nice and chunky, the puzzle cards have vibrant artwork, and the app works smoothly. That said, though, there are 12 puzzle cards in the box, and yes, they can be solved multiple ways, but there is no guidance for different combinations of blocks to use to complete the puzzles, so there isn't much incentive to take them off and try again. Also, for someone who is not too far removed from the minimum age range suggested though, it's really easy. Like, a puzzle in two minutes for almost every combo in the deck, except for the boat, which is in the middle of the difficulty spectrum. On the box, with an oddly small top, there are images of three-dimensional shapes made out of the aniblocks, flying around, and the actual blocks do not connect in this way to form them, which was probably the most disappointing part.

The app deserves some special mention. It's certainly good, and easy to use, but it's still an app, and so, of course, it defeats the purpose of having a screen avoidant time to include it. There's also another disadvantage, which is that there are tons of apps that do this same game already, with digital blocks. They offer more puzzles, with more diverse colors of blocks, in more diverse shapes, and a wider variety of difficulty levels.

Overall, I think there are better toys for your money that do very similar things and offer a lot more variety than this. The phone apps, as mentioned before. We have a board game called Blokus 3D (or Rumis) which have a similar pattern-matching idea, but allow for 3D building. There's also Kanoodle Junior, for example, which is excellent, cheaper, ready to travel, and doesn't require an app. 12 puzzles and a handful of two-colored blocks is just not enough for the price. For that reason, I cannot recommend this...but there are far worse options.

We barely used the book for assembly, but read the more educational "science" book cover to cover.

She and I talk all the time about renewable energy, largely because solar panels are looking like the next big home improvement project around here, and we get what I'd consider a reasonable amount of wind. She found the concepts easy enough to understand, and was interested to see what we'd be able to do in the backyard...and it's not much. The wind we got was not nearly enough to make this project effective, even on what I'd consider a relatively windy day. I put it on the roof for a short time and that helped, but not much. The turbine requires a battery, which makes both of us question where the small amount of power we are generating actually comes from.

So the experiments died off rather quickly, and this became a very short model building project for her that Dad is enjoying tinkering with to see if he can charge one of those rechargable cell-phone batteries. Kid is off playing with the very small toy car that comes with the kit, but doesn't look like it belongs at all.

If you get a lot of wind, then it's probably a lot more fun, but it's for the younger age of the spectrum for sure.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Wind Power V4.0 STEM Experiment Kit | Build a 3ft Wind Turbine to Generate Electricity | Learn About Renewable Energy & Power a Small Model Car | Weatherproof for Outdoor Use

City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS) Here you have some knock-off LEGOs that work...technically.

SUSSED The Weird Would You Rather Card Game | Ages: Teens, Adults, Kids 12+ | 110 Cards | for Family, Friends and More | Fantasy Version This is the third Sussed game that I've reviewed recently, and my second favorite. This one in particular has the highest age range of the three games, going 12-100, which is a little high, although I do believe the clues are a little more difficult to decipher in this set than the others, which I figured should range at the 7 or 8 to adult age range.

This set is far more thematic than the others, having clues that very specifically fit into the theme - adventure, fantasy, sci-fi and superheroes - which is a good concept. Other sets have tried this, but didn't have enough questions to ensure that the theme carried through.

It's a good get-to-know-you game with a definite shelf life based on the limited numbers of cards in the box and the nature of players to discuss. text_fidelity_a:
Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands LEGO would never make something like this. Sure, you can take their stuff and make anything with them, but too many of their kits make a definitive something. This is a definitive nothing, but a nothing that can entertain far beyond what a lot of different "somethings" can do.

LEGO is a toy, and this is often something that they remember to a fault. Here is a LEGO competitor, with bricks that are compatible, that remembers that it's not always a toy that kids want. They want an experience of playing, and that's what this Forest Garden kit gives them. Is it a dinosaur jungle? Is it a very nice tropical garden? Are the characters running from that alligator, or picnicing i the woods? With this, more than with any LEGO kit I've ever reviewed, there is a limitless number of possibilities.

There are no instructions with this kit, which is somewhat bothersome for the finnicky children who need a "right" way to put them together, but the playscape this provides is so unique that I can't give it less than 5 stars.

text_fidelity_a: SUSSED The Weird Would You Rather Card Game | Ages: Teens, Adults, Kids 12+ | 110 Cards | for Family, Friends and More | Fantasy Version Played a quick round with my wife and 6-year-old daughter as soon as it arrived.  The game is quick and easy - a scorepad, a deck of cards, and a basic set of rules.  You ask questions, on mostly random subjects, and each of the two guessers attempts to figure out what the third player is going to choose from a set of 3 options.  The vocabulary and topic selection is a little tough for a bright 6-year-old, but a little rewording from Mom and Dad helped her get through it.  Overall, it's a cute idea, but it might get old quickly with only one deck, and it has minimal replay value, as the conversation quickly turns to "I would have chosen..." which is going to deflate your desire to play through multiple times.  There's not as many questions as you'd like to see since each card has 4 questions and that constitutes a round.  I could see a game like this making a nice icebreaker for a corporate team-building retreat or a get-to-know-your-classmates style game, but for a family game, it was good, not great, and not something that we'll likely keep coming back to.

Klutz Crystal Unicorn Craft & Science Kit Crytal kits are notoriously iffy - sometimes they work, and sometimes they don't - and even the same kit will work sometimes, and not others. It has to be perfect, and I mean really perfect, for them to work at all.

For us, we ended up with crystals on only the base of the unicorn's tail and mane, and not on the tips (go figure). Those crystals are white or clear, and they look exactly like what they are - white crystals on a colored unicorn - not pink and blue crystals as the image on the box indicates.

Add to that the fact that there's roughly 1/3 of the items you'll need to make the kit included (you'll provide scissors, ruler, mason jars, distilled water, and a weight for the unicorn once you realize that it doesn't float), and this is a mediocre buy at best.

These are fully compatible, and integrate well with kits you've already got. The carrying case is nice too, with a top that doubles as a LEGO base plate.

The only real difference between these and your standard set of LEGOs is the instruction manual. These are pretty straightforward to build, but unlike a regular LEGO manual where each page tells you where to put 3-5 pieces, each step in this one asks you to put 8-20 pieces on a model. It's substantially more difficult for youngsters.

Overall though, this is fantastic value for your money.

I've bought two of these kits now, and one includes quite a few guns and grenades, which isn't exactly "fireman" material. Some of the pieces in the second kit are also quite a bit more stuck in place, where they should be free-moving.

LEGO Technic Stunt Show Truck & Bike 42106; Includes Stunt Motorcycle, Toy Truck and Trailer (P10 Pieces) LEGO Technic is very different from regular LEGO blocks, even though they can combine, but the difference is strong enough that this will be a very different type of challenge for young builders. These are more "Engineer-y" than the standard sets, and will teach simple mechanical principles as you build the pull-motion propulsion system from scratch, and kids can see how it comes together.

If regular LEGO is a teaching toy, this is even better.

That said, Technic is harder to be creative with, so these blocks don't get a lot of play with the standard set once the fun of the kit wears away. My daughter had a little trouble building this, but she is on the younger edge of the age range, so Dad had to do a number of the trickier steps.

The ads for this one talk about racing the cars, but it's all imaginary - there's no pull-back action or anything like you can get in Tecnic models - and the two included minifigs are basic to the point of being disappointing. Most of the pieces in this one are very small, and there's not much movement in the final models at all. If you have a little car fan at home, this will thrill them. We're not car people, so we thought it was only just a bit better than OK.

Your children will use the included wooden stakes, or maybe even toothpicks, to score designs into the surface of a black piece of paper. As they scratch, the colors that make up the underlying layers start to show through, and create brilliant drawings.

It's a very nice little project for young ones that doesn't take too much time, or too much effort. Outside of a little sweeping to take care of the fine black bits that fall off the surface of the paper, there isn't much to this one. Of course, the nature of the product requires that your little artist will have to be careful, and take their time, as there's no erasing. I make mine plan out her drawing ahead of time, and make a practice copy before transferring the image to the final piece. Of course, there's always stencils, but those won't be for everyone.

The pages in this kit are nice and thick, but only about the size of two index cards put side-by-side. I was kind of hoping for something a little bigger. The scratch sticks are good quality, as are the stencils.

Overall, a great rainy-day project.

Tech Will Save Us Synth Wave Kit | Educational Music Toy, Ages 8 & Up What a great idea, and what poor execution. What you get here is a little music kit that looks like a kid's version of a soundboard from a recording studio. Your child does a little basic assembly, and then experiments with making sounds. And those sounds are...interesting. Not exactly a kid's first Vivaldi kit, but I don't really think that's quite the point. I'm sure it's possible to make some decent music with this - although I'm sure that it would only appeal to the youngsters.

My biggest problem is that the entire thing is made out of cardboard, and it won't last long enough for your child to actually practice with. Ours was in the trash after two days of very light use. As another reviewer mentioned, mine shipped with batteries, but those were dead.

As an idea, this is excellent. As a kit, you can pass.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills This is not up to the typical quality of Melissa and Doug products in my opinion. There are 12 mini-projects in this "book"(it's an scruffy bubble envelope with other envelopes inside), and each has some very basic scissor projects. The first one, for instance, has your child cutting in straight lines to create a simple memory game. The second one builds on this, adding some cross-cutting, and so forth.

Each kit is good enough, and the variety is greatly appreciated by the kiddos. In some instances, the instructions needed a little work, while in others, they were perfect. In each case, they're language independent and entirely taught through pictures, which is great for helping the kiddos follow along and do the projects somewhat independently.

There are two pairs of scissors included in this package - a straight pair, and a "scrapbooking" scissor that cuts "teeth" - but these safety scissors are entirely too "safety" for me. The straight one works well enough at first, while the teeth scissors barely worked at all. Their entirely plastic frame wears out with minimal use. There are no metal parts on them, outside of the screws. We had trouble making clean cuts as we approached the middle of the kits, and by the end, we just switched to metal scissors as we were mangling the paper more than doing actual cutting.

The problem with the scissors, as well as the complete lack of a storage solution for these projects as they're in progress is enough for me to rate this kit lower than I normally do. My kit arrived mispacked, so I received two #4 projects, and no #3 project. Good projects can be had here, but bring some of your own materials.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Deluxe Scissor Skills

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs: Alien Slime Lab Science Experiment Kit & Lab Setup, 10 Experiments with Slime | A Parents' Choice Recommended Award Winner This is a pretty expensive science kit given what you're going to make - 4 very small batches of slime and a few "experiments" to go with it - but the value of the product is in the education your children will receive from doing it. Most slime kits are "here's the ingredients, now mix and play". This one gives you the ingredients, tells you to mix, and then gives you a "scalpel" and tells you to go to work.

This is a safe kit that is fine for the age range indicated on the box, although young scientists are probably going to need assistance from Mom and Dad on a few experiements, because a few of them are tricky given the limited space in the instructon manual.

You're going to need to head to the store as well, so be prepared that not everything you'll need is in the box. Some items are very common, others are a bit more unusual.

Overall, this was our favorite slime kit, and a great learning tool.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Ooze Labs: Alien Slime Lab Science Experiment Kit & Lab Setup, 10 Experiments with Slime | A Parents' Choice Recommended Award Winner

text_fidelity_a:
Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi This is a very simple stock market game that is somewhat accessible to younger players. Throughout the game, you'll buy and sell ingredients, complete potions with special abilities, and manipulate a cool little stock market simulation gadget that rolls colored containers down a ramp to indicate value.

The game is very simple, and offers players, in my opinion, a few too many options during their turn. Adults and gamers will find that the ability to sell sets at maximum value to be pretty easy because of the ability to sell not only sets, but individual cards (which allows you to essentially set any price for any set you like). To obtain new ingredients, you can buy from the market, buy from the deck, or swap, or use potion effects. That's a lot of choices to handle, and our little gamer found it to be confusing at first because there were simply too many options. She could identify which cards she wanted, but didn't know whether she should buy, trade or use effects to get them.

All told, this is a good game for youngsters, but there is a learning curve to get good. The number of options can be overwhelming and frustrating at first, but after a few plays, anyone as young as six or eight can probably grasp how to do some of the more complex manipulations. I don't think this will ever be a go-to for an adult game night, but for families, you could do a lot worse than this.

Also, the components are great.
text_fidelity_b: Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Natural Play Cardboard Jigsaw Floor Puzzle: Outer Space (100 Pieces) Back in my day, Pluto was a planet. Then, it wasn't. Then, it was again. Now, it's still apparently not.

Melissa & Doug's planet puzzle does not include Pluto or the asteroid belt, but it does differentiate all eight other planets, and it shows orbital patterns, the sun, an astronaut and shuttle, a galaxy, and a few shooting stars. All told, a good representation of the solar system, and a good educational tool for youngsters. The image they chose has enough going on to be very interesting, but it's hard to differentiate where planets lie in relation to each other.

This puzzle has larger than normal cardboard pieces, and mine did have more than a few rough edges that required a little tearing. It's not something that I'd complain about normally, but I typically expect top-of-the-line stuff from Melissa & Doug, and I don't know that this is it. The box is perfectly sized to fit everything, and I like that it has a list of the planets on the side of the box.

Overall, a good solar system, even without Pluto.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Natural Play Cardboard Jigsaw Floor Puzzle: Outer Space (100 Pieces)

Elmer's Collection Slime Kit Supplies Include Glow In The Dark Magical Liquid Slime Activator, Metallic Magical Liquid, Confetti Magical Liquid, Translucent Glue, Metallic Glue, Clear Glue, 6 Count It's three bottles of Elmer's Glue, three bottles of "Activator" and a set of instructions. That's about as simple as it gets. Mix 'em up in a bowl, and you have instant slime. At the end, we have enough of each Activator bottle left to make a small batch of each color once more, even though we used the whole bottles of glue.

You'll literally have glitter all over your hands the instant you touch the slime, and of course, it's slime, so it goes on the table, it goes on the hands, it goes in the hair, and so forth. That activator pack has mysteriously disappeared... The other two activators and glue make very good, consistent slimes that last quite a while if you pack them in a tupperware container.
