text_fidelity_a:
Kodama (2nd Edition) Board Game Kodama is a game about building massive trees in the forest.

Each turn, players take turns adding branches to their tree that have specific features on them like mushrooms and fireflies on them in an attempt to score points based on the goals of the season (you play through three) and secret goal cards (you choose from four at the beginning of the game). Branch cards can grow outward and upwards, so long as each new card you play touches only one other card you've used thusfar, which is much more difficult than it sounds, and so long as each main branch down to the root can score you ten or less points.

The game itself is OK, but not really very special in any specific way. The artist and producers made the strange choice of making this happy & friendly forest a blend of dark blues, browns and greys that depict a nighttime forest, and it makes the cards a little more difficult to read. It also just looks a little off. Aside from this strange point, the game is not bad, and I like how different it is.
text_fidelity_b: Kodama (2nd Edition) Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game Onitama is a 2-player only game that tries to have a theme, but is really quite abstract.

When I heard about it, I was really quite intrigued that this would be added to the Dice Tower Essentials line as an abstract; after all, isn't Tom Vasel the guy who dislikes most abstracts because they're not theme-y enough? Yet here is the third game in his very quality game series that is otherwise highly thematic, and he goes with an abstract. Seemed like the game must be incredible to have cracked that list as an abstract.

I played a number of times with my wife, who admittedly likes this game quite a lot more than I do. I find the game similar to chess or the Duke, in which you have a certain number of moves, represented by cards, and you move your pieces around the board, switching cards with your opponent along the way. There is a lot of doublethink - If I do this, then they know I'll do that next turn, so they might do this... - and I like that element of the game, but the limitation on my moves did tend to cramp my style a little more, and I'd find myself wishing I just had more options. That skill can probably be built up over time playing with this one, but I don't know if it grabbed me enough to make me invest my time with it.

If 3.5 were an option, I'd go with that. Just not my style, and not as good as the expectations led me to believe.
text_fidelity_b: Arcane Wonders Onitama Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Grey Fox Games Deception: Murder in Hong Kong Board Game, Fast Pace Murder Mystery, 20 min, 4-12 Players, Age 14+ ...Who Among You Can See Through The Lies or is Capable of Not Getting Caught This is a murder-mystery game for a crowd that doesn't require any acting. It's much more akin to a social deduction game like Resistance, but with a few different elements.

In Deception, each player gets a combination of 8 cards in front of them: 4 weapons and 4 "clues" - really just random objects. One player is given the role as murderer, and another player knows who that player is, and it is that second player who gives clues to everyone else using clue boards, each of which involves placing a marker on one of five different words. This player does not talk other than to provide a "no" in case of a wrong answer.

The game is good, but doesn't ever hit the next level for me, and it's really because of the clue boards and cards. So many of these objects are very benign things that don't ever see any specific clues. One time, the murderer chose a toy, specificially the toy duck card, and it was my job to attempt to communicate this to the other players. Unfortunately, not one clue card that came up over the course of five different rounds had anything to do with fun, ducks, birds, toys, or any other words of that nature, and that means that the players ended up rather frustrated with me for not giving them anything to go on in terms of guessing the clue. This happened rather frequently, enough that we decided to put this one away after a few tries.

When it works, it's very fun. When it doesn't, it feels rather frustrating. I thought it worked more than it failed, and the components are pretty nice, so I give it the edge from 3.5 to 4 stars, but I am not 100% sure that I'll keep it in my collection.

Adult warning: A game subtitled "Murder in Hong Kong" might not seem like it requires a parental warning, but I know that I was playing Clue and other similar games as a child, and as a parent of a young gamer who is willing to try anything, I feel it necessary to include a warning. Some of the cards in this one are illegal drugs, and the clue cards do use more "intense" words to describe elements of the crime. Oftentimes, figuring out the whodunnit of this one requires you to think pretty hard about how certain weapons might be used to kill someone, so it's not for the young ones out there.
text_fidelity_b: Grey Fox Games Deception: Murder in Hong Kong Board Game, Fast Pace Murder Mystery, 20 min, 4-12 Players, Age 14+ ...Who Among You Can See Through The Lies or is Capable of Not Getting Caught

text_fidelity_a:
Kanagawa Game Kanagawa is a board game about making the most cohesive panorama painting.

The first thing you'll notice about Kanagawa is that it has tremendous components. The little paintbrush bits are unique and well-made, and the way that the cards fit together is really cool. The art and graphic design make it easy for players to figure out how to play, and even the board is well-designed.

Unfortunately, gameplay is pretty basic. Each turn, new cards will be put on the board, either face up or face down depending on the positioning. Players can then either take some of the cards, or allow more to come out, opening up the opportunity to their opponents to take the "best" cards. You then place these cards in panorama fashion on your piece of art, or you can use them as "skill" cards to allow you to paint more interesting paintings on later turns. There are bonus cards, and opportunities to gather more items, but that's really about it.

Aside from the excellent artwork, the only other good thing about this game is that you can explain the rules in only a few minutes. Decisions that you make along the way really are not all that important along the way. You can collect a lot of abilities along the way that you never get the opportunity to use, or you can find that you'd rather not use them because there are better moves for you. Overall, this game was pretty fast, easy to learn, but felt like your decisions were pretty arbitrary, and didn't matter in the end.
text_fidelity_b: Kanagawa Game

text_fidelity_a:
Unusual Suspects Board Game Unusual Suspects is an OK game for the right crowd.

It's essentially an adult version of Guess Who. Twelve cards are placed on the table, and one player secretly chooses one person to be guilty of a crime. Other players ask questions about a character's background or personality, but not their looks or appearance, which the chooser has to answer.

This game can get weird quickly if played with the wrong crowd. Because you have nothing to ask about except an imagined background story, you need to essentially stereotype these characters based on their fashion choices, age, race and gender, and everybody knows it. And as you can imagine, that can be a really awkward experience. In one game, a friend asked "does this character live in a nice neighborhood?" and got a "no" answer, then eliminated the lone remaining African American character based on that answer. We weren't offended, but I'm sure that there are people out there who would be, and those kinds of choices are the meat of this game - you can't ask a question without eliminating a suspect. If you play with people you know, people who are not easily offended, or if you're the type to enjoy a raunchier game like Cards Against Humanity, then this might be right up your alley.

There are 70 suspect cards, and a wide variety of questions to choose from, but the game feels a little underwhelming, even with the right crowd. You can usually make some pretty strong eliminations once you learn which questions you decide to ask to eliminate males or females, young vs old suspects, and once an optimal group strategy is discovered, you can really finish these games incredibly quickly. When it comes down to it, I think the party game market is broad enough that there will always be a better choice for me out there. At the end of the day, there's not too much to bring me back in, and the really funny moments of this game won't necessarily be shared by all.
text_fidelity_b: Unusual Suspects Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Asmodee Hit Z Road This is a very silly game, despite the theme. Not a gory or cartoonish zombie game, it really could be almost anything in place of them: Mad Max-style marauders, for instance. What's nice about that is, if you're anything like me, and you're totally over all types of zombie games, you will still be able to play Hit Z Road.

This game is really a push your luck dice rolling game with auctions. You're trying to survive until the end of the road, and you need to make some meaningful choices along the way that could make your journey much easier, or much more daring. There is some player elimination, but it's not one of those "you can die on the first turn" types of eliminations - our earliest death was about 10 minutes before the end of the game.

I think a lot of people will find the artwork on this game to be fantastic, and I have to admit that it is daring, different, and one of the most unique looking games out there. While I can admire the work that went into it, the art just doesn't appeal to me.

The name, by the way, might be one of the worst in the history of board gaming.
text_fidelity_b: Asmodee Hit Z Road

text_fidelity_a:
Mafia de Cuba This is a pretty good bluffing and betrayal game, along the lines of the Resistance, Werewolf, or for those who are less familiar with board games, maybe even Liar's Dice or the similarly themed Cash and Guns. You get a nice looking cigar box, a bunch of poker chips and a surprisingly light little rule book that packs a lot of fiddly into a very small package (You can do this, or if you do that, you can do between one and three types of thingy, unless you've already taken the what'sit and then refer to page three).

Overall, a very fun and short game if:
1. You have a well-chosen and probably an experienced player be the don. There is actually quite a lot to this role, and a lot of consultation with that fiddly little rule about what you can initially take. The rest of the game is super simple, but first time players will want to see a round first. The person playing as the don has to basically command the entire game, so choosing a shy or confused player can completely ruin the experience.
2. You like the Resistance and games similar, but want something just a little different. This will provide that.
3. You have a group large enough to play this 6 - 12 player game. It handles double digits quite well.
text_fidelity_b: Mafia de Cuba

text_fidelity_a: Thames & Kosmos Kids First Robot Engineer Kit and Storybook I also have the airplane engineering kit made by the same company.  This activity kit has a storybook that runs you through how to put the parts together, and like the airplane kit, you're building something that "doesn't work," i.e. you build a robot, but it doesn't move.  This is a simpler kit, but one that has some staying power, because the storybook is pretty entertaining.  I think we'll come back to this one a few times.

text_fidelity_a:
Creativity for Kids Spark!Lab Smithsonian (Invent The Greatest Board Game) Others will certainly rate this higher than I will, as my family and I are an avid board game family. We have a good 300+ in our collection, many of which have already been introduced to our daughter. So I'm a connoisseur, and she is rapidly becoming one too. This package is not for us.

You can use the pieces inside to create very simple roll-and-move style games, but nothing that even comes close to any level of complexity that a modern board game design (even those by Haba, or those designed specifically for young children) might contain. You can substitute dice rolling for spinning or cards, and there is even an 8-sided die that is going to be new to many families (although this is made out of cardstock, not plastic - a strange choice). There are stickers and a stencil, and most of the equipment is largely blank so you can customize it. Only 10 sheets of paper makes that scoring pad a bit useless.

For most families, this is enough. Our daughter wanted more - cubes, chips, wooden pieces, a larger board, multiple individual player boards, small square tiles...the list goes on. I'm definitely proud of her for that.
text_fidelity_b: Creativity for Kids Spark!Lab Smithsonian (Invent The Greatest Board Game)

text_fidelity_a:
Blue Orange Dr. Eureka Speed Logic Game Each player gets three test tubes, two balls each. As quickly as possible, all players try to reorganize their test tubes and colored balls to match those in the challenge card without touching or spilling any balls, or rearranging the tubes.

The puzzles are complex without being too difficult, and if you play to 5 points, as the game recommends, you will get through this one rather quickly. I found that adults have a significant advantage over kids in this one, but of course, that goes without saying for most games like this. It's an excellent game for logic and dexterity. My daughter enjoys it.

text_fidelity_a:

text_fidelity_a:
Creativity For Kids Spark!Lab Smithsonian "Invent Boundless Bridges" Building Set Very fun little kit that allows the kiddos to build with a wide variety of different materials. Not only do you get cardboard, straws, foam, and so forth, but there are multiple thicknesses of these materials so you can see how different construction methods affect strength. Overall, everything is made really well, and can be used over and over again.

I think this is actually a really strong kit, but I deducted a star for two reasons: first, the booklet is not helpful at all. It explains very little and has only minimal information on how to start, what different types of bridges can do, and so forth. text_fidelity_a: Winning Moves Games Brainspin Creativity Game (1198) Simple doesn't have to be boring. There's not much more to it than that, but it becomes a deceptively deep experience, especially when played with creative types and/or kids.  Overall, I found that my experiences with this were never dull, although I'd imagine that breaking this game out in a group of curmudgeons might have some negative impact. text_fidelity_a:
SmartLab Toys Smart Circuits with 14 Powerful Experiments, Multicolor, Standard This is a really cool kit. It's fairly small in size, but it has so many projects inside that it's ridiculous. Amazing that so much can fit in this package.

The first thing we did was attempt the ten circuitboard projects at my insistence - my daughter wanted to jump in and try the medium and hard stuff immediately, and I wasn't sure I was ready for it. text_fidelity_a:
Lucky Ducks - The Memory and Matching Game That Moves - Includes A Fun Pop The Pig Make-A-Match Card Game Each player takes turn picking ducks and trying to match them to the symbol/color that is in front of them. More likely, it will turn into a free-for-all, as the ducks start spinning around their little track, and little hands start grabbing. All the shapes of the same color also share the same symbol, which makes it pretty easy, and there are exactly three ducks with each of the 4 symbol/color combo. It's a race to see who can get there fastest. Simple enough.

This game is solidly constructed, but has one major design flaw - the shapes that attach to the bottom of each duck are stickers. The eyes are stickers too, but this is less of a problem. Unfortunately, if the stickers on the bottoms of the ducks are torn off, which seems likely to happen given how easy it is for them to be town off of the hard plastic ducks, the game becomes unplayable. I thought that for sure the ducks would be rubber, with the symbols stamped into the bottom, but alas, hard plastic it is.

The concept is OK - running around a ring, then having a the titular Max mash your characters and knock them off the board.  Fun enough, I suppose.  Too bad the construction of the game is so rickety.  It's not helped by the fact that you'll be consistently assembling and disassembling the board to fit it back inside the box. text_fidelity_a:
Magic The Gathering: Arena of the Planeswalkers Game This is a great value for what you're paying. Essentially, this game is based on another very good game called Heroscape. You'll build an arena out of the little pieces in this box, create an army, and do battle with one of the prepainted Planeswalker minis.

I picked this game up as a former MtG player. I was hugely involved in the game from Ice Age through Darksteel. I invested thousands of dollars in the game until it finally became apparent that I couldn't afford to continue to be competitive in the game. What I love about this is that there is a little of what I like about MtG - the deckbuilding, the spellcasting and the strategy - but not so much of what I don't like - the cost.

The game itself is solid if not spectacular. It accomodates up to 5 relatively seamlessly, and it's easy to set up the game as a 2 vs. 2 if you like the team approach, or to just make it a free-for-all. The biggest problem to me with the game, enough to lower it two full stars, is that the game feels like it is missing some essential element that will be added through expansions. It's difficult to identify exactly what it is, but I can't shake the feeling that they took something essential out and going to release it as a big box expansion in the next few months.

As it is, it's a solid game that feels unfinished. I'll eagerly look forward to the (I"m assuming) forthcoming expansion.
text_fidelity_b: Magic The Gathering: Arena of the Planeswalkers Game

Lost Cities - The Board Game Lost Cities TBG is a lot like the original Lost Cities Card Game, but it supports more than 2-players. That's a nice feature.

For those who don't know, Lost Cities the Card Game is considered legendary among hobby board gamers because it's simple, but deep, meaning that anyone can pick up the rules to the game quite quickly, but there's interesting decision-making and complex outcomes to worry about based on your decisions. Of course, it's only a 2-player game, which can be a downfall for many.

The Board Game version is similar in terms of gameplay. If you've already experienced the card game, I could teach you this version in about 30 seconds. Unfortunately, you'll soon want to be back playing the card game. This game lacks a certain something to make it really fun. It works, and it's still easy to learn and play, but I don't think I'll come back to it all that often unless I'm playing with my daughter. For those who are into more complex games, this one just feels...old fashioned. In all the ways that the card game has aged well, this one hasn't.
text_fidelity_b: Lost Cities - The Board Game

text_fidelity_a: Gamewright Forbidden Desert – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Desert Board Game Multi-colored, 5" I always had mixed feelings about Forbidden Island, which I felt was a little too easy and had too many locations which didn't matter one way or the other.  Forbidden Desert is a significant improvement.  First and foremost, it's a lot harder.  Sand builds up quickly, and it's important to keep on top of your water supply.  You also have to do quite a bit of excavating and exploration, which wasn't at all necessary in the Island version.  I love the idea of the storm moving around the board, and just when you think that you're lining yourself up for a straight shot at your objective, the storm can blow by and leave you buried under mountains of sand.  If you had the same reservations about Forbidden Island, don't hesitate to grab Desert.  It's a significant improvement in every sense of the word, and a worthy addition to any game collection.
text_fidelity_b: Gamewright Forbidden Desert – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Desert Board Game Multi-colored, 5"

text_fidelity_a:
Transformers Protectobot Action Figure (2-Pack) At first, I thought the age range on this toy was a bit too low. Then after my children gave these up and Dad got on the job, I realized quickly that the toys were just not that great.

Hot Spot is a fire truck with a really long crane on his hand that you're not supposed to be able to take off, making him awkward to pose as a robot. Once you get him into robot mode, which is no easy feat, you'll have a heck of a time getting him back into firetruck mode. Even once he's there, you can clearly see his robot hands on the top of the truck, and his legs (which form the bottom of the truck and include the back wheels), will consistently half-transform while trying to wheel him around on the ground.

All this and Hotspot is the better half of the duo. Blades, the helicopter, looks like an awkward chicken when transformed into robot mode, which is not helped by the fact that he appears to not have any hands or arms. The instructions for transforming him were incredibly difficult to decipher, as they have frequent close ups of pieces which I can't really find on my model and curvy arrows pointing at different spots. If a 31 year old with a master's degree can't figure him out, how do we expect a 6-year-old with limited patience to do it?
text_fidelity_b: Transformers Protectobot Action Figure (2-Pack)

While I would have loved (although not necessarily expected) some karate-chop action in the parent figures, or flamethrower accessories, this is a pretty cool looking fortress, no wait, I mean dollhouse, and my daughter loves it, even if she doesn't understand why GI Joe keeps trying to rappel up to the 4th floor balcony with his grappling hook. .

Seriously though, she really does love this dollhouse. I think it's pretty good for the price, as it's absolutely huge (close to 3 ft tall), but to be honest, I expected a lot more in terms of the "stuff" inside. There is some detail built into the walls, but hardly any furniture pieces that you can move around. There are some family members included, but only parents and baby, who appears to have just come from the hospital. It's a bit like a family just moving into their first apartment, where all they have is a moldy old sofa and some flowers on the wall.

Everything that she wants to play with is, of course, something I have to buy separately. That's a bit annoying, but typical I suppose, although someone with more experience in these sorts of girl-fortresses might know of a better alternative. Practically speaking, Cobra Commander and Skelator could just waltz right in the front door, as there are no missile launchers, so those must come in one of the accessory packs.

MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries Big & fast are the best ways to describe this RC racer!

At 1:10 scale, the unit ships with everything you need to run EXCEPT batteries for the RC transmitter. You will need to provide some AA batteries here. Also, make sure to charge your running batteries first.

Unfortunately, you will only get about 10-15 minutes of run time per charge. So having the 2 included battery packs is nice. Although, if you swap them out back-to-back, the one charging will not be ready to go before your second battery depletes. And charge time is roughly 4 hours EACH. So, you actually need A LOT of spare batteries if you want to run your car without any downtime.

Outside of this concern, the car is a lot like a hobby RC vehicle that you would assemble from scratch. But at a fraction of the cost. However, the parts are probably not hobby grade, but good enough for the intended audience of this vehicle.

In the mid-eighties, I was really into RC racing (A Tamiya Frog for those who remember), but even back then this was an expensive hobby (I was around 14, so everything was expensive!) as you always wanted to upgrade something - motor, servos, shocks, tires, etc... And I wasn't even running anywhere near top of the line stuff.

In contrast, this unit ships complete for right around $110.00. So, if you're just getting into the hobby (or re-entering), then this car will make a fun introduction/re-introduction without breaking the bank.

Lastly, this thing is FAST. It's rated right around 30-32MPH. That may seem slow when the only comparison you may have is driving in a car at that speed. However, seeing one of the RC cars rocket down the street at 30+ miles per hour will quickly alter your perspective!

Overall, this is a great out of the box setup that's a ton of fun for a kid, an adult or the kid in every adult!
text_fidelity_b: MESIXI 1/10 RC Car Scale High Speed Around 50kmh 2.4Ghz 4WD All Terrains Fast and Furious Hobby 4x4 Offroad Remote Control Truck for Adult and Boy Kid with Two Rechargeable Batteries

text_fidelity_a: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster The recon has always been a pretty good blaster.  Somewhat prone to jamming, and on the short side for range, but accurate as all get out, and good for modding.  Then enter the Retaliator!  This is not your typical Recon with a face lift!  The shell is still recon- but with a new name badge and the digital camo effect.  The GUTS are all new- direct plunger powerhouse.  This blaster will pop the elite darts out to 75 feet (angled shots) and will put darts out to 50 feet level shot.  The accuracy is still there too!  It will take the old Streamlines too(with a noticable loss of range and accuracy)  This blaster will jam- but if your careful to pull the cocking slide back fully (not just till it clicks, but fully back, usually a couple mm beyond the point of the trigger latch engagment) jams are minimal (we actully shot 50 or so shots without a jam!).  I'm not a huge fan of barrel and stock attachments, but these are pretty good on this blaster.  The barrel does reduce range (about 8 to 10 foot lose), but does increase accuracy (we use cardboard standups aprox 2" wide by 4" high and can hit them 8 out of 10 time without the barrel and 9 out of 10 with- at 25 feet).  The new 12 shot clip (mag) is very cool and makes a nice transition between the 6 shot (way to small) and the 18 (nice capacity- but kinda gets in the way).  My daughter uses this blaster to sniper me all the time.  All she needs to see is a foot or a hand sticking out from behind the couch and I'm toast!  All in all a worthy upgrade to the recon.  Great for a primary or secondary carry.  I did take 1 star off because nerf still hasn't made this jam proof- close, but not perfect.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Retaliator Blaster

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary) I bought 2 of these blasters for my daughter and I. We have Nerf battles in the house and She wanted a semi auto (to back up her Recon and Maverick) and I need a backup for the Hail Fire. This is a clip system balster with a fly wheel launcher (need 4 AA batteries). All in all I'm pretty pleased.
Good: This blaster does a lot of things well. It is a semi-auto (requires 4 AA batteries), but does not feel heavy or unbalanced. Easy to shoot 1 handed and can be double wielded. Clip system is nice as we have a lot of extra clips so reloads are fast. The clip release button has a good positive feel and has not accidentally relesed a clip yet. The blaster has a top and bottom tactical rail and will accecpt a stock and barrel extention (although why you would want to do this is questionable as it takes away the intent of this compact blaster). Handgrip is comfortable but may be to small for XL hands. Accel. button has a good feel to it. There are 2 place for sling attachment and both spots are logical! Battery door is a sigle screw affair. Accuracy is better than expected (I can hit a human size target 5 out of 6 times at a 30 foot range). Battery life has been good and Rechargables offer no problems.
Bad: This blaster has more safety switches than a modern Table Saw! There is the jam door switch, the clip sensor switch, dart sensor switch, voltage switch (regulator), accel trigger switch, and probably others that I haven't come across yet. The main trouble maker is the dart sensor switch. It works great until the last dart in the clip. Sometimes the dart pressure is not enough to press the switch arm so the blaster won't fire the last dart (VERY ANNOYING!) The easiest NONE WARRENTY VOIDING fix is to open the jam door, take a thin (about 1/8" wide) piece of duct tape (about 2 inches long) and tape the switch to the top of the reciever. I taped it up and around the body and out the top of the jam door. After aprox 100 shots the tape is still holding and I have yet to have a dart left in the clip. The gun is also prone to jamming if you pull the trigger slowly. When firing off a dart you need to make sure to pull the trigger crisply. This only seems to be a problem on the first shot (probably because I usually empty the clip after that first shot). Another problem I've seen is the dislike this blaster has for non-elite darts. If your first dart in the clip is a streamline version you can almost be assured a jam (funny that it only happens if the non-elite is in the first position on the clip- load it farther down and it fires like any other dart). Honestly if your gonna use this for any formal matches stick to the Elite darts. Range is about 35 to 40 feet- hard to get any further.
Final thoughts: This is truely a fun blaster. It does have a few kinks to it, but nothing that a little duct tape can't fix. It is compact enough to carry as a secondary blaster, but combined with additional clip options (I'm thinking an 18 with a couple six back-ups) this could be a close quarters primary blaster. At the current $20 this is really a no brainer.
text_fidelity_b: Nerf N-Strike Elite Stryfe Blaster (Colors May Vary)

text_fidelity_a:
Evviva Ant Habitat W/LED Light. Enjoy A Magnificent Habitat. Great for Kids & Adults. Evviva Ant Ecosystem W/Enhanced Blue Gel. Educational & Learning Science Kit. Live Ants Not Included This ant farm was a fascinating gift for everyone, not just the 6 year old who got it. We ordered the ants from AntsAlive .com and when they arrived they quickly scurried about, digging their first hole within a few hours. Before you add the ants, you must poke 3 to 4 holes in the gel to help the ants get started. I’m wondering if the negative reviews forgot this step, leaving the ants confused in the farm on where they could go.

I highly recommend refrigerating the ants for 10 minutes before you add them to the farm so they don’t immediately escape. I also highly recommend putting them in on the side nearest the white air hole plug. Inevitably a few ants will have died in shipment and it’s much easier to remove them through the hole then removing the entire lid (as others will try to escape).

Why this ant farm is better than others?
1) The ants food and water supply is in the gel. Other ant farms require food and water be added for the ants; adding too much can create mold or too little and the ants are hungry. It’s challenging to calculate and extra work.

2) The glass is fairly narrow front to back so it’s likely the ants (as they did for us) will dig right to the class so you can see them clearly while they work under ground.

3) The light and magnifying glass make it very easy to see every ant at work.

4) The farm is reusable. You can clean out the old gel and ants and buy new ants and gel for a second use.

I highly recommend this gift for any child aged 4-10. Certainly older children and adults will enjoy it too.

*The attached photos are of the ant farm on day 3.

We kept them in the house for about three days to strengthen their wings and enjoy looking at them, then we took them to school and released them near a creek during recess. Even the older kids joined us. It took about ten minutes for all six to leave the "garden" container thing; the last one even landed on my daughter's hand and stuck around for a few minutes there before flying off. Definitely a great experience and one we will likely repeat (you can order more caterpillars from the website and re-use the "garden," or you can catch your own caterpillars and be surprised by what they turn out to be!).

Slogging through the setup and directions the first time takes about an hour, so expect to take a bit of time to really understand how to play before you actually get to the game itself. It's extremely high quality, as well; the board and parts are beautifully designed and I don't worry at all about anything breaking or falling apart easily. text_fidelity_a: ColorKu by Mad Cave Bird Games My mother-in-law bought this for my brother-in-law for his birthday in June and gave it to him at a family reunion. It was probably one of the most popular indoor activities during those four days! Everyone wanted to play. I bought it for our family for Christmas and will never regret it. Even my 6-year-old loves figuring out where the colors go--it's an educational experience that's also really fun! This game is high quality, made with solid wood and pieces that won't chip or flake easily. It's actually quite beautiful and will last a long time. Definitely good value for the money and you'll get your money's worth out of this game, that's for sure--it's not just a one-person game; the whole family can play at the same time, working together to solve the puzzle. If you get tired of the large deck of starter set-ups that comes with it, you can buy expansion packs with additional starter cards. The only negative thing I have to say about this game (besides that I hate putting it away because I love playing it so much) is that the box was not designed as well as it could have been to hold the board, the marbles, and the starter cards. But it still all fits and it's not a big problem, just a little disappointing and surprising that a game of this quality wouldn't have a box that contained all the pieces in a more logical, efficient fashion. You definitely won't regret buying this--promise!

One thing I noticed right from the start is that they sound like baby rattles—you can really hear the magnets moving around inside as you move them. Melissa & Doug Double-Sided Magnetic Tabletop Art Easel - Dry-Erase Board and Chalkboard We were the unfortunate recipients of this activity set given to us from a family member for a gift. We already have one of those classic standing plastic easels which we love, so this tabletop one is more of a nuisance for us. Trying to be open-minded about making it work since it was gift, I starting exploring it and realized how highly dysfunctional it is. The swinging base bar moves to each side of the board to stand it up, meaning each time you want to use the magnets, you have to swing the bar to the one side and prop it up, and then do that again with the opposite side to use the chalk. This takes some finesse that younger kids will not be able to do very easily on their own. It’s also top-heavy with the paper roll on top, so I took the paper off completely.

Why is a marker included for such young children? No, Melissa & Doug…just NO. I get it for older kids, but not for the starting age of 3. The chalk board side doesn’t have any magnetic capabilities, and also doesn’t have a little tray or spot to keep the chalk organized…did parents not have any input in designing this? Yes, there is a tray on the magnetic side to keep the letters and numbers, but not on the chalk side. The fold-down tray also doesn't have a lid, so good luck keeping your letters and numbers organized in one spot when you want to use the chalk side. Nobody thought it would be a good idea to have a spot for the chalk? Or nobody thought it would be a good idea to magnetize both sides to let a child use the chalk and add some letters or numbers to the same side of the board?? Who approved this?

The magnetic side works fine, but I didn’t even bother to do an inventory of all the letters and numbers before I vetoed this thing and gave up trying to make it work in my child’s room. I honestly don’t have a good spot to even keep it anywhere in my house, and if my kid wants to doodle, we’re heading over to our standing easel (designed with two large trays to keep our chalk and crayons organized). I wish I had a gift receipt. DO NOT BUY THIS!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Double-Sided Magnetic Tabletop Art Easel - Dry-Erase Board and Chalkboard

Since the pen is quite large, my kiddo will often choose the right answer, put the pen down on the dot, but miss the dot slightly which then gives us a red light and a “sad” beep. Even though the answer is right, missing the dot makes you think that you’re wrong because you get the red light and sad sound. I then have to say “try that dot again” and reassure that the answer is correct. I do wish the dots were just a little bit larger to give the pen a broader area to make contact with the dot. It's not a major issue, as most of the time we do hit the dot just fine, but it's also something I've noticed that has happened several times.

Otherwise, these books are awesome, very educational and a lot of fun! More of 4.5 Stars for us.

Educational Insights Design & Drill Bolt Buddies Recycling Truck Toy, Take Apart Toy with Electric Drill Toy, STEM Toy, Gift for Boys & Girls, Ages 3+ The quality is great, and the concept is very creative. We play with this everyday, and think it’s fun, but there’s some thoughts I want to share:

-The clear bolts are somewhat difficult to find on the carpet. I wish the ends (tips) were colored to help make them stand out since they blend into the floor and surfaces.

-The drill bit is always falling out, and it’s also clear, so it can be hard to find it when it falls, and it’s cumbersome to have to keep putting it back in the drill repeatedly.

-The drill has two directions to tighten and loosen the bolts, which is adjusted with the sliding control. The drill itself works very well at tightening and loosening, but it gets a little involved helping my child make adjustments on the drill. My child wants to tighten and loosen a single bolt at a time before moving onto the next bolt, so we’re constantly flip-flopping the controls. Maybe slightly older preschoolers would be more independent using the drill, but I think a manual tool (like a screwdriver) would be the easiest to operate.

Our favorite part of this whole set is dropping all of the bolts in the back of the truck and then opening the hatch to watch all of them tumble out. My child thinks this is hilarious and is by far the best part!

In short, I think this whole set is a great concept, but is slightly overcomplicated. I really feel a simple screwdriver would help simplify the need to shift around buttons constantly, and would even help with dexterity and motor skills more than the cumbersome drill.

I think all of the pieces have a genuine purpose in this set, and the features function nicely, but I do feel the cookie design is a missed opportunity. It would have been very creative for one side of each cookie to represent the unbaked cookie, and the opposite side could have been decorated with a fun icing color or sprinkles, just to add a pop of color and give a start-to-finish concept (maybe a future craft project for us). Otherwise, this is a well-made, quality toy that will be enjoyed for a long time.

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack OK...so here's the deal with these...
5 stars for how much my 17mo old son LOVES them.
3 stars for how the crayon is constantly coming out of the plastic holder.
Averages to...4 stars.
No one is really addressing a few things, so I will...
these are super bright, amazing, soft crayons that are each a very distinct & different color.
In our particular tub, they color perfectly...but we have a somewhat "satin" finish as opposed to the shiny white finish which is what I imagine is the problem for people who say they don't work. I notice they color fantastically on dry or "damp" tub surfaces...but not as well on truly wet, slick surfaces.
We have a clear silicone table mat with a scene silkscreened on that I sometimes wet the back of and slap on the tub wall so he can color away on it like a coloring book page. Again, the crayons work perfectly when the surface is dry or damp, but can't get grippy enough for the color to stick when it's slick wet.

These crayons do constantly come out of the holders but I just keep pushing them back in. They also push back into the holder because the button is where my son grips the crayons in his tiny hands but when that happens he just moves on to another one, since there are 5.

I put these in to a bag of goodies I gave him for Valentine's Day and ours are still going strong with daily...prolific...color & scribble use on the tub, his tub toys, his picture mat, himself, and Mommy....head to toe. He does lots of "body art" with these, and he enjoys using his scrubby sponge for clean up and erasing his handywork, as much as he does the coloring part!

To me...these babies are worth their weight in gold if you have a budding artist on your hands, the right kind of tub surface, and teach the little virtuoso how to scrub it all clean to start with a fresh canvas! We LOVE...and I mean...LOVE them, and I can't see us ever being without them as my son is pretty much obsessed with all things artistic, and where he is allowed to just cut loose & get messy. These are perfect!

P.S. if you are concerned that teaching them to color on surfaces is a bad or confusing message, which makes perfect sense...I'd say that this is the way to let them be creative & have a blast but teach them that coloring on wall is only for the bathtub and only with these crayons....a concept they will need to learn.

I would recommend getting your first set somewhere that you can return them if they don't work on your tub. Also, get a matte finish silicone baking mat, or matte silicone placemat...wet the back, stick to wall & let them color on that. It works great for us!
text_fidelity_b: Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack

Rockin' Rider Charger 2-in-1 Pony Ride-On , Beige My son absolutely loves this. In fact, in the month + that we have had it, this has easily become his favorite toy. My son is 21 months old and average height for his age. He fits on this perfectly but even after he outgrows it, he will still love it- Half the time he prefers to push it around rather than ride it!

The recording for the music is definitely grainy, as many other reviewers have noted. I don't mind this and neither does my son but if that will be a deal-breaker for you, it's better that you know now. If you squeeze one ear, the horse sings and the mouth moves. If you squeeze the other ear, a random saying will come out. My son loves pressing the ears and then hurries to kneel down and watch the horse's mouth move. He loves hugging this little guy and when he prefers to rock on it, he will bring me the base so I can put it back on- which takes a whole 2 seconds; you just set it down on top of the rocker base, pull the plastic piece over the front bar and close until it clicks. Voila! To make it a rideable toy again, you simply push the button and the plastic piece pops open to release the horse.

I definitely recommend this little horse for 1 year olds and up. At almost 2 years old, my son has a while to go before he won't fit on this anymore. This was definitely a good buy and worth every penny!
text_fidelity_b: Rockin' Rider Charger 2-in-1 Pony Ride-On , Beige

text_fidelity_a:
FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive) I had high hopes for this little pooping doggo.. I purchased as a Christmas gift for my daughter (3 years old), who was obsessed with walking our dog and watching him pop (she’s a weirdo). Overall, she has gotten a fair amount of play and enjoyment out of the little fella, so I would *probably* purchase again.

Pros: He makes cute little doggy noises, he’s has soft fur.

Cons: He was much smaller than I expected (but my fault, as size is objective). He was overall much harder than I expected (other than his thin layer of fuzzy fur coat, he’s completely hard to the squeeze). He has wheels (which for some reason I thought he was more automatic than that). The leash is short (it was the perfect size for my tiny 3 year old when we bought it, but our 4 year old friend had to bend over to push it around). The treats / poo pellets are incredibly small. We lost a couple on christmas when we opened the gift.. and then a few more since. We have less than half left now (which I think is an accomplishment since we’ve had it almost a year!).

My toddler and her friends have enjoyed playing with it, but they have 1) been hurt by his hard material build (just minor boo boo, but still) 2) tried to eat the teeny pellet foods (cause, why not?) and 3) shoved other objects in its mouth that they weren’t supposed to. The design concept isn’t bad, but I do wish it was slightly bigger, with slightly bigger treats, a slightly longer leash, slightly more “squeezable”... you catch my drift. And with all that in mind, I probably would have gone with a different puppers.
text_fidelity_b: FurReal Friends Pax My Poopin Pup Plush Toy (Amazon Exclusive)

The problem is that the headband covers are folded in the package, and the crease never really comes out, so it doesn't slide onto the headband well. text_fidelity_a:
Giant Delta Kite 6 x 7.5 ft Easy Flyer with String and Handle, Classic Delta Kite, Brilliant Colors in The Sky What a great kite. This thing took off easy, flew all day and looked great. I had read some of the reviews about the tails tattering in the wind so I took a proactive approach. As soon as I received it I opened it and inspected.... all looked good. The other reviewers suggested putting tape on the ends of the tails...I got a bottle of good old fashioned Elmers white glue and rubbed it on both sides of the end of the tails..about 2 or 3 inches up and let it dry. Well got to the beach and let her go....after a full day sun and fun, I reeled it in and zero tattering on the ends, however there was some unraveling in random spot on the rest of the tails...so maybe next time I will apply the glue up each side.
I would like to add that as far as the string goes, I went to the local wally store and in the fishing section I found about 300 feet of bright yellow nylon cord (used for catfish) about 2 bucks and a reel right next to it for about 2 bucks, Made the task of reeling it in much easier than the supplied equipment....buy it...you will have a good time.
text_fidelity_b: Giant Delta Kite 6 x 7.5 ft Easy Flyer with String and Handle, Classic Delta Kite, Brilliant Colors in The Sky

text_fidelity_a: Buffalo Games - Cinque Terre - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle This is a really well made puzzle. The artwork is great and the quality is exceptional. BUT, it is the most evil puzzle I have ever tried. Many of the mono-color pieces are interchangeable. The computer that designed the cuts might be able to tell the difference but I couldn't. There are (at least) 3 different ways to build the top row that  all seem correct. But then you move on to the second row, which is also mono-color(ish) and suffers from the same issue. So you find out that the top row is all wrong based on how the second row doesn't fit. So then you move onto the 3rd row - where the patterned pieces start AND THAT DOESN"T FIT WITH THE TOP TWO ROWS. So you end up rebuilding the second row based on the third row and the top row based on the now-reconstructed second row. It was maddening. Really, make it tough but only one solution please. Otherwise a very enjoyable puzzle and I'd definitely buy this brand again,
text_fidelity_b: Buffalo Games - Cinque Terre - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle

The issues with this set is the overuse of the gold "prong" connecting pieces in the shell of the technodrome. You have to push them all of the way in, otherwise the shells will not close correctly.... But if you do, you will break at least a few of those gold "prongs". The core structure of the technodrome also appears slimsy, with me having to press down on the sections 1&2 multiple times while connecting the shell pieces and sections 3&4.

This is definitely not for kids, it will confuse and frustrate them. For adults, it is challenging but not in the enjoyable sense.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Krypt Gold 631 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 15152 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly This was my first puzzle of this brand. While the pieces did fit together well, I noticed several pieces that out of the box had pegs that were bent, or paper lifting. While it didnt interfere with the puzzle assembly it just made the completed puzzle look ragged.

I suggest labeling the puzzle map to orient a "top" or "bottom" as during assembly you may accidently turn your map upside down.

Organizing the pieces is what I found most helpful by size, shape, and if has a curve/turn or not. Then when you reach a portion of the puzzle that you need, you can brute force from your pile.

Several pieces are very unique, and thus can serve as anchors to build off of.

The hardest part is the border, something I usually do first, as the pieces do not interlock on the edges, you have to do another layer in in order to interlock the edge pieces. Once I put the pieces in piles of similar size/shape, the puzzle assembly speed went much faster.

Took me about 20-25 hours total.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Krypt Gold 631 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 15152 - Every Piece is Unique, Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

text_fidelity_a:
Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones! At first I put this in the kitchen, I quickly learned that it was too loud for an open floor plan, it made me listen to tv on too high of a volume, so when I switched to the 2nd grit I moved it to a spare bedroom. This worked out great since I go in that room almost daily I was able to keep up with knowing when to change out to the next grit.

This is super easy to set up and get started. It comes with absolutely everything needed to go from start to finish including jewelry items to use so you can show off your stones. The instructions are very easy to follow along too.It also comes with activity books and the jewelry pieces are a necklace, a ring, a keychain and ear rings.

The instructions gives you an idea of how long the stones should tumble in each grit and at what speed.
This is what I did..
-grit #1..I did for 3 days on #3 speed
-grit#2.. I started at 5 days on #2…then opened it up and decided it needed a few more days since they were a bit rough so I did 2
more days on #3 setting
-grit#3.. I did for 7 days on #1 setting.
-grit#4..I did 7 days on #1. The smaller stones were great , the larger stones had a few blemishes yet, but I like things when they
aren’t perfect so they were great for me…I will be making them into necklaces once I put holes in them.

As you can see from my pictures from start to finish how much the rocks changed. Then at the end I wiped them off with mineral oil as suggested in the instructions. This has been an amazing experience to watch the rough rocks transform into smooth beautiful stones.
text_fidelity_b: Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones!

text_fidelity_a: Backyard Discovery Sweetwater All Cedar White Modern Outdoor Wooden Playhouse, Cottage, Sink, Stove, Windows, Kitchen with Pot and Pans and Utensils, Flowerpot Holders, Working Doorbell, Ages 2-6 We've had this playhouse for a couple of months and it still looks brand new - despite the Iowa sun, our extreme heat and rain and freezes.  When we opened up the package, we had a couple of issues with the wood being cracked.  The overall setup is fairly easy if you follow the directions.  Customer service was really great working with when I called to get replacement parts.  To be clear, though, I wasn't aware that we'd have to seal the playhouse.  I only found that out because I'd called for replacement parts.  We used a marine sealant and it is full waterproofing!  We used a chemical pump sprayer to apply it (we sprayed it on and then brushed over it - it is very runny like milk and goes on white but dries clear).  I, originally, expected the wood to be pre-sealed since it was a playhouse specifically for outside.  So, in hindsight, I am very grateful that we talked with the helpful customer service person.  Otherwise, we'd probably have to be replacing the house next year ... and, I wouldn't have been very happy with the purchase.  However, we've had it a couple months now and it still looks brand new!  I'd highly recommend this playhouse IF you are willing to seal it.  Yes, marine clear coat is expensive but so was the playhouse.  All in all, a great addition to our backyard and I'm sure we'll get several years of grandchildren's fun with it!
text_fidelity_b: Backyard Discovery Sweetwater All Cedar White Modern Outdoor Wooden Playhouse, Cottage, Sink, Stove, Windows, Kitchen with Pot and Pans and Utensils, Flowerpot Holders, Working Doorbell, Ages 2-6

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA X1 4 Channel 2.4G RC Quad Copter, Spacecraft (As Shown) So, this is the second one of these that I've ordered; the first was for my nephew. After flying it a bit with him, I decided to give it a try on my own. This is probably the best quadcopter value out there, though I do say this based on other reviews and not my own experience with multiple makes and models. For about $40, you get a very capable quad-copter that you can fly left/right, forward/reverse, up/down, as well as rotate it 360 to keep the "front" of the copter oriented properly, so you're not pushing the controller left and having the unit bank right. It also has a "eversion" mode that basically flips the copter 360 degrees in a loop automatically. This function works left/right and forward/backward, and is very cool,primarily because it's so easy to execute the maneuver.

The unit has a Low and High setting, which trims the controls a bit on the Low setting, and makes for a very good indoor mode while the High setting is best for outdoors and stunt moves. There are trim controls for the throttle, rotation, left/right and forward/back. I've found that the trim does work, and is best adjusted when the copter is outside and has some height off the ground...essentially, you try to hover it and see how best to adjust the controls. Ideally, if you let off the controls, the unit should hover fairly well. The system has no "auto" hover mode that'll auto-adjust the trims to hover, so getting it dialed in is still a manual affair. The controls work well, and I've flown this for maybe an hours indoors and 30 minutes outside, and feel as if I have good control of the thing.

I've found this to be a very sturdy unit, having crashed it numerous times in just about every orientation. It does come with a set of spare rotors, which is nice, however even after using this in a parking lot, I've not yet broken anything. The body of the unit, which offers some protection to the electronics (which then have another plastic dome atop them), comes in several types...bumble bee, UFO, spaceship, etc. Ideally, you might be able to fly w/o it, shaving off some weight and possibly some air resistance, though the fairing does offer some protection and probably shouldn't be removed until you're past the beginner stages.

The battery lasts 8-10 minutes, depending upon how you're flying it. I've found they last more outdoors, probably because you're not making so many direction adjustments. You can get extra batteries and chargers, and I'd recommend it, as 10 minutes isn't enough...you're going to want more. The batteries charge off a USB cable, whether plugged into a computer or using a USB/wall adapter. Charge time is about an hour, give or take.

The directions are just OK, and you'll have to experiment to really get a feel for things. The most important thing to remember is when starting off, you want to try and be on as level a surface as possible, as each time you insert the battery, the thing will auto-level and find it's artificial horizon. If you start off on a slope, you may find the unit won't fly very well, or you'll need to make significant trim adjustments.

The process to start the unit is as follows:

1. Ensure battery for the copter is out, and the remote is off.
2. Insert the battery and immediately place the copter on a flat surface. You should see the slow blinking LED under the fairing
3. Turn the remote on.
4. Move the throttle/rotate lever (on the left of the remote) up once (you'll hear a beep) and then down once (you'll hear a beep).
5. The copter LED should then stop blinking and remain steady RED. You're ready to go...
6. If the copter doesn't start, turn the remote off, then on, and repeat the process w/ the throttle (you shouldn't need to remove the battery). I find I need to do this process twice each time the batter is replaced.

If you crash the copter, you just need to right it, and start flying again...it will automatically reset, and there's nothing you need to do with the remote or unit to get things going again. The only exception to this is if the batter flies out when the crash occurs...then start from step 1 above.

The two things I'd probably change about this unit are to have some LED lights that show the "front" of the copter; as it is, the rotors are white in the front and black in the back...this does help. Secondly, the batter insert/removal is somewhat clunky, but it does work. I'd like to see something a little easier to work with, as getting the batter in and out can be a little difficult sometimes.

Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up I have been enjoying this as a solo game but am happy that it won't be hard to teach friends.

Unlike some games there isn't a finite number of turns...the game ends when someone defeats the boss then each players points are tallied. I like that aspect a lot.

There are some "power" type blocks that benefit all players when one player has success with it.

The art is very cool and whimsical. The paper is sufficient but not very heavy duty. You get plenty of maps...there are 4 of each distinct map design. It's a busy map and I plan on taking the cheapest route possible and using regular sheet protectors and dry erase markers.

I'm not liking the wooden dice at all. For the money I would have really liked some fancier dice. Maybe bigger...maybe more colorful.
You get 4 short presharpened pencils that ...don't have erasers and your first game or two you might need to correct something.

Basically this could have been a print and play. There's nothing at all spectacular about the contents.

My personal little gripe is I don't see how you can be in two places at once. You can attack the map from different sides of the map moving in from starter sections.

That's seems like a lot of negativity but it is a fun little game anyway. You can play it on a small table or most places since there aren't components other than a map and the dice. Also this can encourage people to play who maybe aren't that into games since you don't unload tons of intimidating cards, counters and pieces.

It's a very fine experience. It could've been better for the money though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Dungeons, Dice & Danger – an Easy to Learn Roll and Write Strategy Game for Ages 12 and Up

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448) So....I'm Gen X and we played the original version some in college along with games like Risk and Stratego on weekends. It isnt quite a fluff game but it isnt very hard. I would think both children and adults would enjoy this game. A game adults can enjoy with their kids....or a fun starter game or game for chatting and having a beverage or three.

The best part is there is hardly any explanation needed to get started. Move tiles to open a path to get to the objects on your cards. And....block others from their goals. I love this game especially with 3 or 4 people instead of two. It requires some strategy but luck can make or break it, too.

Harry Potter version! Yes! Well...it is beautiful. The board looks wonderful! But in this version you are gathering "people" or characters rather than treasure items. The premise makes sense. Going through the maze that is Hogwarts gathering people ....you must match cards in your hands to pics on the tiles of the gameboard. Sounds AWESOME. In reality...it is kind of messy because some people look similar. Some people are the big characters...such as Harry or Snape....there were 3 I was like....who on earth is THIS and I thought I was a big fan. So....due to the pics on the game board being rather small....they are also color coded too. If your card is Harry with a blue border....Harry has a blue border on the game tile as well. But is there another character who looks very similar on the board with a blue border? Yes there is. So....yeah, it is really cool BUT pay good attention as the character pictures certainly are NOT as easy to discern as a scarab or diamond in the original. Hey...but it looks great!

I give this game 10 out of 10 because my gripes do not effect the game. If you are are a HP fan....and you already like or think you might like a labyrinth game...here ya go. This is 100% Ravensburg quality. The box is good quality as all the pieces. The box holds everything in the usual labyrinth organized way. Very nice.

At the price point....I really, really, really dont like wooden pegs. They are sort of big, bright and easy to move but I liked the Labyrinth version with the plastic characters NOT the one with wooden pegs. I have no idea WHY if your player piece coincides with a house....such as Slytherin....they didnt atleast make little plastic coats of armor for each house. I just hate generic pegs in fun games. But it doesnt make the game any better or worse. I saw some reviews where people complained about the card quality. It is the same it always has been. The cards are simply there to identify your next goal. This game doesnt require shuffling like Uno or slapping...or grabbing or swapping cards. They are perfectly fine.

Great game. Great Ravensburger quality. Dear Ravensburger.....I sure would love a Scooby Doo version with cool plastic player pieces!

I included pics and pics of game pieces from an earlier version of the original game
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Labyrinth Family Board Game for Kids and Adults Age 7 and Up - Millions Sold, Easy to Learn and Play with Great Replay Value (26448)

text_fidelity_a:
Arizona GameCo Smack it! Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.

Astronaut and Space Toy Action Figure Playset- 60 Piece set includes Astronauts, Rockets, Spaceship Shuttle, Rovers, Satellites and More - Great for imaginative play, school projects and dioramas Description states 50 astronauts. I have 43. And it totals 60 pieces with all the other parts. The lunar rovers are awesome and there are two seated figures to drive them.

This is a total mashup of different time periods of space exploration. Apollo-ish type rockets minus the needles. 2 great fairly accurate moon landing rovers, some type of sky lab, 2 nice space shuttles, 1 cool lunar lander and 2 American flags with stands. 2 flags makes no sense to me but ok. The moon walking men might be in Gemini style suits....no women wore those or walked around on the moon then. There isnt anything really historically accurate here as a whole but it really is a fun collection of space stuff.

There are 10 different poses for the figures I got with mulitples of each. All the figures look great, no flashing or deformities. I am sure they are copies of old figures. Giger counter guy, camera guy, radio, briefcase and more.

Sleeping Queens 10th Anniversary Tin Card Game Excellent easy game for friends or family. Any age I think as long as they can grasp the general rules because there's no reading that is vital to gameplay. Small number adding is required but other players can help with that.

It's an especially good game to make people who don't like games play. Lol. It isn't too much more complicated than Uno....so you can teach it to non gamers quickly and because it isn't so bogged down with tons of rules, pieces and things to remember....people enjoy it and want to play it again. The goal is to gather queens by waking them with kings and adding their point values. Either 50 points or 5 Queens whichever someone achieves first. Of course there's more to it but this is just my review of what we think of it. Its quick...so you'll play it in rounds...we play first to win 5. This version has extra queens and they do take up a fair amount of space spread out on the table so your play area can't be quite as small as some other card games. That's fine though. You can put the queens in a stack and a player can fan them and hold them out to the player choosing each time if that helps with table space.

The quality of the cards is very good. Art work is great! This version in the tin comes with 2 sheets of little stickers of some characters and items. The tin itself is decent quality although mine did arrive with a dent. Not gonna complain...I think it will get more dings and dents because this game is gonna travel and boxes just protect contents imo.

We did discuss it's a little sexist in this house hold's opinion. The premise of kings waking the queens and of course they are sort of gender rigid....a Queen of Books is very good though. All Queens wear dresses and all characters appear as fairy tale people. Whimsical. There's variety among the queens and kings though and we love the Turtle King. None of us felt it was overtly sexist. Would a Sleeping Kings version even it out? We would play that too. Hey Gamewright.....go on and make Sleeping Kings! Snoring Kings?? Is that sexist?

There's magic! Potions and wands so that's great. Knights and a dragon!
text_fidelity_b: Sleeping Queens 10th Anniversary Tin Card Game

Hot Wheels Race Crate with 3 Stunts in 1 Set Portable Storage Ages 6 to 10 Adult review: it's fast. So fast it's over before it starts. I was most interested in the 4 lane gravity drop and it works perfectly. People complaining cars won't loop may not be trying different cars. After picking different cars a few times I have several that loop correctly. The two that came with it also loop correctly. Some of the longer cars don't seem to make it.

This is one of the neatest designs I've ever seen from Hot Wheels. If you wanted the 6 lane kit that's over 200 dollars from scalpers now...this is a pretty great one to settle for. My only complaints on the gravity drop are it's so fast it's really hard to watch and if you're at the starting end...the large solid loop prevents you from seeing the cars until the hit the finish line. If the loop were clear that would be awesome. I also added some old '68 track and will add more....the cars clear the finish with lots of go power left. Add more track :)

I ended up liking the drag race configuration best with added track.

I believe it is sturdy and it's a pretty big track in any configuration. The fact it all folds into itself for storage is the truly awesome part. Room for several cars in there as well.

Good product for young and old Hot Wheels fans and I wish it had been cheaper but feel I got my money's worth. If kids don't lose any of the few loose pieces....I would imagine it will hold value.

Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary Ok. Here's the deal. If you actually order and receive the Elefun version produced with/through Hasbro as the current item listed as of this date shows, here's the real review by an adult:

There are 10 monkeys in a barrel. It is listed on the plastic, throw away wrapping. And that's what you get from this brand. 10. Each barrel has ten color corresponding monkeys.
About the monkeys: they are durable and not flimsy. The monkey's tails are part of the body and are not useable. All monkeys are the same mold.....BUT there are 2 each of different facial expressions. This is not so easy to notice while playing but yes, the monkeys are in facial pairs. All monkeys are the same size.

Now.....lol....from a serious player (lol) that grew up with the 60s, 70s versions: these monkeys have....two arms....one arm is bent closer to the head so it's open loop is a tad smaller. Meaning....it makes a differnece in how easy or hard it is to link them. Also....the hand shape....well....it isn't as pointed and hook like as it was years ago. So yes....it is harder and I think that's a reason there is only 10 now.

Is it fun? Yes. Worth the money?? To me....because a fast food meal costs this much. And replayablity is very high. Also....you can buy two and do color challenges. Or time two players....or lots of creativity to play.

I would rather have a reproduction of the original. BUT these are functional and in my honest review, more difficult to chain over 7; making for more competition.

I think this is a good product for children, teens, families and elderly.

**I also think this could help anyone with motor skill issues or be good for even Alzheimer persons who enjoy things simple and close up.

This is a good product.
text_fidelity_b: Elefun and Friends Barrel of Monkeys Game - Colors May Vary

KLUTZ Make Your Own Mini Erasers Toy includes (8)colors of eraser clay^pencil^clay shaping tool^(2)sheets of papercraft displays I had some low expectations after reading some of the reviews that people posted about this craft kit. Still the price was reasonable so I ordered one. This is not the first Klutz craft kit we've played with - so it was a familiar experience as those other kits. There really wasn't much in the box - the clay, a pencil (without an eraser), a sculpting tool, and a couple sheets of foldable paper props for the erasers you make (if you make the ones shown in the instructional guide).

You get plenty of different color clay - if you limit yourself to making fairly small erasers. The clay we got wasn't dried out - but it did take some kneeding to get soft enough to shape. Baking the erasers was simple - we used a toaster oven. Just be sure to use the right temperature and watch the erasers while they bake to make sure none start melting. Baking time can vary - mostly 15 to 30 minutes depending on the size & shape of the erasers you made.

The erasers are more ornamental than practical - but they do erase most pencil marks.

My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV I like this game console, but really just think it's something that a few people will enjoy more than most. The design of the console is really good, the look of the main unit is very well done. The wireless controllers are decent enough and feel well made. It's the games though that count. The games are a bit underwhelming. There is a good variety of games, from card games (solitaire, go fish, and a few others of that kind) to puzzle games (sudoku, sliding block puzzle, a pattern block puzzle). There are also many arcade style games. This model of the console does not have any of the old Data East arcade games on it. There is another version that does. The front of the box for that one will have graphics showing the Data East games.

I was sort of expecting the games on this to be the same as what is on most of these sort of consoles (famiclone games), but instead these are a bit more generic than even those. Some of the games are difficult to figure out, it took me about 10-15 minutes or experimenting to figure out how the controllers worked with the sudoku game, and even after I did - the controls were so awkward it made playing the game nearly impossible (and given that this game is timed, I never could achieve a decent time in solving the puzzle). Still, there are many that are worth playing. I think one of the reasons I like game systems like this is the challenge of figuring out what makes the game work.

The main game unit take four double A batteries and the wireless units take triple-A batteries (three each). The console hooks to the TV via a composite video cable (yellow RCA plug) and has one audio input (another RCA plug). I'm using the front inputs on my old VCR which is still connected to my television. I like that the controllers are wireless. You don't really need both, many of the games are for single player. The controllers are marked (P1 & P2), as the P1 controller is the main one and it is used to select the games from the menu.

All-in-all, I am enjoying most of these games, and appreciate the game system for what it is - but I would imagine that many people might not.

This system is made by My Arcade Gaming, and I have one of their handheld Go Gamer Portable games which I purchased last year around Christmas time. I was sort of hoping that this new game console would have the same set of games on it that their handheld model has (which are really good by the way), but that wasn't the case.
text_fidelity_b: My Arcade GameStation Wireless - Plug and Play Game Console - 2 Wireless Controllers - 300 Retro Style Games - Battery or USB Powered - Plugs Into TV

text_fidelity_a: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32" Purchased one of these without exactly knowing what I was buying. Sure, I knew it made noise - but didn't know how it did that or what it might sound like ( guess I could have looked on YouTube, but I didn't). Anyway, now that I've got one it's all everyone wants to play with. Basically it's a short tube with a thin piece of taut plastic covering one end (think tiny drum head), and a long loose spring mounted to the center of the plastic. Holding the tube and shaking it causes the spring to vibrate like springs do, those vibrations travel up to the drum head and the sound reverberates into the tube and is amplified out the other end. Makes for some pretty interesting sound effects. Overall I'm more than happy with my purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Remo SP-0207-TD Spring Drum Thunder Tube - Tie Dye, 2.32"
