The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game This game is played a bit different than the regular Monopoly games. There are some similarities though. You get four tokens (and passports), so that seems to limit the number of people who can play. The object of the game is to collect passport stamps - the person to fill their passport first wins. The game starts off with all the major stamps placed on the board - a specific sized one for each property. There are some generic gray stamps that stay in the bank. Landing on a spot you have the option to buy that stamp or it can get auctioned off. When a player lands on a spot that you have the stamp for - the owner is paid a 'Visitor Fee' (basically like rent in the regular game). Another difference are the Here & Now cards and the Chance cards. I think these are what makes the game fun to play. The things the cards can let you do makes the game challenging - just when you think you're going to get ahead, another player can use one of their cards and put a damper on your play. Makes for some lively social interactions (if you get my drift). The dice is a bit different - one die has a icon in the place of the 1 pip (sort of reminds me of the speed die). That icon is the 'Sneaky Swap', it can also still be the 1 in some rolls.

Overall I have to say I've enjoyed trying out this new game (can't say the same for everybody here). I think we're still getting use to the way the game plays compared to regular Monopoly. The games tend to be a bit short - about an hour, but that might be because we still stop a bit and look at the rules to figure out what we're doing. Plus, given the different international locations on the board, we sometimes stop and an go look up where something is. (Helps to keep a globe handy). Fun game - and a bit educational.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game

Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch I'm going to review this not from the perspective of a toy, but rather as a piece of movie memorabilia. Years ago, I use to love to go to the local mall here in Austin and stop by the SunCoast Motion Picture Company store. Where you could buy all sort of movie related items as well as the movies themselves. Over the years I've bought a number of items very similar to this Rocket Raccoon figure for my collection. So when I was offered one of these 10 inch figure to check out I gladly accepted.

I wasn't expecting this figure to be so big - I knew it was suppose to be 10" but it seems bigger than that to me. It came in one of those open face boxes that allow you to actually touch the toy before taking it out of the box, and you can activate the sound effect as the item ships with the batteries already installed and the sound box is set in a demo mode. The sounds it make are pretty loud, they should put a smile on any child face (and a frown on any adults in the room).

Once out of the box, there is some assembly required. You have to pop the tail into the figures rear-end (yeah, I know). It takes some effort to do that, so I suggest having an adult do it. Other than that, the figure is ready to go. Like I mentioned there is a demo mode on the effects box. The effects are controlled with a three-position switch - Off, Try Me (demo), and On. The unit is powered by three double-A batteries which are located in the figures backpack (there is a screw securing the cover to the batteries). Once you turn on the power switch, there are two activation points - one on the figures leg and another on top of the gun he is holding. Pressing one or the other activates both motion and sound effects, plus the figure speaks phrases from the movie. The motion effects are just the end of the gun rotating and the figure shaking a bit. There are some light effects with the end of the gun & gun sight lighting up. There aren't that many spoken phrases - so they can get a bit repetitive after awhile.

The toy is pretty well made - a lot more substantial than most of the movie memorabilia, but then again it was made for kids to play with.

I kept the figure on my desk at work for about a week before bringing it home. I can't tell you how times people stopped and played with the figure (too many times, as that is what prompted me to finally take it home). I haven't seen the movie yet - but it is definitely one that I plan on seeing this summer.

I really like this figure - about the only thing I could comment on would be the detail of the end of his gun, everything else has a decent level of detail, but that part of the gun doesn't. Guessing that is more due to the fact that they made it out of clear plastic so that the light effect could be seen.
text_fidelity_b: Marvel Guardians of The Galaxy Big Blastin' Rocket Raccoon Figure, 10 Inch

text_fidelity_a: Pokemon TCG: Shining Fates Mini Tin, Multi I don’t know what every pack had in it because we bought a boost box for a school fundraiser. I’m an art teacher for an elementary school and I was trying to think of a fundraiser that was different and that all the students would like. I talked my principal into a Pokémon fundraiser. He bought one of these Brilliant Stars booster boxes. I did open about 7 packs to sell cards individually. Of those 7 packs we got 2 V’s. One of them was a Galatians Moltres V (photo attached) secret rare 183/172. I know of at least 3 more V’s one being a Charizard V Star. I know this because a student that had bought a pack decided to open it at recess while I was doing recess duty. A group of boys took off running and hollering. Then I seen the one boy (that had bought a pack) tuck something into his hoodie pocket. I called him over and asked if he had his cards out. Though we sell the cards at the fundraiser they’re not allowed to have them out. They’re supposed to take them home and not bring them back to school. I had him show me what he had. It was a Charizard V Star! Now I’m not Pokémon expert but I’ve learned a little from the students and from researching for the fundraiser. I know this was an awesome card! I was told if I see a student have them out that was supposed to confiscate it. I couldn’t do that to this kid. We had a good talk and I had another student go to my room and get a hard sleeve card case (which we were also selling at the fundraiser) for him to put it in to protect it. I can see him putting it in his pocket and bending it and couldn’t stand the thought. He promised to take it home and not bring it back. I told him I know he would want to show his friends the card and now that he’s not allowed to bring it to school they may not believe him so I told him if anybody questioned him to come see me and I can let them know I seen it in person. It’s been the best fundraiser. It was supposed to last 2 week and we sold out of almost of everything in 2 days!
text_fidelity_b: Pokemon TCG: Shining Fates Mini Tin, Multi

The wood is a little lighter than say the Crayola brand ones, but they sharpen fine and as long as you aren't pressing extremely hard the lead does not break. I pressed fairly hard to blend the trees and none of the pencils broke for me. While this was not an art venture, this page was used for me to test the pencils and I am happy with the results. Before I would color on the page, I used a blank page to scribble a little as it can be hard to differentiate some of the colors from the other shades, but I do this anyway so I am sure about the color I want before I get it on the page and accidentally wreck something.

The colors blended fine, I probably should have gone back and finished shading, but as a test page it worked fine. I mixed this pack in with my other pencils so I can choose from any color I could need. text_fidelity_a:
Ninja Warrior Obstacle Course for Kids - 2X50FT Double Ninja Slackline with Most Complete Accessories for Kids, Swing, Trapeze Swing, Rope Ladder, Obstacle Net Plus 1.2M Arm Trainer I am hoping to upgrade my rating to 4-5 stars after my 9 year old has had time to play on this a few times. A few initial thoughts:

The instructions included were not great, I had to find a YouTube video and watch it a few times to figure out assembly. I’m not the engineering type and no, it’s not hard, but it still took me multiple tries to get it right.

After finally getting it set up, we realized the obstacles were still too far apart for my child. However, the tension is way too tight once it’s locked and loaded so you can’t just easily slide the metal bracket things. Which means you have to loosen the entire ratchet thing and basically start over again. We did this a few times which is a bit frustrating. It definitely takes some trial and error and if you have an excited and antsy kid who can’t wait to get on this thing, it makes it even more stressful.

My 9 year old is a bit tall and during the trial and error period we realized it was too low, so then I had to go get the big ladder and shimmy the slack lines up another 2 feet on both trees. Everything added together just took a lot of time.

That being said, everything looks well made and durable at this point. I still need to make a few adjustments so that hopefully she can play on it this weekend. We will then decide whether to keep this thing or not. The monkey grip is tough and the cargo net is super swingy so it’s tough, she said. We are not planning to use the swing but we did buy a separate wheel thing from the same company.

I do plan on installing the lower slack line, I think that will help her move from obstacle to obstacle while also working her core at the same time. Hoping to provide an update in a week or so.
text_fidelity_b: Ninja Warrior Obstacle Course for Kids - 2X50FT Double Ninja Slackline with Most Complete Accessories for Kids, Swing, Trapeze Swing, Rope Ladder, Obstacle Net Plus 1.2M Arm Trainer

The Electronic Turbo Slam device, first required (3)- AAA batteries (not included). The device, when slammed has pretty loud sound effects/music, which I found annoying after a short while. I also thought there was too much commotion for me with everyone trying to slap down cards to change the letters, and I wasn't crazy about making just (4) letter words. As an adult, baby boomer, I much prefer the standard game of Scrabble -- quiet, relaxed and educational, and with more word potential.

I can see that this would be a great game for parents to play with young children to help them get interested in learning new words -- I would use it as an educational tool, instead of having them feel pressured to make words at record speed.

On the other hand, the speed and noise factor, would probably appeal to lots of teens. Overall, the game is relatively inexpensive, and worth a try for families who enjoy word faster paced, action filled games.

text_fidelity_a: KINGBOT DeXop Rc Cartoon Car Cartoon Race Car with Music Radio Control Toy Action Figure Rc Vehicle for Toddler, CR04 [[VIDEOID:3cfc56c5d4bf143f7ccc504487426748]] My nephew gets freaked out if his Fischer Price remote control car moves his direction, and he's a brave little kid.  That car goes fairly slowly.  This thing flies and is NOT a toddler toy.  There's no way I'm putting the remote control in the hands an 18 mos. old, even as smart as he is!  The remote offers very little control and that's risky when you have something moving that fast around the floor.  The car doesn't stay on a straight path either.  While moving forward it veers left and right at random and moving backwards is crazy.  The colors are vibrant enough to get a child's attention.  The buttons you push to play sounds are easy to work.  Those are the steering wheel, the driver, and the top of the car.  Pressing the steering wheel causes the cute sound of a car cranking, revving its engine, and rumbling while idle.  The top button causes the weirdest, most random song I've ever heard on a child's toy and it goes on for a solid 36.40 seconds.  Yes, I timed it for this review.  It's that weird a song. When the driver is pressed, the car emits an odd vocalization that sounds like a cross between a dog barking and a man shouting "hey! Hey hey hey! Heeey!" (like something one might hear at the end of a nice Latin dance song) in an odd singsong voice.  The headlights flash whenever a button is pushed and do so for the entirety of whatever sound is playing.  The driver is detachable and once it's pressed down well, it takes some force to get it out.  The overall look of the car and remote is cute, like any regular toddler toy should be.  For an older child who knows how to handle a faster paced remote control car, the price is fair.  As a so called toddler toy...no way am I putting this anywhere near a small child.
text_fidelity_b: KINGBOT DeXop Rc Cartoon Car Cartoon Race Car with Music Radio Control Toy Action Figure Rc Vehicle for Toddler, CR04

ThinkFun HypnoGraph Drawing Machine and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Age 8 and Up - Creates Mesmerizing Mechanical Art First, I recommend going to ThinkFun’s website and watch one of their setup videos because the directions that come in the box are missing some important steps. It was really frustrating trying to put this thing together the first time before I realized there were important steps missing in the written instructions.

The box I received said for ages 8 to Adult, but the picture on Amazon says for ages 14 to Adult. I believe this is a better product for older kids. The precision and accuracy needed to be successful with setting this up would frustrate a younger child. I’m going to try it in my 4th grade classroom and I foresee some loving it, and some getting really frustrated with it.

The really good thing about this is that eventually it becomes easier to setup as you practice and learn from it. So, once you play around with it and make some sloppy pictures, you start to make some really cool pictures. Once a child figures out how this works, they will be able to make tons of different pictures as they experiment with different combinations of gears.

So, I was very interested in their new logic puzzle that uses Crazy Aaron’s Putty. This game has some similarities with their other logic puzzles. It comes with 60 cards that show the challenge setup on one side and a possible answer on the back. The setup for each challenge takes the longest than any other logic puzzle because you have to tear the balls of putty off each color. It is challenging, even the first few challenges’ solutions aren’t immediately visible, they take some thought to solve.

I enjoyed this for myself and found it relaxing to put together and solve. I could see some kids not having the patience to play through the puzzle. This book is for four months on up. It is not intended for teething.

The colors are vibrant: blue greens, oranges and purples primarily. The ocean animals look cute and friendly.

The text is riddles in the form of who am I? It is rhyming although some of the rhyming is a tad clumsy, but your one or two-year-old won't care.

I have eight arms and two large eyes

The book uses big vocabulary words, but that's good for children to hear. As a former preschool director, kindergarten teacher and principal, I believe in exposing children to big concepts and expand their sense of the world past their everyday experiences. It grows their minds.

text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Empire Game If the classic game of Monopoly seemed to take too long, then you will appreciate this newer, shorter version. Instead of B&O Railroad, it is updated with businesses and brands like Spotify, ebay, Intel, Xbox, McDonalds and Coke. Instead of zipping around the board with an iron or a dog, you have a choice of a gold token like a coke bottle, game control, French fries, and motorcycle among others.

You choose your token, roll the dice and start buying brands, add brands to your tower, and buy and trade and take over brands with empire cards. First to the top of the tower wins. The game board reminds me of Times Square in appearance a bit.

Contents include: 4 towers for up to four players, 6 tokens, 30 billboard tiles, 6 office tiles, 14 chance cards, 14 empire cards, money pack, 2 dice and the game guide. I like this shorter, express version. I used to call the classic version Monotony, partially because my brother always beat me at it because I virtuously would save all of my $$$ and he would spend his buying up all of the real estate in the first half of the game. In the second half, I would just go around the board and pay him rent for hours on end until I ran out of $$$. Not a good strategy on my part.

I think this new version will be a hit for families who want a quick, fun game for family game night. It has current, relevant brands which is fun. And not all of the brands are about material consumption: there's ebay which is great for selling and recycling, and spotify which is about listening to good music for free - although they may charge a nominal price down the road.

While it involves luck more than strategy, some of my favorite games as a child involved luck: Chutes and Ladders, Candyland, Parcheesi etc. This is just a fun, light game for families to enjoy. When my son comes home for the weekend - he was a board game designer and now video game designer - will get his opinion and let you know what he thinks.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Empire Game

text_fidelity_a:
Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity My grandson is almost three years old, and I thought he’d enjoy this toy...that was until I received it. Upon first inspection you notice a cheaply made zip-up half circle that opens to expose rivets that a child is supposed to insert the enclosed plastic big “buttons”. Let me just tell you that there’s no way that my grandson can attach these things to the mat - it took all my strength and dexterity to get one or two to pop in place. This is simply too difficult for a child of any age and not challenging but frustrating. Then there’s these cute little ocean-themed felt cut-outs that you’re supposed to “hook” around the installed buttons. They’re brightly colored and my grandson did enjoy taking them off and on the buttons for about 15 minutes. Then there’s a few pieces of string...some are about 4” long (too short to practice tying and really too short for a toddler to attempt to thread through four holes on the felt pieces) and others are about 6” long. ALSO, Within fifteen minutes of play my toddler was pulling on the buttons attempting to remove them and the rivets we’re poppong off and the mat was falling apart, not to mention the tiny metal circles all over the floor were now a choking hazard and the mat no longer works in the holes that lost the rivets.

Overall PROs- cute felt pieces that easily attach much like a button hole that toddler can practice with.
CONs-cheap plastic sewn mat, hard to attach buttons, useless strings, mat falling apart during first play.
text_fidelity_b: Alex Discover Snap-to-It Ocean Game Kids Art and Craft Activity

Horrible Guild Similo Fables: A Fast-Playing Family Card Game - Guess the Secret Fairy Tale Character, 2-8 Players, Ages 8+, 20 min I'd never heard of Similo before, but there are other varieties of this card game(History and Myths...in June, at least). They can even be mixed with this one for a different game and there are instructions for doing so in this deck. The game is pretty simple. There's a Clue Giver and the other players are Guessers. The Clue Giver picks one of the characters in the deck(putting it back afterwards, along with 11 other cards) and then uses only cards leftover to give clues(5 cards in hand at a time), with no words or gestures. The 12 cards for the Guessers are spread in a grid and the Clue Giver gives one card per round for a clue. Vertical means there's something similar to the Secret Character and horizontal means there's something different. For example, if I'm the Clue Giver and I picked Aladdin, I could put Genie vertically, since they're from the same tale or I could put Cheshire Cat horizontally, since Aladdin isn't an animal. It's up the the Clue Giver to decide what's similar or different. The game is over within 5 rounds. The Guessers take away one card for the first round, two for the second, etc. If the Secret Character is taken away, the game is over, but if the final card is the Secret Character, the Guessers win.

I like that this game is cooperative. My children have to work together to win the game. We have plenty of competitive games, but very few cooperative ones, so this is a nice feature for us. I also like the illustrations on the cards. They're brightly colored and well done. It also doesn't take long to play, so if short on time, it's a nice way to pass just a bit of time and still have fun.

It's one of those simple things that bring great joy. As far as I can tell, these are the same thing, only they're called Aqua Dragons. The aquarium is also bigger than the one I had as a child. This set comes with a pouch of eggs, a pouch of food, a spoon, a bubble creator(suction tube), a little magnifying glass, and the aquarium. The aquarium has a removable top and lights that come from the bottom. Simply press a button on the side to turn them on and press it again to turn them off. It comes with batteries, though it does say they're only temporary for the "try me" feature and should be replaced. Non-chlorinated water is recommended.

We've had great fun with our little dragons. It took close to 48 hours for us to be able to see them. Of course, at that point they're only a tiny white dot and it gets more fun when they're bigger. This set has potential to last quite awhile, too. The Aqua Dragons can live up to 6 months. After they all die, you're supposed to completely let the tank dry out. This will cause any eggs to dry out. (Don't wash it out or the eggs will be washed away. The eggs won't hatch unless they've dried out.) Once that happens, you can add more water and start with a fresh batch of little dragons.

It's a great kit to create some special childhood memories.

Note on the aquarium: Don't pull the plastic. I thought it had a protective layer and almost started peeling it off. If you do, the design on it will come off with it. I do wish the plastic was flatter against the aquarium, so it's not as big of an issue thinking it's supposed to be peeled off.

You'll also need a computer/laptop/tablet. While you're using Artie, you won't be able to use the internet on that device. He uses his own connection, though when you connect to it, it will show no internet access. I thought it wasn't connecting properly, but it's still working. Because of the trial and error part, I wouldn't recommend this for (average) younger children, unless you have some patience stored up when helping them(though I do think it's an awesome way to help them develop problem solving skills and even some extra patience WHEN they're ready for it). My 7 year old was the most interested. My 5 year old had interest, but he wasn't as gentle with it as he needed to be.

I especially like that the projects are centered around a story. You read a little, then build, read, build..... It makes the whole thing more fun and puts things into perspective. Everything you need is provided in the box, except for 2 AA batteries(so have those on hand before starting). The projects can get a little complicated, particularly when the gears come into the story, but it's not too bad. Some children might need help(or it can simply be a challenge to see if they can figure it out on their own).

The quality is mostly nice. The treehouse is made out of sheets of wood, and it seems durable to me. It won't last through rough play, but for the project, it holds up well. When building the treehouse, you can glue the pieces into place. We chose to take it apart, so we could do the projects again later with my youngest child. (Untying the knots was a bit of a pain, but otherwise, it's pretty simple to take apart.) There are a few pieces that are paper, though, and these are much less durable.

If you're looking for a fun project for a rainy day of learning, this is a nice kit to try.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos 626020 Pepper Mint in The Great Treehouse Engineering Adventure Science Experiment Kit, Blue

Kids First Big & Fun Microscope Science Experiment Kit | Easy-to-Use Kids Microscope | Ages 4-6 | STEM Experiment Guide and Full-Color User Manual | 72 Images | Extra-wide Eyepiec with Light-up Stage I was disappointed in this microscope, BUT it is for preschoolers. Each part was designed with them in mind. It doesn't magnify much, but it's for the benefit of their eyes. It's also designed so that they don't have to shut one eye to see. It's simple! If you're looking for something more advanced, you'll most definitely want to go another route. This one is more of a toy than a microscope.

It comes with 24 slides, with 3 items on each one. (Plus one blank one.) There's an included book that tells what it is on each of the slides(page 27 and 28). There's no storage for these at all. It would have been nice for a container or bag of some sort to be included to hold all of these. For now, we have the microscope and the slides within a basket, and that makes it easy to pull it off the shelf.

To use the light part of the microscope, you have to put in 2 AAA batteries, which are not included. Flip the switch and a light will come on. Just place a slide under the lens. (It will only go one way.) There's a knob that turns on the front, and this will move the slide back and forth. That's it. There's no way to zoom in and out.

I wouldn't recommend this microscope unless you want it as the most basic introduction to very young children(5ish and under). Even then if they've already been introduced to a microscope, they'll probably be disappointed in this one.

text_fidelity_a:
Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House For this kit, you're paying for the convenience of having everything organized and already there. Also, for the "magical" experience you can provide for your child. If you do "Elf on a Shelf" or Santa Clause or anything similar, you'll probably love the added magical part of this kit. (We don't. We're all different and that's okay.) The parent has to be very involved. It's not a kit you just hand over to the child. (The parent portion is in a well sealed container to help keep the secret, since I imagine many parents will attempt to hand it straight over to the child. That was my plan before I realized what it was.) The child will have to do activities, and then the parent will secretly leave another activity in the fairy house. This is suppose to make the child believe the fairies left them a gift. (For example: The child is to craft 3 fairy bells and hang them around their room. Inside the fairy house, they'll place a stick, pebbles, and a leaf. They'll then spin the house and ring each bell to summon a fairy visit.)

The quality is similar to the various "Box of the Month" type subscriptions out there for kids. In my opinion, there's more in the wizard kit. There is the same amount of activities in both, but there's just not as much to do in this fairy kit. (It seems more stickers and easy crafts.) It's not high quality, but it's still nice enough. The crafts are something that could be put together with supplies from a dollar store. But, it's so convenient having everything in one place, especially for a disorganized person, like myself. Plus, there'd the "magical" experience provided for those that desire it.

Though the wizard kit that is similar to this one could work for boys and girls(and this one still could, if desired), this fairy kit is definitely targeted to girls. At the end, I couldn't help but feel sorry for all the little children doing these activities, hoping to see a fairy. While gifts are left, which are supposed to let the child know a fairy visited them, they'll never actually see one, unless the parent does something extra. We just did the crafts, since we don't do imaginary things as real. Without the added magical element, though, this kit just doesn't hold near as much value. If you're like us and don't do Santa and all, I'd recommend another kind of kit. If you do love the idea of pretending fairies are leaving gifts, this might be a blast for you and your child, as long as you don't think they'll be too disappointed that they never actually see a fairy. Overall, I found it a little disappointing, particularly considering the current price(which changes constantly).
text_fidelity_b: Magical Fairy Adventure – Fun Activities, Surprises, and Clues Magically Appear in an Enchanted Fairy House

Overall, this is an interesting game, and perfect for those that know lots of trivia and even those that don't and want to.

My oldest has a huge obsession with dinosaurs, and they are all his brain thinks about, so I thought a dinosaur DNA kit looked like something cool for him. It's really just a dig kit, though, with some added features that require a smart phone. Honestly, we just skipped all that, and used it as a simple dig kit. Even then, we'd already did a couple of them just before this one, so the whole digging process had become a little old for him.

Aside from that, it's an okay kit. The quality of the items to dig out usually aren't great, and this was no exception. My son has had trouble getting all the pieces to stick together as they should with all the dinosaur dig kits he's ever had, and again, this one was no exception. He became a little frustrated at some of the pieces.

If you've never used a dig kit before, they're messy! We've found them to be slightly less messy done inside a pie pan. Even so, outside is always better with these things(on a warm, windless day). Also, they require patience. This one wasn't near as hard to dig through as some of the other ones we've had, but it's definitely not the easiest, either. I'd say it's a medium level on hardness. It takes time to get all the pieces, and that's part of the process. It teaches a young person a bit of what it's like for archaeologists. If they rush the dig, they end up damaging pieces.

Overall, this is a fun little lesson in patience, for both children and adults, but it wasn't quite what I was expecting.

Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game We also have this game in the Dr. Seuss theme, and they're both fun. They're very similar in both cards and directions, but this one is great for little fans of Marvel.

There's a note on the directions page to let you know it's fine to customize the rules for your family. (We tend to do that anyway, but it's a great reminder!) There are 3 stacks of numbered/colored cards(1-red, 2-blue, 3-green). The player turns over one card from each stack. They'll tell the player what to do with which objects. For example, the first card will tell you to "Do a push-up". The second card: "with Captain Marvel's energy ball", and the third card: "on your head". Some tasks are harder than others! Each card will get a certain amount of stars. (At the end of the game, the players will add the stars up. The player with the most wins.) If your child thinks he/she can do the specified task, they will say, "I Can Do That!" If not, they can exchange a card at a time until they feel they can do the task. One of my children was given the task of "Crab walk under the portal, with Spider-Man's web, between your elbows". None of us were talented enough to do that, so he picked again. This is also a great escape route for the shyer(or younger) little ones. Some things will be less embarrassing or more doable for them than others.

There are also "Battle" cards. If one of those are drawn, then any other cards drawn will be put back in the mix. The player will then try to knock down the Green Goblin card with the object specified on the card. If the task is completed, the card is set aside. If not, the player has to put that card in his/her pile as a reminder to discard 2 cards before counting stars at the end of the game. (That way, they can discard to 2 with the lowest number of stars.)

While it may get old with what the players do, it does create a variety of mix and match tasks. The cards are constantly being shuffled. The game ends when all the cards are gone.

This is a great game for when movement is needed. It's not one that the players just sit around and play. The players have to get up and move around. There's also a nice variety of types of objects. There's a plastic block that will need to be filled with air, along with a ball(that's already aired up). There's foam items and thick cardboard objects(Green Goblin and Captain America's shield). My biggest complaint is the "portal". This isn't the sturdiest of things. It's hard to get it to stand up straight, mainly because it has to be rolled up a bit to fit in the box. It makes it hard to get under at times. The bigger/older the child, the harder it will be to crawl under it, either way. This is definitely a game for littler/younger people. Also, I fear that the block won't last long, since objects that require air don't make it too long around my home, in general. (For it to fit back in the box after each game, the air will have to be released. That means you'll have to blow it up before each game. It's not huge, so it's not the biggest deal. Particularly if used in a classroom setting, though, germs/cleaning wipes would be something to put into consideration.)

My children(3, 5, and a tiny 8) have really enjoyed playing this game, though!
text_fidelity_b: Wonder Forge Marvel I Can Do That! Game

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game We just aren't overly fond of this game. It ended up being super frustrating for us.

When you first open the game, you have to put the game board together. This takes a bit of time, but it's not too bad. It looks nice enough, and I like that the game board is thick and sturdy. My boys love the whole idea of the game, and I don't think we've ever played a game where the board stood up. That was really cool! Our biggest issue is how difficult it is to keep the climbers in place. They're constantly falling when they shouldn't be. My children are 3, 5, and 8, so that may have a great deal to do with it. Keeping those climbers hanging where they should proved impossible for us, though. It's also a little frustrating that each player has to move around to play. The game board only faces one way, and you can't move it without making the climbers fall off(even more). That means when 4 people are playing, you can't just sit in a spot and enjoy the game. You have to move around, depending on whose turn it is. That might not be a big deal for many, but it frustrated my little guys.

Overall, we really like the whole idea of the game, and the fact that the game board stands up, but it ended up being incredibly frustrating for everyone.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Yippie Yippie Yeti Game

text_fidelity_a:
DINOTRUX REPTOOL CONTROL TY RUX We gave this to my 8 year old, because he loves all things dinosaurs, and he also likes Dinotrux(which is a Netflix show). He may be a little older than the average child that would want this toy, though.

When I asked him to tell me what he liked or didn't like about Ty, he responded, "I like everything about him!" His favorite parts are that Ty roars when he's first turned on and he dances. He also loves the "hide and seek" feature with Revvit and the fact that he's given directions for what to do.

From the parent's point of view, this thing is really cute, and I love that my boys enjoy him so much. He's sometimes annoying, though. He talks loud! On multiple occasions, I'd find myself jumping when Ty suddenly spoke in his very loud voice. We try not to add too many "loud" toys to our home, and the ones we do usually don't last long, but personally, I've found this one to be worth it. (Some of you won't!)

Overall, this is a really fun toy for Dinotrux fans! All of my boys have enjoyed it, but especially my 8 year old.
text_fidelity_b: DINOTRUX REPTOOL CONTROL TY RUX

text_fidelity_a:
The Secret Life of Pets Scra-ffiti Pad My children really enjoy these scratch off pads! The last one we tried was awful and so messy that I banned these from being used inside the house(though with full permission to use them outside). When this one arrived, it disappeared. I kept asking where it went, with no luck. After a few weeks, one of my children brought it back to me and apologized. "It's just so much fun to scratch it." He had been hiding out in his "toy room"(which is really just a pepped up storage area) scratching away at this pad. Most of the pages were already scratched off, but I did have little areas here and there left to test myself.

So, there you go. These are so much fun that my child was willing to hide it to scratch it in the house. ;)

It's really not near as messy as some I've tried, but it does still leave a mess. One that we had flaked off in dry clumps. It was ridiculously hard to clean up. It stuck to our table, and even with the help of a magic eraser, it took a great deal of effort to clean it up. This one scratches off in better little clumps. It kind of sticks to itself, as opposed to creating tons of tiny flakes. Again, though, it's still very messy(just not as bad as it could be). I don't recommend these anywhere but outdoors(maybe on the porch on a rainy day).

Overall, these are apparently incredibly fun for children, but a pain for parents to clean up.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets Scra-ffiti Pad

text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining My children have enjoyed various kinds of dig kits in the past, so they were excited for this one, too. My 5 year old got this one, and he liked it pretty well.

On my side, though, this particular kit wasn't one of my favorites. The kit comes with a hammer, but that thing was absolutely useless! My child was frustrated with it, so I gave it a try. Useless! The description tells you that you'll get a pair of goggles, but you don't. There's no goggles in this kit, but the instructions recommend that your child wear a pair. Also, I dislike that all of the rocks were clumped in one little spot in ours, and that happen to be right where my child started digging. He got them all dug out very quickly, but still had a great deal of clay to dig through. Discovering "treasures" slowly(at least more slowly than this one) is the whole fun of these things.

Like all dig kits, this one is messy. We've found shallow pie pans to be the best holders. The sides aren't too tall, so it won't hurt your child's arms. It also keeps the mess inside the pan. For the kits that are harder to dig, it makes it super easy to move the dig until your child wants to work on it again. This particular dig is on the softer side, though not the softest we've ever done. Really, it's just right in that area, for our tastes. It's not so hard that it's frustrating, but not so soft that the dig ends in a few minutes(or it wouldn't have if ours had the gems spaced out better).

Overall, if your child enjoys rocks(or gems), this is a decent choice. There are better options, though.
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Geo Smash Mining

text_fidelity_a:
Sesame Street Playskool Discover ABCs with Elmo Playset This toy is pretty neat.

There's not much as far as assembly goes. (Just snapping 3 pieces together, and then attaching the whole building into that.) It only took a minute or so.

Elmo is detached from the rest of the set, and he holds onto a hand "lens". Letters are hidden throughout the building, on both sides. You can tell where a letter is going to be...circle with squiggly lines. You can't tell what letter it is until Elmo's "lens" is held over it, though. To find some of the letters, the child will have to turn a couple of wheels, and lift the trash can lid, but most of them are in plain view.

This is a fun little toy for learning letters. It doesn't take up a ton of room, either. It's somewhat flat in design, so it could easily slide into a little nook somewhere, and just pull it out for learning time. I think most children will tire quickly of it if they have full access to it, unless they have other Sesame Street toys(or something else similar) that could be used with it, apart from just hunting for letters. I think it's probably better for special times, though, for most children. There's really not a great deal to it, but it is fun and neat.
text_fidelity_b: Sesame Street Playskool Discover ABCs with Elmo Playset

text_fidelity_a:
Brio Birthday Train - Toddler You really don't have to use this train as a "birthday" train(though you could, of course). It's also great for teaching little ones numbers. It comes with blocks, numbered 1-6. My 3 year old absolutely loves trains, and he's still learning numbers, so this works out great for him.

If you choose to use it as a birthday train, just to warn you, the candle doesn't stay in place like it should. Each block has a hole in the back of it. You put the age number in one of the cars, and then take any of the other blocks and lay it upside down in the other car. The candle is supposed to stand up in the hole on the back of the block. It just doesn't do that very well, and it tilts sideways.

The train is mostly plastic. The blocks and one piece on the front car are wood, but the rest of it is plastic. It's a cute train set, but I would have liked a bit more wood in the design. I was expecting something nicer than this, based on the price. I also dislike that a driver wasn't included in this set. There's a place for the driver to stand, but you'll have to buy him/her separately.

Still, it's a cute set!
text_fidelity_b: Brio Birthday Train - Toddler

text_fidelity_a:
Chutes and Ladders Board Game for 2 to 4 Players Kids Ages 3 and Up (Amazon Exclusive) This is a cute and fun game, and you really can't go wrong with it. It's a classic for a reason! It not only teaches counting, but it also teaches good/bad behavior through the pictures, and of course, "up" and "down" for the really young players.

My only semi-complaint about the game is the fact that the pieces are so big. It's really hard for me to play with all 3 of my children at once. It becomes too confusing and crowded for them, and they become frustrated. For us, it's a better game to just play with 2 players at a time, so it's a great game for some one on one time with each of my children(which I can't complain about).
text_fidelity_b: Chutes and Ladders Board Game for 2 to 4 Players Kids Ages 3 and Up (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
reCAP Kids EXPLORE Bug Catcher, Creature Keeper, Firefly Mason Jar Habitat, Glow Green Mason Jar Accessories My boys are always catching bugs of various kinds to observe. My 5 year old claimed this jar, and he's carried it around constantly. The handle makes that super easy for him. Also, the lid to this jar glows in the dark, so that's a big hit with all my little guys. (It also has air holes for the bugs to breathe.)

The jar is plastic. It will get scratched! If it gets destroyed, though, you can use any other Mason jar with the lid, and those are easy to find. As I learned in the downloadable pack that's advertised with this bug catcher, you can even use some brands of spaghetti sauce and peanut butter jars once they are empty. This thing gets bonus points for that!

My original review had a complaint about an expired coupon code for the advertised downloadable activity pack. That was all fixed up, and I have our cute little activity book now. The coupon code comes on the label, so make sure you save that! Just create an account with Mason Jars, add the pack to your cart, then the coupon code, and you're good to go for downloading. There are fun activity and coloring pages, along with recipes. It's a nice bonus!

Overall, this is a fun bug jar, and my children have enjoyed it.
text_fidelity_b: reCAP Kids EXPLORE Bug Catcher, Creature Keeper, Firefly Mason Jar Habitat, Glow Green Mason Jar Accessories

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Games Pictionary Man: Double Draw Game I have to admit that I've never played the original game of Pictionary. I have seen it enough on television, tough, to be somewhat familiar with it, and this looks like a cute variation of it. We've had so much fun with this version that I think I'll put the original version on our Christmas list!

This game comes with two "men"(which can be used as either gender). There's also 4 squares/rectangles that can be used as various objects(mail, hat, etc). There are slots on each hand and on the head of each "man" where those can be put. There's also a ball and a box that can be used for props. There are 2 sets of cards(classic and pairs), 2 markers for drawing, a dice, and an hourglass.

If you enjoy Pictionary(or think you might), this is a fun little game. I can almost guarantee at least a little laughter(and we all need more of that)!
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Games Pictionary Man: Double Draw Game

text_fidelity_a:
Mega Bloks Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Sewer Lair Building Kit We're huge Lego fans in my house, so while it may not be fair, I couldn't help but compare Mega Bloks with Lego. We got a few kits to try out, but otherwise, we've only used Lego in the past(though quite a bit of it). Unfortunately, Mega Bloks has just fallen short, for me, and I wasn't overly impressed(for the most part).

First of all, I've been spoiled to numbered bags. While this kit is divided into separate bags, you have to open all of them and dump them out, because the pieces you need for each step could be in any of the bags. I prefer, if I'm using a kit, to have my steps divided by bags. It keeps thing from getting less jumbled and lost, and it provides great "rest" points. It kind of made me wonder what the point of all the bags were in this set.

Second, these blocks just didn't go together smoothly. Some of them require a great deal of pressure to get attached. They hurt my fingers. I even snapped my finger between two of the blocks at one point trying to get pieces together. (Sad, but true.) My fingers just ache after working with Mega Bloks due to the amount of pressure required to get some of the pieces together. Some of the pieces were incredibly frustrating to get together. Not only that but some of the parts from the final product keep falling off/apart. It took so long to put the thing together(with so much pain) that it almost brings some tears to see parts fall off. ;)

Third, the directions aren't as clear as I'd prefer. Sure, as an adult, I figured things out, but for the average child, the directions just make things harder than they have to be.

When I discovered that Mega Bloks were compatible with Lego, I was really excited. I thought that the block building world could open up to more options for me and my children. We're sticking with Lego, though! It seems more organized and the pieces are more reliable. (They have more of a perfect fit than we've experienced with Mega Bloks.)

In defense of Mega Bloks, though, the little figurines are way cooler! IF you are a fan of Mega Bloks, this kit is cool! (I just found it a pain. Literally.)
text_fidelity_b: Mega Bloks Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles Sewer Lair Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Star Wars Galactic Heroes The Ghost This thing is really cool!

Just be aware that there are characters on the back of the box that aren't included in this set. As far as character figures, this one comes with Ezra and Chopper. There are other sets that can be bought to add upon this one.

The main top piece opens up. Characters can stand in various places within. Attachments can be put in there, too. (It won't close with any of that, though.) There's another door within that portion that opens, and this is perfect for storing some of the smaller pieces when it's time to stop playing. The cockpit that attaches to the front can also be removed for more variety during playtime.

On the negative side, the attachments are a pain! Even for me, they were hard to get attached, and then they came off easily. I don't think many children will care for those. The main ship is the best part, though, and it can be played with without the hassle of the attachments!

Overall, this is a cool toy, and I think any little Star Wars Galactic Heroes fan will enjoy it.
text_fidelity_b: Star Wars Galactic Heroes The Ghost

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Hi Ho! Cherry-O Board Game for 2 to 4 Players Kids Ages 3 and Up (Amazon Exclusive) You really can't go wrong with this game if you've got little ones around(unless, of course, they put things other than food in their mouth, and then I'd save this for later). It's a classic board game for a reason.

My husband has fond memories of playing this game with his grandmother, but about a month ago was the first time I'd ever played it. My children have fallen in love with the game, and I'm thrilled they've had the chance to experience it. It's cute and fun!

It's a really quick and simple game to play, and easy enough for very young players to be included, since counting only goes to 4 in the game. (Again, the fruit is very small, though, so don't have it around those that put things in their mouths.) It's actually just right for my 3 year old, and while it's technically too easy for my 5 and 8 year old children, they still love playing it.

Also, with small pieces, I appreciate that there are 4 extra pieces of fruit(one of each color) included in case one goes missing.

Overall, this is a perfect game for preschoolers to play, as long as they don't put things in their mouth.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Hi Ho! Cherry-O Board Game for 2 to 4 Players Kids Ages 3 and Up (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
Bright Starts Pop & Giggle Pond Pal Ball Popper Musical Toy, Ages 6 months + This frog is loud and a bit annoying, but it's still cute!

When this toy comes out of the box, you'll have to put together 3 different pieces. The head has to be attached to the body, and a little spring part attaches to the side. There are 6 different colored balls, too.

This toy does NOT come with batteries. You'll need 4 AA batteries, along with a small screwdriver(Phillips head or flat, either one) to get them into the toy.

There are 4 "piano" keys on the front that make sounds, and there's also the main button that will start the music playing and the mouth to bouncing. The inside of the mouth is soft. When the main button is pressed, the inside of the mouth will move around, and make the balls bounce. When the ball hits the center of the mouth, the bouncing will usually cause the ball to bounce outside of the mouth. This is fun for children to then go grabbing the stray balls. If the child is really young, you'll be the one grabbing the balls. (They will go rolling under couches and beds, so try to play it in an area that will result in minimal lost balls.)

Overall, this is a fun toy for young children/babies. The average mama of babies won't want it around too much, though. Between the noise and running after balls, it's a bit exhausting. For mamas of children that are old enough to chase after the balls, it's a great way to burn built up energy on a rainy day! (If playing on carpet, the balls most likely won't roll quite so much.)
text_fidelity_b: Bright Starts Pop & Giggle Pond Pal Ball Popper Musical Toy, Ages 6 months +

text_fidelity_a:
Peppa and George Giggle N' Wiggle Plush These dolls are super cute!

My 3 year old son absolutely loves Peppa and George, and watches them regularly! His birthday present pick was a Peppa Pig house. He used his own money to buy the camper van, and he has requested a Peppa Pig car for Christmas. He also regularly asks me to read from his Peppa Pig book, and though it's 100% twaddle, I gladly do so. These dolls were perfect for him!

At first, their legs look really weird and twiggy. After watching them "fall down" with laughter, you quickly understand why. This matches perfectly with the shows, and it's adorable(even if I do find this part of the show super corny).

Each doll requires 3 AA batteries. Peppa comes with a set of demo batteries, but George has none. You'll need a small Phillips head screwdriver to get those batteries in.

If you have a Peppa Pig fan, these are a perfect gift. They're adorable!
text_fidelity_b: Peppa and George Giggle N' Wiggle Plush

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Magic: Gold Edition | Playset with 150 Tricks | 96 Page Full Color Instruction Manual | 42 Props | Video Tutorials | Fun for Kids 8+ This is a nice starter set. Some of the pieces come off really cheap, and some of the tricks were hard to do, due to the low quality pieces, but it's still a great set to test whether or not a child would want to invest in a higher quality set.

There is a large variety of tricks. It's lots of fun for children to practice with. My 7 year old(almost 8) has had lots of fun practicing the tricks and then performing it for his brothers. He has had to have a little help from me, but older children could practice in private and then perform for the whole family. (There are lots of pieces, so I'd recommend this for children that take care of their things, as opposed to those that throw their things here and there. The pieces would be destroyed quickly if not taken care of.)

Overall, this is a good set for a child. I do wish that some of the pieces were a bit higher in quality, though.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Magic: Gold Edition | Playset with 150 Tricks | 96 Page Full Color Instruction Manual | 42 Props | Video Tutorials | Fun for Kids 8+

text_fidelity_a:
ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor My boys are 3, 5, and 7(almost 8), and they all enjoy this game. As a bonus, it requires NO batteries!

Both the game boards and the game pieces have both pictures and words on them. Your child doesn't have to be able to read to play the game, but it does make the picture/word connection, to an extent. The game goes so fast that even I tend to mostly just look at the picture, and ignore the words. There is still a slight connection, though, and every little bit helps when a little one is learning words.

The game comes with 7 game boards. These are double sided. The green side is for a less competitive game, and better for the littlest ones. There aren't that many shared pictures on this side, and the players aren't in so much of a rush to grab the tiles. The red side has a bit more competition, since there are more pictures in common. The players have to rush to grab a matching tile, before someone else grabs it.

Each game goes really quick, so you're not spending a ton of time on each game. There are a few different options for playing the game. You can go the traditional "Bingo" route, or you can match designs, play multiple cards, or even fill up the whole card, which is what my oldest prefers. The traditional route is just way too quick for my children's tastes.

Their favorite part of the game is the Zinger. It's super easy to load the tiles, and then slide them into view. They have to take turns sliding the tiles into view, because it's so much fun. The only negative we've seen is the fact that sometimes it seems the same tile is being played over and over(in a row). When you first open the box, you'll have to mix these tiles up, since they are placed together matched. If you don't mix them up, you WILL have the same tile continue to show up in a row. Even then, it sometimes happens that the same one will keep showing up. It is easy to dump them out, mix them up, and then reload them, though.

This is a super simple game, but so much fun for little ones! I even enjoy playing it with them, which is pretty important.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun Zingo Sight Words Award Winning Early Reading Game for Pre-K to 2nd Grade - Toy of the Year Finalist, A Fun and Educational Game Developed by Educators for Boys and Girls, Multicolor

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Kids First Science Laboratory Kit This is a nice kit for children! It's very well made and appears sturdy, except for the hand magnifier. My boys managed to break it the first day we opened the kit, which was a huge disappointment. That said, it was the only piece I let them play with unsupervised, because they were using it to play "detectives". I'd say it was more their fault than the magnifier's.

This set comes with a little booklet with suggested science projects. I'd highly recommend finding some other projects at pinterest, too. My boys were a little bored with the suggested projects. It is a nice kit, full of the basics, though, so there should be plenty of fun options to make use of the provided supplies.

As a bonus, the box that stores all the supplies is really nice, too. It's not the flimsy, cheap storage containers you can buy at the dollar store. This one is thick and sturdy.

As a basic children's set, this is a great option, though to be honest, $45 is a little more than I would be willing to pay for it.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Kids First Science Laboratory Kit

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Start Essentials 3D Pen Set For Kids with Free Refill Filament - STEM Toy For Boys & Girls, Age 6 & Up - Toy of The Year Award Winner I think this thing is awesome!

That said, I do have a couple of warnings to consider. First, it will get really expensive! The sticks don't go very far at all. (The package claims each 6 inch stick will give you 60 inches of play, so I'm going to assume we just need more practice to get that much, as I'm guessing most others will, too.) With this set, you'll get 2 packs of the sticks(48 total sticks...6 each of white, mint green, yellow, orange, blue, red, green, and grey). You'll use those up super quick! These sticks are biodegradable, BPA-free and labeled as "safe". From what I've read, you'll need these specific sticks to go with the 3Doodler.

Also, every time you put a new color stick through the pen, you'll be wasting a bit of the previous stick, unless it works into your design. The whole stick won't completely feed through until you put another one in there to push it on out.

It takes a great deal of practice to get anything worthwhile to turn out. I have 3 little boys and they all want a chance at practicing, so even more sticks are used up in that process. So far, we haven't came up with anything close to what is shown in the practice book, but none of us can call ourselves overly skilled in the artistic realm at this point in time.

All of that said, IF your budget allows for buying lots of sticks to go with this pen, it truly is awesome! (Or you could request packs of these sticks as grandparent presents for the kids.) ;) Letting a child use his/her imagination with this thing is an amazing opportunity, and I definitely recommend it. (I even recommend it for adults, too, because we all need a little childish fun every once in awhile!)

It's easy to use. Just charge it up with the included micro USB cable(or do like me and use your kindle charger), turn it on and wait for the light to turn green. Then, press the button to start it and press it again to stop it. Simple! As I mentioned earlier, there is a book with instructions and some ideas to practice and get started with the pen. There's no worries about getting burned. I tested it out, and while the plastic is a little warm when it first comes out, it's not even close to hot. This allows for a little wiggle room for moving around your design before it completely dries.

In the end, other than the sticks being a costly investment, this is a great little invention, and we've loved it so far!

Melissa & Doug ABC Picture Boards - Educational Toy With 13 Double-Sided Wooden Boards and 52 Letters I've used this set with my 2 year old, and he loves it. text_fidelity_a:
Scientific Explorer Ice Age Creator Kit My boys had tons of fun with this set, but it's really more of a one-time kind of thing. You can somewhat recreate the scene/projects if you keep the base, which is plastic(and washable), but some are harder to recreate than others. Also, there's a mammoth included, which still gets lots of play from my boys.

I'd recommend doing the crystals and the crystal tree first, since it takes a day or so for those to "grow". The snow and the melting pond are pretty quick(though the melting pond does take a bit of time to turn into the puddle).

If you do the snow ahead of time, it won't be as big and "fluffy" when it all comes together for play. I poured some water on ours and it revived, though not to the same degree. It's better to wait on it. (It's super cool watching the the pieces soak up water and grow, though!)

Also, when growing crystals on the pipe cleaner, use HOT water, not warm as the directions said. Ours didn't grow, and based on looking at other recommendations, hot water is needed.

You can save the snow part and the melting pond for reuse, but just to warn you, if the snow part gets into the pond part, it won't come out, and it won't be crystal clear anymore. By the time my boys finished playing with it all, none of it was salvageable.

Overall, this is a really fun set of experiments! We had fun with it!
text_fidelity_b: Scientific Explorer Ice Age Creator Kit

ALEX Toys Super Art Table with Paper Roll Kids Art Supplies This table is really easy to put together, and it didn't take long at all. It even comes with a screwdriver to put the pieces that hold the paper roll onto the bottom of the table. All of the legs screw right into the table.

The directions say to place a plastic ring onto the leg before screwing it into the table/bench. I looked and looked and had decided they had been left out of my box. I finally discovered they were all already on the legs. Save yourself some time, and check the legs first.

Be careful picking the table up. I cut my finger on the bottom of the table, where the opening is for the paper. As long as your children aren't playing underneath the table and moving it around, it shouldn't be an issue for them, though.

Each bench will only hold 2 normal sized children. It's easy to look at the picture and think that 3 children will fit on each bench, but only 2 will.

It's a cute table set, and my children have already fallen in love with it. My 2 year old has repeated over and over, "It's cute! Cute, cute, cute!". They've enjoyed creating art at their new table!

text_fidelity_a:
Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure (Due to the malfunctions on our particular dog, and the fact that he doesn't walk at all, I was tempted to give it 3 stars, but he's so cute and fun, I went with 4.)

I have a few Paw Patrol fans in my house, so this is a pretty amazing toy.

By pressing the badge on the front of Chase, your children are given a mission. Chase talks and interacts through these missions. For example, chickens have gotten loose, and your child needs to help gather them up. The net compartment opens up, and your child will fire the net out. Chase comments on catching one, and then asks for the net to be reloaded. (One time the net got stuck, and didn't fire out, but he still exclaimed praise at catching a chicken, so it's not perfect.) He won't interact to various things that your child says, but he does have built in interaction, which is still pretty cool.

There are 24 different missions, and Chase moves around a bit through these. I was expecting him to walk a bit, but he never did. He just moves his head around, and moves from crouching to standing positions. There are two compartments on his backpack. One has a net launcher. The other has a microphone(that your child can talk into) and a flashlight. There are various buttons for each feature. (One for opening each compartment, one on the net launcher to launch, one to make the light come on the flashlight, and one to turn on the microphone.) Some of the items come on automatically through missions, but others require your child's assistance, when Chase asks.

Although this is an awesome toy that I'm pretty sure any Paw Patrol fan will love, we did have a couple of negatives with ours.

When the box was first opened, the head was detached a bit, but thankfully, it went back on pretty easily. Also, the button to launch the microphone/flashlight wouldn't work. I tried everything I could to make it work, short of tearing it apart, and tried numerous times, but it never worked. It didn't work when it was supposed to automatically open during missions, either. Thankfully, we can just pull that compartment open. During missions when a child is asked to launch the microphone/flashlight, pulling open the door makes the task recognized, just as if the button worked. So, it's not a huge deal, but still disappointing.

I really do wish he walked a bit, too! The way he's designed, it looked as if he would.

A couple of notes:
-This toy DOES come with batteries, but require 4 AA if you'd like to buy extras.
-If your child can read, know that the box this is delivered in says what's inside, though there are no pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Paw Patrol Mission Chase Figure

SpongeBob SquarePants Operation Game Before having children, Spongebob was one of my favorite cartoons. Though, admittedly, he gets on my nerves now, my children occasionally watch a Spongebob adventure, and they were super excited about this game.

The whole game is on the simple side. You'll need a phillips head screwdriver in order to put in 2 AA batteries(NOT included!). Put the pieces in the correct spot, and then you're good to go. You can play solo, or multiple players can take turns. It's pretty easy, so even younger players can be successful at it.

Just like the game, the board is on the simple side. It's lightweight, and nothing fancy. We've had a Buzz Lightyear version of this game in the past, and the quality of the two are very similar. The tweezers are attached to the board, so that makes it much less likely to get lost.

The "organs" are very small, as most probably already know, so make sure you use caution if little ones are around that still put things in their mouth.
text_fidelity_b: SpongeBob SquarePants Operation Game

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats This is seriously one of the cutest games ever! I love the variety within it, too.

First of all, the anteaters themselves are very well made! You get two of them. Sometimes you get "masks" and they're pretty crappy, but these are quality. To wear these, there's two felt-like straps that will fit along the back of a child's head, along with velcro piece at the end of one strap. This means it will fit pretty much any child's head, because you can tighten or loosen as much of the strap as you want. There's another piece of velcro attached to the underside of the anteater's snout. This is what picks up the felt-like ants. Super, super cute!

Within this set is also the instructions, of course, along with a timer and a set of cards. These cards are similar to the cards within most matching games out there. We have several of them. They are small, square, and thick. One side of each of them simply shows an anteater at a picnic. The other side either shows various types of food for a matching game(This is also great for speech development!), or one or the other side of a colorful ant. This is also for matching, and a great way for the youngest players to learn colors. There are also a few "tummy ache" cards, which shows a sick anteater. A player will lose cards they've matched when this card comes into play.

You can really mix and match the various games in any way you want, especially depending on the ages involved. You can simply play "hide and seek" with the ants, or allow a player to find an ant once they find a match within the cards, or find the color of the ant they've matched together. You can add the timer for the older players or just to add a bit more challenge, if desired. You can also simply play a matching game with the cards for a quieter game. There are many possibilities for playing this game, so I imagine it will take longer to get "old" for most little ones.

Overall, this is a wonderful game, and one of the most fun ones we've had the pleasure of playing!
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Anteater Antics Action Game With 2 Plush Hats

text_fidelity_a:
Pass the Stache Board Game The purpose of this game is pretty much to match "moustaches" with cards. Each player picks a "moustache" and holds it under their nose during the game. When a card is turned over that matches their chosen "moustache", they slam it down on the card, causing the attached suction cup to attach to that card.

It's a great memory game! If the player smashes the wrong card, they lose 2 of their winning cards. Each player has to remember which one(style and color) they have under their nose. It's also great for motor skills, since they have to aim for the card, possibly in a race against another person.

I was pleasantly surprised at how sturdy the "moustaches" actually are. (The handles remind me of a kitchen spoon/spatula handle.) The "moustaches" are larger than I expected and they're a sturdy rubber material. There are 6 different shapes/styles in 3 different colors(black, yellow, and brown).

I've had lots of fun playing this game with my newly 6 year old(delayed) and my 3 year old. My 19 month old has had fun, too, but he doesn't play by the rules. ;) This is a great game for some family fun. Laughs are pretty much guaranteed!
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

The Learning Journey: Learn With Me - Color Fun Fish Bowl - Color Teaching Toddler Toys & Gifts for Boys & Girls Ages 2 Years and Up - Preschool Learning Toy, Multicolor I thought this would be a fun learning activity for my 18 month old while I have “school” with my 3 and 5 year olds. BraveRats - A Game by Seiji Kanai After attempting to play this game, I was confused. Honestly, I went to look around at reviews to see what I was missing. Really, once the initial confusion is dealt with, this is a fun little game!

text_fidelity_a:
BOOMco. Rapid Madness Blaster (Discontinued by manufacturer) I'm just combining my thoughts on the various guns and products into one review, in case anyone would like to do a bit of comparing in one spot.

Darts:

The darts are kind of like a third of a straw, with a cool rubber-like tip. These tips ONLY stick to the special targets, which are on the shields(both the wearable ones and the ones that attach to the guns). There are also targets that stick to the wall. (I just taped the top of these targets, as opposed to sticking the whole thing on the wall.) We tested these out on mirrors and windows. They really don't stick to anything, but the special targets.

They're mostly bright colored, which makes it easier to find them once they've been shot. You'll have to take several time outs just to gather darts.

This company has made it perfectly clear that these darts are NOT made for little ones. I just want to reinforce that. I have an 18 month old that puts things in his mouth constantly. We found a large rock in his poo diaper. :S These are simply irresistible to him with their chewy rubber tip. He's chewed the tops off a few of them, even when we were trying to keep a close eye on him. The tops DO come off when chewed on, so these are definitely a choking hazard for little ones.

I try to teach our boys to never aim a gun at anyone, but I've been hit with a few of the darts. One hurt, but the others didn't. I think it depends on how close the gun is, and simply how the dart hits a person. In general, they don't seem to hurt too much.

Other than chewing, they seem pretty sturdy, though. They're had lots of use and bending, but they still work in the guns.

Farshot Blaster:

This is the smallest gun in this line(that we have...there seems to be a smaller "clipfire"). You pull back the top to "pump it up". It will only hold 1 dart at a time for shooting, but 2 spares fit in the bottom of the gun.

This gun is the easiest to aim, as far as target practice, and if that's what you'd like it for, I'd recommend this one. I've found it to be a great stress reliever. When the little ones are creating chaos, I can pull out this gun, tape a target to the wall, and do a little target practice.

Twisted Spinner Blaster:

This is the medium sized gun in this line. To shoot it, you pull an arm on the gun back towards yourself. The darts are loaded in the round end. It will hold 8 darts. As with all the guns, it comes with removable shields.

This one is a little harder to aim, but it's still fun.

Rapid Madness Blaster:

This is the largest gun in this line. You push and pull an arm to pump it up. The trigger is super sensitive, so it takes a couple of seconds to shoot all 20 darts that it holds. Those darts are held in a clip that slides into the side of the gun. This one is the most fun, BUT you don't get much shooting time before having to round up darts.

Bandolier:

This is an adjustable strap that you can wear across your body. It has a special target that the darts will stick to. It will also hold 12 extra darts.

Eye goggles:

These are pretty cool. As advertised, they won't fog up. They're made of a thick-like plastic/rubber, and give you "bug vision". They're also adjustable. My little ones are younger than the recommended age, but the clip kept coming off with them, and we put the goggles back together so much that I wanted to throw them away. Educational Insights Shelby’s Snack Shack Game and Board Book Combo: Preschool Math Game, Board Game & Board Book, Ages 4+ We'd already bought the Sneaky Squirrel Game, which is similar to this game. We've though it was one of the cutest games ever, so we were thrilled to add this one to our collection, too!

With this game, you'll get one of the cutest boxes you've ever seen! (Let me note here that the top and bottom of the game box do NOT fit inside each other. It's the same with the squirrel game.) You'll also get a super cute pair of Shelby tweezers, 4 bowls, a packet of bones, and a double spinner.

Playing the game is pretty simple. There can be up to 4 players at a time. Each player will spin first to see if they will get bones or lose bones or just lose a turn. The second spin is to determine how many bones they will win/lose. If they land on a seagull, it means they will lose bones. If they land on the hungry pug, they get to steal bones from another player. Busy pug means they lose a turn, and landing on the bones mean they win bones for their bowl. They can pick up the bones they win/lose with the tweezers.

The tweezers are a great way to develop motor skills. The game itself is a great, fun way to learn counting skills. My 5 year old is delayed and really struggles with numbers, so I'm always thrilled to find a new, exciting way to teach them to him. This is also a fun game for my 2 year old. It IS pretty simple, so I imagine, on average, 2-4, maybe 5, is probably the best ages for this game.

Overall, this is a super cute game! I can highly recommend this AND the Sneaky Squirrel Game for your young little ones!

You get 4 cards that have a raccoon in his/her underwear. (There are no bras on the underwear cards, just underwear/panties) The basic raccoon cards all look the same, though. The face on the raccoon is a plastic piece that's raised off the card. The outfit cards have a hole where the face goes, so the outfit cards actually fit right onto the raccoon card.

Your little ones will roll two dice. They will get a color and a piece of clothing to look for. For example, if they roll a red and a picture of pants, they will look for a card with a red pair of pants on it. The child that gets 5 outfit cards first, wins.

So, it's a quick game. My 2 year old has a tiny attention span right now, and there's very few games that hold his attention. This game is a good choice for him. It's teaching him his colors, taking turns, types of clothing, counting. It's a wonderful little game!

It's also fun for my 5 year old, but he is delayed. I imagine the perfect average ages for this game is 2-4 years old. It's pretty simple for an older child.

Overall, this is a very cute game, and I highly recommend it for little ones just learning to play games!
