Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up My oldest son(5) recently started daily injections. As you would expect, he hates them. We try to do something fun after each of them, and this was used as one of his "surprises". It did the trick and took his mind off that mean needle.

This game is really fun! Not only did my children enjoy it, but I did, too. It does come with a few issues, though.

First of all, as I put the thing together, the instructions say to never use your mouth to blow up the balloon. You must use a balloon pump. A balloon pump isn't included, so I chose to use my mouth to blow up the balloon, since I had excited children waiting to play. It went fine. I was able to blow up the balloon while it was in the frame without any problem.

Secondly, we couldn't get the top clip piece to stay put. There's a clip that holds the 3 pieces of the frame together at the top. It kept coming lose no matter how tight I tried to get it. When I took the thing apart, I couldn't get one frame piece to come apart. So, 2 were so lose the whole thing kept coming apart, but one was so tight I had to put it in the box together, and therefore, couldn't close the lid.

Third, one of the sticks was broke within minutes of playing the game. Thankfully, there are 4 extras included, so we can still play. Plus, the recommended age is 8 and up. I played this game with my 2 and 5 year olds. The 2 year old is the one that broke the stick, so I'm not taking stars off for that issue or anything. It's simply to warn you that they do break pretty easily.

There are 12 balloons included. They are all the same: blue, with a face. They are the regular sized balloons, so I imagine this game will work perfectly fine with store bought replacement balloons. You just probably won't have a face on there.

I know it sounds like a lot of complaining up there, but we really enjoyed this game!

The basics: You put the thing together, which is really simple. You put the balloon in the frame, blow it up, and then wrap it around the "hook" at the bottom to keep the air in without having to actually tie it. Super simple. You take the sticks and put them in the holes(6) until you hear the first click. Then you take turns rolling dice. Whatever number it lands on is the amount of times you push in a stick. It can be the same stick or one click each on different sticks. Whoever pops the balloon first loses(or wins if you're my children).

Overall, it's a fun game that's worth the issues that come with it.
text_fidelity_b: Boom Boom Balloon, Exciting Anticipation Family Board Game Outdoor Summer Toy, for Kids Ages 8 and up

You're working those brain cells to build these railways! There's a booklet included with lots of different railways to build. It gives you step by step instructions by picture. You DO have to pay close attention to what color block you place where, and where the holes line up, and how many blocks you use. It all has to line up just right. That said, I wouldn't call this a difficult toy at all. It *will* exercise the mind, though.

I like using it with my 5 year old. It's helping him to follow directions. Of course, I still have to help a great deal. It's also helping him with counting, which he struggles with. It's helping my 2 year old learn his colors. Plus, we're ALL learning patience! ;) These railways fall down pretty easily, since it's basically stacking blocks on top of each other. Honestly, for most 2-3 year olds, I think this thing probably isn't the best idea just yet. For older children, it's wonderful. It has potential to grow with them for *years* to come. My ONLY complaint with this thing is the fact that the marbles have nothing to catch them as the come out of the final holes/blocks. They just roll away. We have a 7 month old that crawls everywhere and puts everything in his mouth. We're always careful, but playing with this thing, we have to be extraordinarily careful, especially due to the free rolling marble issue. So far, we haven't came up with a "catching place" for those last marbles, but I'm sure we will in time. We just can't use all the marbles at one time, and keep a close count on what we do use.

The extra caution we have to use is WELL worth it, though!!

Fisher-Price Little People Fun Sounds Farm The "Little People" toys are favorites at our house. We have quite a few of them, including an older version of this barn. They're fun, educational, and classic. They're toys you can't go wrong with!

This barn is really simple to put together! While my husband put together a train set, I got the easy way out with this toy! Almost all the pieces simply pop into place. The only thing that requires a screwdriver is the two screws that hold the ladder in place on the back of the barn.

This set comes with the barn, 3 fence pieces, a bale of hay, a farmer, chicken, horse, sheep, and cow. There's different little activities you can do with the bale of hay.

There are certain places that trigger sound. The sound isn't overly annoying or loud. Of course, I prefer toys with no sound at all(life is loud enough with 3 boys!), but I can easily deal with this toy.

Overall, I have no reason to not recommend it! There are very few children who wouldn't love playing with animals and a barn! There's lots of room for imaginative play here! Plus, I love that there are other toys that we can "add on" to this set. We already have a tractor that goes perfectly with it.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Little People Fun Sounds Farm

text_fidelity_a:
Thomas & Friends TrackMaster, Castle Quest Set You just can't go wrong with a train set for children! With 3 little boys, trains are extra special in our house.

Thankfully, my husband put this train set together. The first time takes awhile since you're learning the pieces. You WILL need the instructions, or at least the picture to look at. Make sure you don't immediately throw everything away. Putting it together gets easier and easier each time. If your little ones are like mine, they will feel the need to take it apart time and time again. :) Otherwise, the set up is super simple.

The train itself stays on the track very well, but once we hooked the wagon part on the back, we couldn't seem to keep it on the track. It kept running off. That's my only complaint with this set. We don't *need* the wagon to enjoy, though. Of course, if you're actually playing with the crown, you will, but the crown got misplaced pretty quickly at our house. Those small extra pieces really don't stand a chance at our house most the time.

Overall, this is a train set that we really enjoy, and recommend! It's the second of the "Thomas" sets that we've added to our collection. We like them!
text_fidelity_b: Thomas & Friends TrackMaster, Castle Quest Set

text_fidelity_a:
Mattel Hot Wheels Ballistiks Rapid Fire Blaster Playset My two oldest sons loved this thing when we first got it. They took turns "shooting" it. The car wouldn't open very often, though.

It requires batteries, which are *not* included. It seems to work just fine without them, though. When I first opened up the package, I didn't have any batteries handy, so I handed it to my excited little ones anyway. There's a lever to pull that shoots out the car.

I wish this "set" came with at least one more car. You only get the one!

This isn't a toy that will keep kids these days happy for long. It's one of those toys to hide and bring out occasionally when you need to keep them occupied for a few minutes.

Fisher-Price Disney's Jake & The Never Land Pirates, Hook's Jolly Roger Pirate Ship We got the Bucky ship a couple of months ago, and since my oldest(4 1/2) is a huge fan of "Jake and the Neverland Pirates", he fell in love with it. It is still one of his most played with toys! He loves it, so you can imagine his excitement of adding The Jolly Roger and Captain Hook to his collection! He adores playing with both of them together now. They both use the same missiles, so he can shoot them back and forth between the ships. We've even had fun playing the "missile" game with him.

While the Bucky ship has sound effects, The Jolly Roger doesn't. It's smaller and quieter(and less expensive) than Bucky. I do recommend them together, though, based on how well my son likes to play with them at the same time. This is especially true if you have more than one Neverland fan!

Overall, we adore these toys, and highly recommend them for the "Jake and the Neverland Pirate" fans.

iTikes Map This is such an amazing educational toy! My 4 year old is already learning new words. He's learning about different cultures and animals. He was thrilled that there is a solar system map included, since he is obsessed with all things concerning the solar system right now.

There are 6 maps included:
Solar System
Dinosaurs
World Cats
World Dogs
World Facts
World Music

There are a few things that could use improvement, though. If you don't keep the thing turned upright, the maps will fall out. The clear top won't latch very well. If your little ones happen to turn it upside down, you'll most likely be picking up maps. Also, there is a slight delay between touching the stylus on a picture and anything being said. My son got a little impatient sometimes. At times, I even wondered if it was working. There were also times that we touched the picture over and over before it would work.

Overall, while it can be annoying at times with not working right, I found it worth it due to the educational/fun value. Getting my son to sit still and learn is a huge deal! :)
text_fidelity_b: iTikes Map

text_fidelity_a:
Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck My boys love this thing! They are 1(average for age) and 4(very small), but they are about the same size. It's the perfect size for both of them, but it is on the small size. I don't think it will be too long before they get too big for it. Of course, another little will be right behind them to give it more use!

They have so much fun with it, of course I recommend it. But, there are a few MINOR negative issues I have with it.

-Keep the instructions initially! Getting that handle attached is more difficult than it would seem. Also, you want to have some strong hands close by to push in the wheels. It was extremely hard for me to get them to pop in. I do admit my hands are pretty weak, and I am an exhausted pregnant momma. The average person might not have trouble with them, but I'd be on the safe side. :)

-There are little velcro strips on the bottom that is suppose to keep the cloth in place. It doesn't work for us. It keeps coming loose as the boys play, and we have to constantly reattach it. Thankfully, it's not long enough to drag the floor too bad, so it doesn't create a tripping hazard.

-My boys do tip off the back a good bit while riding. Since it's so small, it has never caused them harm. They jump back up and keep playing. I do think it surprised them the first couple of times, but they are used to it by now. It might not be the best toy for really young children just learning coordination, though.

Overall, despite my small complaints, I still think this is a great toy that will provide lots of fun!
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Pillow Racers Fire Truck

text_fidelity_a:
Puzzle Conserver, 200 ml I tested this conserver out on a cheap puzzle just to get a good idea of what it was like.

Make sure you shake the bottle well. I purposely left a spot kind of bubbly just to see if it would dry smooth. It does NOT! (as I'm sure most of us suspected) You need to spend time smoothing it out. Even the spots that I worked at smoothing out dried a little "smeary", but from a distance you can't tell. You also need to work at getting it in the cracks.

It dries quickly. The bottle says to wait about an hour for drying. It also recommends using the whole bottle within 12 months for best results, so it does last a decent amount of time.

Overall, this is a decent puzzle conserver(coming from an amateur puzzle conserver).
text_fidelity_b: Puzzle Conserver, 200 ml

text_fidelity_a:
Alex Little Hands String A Farm Kids Toddler Art and Craft Activity My oldest(4) is receiving occupational therapy at the moment, and this toy is perfect for that cause. I do have to admit that it's lost its challenge for him pretty quickly, though. He does still enjoy it!

At my youngest son's 18 month appointment, it was requested that we work on his motor skills, so this toy is even more appropriate for him. It's still challenging for him. More than anything, he enjoys pulling the beads on the string around in the floor like a train. It's a good thing that it's durable! It's also great for teaching him animals, sounds, counting, and even promoting language.

Overall, this is one of those toys you just can't go wrong with! It seems very durable, like most wooden toys, and both of my boys have found lots of ways to enjoy it. I'd say it's probably best for 1 and 2 year olds(a little older if there's a delay of any kind).

text_fidelity_a:
Dragon Nursery 24 Piece Floor Puzzle This is a beautiful, high quality puzzle. I have 2 boys(4 and 1), and they aren't always the most easy on their toys. I like that the puzzle pieces are big(much bigger than I expected!), thick, AND they are easy to wipe off. It's like this puzzle was made just for my boys! ;)

My oldest(delayed educationally) is way past the big wooden puzzles, but not quite ready for the smaller jigsaw puzzles. This is the perfect intermediate puzzle for him. While it's still too advanced for my 1 year old, he still enjoys "helping" and seeing the picture come together.

This is a floor puzzle, because it is pretty big as far as puzzles go(3ft by 2ft), but we actually prefer just putting it together on the table.

If you are one who likes to conserve puzzles once they are put together, this puzzle creates a beautiful picture! It would be great for a little boy's room. We enjoy this one so much, though, that we're going to keep using it for awhile.

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3) This is one cool Mickey! In fact, he's so cool his "ice cream doesn't melt"! (one of his cheesy phrases, not mine) Seriously, this has to be one of the coolest toys ever. Not only do both of my boys(16 months and 3 3/4 years) like it, but my husband and I love him, too. Whenever we have visitors, we have to pull this Mickey out, just to show him off. Sad, but true. One day, my 11 year old nephew was over here, and he even commented that this is the "coolest Mickey ever", and his little brother has the original dancing Mickey. I'm not familiar with the other dancing Mickeys, but apparently this one has more features.

My only complaint is the batteries, which really can't be helped with the kind of toy it is. This is more of simply a warning for you than a complaint. This Mickey really sucks the power out of batteries! He takes 6 AA batteries. He does come with a set, but they will wear off REALLY quickly. I would definitely have a high quality set of batteries waiting nearby. When the batteries get low, he will keep moving, but he won't be able to do the really fancy moves, like the handstand, and leg spins. Those are my favorite, so it's disappointing when I don't get to see those. ;)

To make him dance, all you have to do is press his nose. He will only do one set of dance moves and then he will tell you if you want to see more, just press his nose. He turns off pretty quickly. I'm sure this is so he won't use up the batteries even quicker. I like that he's smart, too. When he falls over, he asks for help getting up. When you help him up, he says, Thanks, pal!". There is an on/off switch on the back of his head. I have to make use of this switch when my youngest takes a nap.

Overall, if you don't mind the big investment price and the many batteries he will require, we HIGHLY recommend this Mickey!
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Master Moves Mickey (M3)

text_fidelity_a:
Fisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Musical Pirate Ship Bucky [Amazon Exclusive] My oldest son turns 4 in just over a week, and he absolutely LOVES this toy! It's one of the few toys that he goes back for again and again.

There are two doors on the ship. One is to the back of the cabin and one is over "tick-tock"(the crocodile) who pops out with the press of a button. These doors come off pretty easily, BUT they pop right back on just as easily. There's also 3 "missiles" that shoot out of the cannon on the front of the boat with the press of a button. These worked great for us, but to be honest, those small pieces get lost pretty quickly. My son usually plays with the ship without those.

My favorite feature is the pegs that are placed ALL over the ship. There are little holes on the bottom of Jake and Skully's feet, so you can place them on the pegs and hold them in place while playing. There's even a little clear bar at the very top of the ship that you can put them on, so it looks like they're flying. I think it's a really cool feature!! I also really like the "rocking" motion of the ship when it moves. It kind of wobbles back and forth to look like it's floating on waves.

My only complaints is the sound, first of all. The music sounds kind of like it's coming from cheap speakers, and I find it annoying. My son loves it and likes to press the buttons to hear the music and phrases. If you really didn't like that feature, the batteries could be taken out. (I haven't resorted to that, but it is an option, since my son knows how to swap the on/off switch). Secondly, I do wish that this set also came with Izzy and Cubby, instead of just Jake and Skully. There are stickers on the side of the boat of Izzy and Cubby to look like they are looking out the window waving. I guess that's an attempt to make up for not having them as figurines. I know that you can buy separate figurines, but I don't know if they have pegs on the bottom of their feet to work with this ship.

Overall, our whole family gives it 2 thumbs up! We all love it, and definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Musical Pirate Ship Bucky [Amazon Exclusive]

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over

Ravensburger Deco Mandala-Designer Drawing Machine My rating is probably closer to 3.5 stars, but I'll go with 4.

This wasn't completely what I thought it was going to be. It doesn't do as much as I was expecting. I wanted it to make greeting cards with it, but my results looked less professional than I had hoped. Don't get me wrong. I wasn't expecting anything magnificent, but I thought it would look better than what I ended up with. That could be more my fault than anything else, though.

The thing that I dislike the most is the type of pen you have to use. I wish it would work with colored pencils. You have to use a TINY pen with the stencils. You're suppose to color in after you've traced the stencil, but I think options would be so much greater if this product could be used with other things. My son really enjoyed playing with the stamp and butterfly punch. There's only one of each. A couple more stamps would have added to the fun! The paper it uses(comes with 10 sheets) is smaller than letter size, so you'll have to buy more or cut your paper to fit when you run out.

This product does need 4 AA batteries, so make sure you buy some of those, too!

Overall, it's fun to play with. I think younger girls would have a blast with it, and I do think they are its target age group. I feel like the price is a bit much for what it does, though.

Fisher-Price Imaginext Mega T-Rex My little boy is almost 3, and he loves this toy! My husband and I have even had fun with it, but probably just because our son gets so excited when the little missiles shoot up in the air. That would probably be the only warning I would have with it. For a toy, the missiles can go a good little distance, and could possible poke someone in the eye. The chances are most likely low, but it could happen.

The only thing that I somewhat didn't like is there's no directions. We just had to figure out on our own and by looking at picture on the box where the extras attached. It didn't take forever or anything, but it was annoying trying to guess at where the pieces went. That is a very minor issue, though!

The dinosaur doesn't really do a whole lot, but I think it's great for creative play. You have to hold the button down for it to roar, and as soon as you let go, it stops. As a parent, I actually really like that feature. I hate when you mash a button and have to listen to noise for several minutes. As I mentioned earlier, there are two missiles that you can launch into the air. There's also a little man that rides on the dinosaur's back. He sits in a compartment. The little flap that keeps him in this compartment comes off really easily and that annoyed my son, but it goes back on easily, too.

We like this toy so much for my son that we're planning on adding to our collection from the same line of toys this Christmas.

text_fidelity_a:
Easy Bake Ultimate Oven, Pink/Purple I got the Easy Bake Ultimate Oven for my little boy. What woman doesn't love it when a man can cook?! ;) He's almost 3, so not quite the targeted age, but we still had fun with it.

What we like:
-I like that it's purple, which is a LITTLE bit more on the neutral side.
-It cooks very quickly. You preheat for 20 minutes and then cook an average of 10 minutes or so. You get exact directions, though. I was expecting a MUCH longer cook time.

What we didn't like:
-You can't watch the food while it cooks. I wish the front was clear, and it would have made this a much better learning tool, and made it a lot more fun.
-The portions are TINY! Seriously, I don't think it would fill up a mouse! But, I guess I have to expect tiny portions for it to cook so quickly. And, I think it's more of a "time together" kind of activity!

Just some neutral information we learned. You can cook "regular" food in the oven. If you're like us, you can't pay a lot of money for tiny mixes that produce 1/10th of the size of a normal cookie. Just save a little batter from when you cook. I also learned that you CAN burn food in this oven. :) So make sure you set a timer.
The pictures in the directions have cute, perfect little cookies and cupcakes. Ours didn't even come close to looking that great. Maybe with a little more practice?!
This oven comes with a batch of cookies and cupcakes w/frosting, sugar crystals, and cupcake wraps. It also has two cooking pans and an "arm" to push the pans into the oven. It has spots marked to make sure you get them to the correct spot to cook and cool. Overall, we've had a lot of fun with it!

And this is probably obvious, but it's electric. ;)
text_fidelity_b: Easy Bake Ultimate Oven, Pink/Purple

text_fidelity_a:
Magnatab — A to Z Uppercase — Activity for Fun and Learning — Sensory Activity — Ages 3+ SUMMARY
This is a fun and clever toy that can really help kids learn their letters. It certainly captures their attention initially but after 2 days it doesn't seem to be interesting any more. For longer term interest I would suggest the Magnatab that is more of a doodle pad. It is a durable toy and looks like it would stand up in a classroom. However, the magnetic stylus is not attached to the rest of the toy and could very easily be lost.

FULL REVIEW

KIDS COMMENTS
My kids want you to know that they like the sound that the beads make when they pop up and they like how the beads "appear" when they put the magnet to them.

FORM - A+
This toy is nicely sized. It perfectly fits in an adult or child's lap and has a nice curved edge around the back that makes it nice to hold. The letters are nicely sized and spaced on the board. The stylus is comfortable in the hand and easy for little fingers to hold without being bulky. The slot that the stylus fits into for storage is super clever and has a magnet that holds it in place. In concept and usage I like this better than a stylus attached with a string or plastic loop. However, practically, I'm afraid that the stylus will be lost since it is not attached to the rest of the toy.

DURABILITY - A-
I immediately gave this toy to 4 children, ages 7-18 months. They loved it for the first two days. It got tossed, sat on, fought over, and played with pretty constantly. The only problem that I saw was some faint smudging of the black print on the Magnatab. It looks like some excess toner being wiped or smudged across the surface. However, none of the print has come off yet and the direction arrows are still nice and dark. I believe this toy is durable enough to stand up in an education environment. Other than the stylus issues described above this toy would be a good investment for a school or day care.
text_fidelity_b: Magnatab — A to Z Uppercase — Activity for Fun and Learning — Sensory Activity — Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors The Alias is potentially a great example of the new generation of quadcopters with electronic flight control boards that provide six axis stabilization. When their transmitter control levers are properly trimmed at the beginning of each flight they will hover very stably and are easy to fly even for a beginner.

Unfortunately, LaTrax and Traxxas (LaTrax makes the product and Traxxas provides all customer support) released the Alias before they found a good quality motor that works properly with the Alias. Since the Alias uses four motors and is inoperable if any one of the motors fails this is a major problem.

My Alias flew great for the first two days, but then it became very unstable and flew unpredictably. After only the the sixth or eighth flight one of the motors failed and the Alias would not fly at all.

Traxxas told me the Alias does fly unpredictably when one of its motors is weakening and getting ready to fail. They said they would send me a free replacement motor, but so far it has not arrived. Looking at other Amazon reviews, and on the internet, I see that many other people have also had very early motor failures. I strongly recommend people should not buy the Alias until LaTrax and Traxxas have figured out the early motor failure problem, presumably by finding a better motor.

Update: January 14, 2014

After two initial days of use before one of the motors broke, I have been unable to fly my new Alias for two and a half weeks now. Traxxas keeps saying they will send me a new motor as soon as the most recent batch they received "gets through quality control". I fear I have wasted $150 to buy the Alias.

Update January 20, 2014

After three weeks Traxxas finally sent me a replacement motor ....drum roll.....however, they sent the wrong motor! Traxxas checked their records, agreed they had sent the wrong motor, and promised to send the correct motor. I am pleased they are trying to provide good customer service, but I am now in my fourth week without being able to fly my otherwise excellent Alias after one of its motors broke on the second day after I opened it at Christmas.
text_fidelity_b: Traxxas 6608 LaTrax Alias Quad-Rotor Ready-to-Fly Helicopter, Assorted Colors

text_fidelity_a:
Skull Party Game | Bluffing Game | Strategy Game | Fun Game for Game Night | Family Board Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 13+ | 3-6 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Space Cowboys I really loved this game. Will disclose, I've only played it once since I've got it, but it was very fun that one time.

It takes what I love from Liar's Dice, but gives it more suspense in my opinion. Liar's Dice can reach a point where for certain someone is losing a die, but in Skull, sometimes, it's just a challenge of what you pick up, and who you know for a fact has a skull on their mat. I love the suicide bluffs people pull with putting a skull down then bidding, and the whole bidding idea is really fun to me too.

The art is really pretty, though there are a few skulls I think that look more boring than others, all look good. The material is a hard cardboard with great texturing, feels like a coaster almost, I think it can be very durable, but getting them out of their original squares was a little bit of a challenge to not tear any. I also love how small the box is, you could carry this to any place you want rather easily. I almost am a little sad that it only has enough for 6 players, I could easily see this going further than 6 players, but playing with 6 players, it was very fun. I loved every second.

I rate this highly because I love the set, but I will admit, this game could be easily played with cards instead of this. It wouldn't be difficult not even slightly, with no rules adaptations other than changing the skulls to faces, and flowers to numbers. That shouldn't dissuade you from purchasing this though, this is a really cool set, that will last a good amount of time, and it is a nice bit of decoration anyway with that pretty box! This will likely become a board game of mine to play whenever I can, for a very long time.
text_fidelity_b: Skull Party Game | Bluffing Game | Strategy Game | Fun Game for Game Night | Family Board Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 13+ | 3-6 Players | Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Space Cowboys

text_fidelity_a:
Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera After getting an X12 over Christmas, and having an absolute blast crashing into everything while learning to fly indoors, I decided it was time to see what it was like outside. Flying an X12 outside left something to be desired, so I began researching to figure out what might fit the bill. After reading MANY reviews and watching a ton of videos, I chose the X5c. It fit my budget, and I got the impression that it truly was a great quad to learn on.

Well, after only a few short months of owning it I can say with certainty that the X5 has certainly held up its end of the bargain, and then some. I say "X5", and not X5"c", because the camera that comes with this thing is pretty lame. The angle (or field of vision, if you prefer) is very narrow. And I don't know if this is simply an issue with Macs, but I had to reformat the SD-card all the time- simply deleting files didn't work. Otherwise, the camera would believe that there wasn't enough space on the card and wouldn't record. So, this made it very easy for me to make the decision to jettison the camera all together, and just let this bird fly free. And I didn't stop there... the feet were no longer necessary either, so away they went too. The prop guards? Never even bothered attaching them to begin with. Flying this thing was kinda fun before getting rid of that stuff, but it became much more fun without the extra baggage.

From the beginning, I chose to learn on "advanced mode", just because it was faster, more responsive, and more challenging. However, I was by no means "advanced" at flying these things. The first time I took it anyplace that wasn't my tiny front yard, I took it to a local park and flew it up kinda high. Well, then I experienced that common thing where you kinda get disoriented with where the quad is in relation to nearby trees, and somehow I flew it into some woods with it impacting the first few branches at around 50 feet. Somehow, by some miracle, the thing didn't get hung up in any of those branches- I'm attributing that to the fact that it was still winter time (not many leaves to help hold it there)... so, where does it ultimately land? Where else, than in a creek? Yup! Brand new lil quad... in the creek. I just took a big deep breath and hung my head when I realized this. Somehow the thing was still on when I fished it out (it never completely submerged- landed in shallow area). I immediately turned it off and removed the battery before shaking it out best I could. Then I brought it home, opened it up, and placed it on the floor about a foot away from a space heater to allow it to dry out for the rest of the day. The next morning, I put everything back together, popped the recharged battery back in, and everything worked perfectly. From then on, I became much more careful about flying at any sort of altitude that included potential trees... and creeks, for that matter. It also didn't take me long to see the need for more batteries. I bought one of the packages available here on Amazon, where it provides you with four batteries and a 4x1 charger to charge them all simultaneously. I also bought to extra batteries before getting the 4x1. So, now that I have 7 batteries, I find myself not only enjoying the thing more, personally, I also have found more time to teach others how to fly it.

O, and before I forget... another sad, yet awesome, thing that happened: I was on my way to go begin my marathon of marathon study sessions for finals when I stopped by at a nearby church to catch about 10 minutes of flight time. I parked in a different area than usual so that I could see what range I could accomplish, and then flew it back with more altitude and speed than I'd intended.... well, I didn't turn fast enough and right behind me was a nice tree waiting to catch the quad. It got stuck at probably 40 feet up. I found various things laying around to throw at it, and even when I hit it with a lightweight block of wood, the thing still didn't budge. I climbed as high as I could, but the branches became too thin and there was no one around to spot me if I fell. Not worth it. So, I just had to let it be. I thought to myself... o well, you need to study anyway. This thing was obviously only meant to be an ill-fated distraction. So I went on my way and decided that I'd re-evaluate the situation only after I'd gotten through at least half of the material I needed to cover. So, a week and several thunderstorms later, I returned to the scene to find the quad stil sitting up in the tree looking all happy. I devised a telescoping "pushstick" made out of an 8' cardboard tube and some quarter round. I tied a rope to it, climbed the tree as high as I could, and then managed to push the quad out of the tree after extending the "pushstick" to a length of almost 20 feet. Took the quad home, opened it up, and it was bone dry and with no signs of rust of weathering. I put it all back together, and it worked. No problems at all. It's amazing.

I've crashed this thing into everything except for myself or other people. I've let my dog chase it, and eventually she even got ahold of it. Still, the quad survives. It slammed into a road sign at full speed earlier today. It survives. I've put this thing through tons of punishment, and thus far, the only thing I've needed to replace is two of those tiny cogs/gears at the bottom of the motor (the ones that engage with the larger gears that actually spin the props). These smaller gears seem to have a tendency to slip over time, and then they fall off. I've gotten into the habit of performing a little flight check before each flight, and confirming that those are properly seated seems to have made a big difference. Still, I have extras now. In anticipation of eventually burning out a motor, I also went ahead and purchased an extra CW and CCW motor. The nice thing about the prospect of changing out the motors is that the new ones have a metal gear that seems like it won't slip like the little plastic ones do. I dunno; we'll see.

I know I'll eventually destroy this thing, but OMG it blows my mind how much it's been through and is still going strong. I'd post a picture of how beat up it is, but I'm afraid it wouldn't really do it justice. It's scratched all over, one of the props was bent and then reshapaned before getting chewed on by my friend's cat. Still, the quad survives...

Once I finally burn out a motor or somehow destroy this thing, I'll update my review to let you know how it goes. Overall, I'm getting a lot of good times out of it. Still learning new ways to enjoy it. Definitely the start of a new hobby.
text_fidelity_b: Syma X5C 4 Channel 2.4GHz RC Explorers Quad Copter w/ Camera

Patchwork | Strategy / Puzzle Game | Family Board Game | Two Player Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 8 and up |Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Lookout Games , Brown Easy to learn, fast to play, and fraught with surprisingly difficult decisions. The basic premise of putting together a quilt becomes very complex when you're weighing interesting opportunity costs on every single action. At the end of the game, everything boils down to how many buttons you've collected versus how much space on your quilt is unpatched by the time you reach the end of game board with a finite number of spaces. Do I spend a small amount of buttons to fill a large section of my quilt? Do I spend more buttons to fill less quilt with a patch that gives me more income but may move me more towards ending the game too prematurely for victory? Do I not buy any patches, and just advance along the board and collect buttons? It's shockingly complex and interesting considering the simplicity of the mechanics.

I'm a big fan of two player games, as it's great for my wife and I to always have something to do together. This is particularly great for the two of us because set-up is fast and the rules are simple enough that you never waste time referencing the instructions. So we even get to play on busy weeknights.
text_fidelity_b: Patchwork | Strategy / Puzzle Game | Family Board Game | Two Player Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 8 and up |Average Playtime 30 Minutes | Made by Lookout Games , Brown

text_fidelity_a:
7 Wonders We're a game playing family. With 84 board/card games and counting, I feel like something of an expert on board games. This was an exceptionally good game. Unlike some strategy games, there doesn't seem to be any one strategy that's going to always work. You have to be flexible, depending upon which wonder you end up with, the cards you get, and the strategies your opponents are using. You have to pay particular attention to the strategies of your nearest neighbors on either side because many actions and many cards play off of them. No cards or actions play directly off of an opponent who is not your neighbor. That, too, is a nice feature. It's not that you shouldn't watch what the people across the table are doing, but it's more important to know what the guys to the right and left are doing. Especially when you're dealing with higher numbers of players, that makes it easier to keep up with. That's a big part of why it works as well for 7 players as it does for 3. That, and the fact that game play is simultaneous -- no turn taking! So there's very little down time and the games moves quickly.

The only reason I didn't give this game 5 stars is that the game comes with rules for a 2-player variation that I do not believe is very good. I was hoping that this would be a game I could play with my husband after our (young) kids went to bed, but after trying several times we both agreed on two things:

1) There are much better 2-player games.
2) This game is much better with 3-7 players.

For those reasons, we will only pull it out when we have friends over. But it really, really is a top-notch game for the right number of players. I mostly wrote this review to caution people who are considering buying it more for it's two-player extendability than anything else.
text_fidelity_b: 7 Wonders

text_fidelity_a:
FRR Torch My Blazin Dragon When I first saw this, I figured "Hey, that's a Furby". After seeing it use for a bit, I still have the same vibe (and for the record I found the Furby to be awesome), but it's really much more.

First off, it's absolutely adorable, and it looks better in person. Even without the interactive robotics, this would be a hit based purely on the looks. Those good looks come out in the packaging, which wasn't too painful to extract the dragon from. You will need a screwdriver and C batteries to bring it to life. Boy does it come to life. The "fire breathing" effect works well, though with caveats . For starters it needs water to create the effect and that means distilled water, filters, and refills. All in all it works.

It's a little rough around the edges if you're looking to critique the toy, but kids love it, as does the kid all of us.
text_fidelity_b: FRR Torch My Blazin Dragon

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Aquaticz 1 Hole Cornhole Water Ball Toss Game It doesn't take much to make an afternoon in the pool fun, but a little game to pass the time doesn't hurt. This gets the job done and it also works for the land lovers too (I'd use bean bags for that scenario). Do note that unlike typical "corn hole" games, here you get one target. That makes sense given the typical in pool use, but may surprise folks used to land games. There's nothing to stop you from buying two however.

Ideally there would be some form of anchor to stop these from floating all over, but there's not. Being what it is, it won't be hard to add some nylon rope tied to something heavy ish, which we did sealed plastic weights for canopy tent.

**update**
The bags that came with the [[ASIN:B01BEU874K Franklin Sports Aquaticz Bocce Set]] work great with this set!

I wish this had some floating bean bags, a second target, and an anchor. I imagine the first one is easy enough to DIY, but I haven't tried it. The other two are simple fixes. Anyway 4 stars, but no real faults.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Aquaticz 1 Hole Cornhole Water Ball Toss Game

text_fidelity_a:
Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd One day I'm gonna miss the fum little prisons that keep our little one out of harms way, but until that day, I love this little crate for children.

It's nothing revolutionary--hell, after my St Bernard grew tired of his crate I thought--damn, this would be great for children. Apparently someone else thought that, and from the likes of what's out there, a few others did as well. Anyway, we've evolved to the point where decorative monsters and fun colors make it seem more humane and fun and less "now I have my hands free to drink a beer" (note that I do not use this to support my drinking habits, as I'm ok with kids crawling on the dirt while I drink--I just hate doing added laundry). The monsters seem to amuse me more than junior, but perhaps that says something about the dark voices I hear rather than the artistic merits of the designers. I appreciate them nonetheless. The collapsing and folding bit is nice, so we can take it to family day at the demolition derby or one of those bikini car washes. The "sets up in under 1 minute" is true, but it's even quicker if you do it yourself (junior is still working on the hand-eye coordination) and you put down the beer. Best of all--the wheels! Why fold it up and take up all the space in your car for a car seat, when you can tie this to the back of the family truckster and give junior a chance to enjoy the great outdoors while you drive! The comprehensive padding (and bouncy floor) will come in handy when junior joins the toddler wrestling set, and future WWE fortunes will easily cover the modest investment in this play yard.

In all honestly, this is a nice play set. No kids gets were harmed, neglected, or otherwise in need of CPS. Have a great day.
text_fidelity_b: Cosco Funsport Deluxe Play Yard, Monster Syd

text_fidelity_a:
NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Professional Rock Tumbler Kit- Advanced features include Shutoff Timer and Speed Control - 2lb Barrel, 1lb Gemstones, 4 Polishing Grits, Jewelry Fastenings and Learning Guide This is a lot to pay for a rock tumbler, but ...

This is by far the best model I found complete with all of the bells and whistles, and is quiet (and gets quieter as the stones smooth out) to boot. You can set the number of days, it can handle a ton of rocks (well 2lbs), offers speed control, and protection against thermal overload (in case you put too much in there). I've had no leaks and while some of the stones are blah, many look amazing!

Do note this really takes patience, as the steps take days, but your simulating what may be decades of natural effects, so it's not that bad. The real benefit comes with interacting with your kids (or whomever you partake in this with), experiencing the science, and the thrill of the reveal. As noted in the Q&A section, you can use any rocks (up to a certain size) and grit. Thus you can use rocks you find in your travels!

Back to the price, if you compare it to other tumblers and even vaguely similar devices (for different purposes) such as marinading machines (yeah, there's such a thing), water tight tumbling devices that can hold pounds of stuff generally cost this much or more.
text_fidelity_b: NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Professional Rock Tumbler Kit- Advanced features include Shutoff Timer and Speed Control - 2lb Barrel, 1lb Gemstones, 4 Polishing Grits, Jewelry Fastenings and Learning Guide

It really does help capture some of that energy and work on some motor skills, but it's mostly a fun activity, and as a bonus the cats find it amusing.  It's not perfect however.  "Some assembly required" and "Batteries not included"--oh and they're D batteries.  The balls could fly a bit higher/further, and it's not a huge draw for kids. text_fidelity_a:
Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game At it's core it's what you expect--Monopoly. It has the classic game play at its heart, and if you like Monopoly but are looking for a change of pace, this is for you. If you don't like Monopoly, there are some game play changes (unlike some of the novelty sets), but it's still basically Monopoly.

The changes include the cosmetic ones (renamed spaces and restyles but well made pieces), as well as the passport idea. All in all its less cutthroat and more fun, but not that much more interesting than Monopoly. It'll get played again, but who knows when.

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended I'm not quite the telescope connoisseur, though I'm quite well versed in optics (avid photographer), and I've discovered there's a bit of a gulf between the "wouldn't it be nice to have a telescope" and those sold to diehard astronomers. This one falls into the former category, and as such I"m not really comparing this to higher end models.

In the lower end realm, I still expect clear optics, no noticeable optical defects, and a stable base. This one checks those boxes. The optics look clean and clear to the naked eye, though lab testing would show where higher end models excel, and it's not the brightest lens (all lenses lose some light due to transmission loss in lens materials and dispersal), but it met my expectations. The tripod is well built enough for this model telescope, but it's no remarkable. As it's geared towards budding astronomers, especially youngsters, the included guide and list of projects to get you going is definitely a strength.

4 stars due to no faults of it's own, though it's not that remarkable either. Recommended, though may want to consider other models.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos TK1 Telescope Plus Astronomy Educational Science Kit | Refractor 60/700 | Aluminum Full Size Tripod with Altazimuth Mount | 35X, 70X, 140X Power | Parents' Choice Recommended

text_fidelity_a: Avalon Hill Betrayal at House on the Hill, Green It's been ages since I've done any role playing save for on a computer (or in the bedroom ;-), and when it turned out that the monthly game night involved what essentially is role playing, it was like old times.  The game is rather simple in concept, though in execution it has nearly endless depth.  So many permutations can be played!  The nuances such as rolls and even the dice themselves (I never rolled a zero before) make it enjoyable whether you're having a good night or not.  Let's face it, some of the players will draw more powerful cards or characters, but you're never really out of it, well until you die.  Anyway, it's a fun game, and quite a departure from more traditional board games.  The overall setup is a blast too.
text_fidelity_b: Avalon Hill Betrayal at House on the Hill, Green

text_fidelity_a:
Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot We had the pleasure of playing this in our most recent game night, and it was delightful. You start with a few "quests" based on bamboo for pandas to eat, bamboo in the "fields", and the arrangement of those "field" tiles (as well as access to water ...). It's actually rather simple. Each turn you get to expand the game by adding field tiles (up adding water or other upgrades to the tiles), grow bamboo, have the panda eat the bamboo, or take on more "quests". As everything but the bamboo the panda eats belongs to everyone, there's a passive cooperation, and other than the score at the end (based on completing those cards), it doesn't feel that competitive. If another player lays down irrigation, that's not irrigation that solely benefits them or takes away from what you have, rather it adds to what you have and may well help complete one of your quests. We played with folks from 7 years old on up, and everyone had a great time.

The only real negative (and I don't see the need to deduct any stars from the rating) is that this is at max a four player game. I could'd imagine playing with less than 3, and 4 really is the sweet spot.
text_fidelity_b: Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot

text_fidelity_a: Fisher-Price Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, Silly Wheelie Mickey When I first saw this in the flesh, I must say I was impressed (and a little jealous).  It's bigger, heavier (in a good way), and more robust than what I imagined, and it seems really well built.  The toy is ready to go (batteries included) and seems built for real world use.  It works best on hard floors (laminate and wood especially), and the little rubber tracks in the rear wheel (which doesn't rotate as wheels do) do a good job of moving the bike, popping wheelies, and avoiding picking up too much of the hair and debris my St Bernard leaves in his wake.  Speaking of which, the big dog and cats love it too.  The toy moves better than you'd think, and it's every bit as durable as you'd like.  It does get stuck along the wall or fall over, but it keeps going.  Carpet doesn't work nearly as well as harder surfaces.  I wouldn't recommend it for carpet (unless the dense hard stuff). The bright colors and ever present Mickey marketing seem to help keep the kids going as well.  As noted in another review, this isn't really interactive or educational, but it's a fine toy.
text_fidelity_b: Fisher-Price Disney Mickey Mouse Clubhouse, Silly Wheelie Mickey

text_fidelity_a:
Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players My wife and I bought this as we are getting more into tabletop gaming (thanks Wil and Felicia!) and I wanted something adventurous and less involved than a city- farm- building simulation game.
This is fairly fun, but the main reason I am writing a review is to specify why I didn't give it four stars and who should get the most enjoyment out of it.
To start out, you choose (randomly for a bit of extra challenge) a character class. These are more realistic classes such as a SCUBA diver, rather than a mage or warrior. Each class has a different special ability, for example the diver can traverse water tiles more easily than other classes. Then you randomly generate the playing field by placing the heavier island cards in a specific formation. Combining the random character roles and the random board is a clever way to make every game different and make sure the players have to think critically rather than relying too much on rote strategies.
Your goal is to traverse the board to collect treasures, cooperating with your fellow players by using each person's ability and the convenience of their position on the board. You may even bail each other out of dire situations by airlifting them to safety or using your special ability, because while you are trying to reach the treasures the island is constantly flooding.
If you ever wanted to play Indiana Jones this is a pretty good start. But for my wife and I to keep it interesting, we have to play on the hardest difficulty level (starting out with more of the island in a flooded state) and even still we have succeeded at our task 100% of the time. Because of this, the game gets old too quickly, which is a shame since the premise is fun, the concept is exciting, the gameplay is perfectly tight, and the artwork is gorgeous.
I do think there is a more appropriate audience for this, which is kids of perhaps 9 years to 13 years playing with other kids or in a mixed group with adults. I think the game will be more challenging for kids and I think playing with kids will make it more fun for the parents/cousins/uncles and aunts etc.
For two adults who are strategy-oriented people, there are more complicated games that are perhaps less beautiful and tightly designed but nonetheless more consistently engaging.
text_fidelity_b: Forbidden Island – The Cooperative Strategy Survival Island Board Game,2-4 players

text_fidelity_a:
Cephalofair Games: Gloomhaven, Award-Winning Strategy Board Game, For 1 to 4 Players, 60 to 120 Minute Play Time, For Ages 14 and up I purchased this game while it was on sale, and after playing it for ~20 hours, I would gladly have paid double for the experience. While it is true that it can be a bit intimidating at first for most people, after the initial steep learning curve is over this game really begins to shine. Unlike other legacy games, Gloomhaven is more forgiving in the sense that you don't actually lose anything, but rather you learn from your mistakes and get to try again without penalty.

Even if you don't have other friends who would be willing to play with you, playing by yourself (controlling two characters at once) is incredibly fun and engaging. I would recommend playing with 2 to 3 people though.

My only gripe with the game is that it doesn't include any real solution for organizing the game once you start playing. I would highly recommend Broken Token's Gloomhaven organizer as well as the removable sticker sheet. The BT organizer may be expensive as well, but it's worth every penny.

text_fidelity_a:
Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot This is video pinball as it used to be, before today's highly sophisticated physics simulators: floaty ball mechanics, dumbed down special features, bizarre flipper behavior, etc. Which is what I expected.

But I have to say, I'm impressed at the care they put into it nevertheless. They carefully reproduced the major playfield features and loops, the special modes, the multiballs, the spinning pizza. They made the marquee its whole own separate screen so they could have the interactive elements. They have a clever alternative for the plunger (hold down the button for longer to shoot harder). The flipper buttons on the side can get a little finger-cramping, so they put duplicates on the back of the unit so you can hold the whole unit. And, for better or for worse, they reproduced all of the boys' voices. Ugh. And unless I'm mistaken, unlike most of the Tiny Arcade series, it actually saves your high scores.

It's not all good - the "Start Game"/"Game Over" text is hilariously blocky, like an Atari 2600 game, and it pops up on the playfield. I don't know why they didn't put it on the marquee LCD where it belonged. The ball vibrates weirdly on the habitrails. A couple times, particularly in multiball, I've had the ball just simply fall through the hinge of the flipper. But these aren't huge concerns, and they're easily laughed off.

One warning for sensitive and/or young users: I've always thought the original pinball game's marquee's presentation of April was excessively sexy (she's a hero in her own right, not eye candy, darn it) but in the cut down version it looks like... uh, something else entirely.

All in all, this way exceeded my expectations. And it's actually quite fun! I'm not interested in the other "boardwalk arcade" games so far, but I'd gladly buy more pinball games like this one if they're at a similar level of playability.
text_fidelity_b: Boardwalk Arcade Pop-A-Shot

text_fidelity_a:
Micro Arcade Qbert I've bought almost all of this company's whole Tiny Arcade series, and have really liked them. The games are dumbed down and reprogrammed for the tiny screen - MAME emulation, they ain't. But generally they get the basic feel of the games right and are great fun to play.

These are really, really bad ports. I've played a lot of bad Atari ports in my day, but these are some of the worst. Super Breakout is incredibly slow and the ball behaves ridiculously. Asteroids is destroyed by the fact that the titular asteroids do not follow any kind of physics whatsoever - after you blow one up, the chunks shoot in every direction.

I also have the Series 1, which has the cream of the kinda rotten crop, Missile Command. Missile Command is full of bugs - it just randomly spams the "OUT" and "LOW" indicators any old place on screen, totally at random. It's hilariously nerfed - I survived many rounds with my missile batteries destroyed because the Russkies just couldn't seem to aim at anything they didn't already level. Missiles explode immediately and the explosion fades away almost instantly, completely ruining the strategy of the game. And yet, though it's a lame version of the legitimate game, it's nevertheless a curiously addicting game in its own right.

Centipede comes off very badly. The game does not work well with the control scheme, and the bubble buttons are an even worse replacement for the trackball than normal d-pads. Everything is off kilter and badly tuned - the centipede will be at the bottom row in a matter of seconds. I thought this was the least fun of the four "main" games.

The bonus game is Pong. Pong is Pong, kind of, sans the paddle controller. It frankly disappoints me about myself that I still have so much fun with it.

That said, these are still kind of fun, in the way the old Tiger LCD handhelds could be. They're really far from the originals, but in a pinch, they're nice to have around.

The build quality is bizarrely misweighted. The bubble-switch buttons have really firm resistance, but I kinda like them. They have a sound on/off swith that is sorely missed in the Tiny Arcade units, and the feeling of the back of the unit is great, but the actual screen area picks up scratches like it was made of butter. I got an Amazon Warehouse Deals used one, and had to send it back because the screen was just unusable.

So, as long as you don't put them in your pocket with your car keys, and as long as you have a lot of tolerance for cheap handheld jankiness, it might be worth your pennies. But buyer beware - a LOT of tolerance is required.
text_fidelity_b: Micro Arcade Qbert

text_fidelity_a:
Yahtzee 80 Score Cards I don't for a second believe that this box originally held these score sheets. First of all, the box was banged up, roughed up and taped together; obviously used. Second, the score sheets inside don't nearly fill the box, there's easily room for 2 pads of these cheap lightweight "cards". Which also are much shorter & narrower than the box. The pad simply doesn't fit right, it bangs around loosely inside.

Personally, I think it looks like someone with a game room hoarded a bunch of Yahtzee score card boxes (or bought them on Ebay), then xeroxed copies of a scorecard to make pads using just slightly heavy weight paper, and sold them to us suckers. The person didn't even bother to copy the back side of a real Yahtzee score card, which has a graph for a running total.

The only thing I'm happy about is that I didn't order a second one to include in a gaming package for my grand kids.
text_fidelity_b: Yahtzee 80 Score Cards

text_fidelity_a:
Estes Syncro X Nano R/C Quadcopter, White (Discontinued by manufacturer) Great quadcopter which is hampered by a so-so controller. I applaud Hubsan (Estes is their distributor in the US and uses the Estes brand on these Hubsan Q4 nanos) for making a controller with the same size as the quad. The boards in these nano-controllers are exactly the same as in the Hubsan X4 controller, with a few functions disabled. The function I really want (and I'm not sure exactly why they disabled this) is the 'Expert' level. This basically gives the sticks 100% range (rather than about 30% on the basic level). You need this extra range on the nano because it tends to drift due to its light weight. [[ASIN:B00IZC6C8E Hubsan H107L X4 Mini RTF RC Quadcopter]] controllers pair with the Estes Synchro X Nano with no problem. Using the bigger controller allows you to do flips, which are actually easier indoors than with the Hubsan X4, because the light nanos don't drop as much during a flip. Overall a well engineered and implemented toy that is cheap and lots of fun.

Suggestions: purchase extra blades from RCSuperstore.com ($2.38 a set) and extra batteries (~$4 ea.) The batteries are taped to the board, but you can just pull them off and substitute light velcro, leave the top off and swap out batteries just like you do with your X4. The batteries need to be secured in place in the nano, or they would constantly cause drift. If you travel, take a phone charger to charge up the battery. In general, these batteries will wear quickly unless your charger has power management. Buy an [[ASIN:B00IBDOB5I Anker® 40W 5-Port Family-Sized Desktop USB Charger with PowerIQ™ Technology for iPhone 5s 5c 5; iPad Air mini; Galaxy S5 S4; Note 3 2; the new HTC One (M8); Nexus and More (White)]]and your batteries will charge much faster and last much longer.
text_fidelity_b: Estes Syncro X Nano R/C Quadcopter, White (Discontinued by manufacturer)

Dromida Ominus Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Quadcopter Ready-to-Fly (RTF) Drone with Radio System, Batteries and USB Charger (Yellow) Putting aside difficulties with flying the quadcopter, I ran into major connectivity issues. About every two minutes the connection between the remote and quadcopter would go out, requiring that the battery be unplugged, reconnected, and the remote turned on and off. It was extremely frustrating to have to go through this so often.

Oh, and how stupid is it that there isn't an on/off switch on the quadcopter? To power it on and off you have to literally connect and yank the cord.

I had a hard time flying it -- no matter how much I tried, I could not get it to just hover. As others have noted, the scant directions provide no help with how to fly it.

Also, you really need a very large wide open space to fly it, like a baseball field.

I'll concede that I may just stink as a quadcopter pilot, but the connectivity issue is reason enough to junk it.

text_fidelity_a:
Cheerson CX-10 Mini 29mm Diameter 4CH 2.4GHz 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter UFO RTF Green I would recommend this drone as anyone's first drone, or as a cheap toy to keep in the office.

I've purchased several of these for the children in my family. The are small, light, and perfect for flying indoors. I've crashed mine several time from 8-10 feet up and they just fall about bounce off the ground. The basic-ness of this drone reinforces the skills needed to fly all drones at a very low entry cost. In this way you don't feel bad about trying things and crashing. The features are very basic with the only programmed/smart option is a flip. There is a sort of hidden option to unlock "acrobatic mode" (read the instructions to unlock) which is really just turning the sensitivity of the controller, but definitely a challenge for new flyers.

Once you master flying this little guy around jumping up to a bigger "smarter" drone is a piece of cake, and if anything goes wrong you have the fundamental skills to fly and land.

text_fidelity_a:
NERF Infinus N-Strike Elite Toy Motorized Blaster with Speed-Load Technology Holiday gift for my 6 year old -- and a waste of money. He got around 30 minutes of joy, because when it works it's kinda-sorta cool. But it takes too long to start firing, especially in the heat of battle, and it lacks enough power to send the darts very far.

The big problem is that this thing constantly jams, especially if the batteries start getting low. And this thing chews through batteries like few toys I've seen before. The jams are super frustrating, often tricky to resolve without doing any damage the gun or ruining the dart.

I've figured out through trial and error that this gun is very sensitive to dart width. I discovered quite by accident that some Nerf darts, even with the same color tips, have slightly different widths than some others. There are letter codes on the side of the dart that seem to correspond to which ones work better. The "J" ones we have seem to be okay, the "A" ones not so much. The difference is subtle, but you can tell when loading some of the manual guns, as some darts will offer more resistance. The tolerance is not an issue with those guns, but it's a huge problem with this one, as the wider darts consistently jam. Of course we don't have all of our darts sorted by 1mm width differences or tiny letters printed on the side of the tips, so every time my child wants to play with this gun we have to go through and check each dart one at a time to increase the odds that we'll have a good experience. That's ridiculous.

I think we paid around $50 for this. I think it's worth around $5. Not recommended at all.
text_fidelity_b: NERF Infinus N-Strike Elite Toy Motorized Blaster with Speed-Load Technology

Speed
On High mode it really tilts.

Range
The wireless range is excellent and the battery life is just fine. I've flown it at least a hundred feet away with no loss of a connection. So far I've been happy with the battery. Charges in 60 minutes and flies for 8.

Fun
Finding a good building to fly in is key. The building I work in has an open 4 story architecture with bridges at each level. The flip button is also fun for impressing on lookers.

Note
Plug the battery in when it is level so that the gyros are initialized correctly.

text_fidelity_a:
Name 5 Game This is, hands down, the worst game I have ever played for several reasons that all share a central theme of poorly laid out rules. I will share the 2 most glaring flaws from my experience w/ this gem of a game.

#1 A large portion of the categories are so subjective as to make them unplayable. For example, one of the categories in the game is, "Vacation Destinations." Who is to say that literally anything I say is not a valid answer? I could just name any destination on the planet. Who is to say I DON'T want to vacation in Darfur or at my ex-girlfriend's house? This is just one example, there are literally hundreds of categories where anything you say could be construed as a valid answer. The rules are ambiguous and fall back on self-policing as a substitute for a well thought out set of guidelines. The lack of a set of coherent rules leads to an endless debate about the validity of the players' answers that becomes incredibly boring to watch and incredibly frustrating to participate in.

#2 The arguments over what is and what is not a valid answer aside, an average round of this game takes about 10 minutes to play through. So unless you feel like going through the aggravation of playing more than once, you're not getting much bang for your buck. HOWEVER, it is worth noting that portions of this game can run on ad infinitum; one of the poorly engineered "challenges" in this game is to square off against another team to name as many items w/in the category chosen, obviously the one who runs out of ideas loses the challenge. Sounds like a decent idea, BUT instead of placing a time limit and perhaps writing down as many ideas as you can think of, like w/ Scattergories, this game has you go back-and-forth in a turn-taking verbal manner. The category we squared off w/ was "Foods That Begin With A." My god, the list went on and on for 10 minutes before everyone got bored and just called that round a tie. These challenges will not appear in every game; if you have the bad luck of stumbling into this challenge during your game, I advise you to get out a book or go make a sandwich while the teams face-off.

My advice to those considering this game is to buy Taboo or Scattergories instead. These two games are in the same genre and are time-tested winners w/ a clear set of rules. This game needs to be re-engineered with some attention paid to making the categories more thought-provoking and objective. I would recommend this game for parents with 5 year olds that just want to let their kids mess around and yell out random things for 10 minutes.
text_fidelity_b: Name 5 Game

Hot Wheels Workshop Track Builder Speedtropolis Track Set This is a really fun piece for a Hot Wheels set. I liked it a lot. It has three places where you can connect other tracks and sets, which is cool, because then you can connect other sets or tracks with it. The best part is the part where cars make a one and a half times turn around from the top level to the floor.

There's a car elevator that's supposed to bring cars from the floor to the top level. However, this is really hard to move, and requires so much force that the car will fly off the elevator before you can successfully levitate it to the top. None of the tracks that come with this can be used with other sets, because of the way they fit together. So, if you misplace any pieces, then you really have to throw the whole thing away, or put it in your junk plastic pile. But, those are the only two negative things.

text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Star Wars Death Star (10188) (Discontinued by manufacturer) From the pictures, this looked kind of goofy at first. I really wanted the other Death Star, but that's much harder to find than this one. This one is still super rare, and I didn't fall in love with it until we put it together. It has so many cool scenes from the movies, and so many working parts. It even has a removable tie fighter, with a tie fighter hanger. It's got a ton of cool figures that I haven't seen anywhere else, like R2-D2, Assassin Droid, R2-Q5, Protocol Droid, Interrogation Droid, Palpatine, Darth Vader, Imperial Trooper, Luke Skywalker (Jedi, Stormtrooper, and Tatooine), Obi Wan Kenobi, Han Solo (Stormtrooper and Black Vest), Stormtrooper, Princess Leia, C-3PO, Grand Moff Tarkin, Mouse Guard, Royal Guard, and Chewie.

It took four of us two full days to put this together, over Christmas holidays, but it was well worth the effort. The scale is a little strange, but it's that way in almost any lego set. We calculated that if they made a Lego Death Star to the scale where people would actually make sense, then it would have to be 2 miles across. So, they had to make some design choices so that a lot of stuff isn't really to scale. For reference, the real Death Star is 100 miles across. This set does mix up different scenes from two different movies. But, they're really cool scenes. A lot of the parts work, like you can crush Luke and Leia in the trash compactor and you can move and aim the Death Star ray on two different axes.

The instruction book is ginormous. There are about 500 different steps in total. It's spiral bound, and you have to be really careful so that it doesn't rip. Overall, this is an epic set, and I highly recommend this to anyone who's an expert with Legos.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars Death Star (10188) (Discontinued by manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
USA License Plate Map 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle in the Shape of the US - 31 inches long - Cool Wall Art [[VIDEOID:ece742fa9f80992e2861a156e954114a]] I really like puzzles of maps, and this one is very interesting and unique. It was a pretty easy puzzle to put together, because the license plates from each of the states have a ton of different colors and patterns on them.

Since this is a shaped puzzle, you'll have to rethink how you do puzzles, especially if you put the edge pieces together first. Literally the last piece I put together was an edge piece from California. It's hard to put the edge pieces together, but there are tons of easier parts to put together, so if you're flexible, then it is very doable.

Each state is in the true shape of the state, and it has a license plate or plates instead of any kind of map. There are some vanity plates, like "Elvis Lives" and "Polkatown," but most are regularly-numbered plates.

The puzzle pieces are very average thickness and they're very average quality. They're not great, but they're not bad. But I got this for the shape and the design, so I was very happy overall.
text_fidelity_b: USA License Plate Map 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle in the Shape of the US - 31 inches long - Cool Wall Art

text_fidelity_a:
Buffalo Games - Vintage America - 2000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:70993f24c2cce65d6b7aea10ebd6a5fc]] This is an awesome puzzle! It was so much fun to put together. It's actually pretty easy for a 2000 piece puzzle, because of all of the different colors and patterns. I'm not saying it's super easy, because any 2000 piece puzzle is an intense challenge. But, it has lots of clear detail, and with most of the pieces, you're able to get a pretty good idea of where it actually goes by looking at the picture. That makes a puzzle fun and not frustrating. The hardest part to do was actually the "America" part, because it had a lot of solid red. But overall, all of the parts of the puzzle went at a pretty good pace.

I felt that I built my skills a lot with this, and now I can fly my bigger copter a lot better than I did before I played around with this.

An awesome thing about this is that you can separately order every part of this copter. And, unlike many electronic devices, the sum of the parts is about the same as getting a new one. So, I guess you could also just get two, and when one breaks, then fix it with the other one. Or wait for them to both break and then Frankenstein a whole one back together. But, because these have such available and interchangeable parts, then I can't give it less than five stars.

This is also really easy to get stuck on top of a roof or in a tree, so I recommend flying it in a pretty open field. They do pretty good at crash landings, too, as long as they land on grass, which was most of my landings.

It is packaged with a bunch of replacement blades, too, so you don't have to worry about breaking a few of them. They're easy to replace, too.

Then the pieces of paper are handed in, and the person who is It has to guess who wrote what question. The person who is It gets one point per right answer that they match with the people playing the game.

It's a fun, and simple concept, which makes for a fun and simple game. And, the questions are awesome. I've gotten a few "getting to know you" books in the past, which have lists of supposedly interesting questions. All of those books pale in comparison to this awesome game. These questions are intense, interesting, and none of them put too much pressure on you.

My girlfriend and I found ourselves just reading the questions and answering them a lot, just by ourselves. It's a great way to talk about tons of different topics than the ones that usually come up. Like I said, these questions are great.

I usually really don't like party games like this. I usually like strategy games better. But this is one party game that I love.

The rules were a bit confusing, since they used the old 1959 rules. Here's my summary of the rules: You can only move your pawns out of start if you pick a 1, 2, or sometimes a Sorry card. If you get a 1 or a 2, then you only move out to the first circle. You only slide when you get on the first part of the slide. If you can't move, you don't move, and you need an exact count to get into the Home square. Follow the rest of the instructions on the cards.

Monopoly Empire Game [[VIDEOID:8f653ee987e2df8b52e209e097da8a22]] This is such a cool game! It's a scaled down version of Monopoly, and each game only takes 5-15 minutes to play, instead of the hours of a regular Monopoly game. So you'll hear something with this Monopoly game that you won't hear with any other Monopoly game, which is "Want to play again?"

It still captures the essence of Monopoly, so it still feels like a Monopoly game. It's more of a social game than a strategy game, but that will make it more fun for more people.

They've taken out the property cards, and replaced them with little tiles and a tower. The number of tiles, not the original value of the tile, determine how much that you pay when you land on someone else's property. The old Community Chest cards are now Empire cards, and you get a couple to hold on to at the start of the game, and you can use these strategically, and do various combos with them.

It's very fun, and I liked it a lot. If you get just one game this year, this should be the game you pick.

Pros:

+Extremely well designed
+Has cool brands like Fender, Nerf, and Coke
+Quick version of Monopoly (I never thought I'd ever use quick and Monopoly in the same sentence.)
+They did an awesome job of play testing this game. It's very balanced and very fun. Whoever worked on the team that made this game should be promoted.
