World Series of Yahtzee Board Games [[VIDEOID:9706f008dc0f922f2a22889963de0e00]] This is a digital, board-based game of Yahtzee. I think it's made to compete with [[ASIN:B0042ET8S0 Uno Attack Game]] and [[ASIN:B001G5431A Bunco]], and it is much more fun than both of those games. Sometimes making a classic into a digital version is a mistake, but the designers did an awesome job with this game.

It's still [[ASIN:B00000IWH6 Yahtzee]]. You still get five dice, and you have to match the classic Yahtzee combinations of Yahtzee (five of a kind), four of a kind, three of a kind, full house, small straight (sequence or run) and large straight. But, everybody plays at once with their own sets of five dice, and the computer in the middle moderates everything, so goes very quickly and it's exciting.

The little buzzer in the middle is pretty sophisticated for a simple computer. It records who buzzes in and in which order you buzzed in, and it plays some fun countdown music. You get five seconds after the first person finishes to finish rolling and to buzz in yourself. Each person can collect up to one card per turn, based on what they rolled, but if you're not lucky, or if someone else gets your combination first, then you don't get any cards per turn. Usually turns take about thirty seconds each, and a full game all the way through will take about ten minutes, so it's very fast paced and fun.

I really liked the original Yahtzee, and I really like this too.

Pros:
+Very fun new version of an already fun classic
+Doesn't waste paper like the old version
+No more waiting around for slow players, like the old version
+You really should start playing this instead of Bunco, since there's a lot more strategy in this game
+You can roll the dice as many times as you want, where in traditional Yahtzee, you could only roll the dice three times per turn

Cons:
-The black dice with the red dots are so much cooler than the rest of the dice, so everyone will be fighting over these
-Made out of cheap plastic cardboard. If you love this game, which you probably will, and if you're not a dainty family, which you probably aren't, then you'll break these pretty quickly and go through about one of these games per year. It's still cheaper than a night at the movies, though, and this game is fun enough to justify getting a new one.
text_fidelity_b: World Series of Yahtzee Board Games

Hive- A Game Crawling With Possibilities [[VIDEOID:6e39915180719f8cf806a7bff52071ca]] I hate to say it, because it might scare people off, but this is a lot like chess. But it's a ton more fun than chess, and it takes much less time to learn, so I think you'll like it even if you hate chess. And if you love chess, you'll love this game. It's also a pretty deep strategy game, so if you love strategy games, you'll love this.

Instead of playing on a board, you position your hex pieces adjacent to your opponent's pieces, and then move them around "the hive" (the collection of pieces in the middle), until somebody's queen bee is completely surrounded, and that person loses the game.

Here's a list of the pieces, and what they can do:
*Queen bee, similar to the King in chess. Can only move one space
*Beetle, moves only one space, but can move on top of other tiles (a big advantage)
*Spider, moves three spaces in one direction (the worst piece, in my opinion)
*Soldier ant, moves anywhere outside the perimeter of the hive
*Grasshopper, can only move by jumping over pieces

And, if you want to buy expansion packs, you can get
*[[ASIN:B003WZGDEW Mosquito Expansion]], which clones the ability of pieces it touches
*[[ASIN:B00472O260 Ladybug Expansion]], which moves like the knight in chess. Two on top of the hive, and then one down
*Or, [[ASIN:B00472O26K Hive Carbon]], which is black and white, and has the exact same pieces as this game, plus the pieces in the expansion packs

Pros:
+Very sturdy construction
+You can play on any surface
+Very quick to learn, and even quicker to teach. You could be playing this 5 minutes from now
+Extremely fun strategy game. I love it!
+Even if you hate strategy games, you'll like this. Unless you play with someone better than you that keeps beating you, and then you might not like it too much.

Cons:
-Completely different than any strategy game you've played, so it will take a while to build your strategy
text_fidelity_b: Hive- A Game Crawling With Possibilities

text_fidelity_a:
Transformers Ultimate Bot Shots Battle Set [[VIDEOID:d101db08d87b73f8879f557a27621e25]] I love Transformers, so I probably added a couple stars to this product just because I love Transformers so much.

This is supposed to be a rock, paper, scissors game, and each toy has a rotating plate that you can pick red, blue, or green. But, you'll end up spending more time trying to make it work, than actually playing.

My Megatron arrived broken, and I would guess from the shape of the other three toys, that one of your toys will be broken. I would have returned it for a replacement, but I was pretty sure that every set would have a broken Transformer.

It also has an online game. This is the worst type of online game, because it's highly addictive, it encourages you to buy more toys just so you can get higher levels in the game, but the game isn't fun and it's not very educational. The online game is also a glorified rock, paper, scissors game. If you don't want begging kids, have them stay away from the online game. You get four coupons that give you one online robot each.

Pros:
+It's an officially-licensed Transformers product.

Cons:
-My Megatron arrived broken, and I would guess from the shape of the other three toys, that you'll get about 1 out of every 4 of these toys that are broken.
-The toys transformed too quickly. They're supposed to wait until they hit something.
-The plates that change color on each toy was totally stuck on two of them
-No matter how you dress up rock, paper, scissors, it's really not that fun of a game.
-The pieces that aren't already broken will probably break after only a few uses.
text_fidelity_b: Transformers Ultimate Bot Shots Battle Set

text_fidelity_a:
Rio Grande Games Stone Age [[VIDEOID:9645a95d436279cab83d9584b2798107]] In this video, I show one round of playing the game. The game is fast paced, and it's about an interesting time in human history.

This is a pretty fun game, but for me it got old really fast. I really like empire building games, like [[ASIN:B002L6HJCI Age of Empires]], so I thought I would love this. But, I just liked it, I didn't love it.

The problem is that there's really only one strategy to the game, which is this: Get as many civilization cards as you can, and try to spend 100% of your resources by the time the game ends.

Pros:
+If you love the stone age, then this is probably a pretty good game for you.
+It's a pretty fun game.
+If you have a group of super casual gamers, you'll probably enjoy this for a long time. But all it takes is one serious gamer to disrupt the game for everyone.
+The game goes by pretty quick, and gets quicker the more you've played it.

Cons:
-Scoring is a little confusing. You typically score about 200-350 points on a game, but the score only goes to 100.
-Limited strategies, since there really is only one strategy
-Not enough luck to make it fun for casual gamers
-I wish they would have play tested this game a little bit more. I got the feeling that if they would have changed a few things on the cards and scoring, it would have been an awesome game. For example, civilization cards are way too heavily weighted.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games Stone Age

text_fidelity_a:

I put this together faster than I've ever done a 500-piece puzzle before. I think it's because of all of the varied textures, and the bright colors.

text_fidelity_a:
Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball I'm someone who will cheat at something if I can. Like when I was was a kid, and I played [[ASIN:B00000IWCT Monopoly]] with my little brothers, I would steal money from the bank, just because I could.

Each piece of this puzzle has a number on the back of it, and the numbers tell you which pieces fit together. So, it's much easier to flip over all of the pieces of the puzzle, and put it together upside down, that by putting the puzzle together by the picture. And it's much easier by a lot. I think that everyone who does this puzzle will eventually get frustrated, and resort to doing the puzzle upside down, which I consider 'cheating.'

It's very solid, and very strong, when you put it together. The pieces are made of sturdy plastic, not cardboard, like other puzzles. Also the pieces seem like they're cast, or molded, and not cut. That's why the globe surface ends up smooth. But, because all of the pieces were manufactured separately, instead as a whole puzzle, then the picture doesn't always match up from piece to piece.

It comes with a cheap stand, but it looks pretty nice when it's assembled and displayed. I hid a few coins in the middle of it, so it rattles when you move it. It's got lot of area in the middle for a small sphere, so it could double as a secret safe.

Pros:
+Very sturdy, especially when the sphere is completed
+Nice picture, with a bunch of cool zodiac symbols
+High quality

Cons:
-Has numbers on the back of each piece of the puzzle, so it's super simple to assemble
-Plastic, so it doesn't feel like a real puzzle
-The picture doesn't always line up from piece to piece
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Zodiac 270 Piece Puzzle Ball

text_fidelity_a:
Logo Board Game For what it is, a trivia game just based on popular brands, this is probably as good as it gets.

The gameplay is simple, and they've devised a way to play with only using cards and the board, so no die required. The board is a path made up of 4 colors that the instructions say are in 'random' order. And even though the random order would never pass any randomness tests, it makes for game play that moves along.

The cards are the best part. Each card is usually dedicated to a different brand, so you could just thumb through the cards and pick your favorite brands by the pictures on the faces of the cards.

And, you'll probably wonder, since playing this is really similar to watching a couple hours of commercials, "Shouldn't they be paying me to play this game?"

Pros:
+Tons of trivia about tons of different companies
+You can play without dice, so this will last a lot longer than most board games
+Both easy and hard trivia questions, so people don't feel too stupid
+Even if you are really bad at trivia, this game will only take about an hour to play (15 minutes if you're awesome)

Cons:
-All the standard cons that go along with a trivia game. It makes the smart people feel smarter, and the dumb people feel dumber. I'm pretty dumb at trivia, so it was nice to play a trivia game and only feel mildly dumb.
text_fidelity_b: Logo Board Game

What I expected was a gold-colored putty with some fine glitter. What I received was clear putty with a ton of cheap glitter. We're talking about dollar-store kids' craft set glitter, not the nice glitter used for embossing. This basically looks like someone squirted a bottle of glitter glue into a putty tin.

Not only that, but I played with it for a minute and glitter already started coming off in my hand. It probably wouldn't take long for this to lose its luster.

Thinking Putty is fun stuff, so I suggest passing this up and getting a tin of the Super Oil Slick instead.

Chutes and Ladders Board Game Like many of us over 40, we grew up with this game and recognize the graphics of the Classic Chutes and Ladders Board Game. Recently, after my dad passed, we cleared out our old house and found my old game. It followed my brother home to his family, but now I'm curious to compare the two.

Outside of nostalgia, the question is if the game stands on its own in 2015. My four year-old boy thinks so. He doesn't care about 1972 (or even know it existed, as time began with him, as he sees it). He begs to play it, right along with Trouble! and Legos.

Essentially, there's no strategy. The person going version has a small chance of winning, but for all intents and purposes, it is pure chance.

To move forward, the player spins from 1-6. Whatever square he might land on is either neutral, a ladder or a slide. Slides move him back to an earlier square, ladders move him up, and neutral squares allow him to stay put until the next move. There is no decision making.

Is it fun? Very much so, according to my boy. As there are 100 squares, there are plenty of opportunities to climb ladders and slide down. It is a little tricky to follow which direction to go, as the numbers start left-to-right, but zig-zag at each end. A patient older child or adult needs to be on-hand to help with game play.

Anthony Trendl
anthonytrendl.com

Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary) It might seem as if 50 cars is too much at once.

Days as a five year old were best filled with playing in complete abandon. The freedom proffered by youth needed only a few toys to complete the ever-present joy. A few toys which mattered included several tattered but friendly books, a truck or two, an odd shovel and bucket, and, the coup de grace, a Hot Wheels car. Mattel makes a track as well, but a well-made car could take a boy places. This set of 50 is what kindergartners drool over.

A boy has everything in this set: vehicles of all colors, a few truck varieties, some funny looking cars. There are plenty, and frankly, since a few will invariably wind up lost under the couch, eaten by the dog, and buried with other treasures in the garden, having 50 quickly becomes justified.

Why a Hot Wheels car? Because they are made with hard steel. They are painted with a slick color. They hold up to frequent tastings, sand grindings, dirt smearings and other nonsense that comes with power racing in a sandbox. Sticky chocolate wipes off with warm water, and grime comes out with a good spray under the faucet.

The wheels themselves have a bounce peculiar to a genuine Hot Wheels vehicle. That's how my brother and I made sure it had adequate fuel. Ten bounces should be enough, we figured, and usually, we were right.

I fully recommend the "Hot Wheels Basic Car 50-Pack."

Anthony Trendl
treefortbooks.com
text_fidelity_b: Hot Wheels Set of 20 Toy Cars & Trucks in 1:64 Scale, Collectible Vehicles (Styles May Vary)

Hasbro Gaming Deluxe Turntable Scrabble Remarkable. Scrabble is cool. Hep. Rad. Outta sight. But Scrabble in this deluxe form is sublime, intoxicating. The pieces stay put, thanks to little walls around each space. You can spin the board so as to not need to examine it upside down. The pieces never slide around. The plastic coating lets you wipe it off, unlike the cardboard version which stains. Nothing is compromised from the original, flat cardboard version, but everything is improved.

OK. Not everything. It still can't help you dump the Q, Z and J at the end of the game without a U. And it is unlikely to assist you in stopping your grandmother's amazing ability to squeeze you out of that triple word score you hoped to grab with a seven-letter word. Take that up with Gram. Just remember who made you the cookies.

Seriously, I recommend this to any family or commited Scrabble player. Families need it for that `full-body contact' style of play that sometimes happens with children or cats involved. Commited Scrabble players need it for pretty much the same reason!

I fully recommend this game.

text_fidelity_a:
Indie Boards and Cards Flash Point Fire Rescue 2nd Edition, 10 years + My family really loves cooperative games. Games like Pandemic, Shadows over Camelot, Castle Panic and Forbidden Island are all hits at my house. With all the buzz around Flash Point Fire Rescue, I had to try it out. The game comes with two sets of rules, a basic "family" set of rules and the advanced rules. Basic rules are fun, but the advanced rules is where the strategy comes in.

The premise is that you are a firefighter and you are rushing into the house to rescue people and animals. each person has a role that they play, but that can be switched during the game if another role would be more helpful. The game can be very intense as the fire continues to burn and flare up as you play.

Overall, this game really fits the coop bill perfectly and it's been a hit in our family. I'd recommend it if you enjoy cooperative games and want to pretend you're a fire fighter!
text_fidelity_b: Indie Boards and Cards Flash Point Fire Rescue 2nd Edition, 10 years +

text_fidelity_a:
Alderac Entertainment Group Love Letter Love Letter....doesn't sound like a game I'd like to play to be honest. It also comes in a red velvet bag....ewww.. However, once you get past the name and the bag you realize what a great game Love Letter is. So very simple with only 16 cards and only two cards to pick from on your turn, but so much strategy in how you use those cards.

Basically each card has some text on it indicating what you can do with that card. You draw a card on your turn, pick between the two cards and do what the discarded card indicates. Player with the highest numbered card or the last player in the round wins the round and gets some attention from the princess.

Overall this game is a very simple but very fun game that can be played in 20-30 minutes with 4 players. Can't recommend it enough.
text_fidelity_b: Alderac Entertainment Group Love Letter

text_fidelity_a:
Dungeons & Dragons: Lords of Waterdeep Board Game A D&D themed euro game. What more could you want? :)

Lords of Waterdeep is a worker placement euro game through and through. You will be placing your "agents" out in waterdeep to recruit clerics, fighters, wizards and rogues to help you complete quests. Each Lord of Waterdeep has a specific objective for you to complete, like focusing on certain types of quests. You get points by completing quests and bonus points if those quests are of the type requested by your Lord.

This game has similar mechanics to Stone Age, Caylus and other worker placement games, but if you like Euro games and D&D, this is a great one to pick up. It plays in as little as an hour and even though the box says 12+ my 9 yr old plays it with ease.
text_fidelity_b: Dungeons & Dragons: Lords of Waterdeep Board Game

text_fidelity_a:
Greater Than Games Sentinels of The Multiverse Enhanced Card Game (2nd Edition) Sentinels of the multiverse is a cooperative card game where you and your friends play as super heroes from the sentinels comic universe fighting a villian in a few different locations. The game is pretty easy and straight forward, but not easy to win. We've had a lot of fun trying all the different combinations of locations, heroes and villians. There are plenty of expansions available to keep the game fresh, but even with just the heroes, villians and locations included in the game there is plenty to do.

Definitely pick up the "Enhanced" version over the previous version. It's usually only a few bucks more, but will get you a bigger box that can handle the expansions, card dividers for all included cards as well as dividers for all expansions and promo cards (available from sentinels website) as well as tokens to track damage, modifiers, etc. Previously this was done with a sheet of paper/pen.

Overall this is a fun cooperative card game. If you have any interest in card games and super heroes, this game is for you.
text_fidelity_b: Greater Than Games Sentinels of The Multiverse Enhanced Card Game (2nd Edition)

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance I picked up The Resistance to play at family gatherings where mafia and werewolf didn't go over so well. People didn't like getting eliminated and didn't like someone needing to moderate/narrate the game. The resistance is best played with more people. The more the merrier definitely is true here. Some people will play as the resistance and some as spies. The spies are trying to sabotage the missions while the resistance is trying to complete the missions. The game has a mission leader who will pick which players are going to go on the mission. The game then opens discussion to all players to decide if that is the best choice of players for the mission.

Overall, We enjoyed the game, but when playing with only 5 players, it's a bit too easy and people don't really get into the discussion. When playing with 8-10 players, the game is a lot more fun as people really get into the accusations and deciding who should go on the different missions. Since people aren't eliminated like mafia and werewolf, people tend to enjoy this game more.
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance

text_fidelity_a:
Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition Ok, I have to start this review off by saying I had my reservations about this game. I absolutely love Euro strategy games like Puerto Rico, Agricola, Power Grid, Caylus, etc, but I'm not into card games. In fact, I pretty much hate card games.

This game was getting a lot of publicity on BoardGameGeek and everyone was raving about it so I decided that I should buy it to give it a shot. I'm glad I did.

The whole point of the game is to build your deck of cards and build up a collection of victory points. The reason this game shines is because it is a quick game that only takes about 30-40 minutes to play. It is also very fun because as you are building your deck of cards you aren't usually getting rid of the cards. If you spend some gold to buy a card that gold goes back into your discard pile and will eventually be shuffled for you to use again in another turn.

There are over 500 cards in this game with around 25 different action cards available so you can vary the game a lot depending on what cards are currently on the table. The only downside is that someone that has played the game a lot and knows a base strategy can usually beat a new player easily.

Overall this game is very addicting and short, which is a good thing. You can play multiple rounds of this game in an evening as opposed to one game of another typical Euro.
text_fidelity_b: Rio Grande Games - Dominion: First Edition

text_fidelity_a:
VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys Oh, what have I done?

I bought Patrick the Pygmy Goat as a gift for my goat loving wife this past Christmas. Upon seeing it Christmas morning, her eyes lit up and she took to it immediately. I thought I had made the perfect choice.

Or so I thought.

I quickly found that it seems Patrick was always watching me. At night, he would sit atop the pillows on the bed watching over his new domain. Despite the fact his head seems to be affixed to only look to his left, it still seems he is looking at me no matter what side of the bed I’m on. When I tuck in my wife at night, he is there staring. When I come back from brushing my teeth, he is there staring. When I lift the sheets to turn over at night, he is there staring into my soul.

I’m pretty sure he is plotting against me. I can see him in the window looking down at me when I take the trash out to the street. I get phone calls with the sounds of capra aegagrus hircus breathing on the other end. Sometimes he is there under my feet when walking by or sitting on my chest when I wake.

I’ve spoken to my wife about my concerns, but she laughs them off. I’m starting to think she is in on it with the goat. With Patrick. Even now, he is watching me type.

Despite the above concerns, he appears to be a really great stuffed goat. My wife falls asleep with him in her arms each night as he whispers, whatever it is he is saying, into her ear.
text_fidelity_b: VIAHART Patrick The Pygmy Goat - 18 Inch Large Stuffed Animal Plush - by Tiger Tale Toys

text_fidelity_a:
Magic the Gathering Cards - Khans of Tarkir - Booster Packs (6 Pack Lot) I ordered 18 boosters (3 of 6 booster bundles) and two of the bundles showed signs of being tampered with. Extra cuts on the bottom edge of the pack, packs that were ridiculously easy to open -- I've never opened boosters that basically fall apart along one crimped edge consistently like these did. I really don't trust that someone hasn't sorted through these and skimmed the fetch lands out or something. I can't prove that they were tampered with, the right numbers of cards were all there in the right proportions, but it sure feel like this is some kind of scam the way those packs fell apart.

tl;dr: Stay away, get your boosters from sealed product like sealed booster boxes, sealed fat packs or sealed holiday boxes instead; the packs I got in bagged bundles from my seller were fishy as hell.

text_fidelity_a: Hanatora Air 2S,Mavic Air 2 Wall & Car Charger Compatible with DJI Air 2S,Mavic Air Battery, 5 in 1 Rapid Multi Parallel Charging Hub Drone Accessories I tried both the charging and the discharging function. It seems that it functions as claimed. The max charging rate is 2.2 amps per battery. Discharge is at a lower rate of about 1.5 amps. Rates taper off neat the end of the cycle. The charger won't start to charge a battery that is at or above 90% full. It will not start to charge a battery that is too hot. The instructions imply that balancing is applied at the end of the charge or discharge which is very important for the health of LiPo batteries. Taking the unit apart, I found the internal construction to be reasonable with well-sized and quality components. Soldering looks good and much better than I had expected. I will stick with the DJI charger and hub for charging my batteries as I am usually not desparate for lots of charged batteries quickly. However, I really like being able to discharge the batteries for storage so that will be my main use for the charger. I would say this is a good purchase for maintaining our expensive batteries.
text_fidelity_b: Hanatora Air 2S,Mavic Air 2 Wall & Car Charger Compatible with DJI Air 2S,Mavic Air Battery, 5 in 1 Rapid Multi Parallel Charging Hub Drone Accessories

text_fidelity_a: ROKR 3D Wooden Puzzles Vitascope for Adults - Model Building Kits Mechanical Construction for Adults to Build, Educational Brain Teaser DIY Crafts Kits, Halloween Collection Gifts for Men (Vitascope) This was a gift from my daughter. It was not hard to assemble. However, I did have to use a magnifying glass to closely examine some of the illustrations. There are a lot of extra wooden pieces included which takes some of the stress out of assembly. You don't have to worry so much about breaking a piece. One piece shattered in my hand during assembly but there was another available. One sub-assembly with metal rods and lots of disks kept falling out during assembly and it was annoying to put back in. I should have just taped it up temporarily to keep it in place until the later steps where it is securely fastened. It is a very clever device. Turning the crank makes a film loop advance on the reels and a little generator lights a lamp to project the clip. It is Charlie Chaplin doing a very short dance. Really, there is no use in wanting more clips or stressing about how you can't view other movies. That's not the point of this. text_fidelity_a:
UGears Models 3-D Wooden Puzzle - Mechanical Horse Mechanoid This horse is striking in appearance. It looks wild and spirited. It is quite a conversation piece on its looks alone. I would give it five stars alone for that. Movement is not as spectacular, but it does move. There’s a winding key and start/stop control levers. The horse is not able to take more than 5 steps without halting or simply falling over. It looks like the last motions of a horse before succumbing to the effects of a trank dart. The kit is a real bear to assemble. The instructions must be heeded. You may find you have to flip ahead a few pages at times to see just what this subassembly is that you are working on and where it is supposed to go. I knew at the start that I would need to sand the pieces and use the provided wax. Ther's not a whole lot of wax. It’s a 1 inch slice of a candle but the important thing is that it enough for the horse. The wax is somewhat soft, like beeswax. I had no problem with missing pieces. There are six boards with laser cut parts. If you don't see anything missing, you have all the parts. Assembly is a bit tedious and somewhat painful. As the model continues to take shape and become more horse-like there is the adrenalin surge all model builders feel when they are nearing the end. Once assembly is completed the key is wound and switch is moved. My model just sat there. C’mon little horsy, let’s go. Well, back-winding the key overcomes the initial friction and horse begins to haltingly show movement. Lots of going back and forth with the key helps to distribute the wax and the horse becomes more limber. After lots of massaging like this you can get the horse to take 4 or maybe 5 steps. Max is 9 and only rarely achieved. It will usually fall over to announce it is finished walking. Well and good. It is still a cool model and I would build one again. I’m giving it 5 stars but 4 would be reasonable too. I wish it walked a bit better and that the instructions had a bit of expository text. This is a worthwhile model that will occupy 8 hours of your life in assembly. It is ingenious.

I have a few hints on this horse:
Mine locked up once while fully wound up. I could not get it to operate at all. I tried moving the legs and rapping the body with my knuckles. Nothing! My horse was dead. It was not until I grasped the horses neck and moved it forward and back that the gears unlocked. This only happened once, but it was super frustrating as I was contemplating opening up the entire model to fix it.

Understand at the outset that this horse can’t walk for long. If you watch the clever videos the horse appears to leave its stall and seems to be on a journey to a pasture or whatever. If you look closely the horse only takes a few steps in each scene. Clever editing makes it look like the horse can go on a pastoral journey. Not really complaining because all the ad copy and literature says the horse can’t go far. This is only a problem if your expectations are too high and unrealistic. It is what it is, a model of mechanical horse. So enjoy that as I do I.

My rubber band broke. I suppose it had a nick in it that grew over time. I was able to cut out the broken piece and retie the rubber band but it is not easy working in the body of the assembled model. So do examine the length of the rubber band before assembly.

Update on the rubber band issue 5 days later:
The rubber band broke again. No, I haven’t over wound it. I’ll have to see if I can get a replacement from somewhere.

The rubber bands for the horse’s mane and tail are genius. Looks great and the bands lie perfectly when cut. I was worried I’d need hair styling skills to make the horse look good. It was no problem.

Seriously, sand everything. Knock down the edges of the large pieces as well so they lose their painful sharpness. If you have to reach into the interior of the model later you will be glad you did.

Some parts are seeming impossible to press together with human hands. I finally resorted to a small furniture clamp with soft jaws to supplement my finger strength. I think pliers or small c-clamp would work, as well.

A cushiony work surface was helpful in supporting a board while I was breaking a part loose from the board. I used towel I use for assembly projects.

It really takes 8 uninterrupted hours to assemble this model no matter how skilled you think you are. If you leave out trying to be extra careful and the extra sanding I guess you could do it in about five.

On page 13 of the instructions I was confused. The diagram seems to suggest that the rubber band should be folded upon itself in thirds. After puzzling on this I covinced myself that doubling the band was correct and it turned out to be right choice.

Check for proper operation of parts during assembly. In some steps you are "told" to operate the key and check that the parts move freely. This is very important. Once the horse is fully assembled getting back inside it is a difficult task since gear timing must be maintained.

There is a down side to using the wax. Your hands will get a coating of wax and when that is transferred to the horse there will be discolored spots. Try to keep the wax from where you don't want the wood to darken. I washed my hands frequently and still ended up with a horse that is more pinto than wood white.

There are no troubleshooting hints in the instructions. If you can't find help on the website you are on your own. I do have a vibe from Ugears that they are helpful and I think you can correspond with them and get help if you have a bad problem.

HUBSAN X4 H107C HD 2MP Camera 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter Red/White (PH-H107C) At first I received the SD version instead of the HD version from one seller on Amazon. I returned it.The Little One's Choice got it right and sent me the HD version for which I had paid. Make sure you get what you paid for. It should say "HD Camera" in big letters on the Hubsan box. Unfortunately, the correct one they sent had horrible very dark lines in the video in all types of lighting conditions. I had to return it. The replacement was fine.

My "review" is going to be a bit rambling from an experienced guy to those who are tying to get started in this hobby. My hope is that I might have something to say that the old-timers might find useful as well.

My short review in this paragraph is that this quad is awesome (overused word, I know, but it fits here) for the price and simply amazing. I've had hours of fun with mine and I own 2 other non-camera Hubsans, one Proto-X and a Blade Quad Nano. This Hubsan quad is the most bang for the buck. I've also got big copters that are gathering dust while I have fun with these small ones. Strangely, I'm not missing them. Did I mention these little things are fun?

It is refreshing to the point of joyfulness to be able to fly this quad around since it is so relatively inexpensive and nimble. I bought several bags of props out of an abundance of caution and have not used one yet. Still, I don't crash much, so if you are new at this, you might need more propellers than the one set provided. I bought some spare batteries (they are blue, sold in a set of 5) and a couple of the Traxxas 2-port chargers. These work fine and let you have more charged batteries handy.

I want to say this quad is easy to fly. For me it is very easy, but it is also fun. I understand that for those who have never flown any type of RC rotor craft that you will have to be serious about learning to use and fly this little thing properly.

Don't be frustrated if you crash a lot at first. Fly in an open area outdoors if possible. If you fly indoors, which I know is a very attractive prospect at first, you will crash into walls and ceiling often and perhaps lose some propellers. At first you may even forget which hand "does what" and crash pretty hard. The body of this quad is tough, but I have seen some photos of broken ones. All of those slammed hard onto concrete walls or slabs.

If a crash is imminent, learn to cut the power immediately. Throttle off completely. You do not want the motors stalling against an obstruction. They will burn out if you abuse them that way. Also, never try to bump the throttle to kick the motors on in an attempt to flip the copter upright if it sets down at an angle. Motivate your body to the quad, pick it up and set it down straight. It will last longer that way.

The rotor guard is taped to the bottom of the tray. Use it if you are unsure of your skills. By the way, when removing the props to put this on, do be sure to hold down the motor body. If it comes up too far the motor wires will snap off. It is only held in place with friction. Use a pinching grasp to pull the prop off. There's a little wrench to help with pulling the props. Use that if one came with your quad. Some people don't get one, I don't know why.

This same type of grasp is also the correct way to disconnect the battery. If you pull by the wires, you will soon have a broken connection. Try to grasp both sides of the connector with your thumbs while you squeeze to persuade the connector away from its mate. Try to make contact with as much connector, not wire, as possible.

There are many videos on YouTube which are instructive for newbies. Especially helpful even for an experienced guy like me was one video that showed how to restore a stuck motor to working condition with a pair of pliers. Especially learn how to reset the gyros with the transmitter and how to zero-out the transmitter itself. Read the instructions carefully and you'll see that you can adjust the sensitivity of the transmitter relative to control input. Learn and understand how to use the trim buttons. There is a lot of info in that little manual. It's not the greatest manual I've seen, but it is a good effort at one and most of the hazy parts are cleared up on YouTube.

I've found that when the lights flash during flight to signal a low battery (time to land!) that the voltage is about 3.7 volts. This is a pretty safe voltage for storing a LiPo so if you are not going to fly again soon don't bother to charge it. Letting a fully charged LiPo sit for more than a week can be hard on it. Take good care of the battery by never flying it to the point where it is dead. In fact, as soon as you get the flashing warning - land! If you are flying outside where you can't see the warning well in daylight, I'd recommend setting a kitchen timer set to 5-1/2 minutes and timing your flights. Better safe than sorry. Once you run a LiPo down too far it's gone or soon will be.

If you have spare batteries all charged up during a flying session, avoid the temptation of replacing an exhausted battery with a fresh one and getting right back up into the air. My opinion is you should let the motors cool down for a few minutes first. They will be very hot after you complete a full flight so give them a chance to cool a bit before you take to the skies again.

They sell higher capacity batteries here on Amazon. I believe they are 500 mAh. I would not recommend them. Any longer flight time potential will be offset by the extra battery weight. Also the motors will have to work harder at higher RPM to keep the quad airborne. I think the stock capacity battery size is well-suited to this quad.

The instructions encourage you to stuff the battery leads up into the copter body so they don't hang out. I just let them hang out. Stuffing them up in there just stresses all the connections and solder joints and the wires don't stay up in there very will anyway. Just my opinion on that one, folks.

The motors are amazing on these little quads. They are good for about 70 hours of actual flying time. That's really pretty good. Still, if you are going to use the quad a lot and put about 100 flights on it, you will eventually have a motor go bad. It is a good idea to have a spaare motor kit. The motors on the 107C are 8.5mm wide. The motors from the 107L will NOT fit. So get the correct ones.

If you have to replace a motor, you'll have to be able to solder or know somebody who can do it for you. It's a simple soldering task for an experienced RC hobbyist so members of that ilk will have no problem. If you are just leaping into RC with this quad and don't have those skills because you haven't had to suffer the school of hard knocks like we old-timers did, you just have to learn soldering or lean on somebody who can do it for you. Some solder and a basic pencil soldering iron can be obtained for less that 20 bucks if you want to learn a new, useful skill.

As for the HD camera, it is quite sufficient. This little camera will never be super stable outdoors in wind but the video is still quite good. In windy conditions, you MUST press down the right stick to get into expert mode. If you don't you will not have sufficient control movement to fight the wind. You will watch helplessly as your copter drifts away from you if you can't bring it down immediately. Incidentally, while in expert mode if you are afraid of flipping the copter because of the unlimited control movement it provides, just click the left stick down to enter "no-flip" mode.

Also regarding the camera, you must follow the correct procedure to obtain video. Turn on your transmitter with the throttle completely off. Insert the SD card. Connect the battery. Wait for the red light to turn off in the SD card slot. All you should see is a tiny blue light (NO red light). Now you can press the little switch on the side to start recording. You'll see the tiny red light flashing. When you finish your video flight, you must press the little switch again to stop the video. Wait for the red light to go out (indicating the video file has been saved. Now you may unplug the battery. If desired you may also unplug the SD card now.

If you don't use the switch to stop the video, or if you unplug the battery while the red light is flashing, you will save no video.

Always plug/unplug the SD card with the battery disconnected! Also, the SD card socket is not like those on many mobile phones with which you may be familiar. There is no "spring action". You just slide the card in until it bottoms in the slot. If you keep pushing it when you feel resistance thinking you are going to push against the locking spring, don't do it. Push too hard and you could harm the card socket. So go easy on it!

It is amazing that we can now buy a gyro-stabilized copter and get it hovering with so little "learning". It was not unusual for people to spend weeks just learning the touch to get a single rotor copter off the ground in one piece and into a hover. Now it is so much cheaper and simpler. I won't say easy, because as I have said if you are absolute noob you have to learn the controls and develop your skills. Still, you should be able to get it off the ground and hover without too much agony.

If you are interested in flying RC, I don't think you can go wrong with giving this quad a try. I feel it is a bargain price and rewarding and fun to learn to fly.

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Geometric Dome Climber Play Center (Primary Colors), 60-Inch I was looking for some play equipment for my 4 year old since our new house doesn't have a playground in walking distance. I eyed this for months before finally deciding to go ahead and order it from another site where I found a lower price due to a coupon I had. I was surprised at the small size of the box. Assembly was fairly easy but took a few hours. Once the pattern is established, it is pretty self explanatory. I was very impressed with this when completed. The handles are like rock wall handles and great for kids who need more to grip. My 4 year old is now scaling this thing with no problem. A month in, I don't see any signs of wear. The color is nice because it blends into the landscape. Pulling through the neighborhood, it doesn't stand out like an eyesore. We have this and the matching small swingset from lifetime. I would recommend Lifetime's products to anyone. This feels commercial weight. We have it placed above a bed of thick mulch to cushion falls, but it is also easy to move if we need to place it somewhere else in the yard.  For the price, you can't beat it.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime Geometric Dome Climber Play Center (Primary Colors), 60-Inch

text_fidelity_a: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set I absolutely love this swingset. We ordered it from Costco, because the price was a bit lower. We already had the matching jungle gym, so we didn't really want to get the larger monkey bar swingset. I found this one and thought it was perfect. I was right. Assembly was a bear. Based solely on the weight of the pieces, you need a few people to put this together. It takes some maneuvering to get the pieces together and in place, but once they are together, they are solid. The swings and ring were a bit high for my 4 year old, so we picked up four 6 inch sections of chain from the local hardware store and some quick links. Problem solved. We left one of the swings higher for the older kids. My son and I swing on it together, and it only moves a bit. We will likely anchor it in the future, but for small children, it stays in place well enough. The coating on the swings is much better than the normal covered chains which crack and come apart. This is thick rubbery substance that fully wraps around the chains. We didn't use the feet on the bottom as it allows the set to settle into the ground a bit as we use it. The set looks professional, not tacky, and unlike wood sets, I won't be out there trying to clean it and check for splinters constantly. I can see this being used for generations. Great item. Seems like commercial quality.
text_fidelity_b: Lifetime Heavy Duty A-Frame Metal Swing Set

text_fidelity_a:
Tegu Robo Magnetic Wooden Block Set, Electric Aqua, 8 PIECE We received our first Tegu product in a Citrus Lane Subscription box. It was just 4 triangle shaped pieces. They were great, and I wanted to try more without getting a huge set in case they lost their luster with my son, which tends to happen with kids. We ordered this set to go along with the 4 pieces we already had.

The wood is lightweight and smooth. It is almost soft to the touch. The dyes used are non toxic. The magnets are safe since they are encased.

This set is great. My son likes robots, so the Robo look on the side of these blocks added to the fun. He can rearrange them into various new robots. We stick these in a busy bag for church, and they keep him occupied most Sundays.

We will most likely end up with more Tegu. The cost seems reasonable for a humanely produced toy made from quality materials.

The only problem we have is that sometimes the poles of the magnets don't line up, so they do not attract. We are used to Magformers and don't have that problem with those. I would still recommend these and consider them a go to gift for preschoolers.

text_fidelity_a:
Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules This is the best deck building game EVER!!
I am in my 20's and have only recently been introduced to deck building games, and instantly fell in love.
DOminion and the DC Comic deck games are my favorite, but Dominion provides a larger variety because the cards used change.
The game its self comes with several possible versions of the game.
For example, the game is plaid with several action card decks to draw from, but Dominion comes with twice as many action cards. So, no game is exactly alike. The rule book comes with various options of which action cards to play with for certain kinds of games.
This game is dynamic!

I first played Dominion at a bar with board games. After a few times I fell in love and bought this second edition. The cards are beautiful, more colorful than the first edition. (I attached some photos to see to see the cards)

It says that the game can be played in about 30 minutes... for me it takes closer to an hour with 3 players. It also probably depends on what type of game you play (which actions cards to choose to play with) But because we are still learning, maybe we go a little slower, constantly re reading what the action cards say/do.

At the end of the game, who ever has the most victory points wins.
text_fidelity_b: Dominion 2nd Edition | Deckbuilding Strategy Game for 2-4 Players, Ages 13+ | Updated Cards, Artwork, Streamlined Rules

Superfight: Core Deck - A Card Game of Absurd Arguments | Fun Family Friendly, Party Game of Super Powers and Super Problems, Enjoyed by Kids, Teens, and Adults, 500-Card Deck, 3+ Players, Ages 8+ We got this as a group game to play Memorial Day weekend and while we did not follow the directions (we made up our own - see below) - it was amazingly fun! We played late into the night and still talk about some of the awesome and amazing combos! (it's hard to beat three Jason's made of lava - even if you have the hummus the card). So much laughter and I look forward to playing it anytime I can!

For those interested on how we played as a large group: we divided up into teams of two or three. Each team got one white (character) card and two black (attribute) cards. They had a minute or so to talk about strategy amongst themselves. Then - the SuperFight was on! We went around the group and each team got to tell everyone about their character (& abilities) and then debate with each other on why they would win. Everyone as a group agreed or disagreed depending on the strength of the debate. We didn't keep score, but just round by round. Lots of fun and easy to play anywhere!
text_fidelity_b: Superfight: Core Deck - A Card Game of Absurd Arguments | Fun Family Friendly, Party Game of Super Powers and Super Problems, Enjoyed by Kids, Teens, and Adults, 500-Card Deck, 3+ Players, Ages 8+

The current product image is misleading, however, so I've posted photos to show how this nice little set comes. text_fidelity_a:
LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function I really love these Duplo Lego sets. While I do not have any little ones in the house, I like having some toys on hand for the occasional visitors with kids. These are always a hit and now when friends with little ones come over, the kids always remember our place because of the "Lego Lady!" haha! Bringing out the Legos has brought shy little ones out of their shell as they put together the pieces and play away.

This train set is great! it is super simple to put together, as with any Duplo set. You will need to unscrew the battery box to put in 4 AAA batteries, though. If you're lazy like me and don't want to trudge out to the garage for a screwdriver, you can easily open it with a table knife (haha.. see pic). To make the train go, first be sure there are batteries installed and then push the on/off button on the bottom. put the train on the track. The wheels straddle the inner upright portions of the track (see pic). Then simply give the train a little push and off it goes around the track.

To control the train, use the little action tiles. These are flat pieces with a small icon on them. There is one for each of the following actions. When the train goes over it, it performs the action:
- whistle (yellow) makes a train whistle sound
- horn (white) makes one toot sound - I thought this was for the lights but those didnt come on when it went over this one
- water (blue) stops for a bit there and makes a sound like it is getting water for the steam engine
- reverse (green) stops and reverses the train
- stop (red) stops the train

The action bricks are really easy to put down on the track - they just lay in the middle of the track and don't actually attach. So it is easy for the little ones to pick them up and move them around. This is super fun for the kiddos and definitely keeps them happy occupied for quite some time!

There is an App you can get as well - works for iPhone, iPad, and Android devices. It has nothing to do with the train set itself, though. I thought maybe it did, but it is really just a separate app/Game. It is a fun little game for young kids, though. App Tip: if you have an iPhone and aren't getting any sound with the app, be sure you don't have the device on mute. (for iPhones it is that side button you switch on/off). I don't have an iPad but I suspect it could have the same issue.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO DUPLO Town Steam Train 10874 Remote Control Set - Learning Toy and Daycare Accessory for Toddlers, Boys, Girls, and Kids 2-5 Years Old, Push and Go Battery Powered Set with RC Function

LeapFrog My Pal Violet (Frustration Free Packaging) Three of my four kids have had a LeapFrog My Pal Scout or Violet. Our first born would have had one but I don't think they were made back then. These little interactive toys are so great! Here's why I think your little ones will love them too!

1) It doesn't just talk, Scout/Violet says your child's name, puts their name into songs, and engages the child on a personal level. As soon as my kids realized it was talking to them they would laugh and try to make it do it again. It is still their favorite feature.
2) You can further personalize the Scout/Violet to sing/talk about your child's favorite animal, food and color. The pup uses these favorite things in silly songs. Warning: they are catchy and you will get them stuck in your head!
3) When your child changes, so does Scout/Violet. Anytime the favorites change you can just set the pup to match. The cord to plug it into your computer (USB) is housed right in the back of the pup. Once upon a time the cord was not attached. Be thankful it can't get lost with these newer models.

text_fidelity_a: Melissa & Doug Farm Sound Puzzle - Wooden Peg Puzzle With Sound Effects (8 pcs) [[VIDEOID:cd72f835dae1d0a3c3f6f6b497d37389]] This is the least child intuitive toy I have ever encountered. Shame on Melissa and Doug- a company that big should have tested this one out before producing. Here's how this puzzle works- as you REMOVE the pieces, the song plays "old mcdonald" but apparently you need to teach your toddler to remove it in the CORRECT order, starting with the farmer and WAITING after removing each piece to hear the song play. Now if you child removes it too quickly they obviously miss all the sounds- if they even hear them within the song. I was expecting to TEACH my toddler animal sounds by hearing them as he placed the pieces. NO such luck. Who in their right mind made a puzzle that plays the sounds when you TAKE out pieces? Most of the kids dump it over so they can make the puzzle. And then there are no sounds when the pieces are placed, disappointingly. Wish I had read reviews, but who would think that Melissa and Doug could RUIN a classic sound puzzle? Somehow, they managed it.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Farm Sound Puzzle - Wooden Peg Puzzle With Sound Effects (8 pcs)

I am impressed how quickly they caught on to the complicated rules that change slightly every round of the game. Basically, there are 11 (!!) rounds in this game, and each round, another card is "wild" and each round the size of the hand increases by one card. You can't play this game without a pen, paper, and perhaps even a calculator at the end to tally up the scores.
What annoyed me the most was the length of the game. Eleven rounds is veeeeeeeery long. And I paid $11-12 dollars for what is basically a deck of cards. They're not like a deck of normal cards, because they have 5 suits and are missing the 1's and 2's but they are just paper and ink and some instructions. They should have been half that price. I can't really see my family playing it again, as I can't really include my younger kids and they won't be patient for the hour it will take us to finish this game.

It arrived quickly, as we've become accustomed to when shopping Amazon, so ordering on December 27th for a January 2nd party was not a problem. It's been in my son's grubby little paws for five days  now and he is enamored of the thing.  It's wonderful to see my very large, very rough and tumble four year old boy carefully, slowly, cautiously navigate this little ball bearing around the maze.  He twist it, turns it, lifts it so he can see it from the bottom, and growls when the ball falls off the track.  But then he gets right back to it.  He has beaten it, but that doesn't seem to diminish his interest in trying again.  Whoever came up with this idea for this toy has my respect.  I only gave it four stars for durability because it seems like it could be a little higher quality.  For such an amazing toy, the materials should be of a high enough quality to make it an heirloom.  It is honestly one of my favorite toys, along with quadrilla and magnatiles, so I wish it was a little more substantial.  We have had no problems with it as of yet, though, after five days of heavy use.

Brybelly Sure Stick Rubber Foam Poker Table Top Layout Card-playing is a huge family event for us. Not just poker, but all kinds of different games. We don't have room for a separate game table, we usually play at the kitchen table. When I saw this product online (and found out that the dimensions are very close to those of our kitchen table), I decided to give it a try. I was a little hesitant because it was a tiny bit more expensive than I thought was appropriate for a card-playing surface. Having used this product, however, it is worth every penny! There is nothing negative that I can say about it. Here are the positives:
* rubberized back prevents it from sliding around on the table
* green fabric surface allows for perfect movement of cards on the table (cards slide just the right amount when playing or dealing, but don't skitter off the table on to the floor)
* attractive green color
* fabric surface resists stains
* the ability to roll it up after use and store in a conveniently sized carrying bag (with a handle) is a real plus!
* there may have been just the slightest funky smell when I first opened the package (I have a super sensitive nose) but that smell has completely dissipated
* perfect size (for us anyway); I'm sure it could be cut to fit a smaller table, though that would mess up the white outline

I am very, very happy with this product! It fit the bill perfectly.
text_fidelity_b: Brybelly Sure Stick Rubber Foam Poker Table Top Layout

text_fidelity_a:
LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink My grandmother purchased these as a special gift for 2 girls ages just turned 2 and almost 4 as there was some resentment from their new baby brother. She told me there were many good reviews and thought it could help the girls stay busy when Mommy needs to help their brother. These are a life saver. We even got the headphones to match so there is not fights over I can't hear my book because of your book. It was also amazing we got 2 system to solve fights. I just took a label maker and put each of their names on them.

They did get the first series of books. However the almost 4 year old is flying through the books as they are easy for her. So we just got one next level up book and that seems to be more her speed. Each system we were able to download 10 books and the sample book. Unfortunately it won't fit more. So as the older one gets more advanced, we will delete the younger books.

The system does take AA batteries, so I suggest keeping a spare set on hand. The downside is there is no warning of low battery, so it helps to have new ones ready to go. You also need a small screw driver to put them in.

I also suggest getting (or making as I did) a tote bag for them to store their system and books in.

The device is easy to open. They do need assistance with the books sometimes. I do wish the stylus pen cord was a bit longer, but that may be a safety thing too so the kids don't get hurt.

Even if you cannot afford the books right away (keep an eye as I often see them go on sale for $5-6 here) the starter book has 5 pages of activities to entertain the children.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapStart Interactive Learning System, Pink

Niya - a game by Bruno Cathala I love to play games! Over the years we've played lots of party games and games for groups (may have something to do with having 6 kids), but now that we are empty nesters we have been looking for games for 2 players. I don't particularly like games that are super complex, where you have to read every card and figure out how it interacts with the other 200 cards. Niya can be explained in 5 minutes and played in 10-15 minutes, but it is also strategic.
The quality is excellent, with a great metal tin instead of a cardboard box, sturdy board pieces, and weighty playing pieces.

All in all a great game. Highly recommended.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall) This unyielding, oversized beast hangs out in my daughter's room and watches her while she sleeps. It has given me pause a couple of times because it has a very serious, fierce Cheetah face. Angry even. This isn't your garden variety Beanie Boo or cute puffy kitty plush. This is a predator and it lets you know it.

Way back when I was a kid, back when we wore newspapers around our feet instead of shoes to trudge to school in 18 feet of snow, I had a panther like this. It was all black and scary enough to send the house cat running full speed out of the room with a puffy tail. I loved my Bagheera so dearly, like my daughter loves this Cheetah. Some sort of magic happens when little girls receive a giant stuffed cat for the Christmas of their 8th year. Alas, my Bagheera crossed the stuffed animal Rainbow Bridge many years ago, but he will always be fondly remembered.

I am very happy that my daughter is also able to shower her love on a giant, regal stuffed animal like I did as a kid, when we lived without electricity or indoor toilets, and my only source of heat was snuggling with my stuffed wild cat. I always took my Bagheera to the outhouse with me in the dead on the night to scare off the wolves, coyotes, and wild boar. That I am here writing this today is evidence that my stuffed cat had a huge impact on my young life. I have no doubt that this Cheetah would also do a great job of deterring bears and badgers on a late night stroll to use the toilet. Thankfully my daughter will never have to deal with such harrowing circumstances, but nevertheless, even if its only job is to sit in a room looking majestic, I highly recommend that you gift this Cheetah to a lucky kid.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Giant Cheetah - Lifelike Stuffed Animal (Stands Nearly 3 Feet Tall)

text_fidelity_a: Melissa & Doug Easel Accessory Set - Paint, Cups, Brushes, Chalk, Paper, Dry-Erase Marker I bought this accessory kit twice because I bought two Melissa and Dave easels for my grandson and twin granddaughters. You get everything that you need for your child to begin painting immediately. It comes with a sturdy roll of paper that fits nicely atop the M&D easel. The paper can also be used without the easel for painting, drawing and coloring.  It comes with bottles of paints in the primary colors which can easily be mixed to create other colors. The paint clean up is easy, but I still recommend a drop cloth under the easel. Since your child is sure to get paint on themselves, some soap and water will get it off quickly. It comes with cups for the paints that includes tops with holes for the paint brushes that also come with the set.  The cups minimize spillage of the water. It also comes with chalk and an eraser. The kit contains everything that your child needs to begin painting, except a drop cloth and an apron. Otherwise, you don't have to concern yourself with buying the items separately. Finally, the paper can be refilled easily as it comes in a two-roll pack for less than $10. I recommend this kit without reservation.

text_fidelity_a:
Melissa & Doug Jumbo Paint Brushes (Set of 4) | Arts & Crafts | 3+ | Gift for Boy or Girl I've bought this easel for the second time and I cannot recommend it more. The first, I bought for my grandson for his third birthday. He used it to the exclusion of his other toys. My daughter set it up in their back yard and he paints for hours. After the first month, he knew where the accessories were located and he'd set up his supplies by himself. The easel is sturdy and my son-in-law had no problems putting it together. My grandson does not indicate any chance of giving up the easel too soon.

I bought the second one for my 2 year old twin granddaughters. They too love the easel, and its invitation to be creative. At first, I was worried that the twins would fight over it, but that has been no problem since while one works on one side, her sister works on the other. The easel is adjustable so it grows right along with them and they can use it for years to come. It is not plastic, but constructed with a solid wood frame and includes a tray on both sides to hold paints, eraser and other accessories. Also, there is an area at the top of the easel to put a roll of drawing paper, so paper is always at the ready, Once it runs out, you simply replace it with another roll.

The easel is worth the money. I was pleasantly surprised when I returned to buy the second one because it had dropped in price; however, even at the higher price the easel was well worth it. Once again, I recommend this item without reservations.
text_fidelity_b: Melissa & Doug Jumbo Paint Brushes (Set of 4) | Arts & Crafts | 3+ | Gift for Boy or Girl

text_fidelity_a:
Pressman Charades for Kids - The 'No Reading Required' Family Game, 5" Yes my grandkids love this; they are ages 5 and 10. The 5 year old can read some words, but not all, so we keep him to acting out the picture. Whoever guesses correctly "wins" that card and that is the point system. 4 cards wins the game. If someone does not guess correctly, the "actor" wins the card.

I would say that for the younger ones acting out a picture, it is helpful to have them "coached" as they act out because they don't always understand how to act out in a different way that can make a clue understandable. For instance, our 5 year old had to act out the picture "feeding a baby", but he didn't hold his hands exactly correctly and he didn't know how to add some other actions to help us understand that, i.e., rocking the baby, or shaking the "bottle", etc. A "coach" can help the younger ones with adding additional actions to their hints.

I think it helps all kids with standing up in front of others, self-esteem, considering how visual actions are important and ways to get across a message clearly so others understand. The 10 year old often said "this is easy" until he tried acting it out in a way for us to understand what his clue was.

I highly recommend. Young ones will need some help in acting out the pictures.
text_fidelity_b: Pressman Charades for Kids - The 'No Reading Required' Family Game, 5"

text_fidelity_a:
Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary) Got this for adults in family to play. 2 to 6 people play. No one had played before so we were learning strategies as we played. The only time limit is the one minute timer each person has in front of them when it is their turn to ask questions.

To start, a plastic adjustable headband apparatus is given to each player; maximun of six players. Tokens are passed out, 3 per person, one card is dealt to each person that is kept face down and not read; each player takes their one card and place it in the headband on their head so it faces out towards the other players. Do not have mirrors or reflective items nearby so no one can accidentally see their card. If a player leaves the table for a moment, they remove the card and place it face down on the table and return the card to the headband when they return, being careful not to read the card. In addition, a card of helpful questions is passed out to each player to help them ask meaningful questions to get critical answers so they can correctly guess who/what they are on their card.

Rules say the tallest person starts the game, but you have the freedom to start it in any way and play continues to the left. It is also extremely helpful to have a sheet of paper with pen or pencil so you can record answers to the questions you ask. It is hard to remember what questions you previously asked and valuable time is wasted if you are repeating questions that were already answered. We also learned great questions to ask as each player asked their own questions. The players answer with "I don't know", Yes, No, Could be, according to their knowledge of the question. Try to think before you answer and be sure you know the answer because that is critical to the player getting the correct information.

We played this game a lot and got better with each game as we learned how to ask very "to the point" questions. For instance, to start the game, you want to find out if you are a person (George Washington), place (the Great Wall of China) , or thing (jalapeno), (3 separate questions) and each time the other players will answer you with Yes, No, Could Be or Don't know. If you are a person, are you alive or dead? are you fictional (James Bond) or real (John Travolta); am I female or male; am I old or young, etc. The little hint cards do not give you all these options; you have to figure out how to ask your questions in a meaningful way. Each person asks questions until the sand in the timer runs out and play passes to the next person to the left. Keep going around the table until someone guesses their card correctly, and they win and surrender one token. A new round with new cards is started. Rounds are played until someone wins the most rounds and all their tokens surrendered.

You can surrender your card and get a new card and be penalized by receiving an additional token from "the bank" if your questioning is not getting you anywhere, or just start over from the beginning with your questioning because you may have misunderstood an answer that is leading you in the wrong direction. But we usually stuck it out and re-asked questions to find the correct path.

It is a very challenging game; you must be able to think out your progression of questions to reach a conclusion before anyone else. The first player to surrender all their tokens wins the game. The more we played, the better we got at asking questions and the faster we could complete a game, although it could be as long as 45 minutes. A very lively and intriguing game and highly recommended. It could be frustrating but keep a cool head and focus on "how" to ask critical questions. We will play it at all future get togethers and I can't wait until we do.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Hedbanz, 2nd Edition Picture-Guessing Family Board Game, for Adults and Kids Ages 7 and up (Styles May Vary)

text_fidelity_a: A Game of Thrones Boardgame Second Edition If you are a fan of Game of Thrones and board games, this was made for you. It's a complex game that you will probably screw up a few of the rules on your first few playthroughs. Warning though: Even if one of your friends is a fan of the books or show, it might not be enough if they are not a patient person or avid board gamer. Attention spans expire and people get salty and this game can last for 5 hours. We've had people that we explicitly DO NOT play with after making the mistake of teaching them (teaching is a heavy time investment). If you have a good group of people that aren't snarky and that don't have bad tempers, then you should have a blast.

text_fidelity_a:
Nerf Official: Lazer Tag Phoenix LTX Tagger 2-pack - Fun Multiplayer Laser Tag Game for Kids & Adults, Ages 8 & Up (Amazon Exclusive) I was skeptical about playing with laser tag guns. I'm an adult and the ones we had as a kid sucked. These are different. There is recoil when you shoot. When you run out of ammo you have to physically reload the gun, a pop the clip out and put a new clip in motion. We thought that one pair of the guns (we got two sets) was defective. Turns out we are just idiots and had 2 of the 4 the guns set to outside mode. That makes the guns far more vulnerable to getting hit as outside mode is for over longer distances (to the point where we were shooting at the ceiling with the gun going off like it was a direct hit). Once we had all the guns set to indoor mode it corrected the problem and it was extremely accurate.

These turned out to be a lot of fun and we are ordering another pair today!
text_fidelity_b: Nerf Official: Lazer Tag Phoenix LTX Tagger 2-pack - Fun Multiplayer Laser Tag Game for Kids & Adults, Ages 8 & Up (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a: A Game of Thrones The Card Game Second Edition Core Set | Epic Battle Game | Strategy Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games Great game! Nice community for it online and in most cities. But for casual and new players, you need to know that if you want to play competitively or "correctly" you need to buy three of these. You are allowed to have up to 3 of the same card in your deck which makes the odds of drawing those cards higher. There is an out-of-the-box game where you can play with pre-built decks that aren't "competition legal". In reality the most fun is had with 3 core sets. They release chapter packs monthly and big box expansions once or twice a year. If you are into games and into game of thrones, you will enjoy this.
text_fidelity_b: A Game of Thrones The Card Game Second Edition Core Set | Epic Battle Game | Strategy Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 1-2 Hours | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

text_fidelity_a: MindWare Qwirkle Board Game the game itself is fine and adults will probably enjoy it.  a big problem is that it is very hard to distinguish the red and orange.  a second problem is the pieces are not fun to handle.  for example dominos and mahjong tiles and chess pieces are fun in different ways - they click and are smooth or each piece is different.  quirkle tiles would be much improved if the different designs were carved and raised.  it could easily be made fun for everyone including the visually impaired by making small differences in the colors - like red is inset and orange is raised, blue has an extra groove and so on. i improved the game for children by using a big bag of different stones like mancala stones.  when each person made a 2 point move, they got two stones.  this means you dont need pencil and paper to add up, and its more fun for each person to have their own dragon hoard. if you run out of stones, just take twenty (or some even number) from each person and put them back in the bag.
text_fidelity_b: MindWare Qwirkle Board Game

Vermont Teddy Bear Plush Dragon - Dragon Stuffed Animal, Green, 18 Inch UPDATE 2/20/2020: After several weeks Vermont Teddy Bear did the right thing and replaced the defective toy. The replacement is in perfect condition and appears to be of excellent quality. I have updated the overall rating.

Originally I gave a great review as it was a gift and the recipient loves it. Since she cant have flowers on the ICU floor of the hospital. After having had brain cancer surgery, I sent a stuffed animal and candy lieu of flowers. She sent me a couple of pictures and I noticed that the LH ear and tusk are not properly positioned or or even close to symmetrical with the RH side. The left ear has a large section missing at the top. I later spoke to her over the phone and asked if the features of the animal were symmetrical. She said no they were not but she loves it anyway (Of course she would say this). I however, am very disappointed that I sent her a defective gift. I bought the "VERMONT" brand for its reputation of quality products. I have since seen reviews of Vermont having similar quality issues with miss-aligned facial features on their stuffed animals. I suppose quality issues can be expected since the Vermont stuffed animals are now manufactured outside of the USA as a cost saving measure. (This is stated on the "Vermont" website) The stuffed animals are now only stuffed and sewed closed here in Vermont, USA. (Also stated on the "Vermont" website) Quality control should never have allowed this defective product to be sold and shipped. The decision to ship a poor quality / defective product has just cost Vermont a customer and a bad review. I would rather pay a bit more for a quality product than less for a poor one. This is exactly what I thought I was doing with this order. obviously cannot return it for replacement due to the circumstances. I will NOT be buying Vermont brand products going forward. I can pay less for crap and at least I'll know what to expect when it arrives.
text_fidelity_b: Vermont Teddy Bear Plush Dragon - Dragon Stuffed Animal, Green, 18 Inch

Toys for 3 Year Old Boys - Race Track Car Toys for Boys 3-5 Years Old - 4 Year Old Boy Birthday Gift - 3 Year Old Boy Gift Kids Games Ages 3-5 - Magnet Toy Thinking Fine Motor Skills Toys for Ages 2-4 The idea is great and at $20 (Black Friday) it’s not the worst toy. The problem is that all of the mechanisms are so flimsy that it’s just not a good toy for the age it is meant for. They get frustrated when things don’t work and don’t understand why things don’t work when they take the correct action. Add to that the helicopter mechanism not working at all because it’s too far away from the car, and you just can’t enjoy the toy.

So I mentioned the helicopter doesn’t work. It’s too high for the magnet to grab the car. So your 2 or 3 year old won’t understand at all why one of the knobs doesn’t work. Then the car gets to the bridge, which at least works most often. Then the grey lifting part which constantly comes out of its socket. Then the area where the cars turn…if you aren’t slow and gentle the cars will get bumped off the track. Everything is just so flimsy.

Due to all the issues, as an adult it’s impossible to get a single car all the way through the circuit, even when being as careful as possible. So there’s no way a child can possibly make it happen. Don’t get me wrong, my kid is still playing with it but she doesn’t use any of the buttons or levers…just kinda pushes the cars around the ramp (which comes off every single time she moves the toy)

2 stars because my toddler is enjoying the toy, despite all of its flaws. But none of the things it claims to do…are happening. We will trash this toy in about a week or two.
text_fidelity_b: Toys for 3 Year Old Boys - Race Track Car Toys for Boys 3-5 Years Old - 4 Year Old Boy Birthday Gift - 3 Year Old Boy Gift Kids Games Ages 3-5 - Magnet Toy Thinking Fine Motor Skills Toys for Ages 2-4

VTech Baby Lil' Critters Shake and Wobble Busy Ball Amazon Exclusive, Purple This toy is GREAT for entertaining a baby. Due to the language and songs played, I would NOT RECOMMEND this toy for any vegan or anyone who isn't interested in supporting the dairy industry. It's one thing to sing cute songs about happy cows on the farm...but it almost felt cult-like with its lyrics constantly berating your child about how they should drink their milk. I don't love that.

My baby has been entertaining herself with this toy since she was 4 months old. At 6 months, she still likes it a lot. It is used at the dinner table to keep her entertained while we all eat. It almost always works through most of the meal. I highly recommend it as a toy that can distract a child. We don't let her have it outside of mealtime so it keeps it fresh and interesting.

It does have a surprising amount of songs to it. Even several weeks after ownership a few songs were played that we hadn't heard before. But there are some songs that get played all the time. 2 months of ownership and the parents aren't yet annoyed by it so that's a good thing.

I took a star off for the incessant dairy promoting lyrics which just seem strange and I'm convinced that the dairy industry had some involvement in their creation.

The most fascinating thing is that this could be considered a "smart" train set - there is a sensor built into the tunnels so that once the train goes through, it can perform an action like stop, or sound horn.
