You can do an "easy mode" or a "hard mode" - the difference is that one type of flashlight illuminates the whole "path" of its light, while the other just has a small "spotlight" circle. The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games First and foremost, this is a LIVING card game. It is not a COLLECTIBLE card game. Big difference! The latter just means that you can buy new expansions to expand your gameplay / add mechanics / etc. The latter means you have to go and buy packs at the store in order to get newer and better cards. In a collectible card game, a billionaire can go and buy all the packs and have the best deck ever. In this game, everyone who buys the game (and its expansion cards) will be on even footing. I find collectible card games to be somewhat predatory given they're essentially like gambling. Okay, on to the review.

High level message is, not great but not bad either. If you love Lord of the Rings you'll have a better experience. If you're neutral on it, then you're not going to enjoy the complicated grind of learning how to play.

Pros
- Beautiful artwork
- Good use of the LOTR lore in the gameplay and story
- Decent length of games - assume 1 to 1.5 hours
- Pretty good mechanics, once you understand them

Cons
- Phew, this game is complicated. The first sign that it's complicated, is the fact that there are TWO rule books, each of hefty size. This is not the kind of game you whip out on game night with a bunch of casual players. You need other folks who are dedicated to play this game, willing to watch a YouTube video together, or something, and then willing to stumble around for the first hour to get this done.
- So many things to keep track of... there's spinners, dials, tokens... did I mention this game is complicated
text_fidelity_b: The Lord of the Rings: The Card Game Revised Core Set | Adventure/Cooperative Game for Adults and Teens | Ages 14+ | 1-4 Players | Average Playtime 30-120 Minutes | Made by Fantasy Flight Games

Deep Dilemmas - 'Would You Rather' Conversation Cards for Ridiculous Debates & Funny Interactions. 200 Original Ice Breaker Question Cards for Adults, Couples, & College Students - Ages 16+ I've picked up a bunch of these conversation starter games and some are better than others. I would say this one is right down the middle. It's a very straightforward concept - on each card is two choices and you're supposed to pick each one. The problem is that maybe half of them are real dilemmas, while the other half are no brainers. For instance - "would you rather live on a 50th floor penthouse with no elevator or have $2 million in dimes". These are the kinds of questions that might as well not be there because everyone just picks one of the answers and there's no discussion needed, which defeats the point of the game. In some ways I feel like they knew this going in - on the side of the box, it's actually printed that the playtime is up to 60 minutes - with 200 cards, that averages out to 3 cards per minute.

All in all, can't really recommend. You could probably spend an afternoon and come up with better ideas on your own.

text_fidelity_a:
Lorsaberus Light Saber, 10 Mode Sound RGB 12 Color Changeable Metal Hilt Light Sabers, Dueling Smooth Swing Light Saber Sword Toy for Men,Children's Day Gifts (1 inch Blade)-Grey [[VIDEOID:3325afb06624e7eb67d7487ba5918892]] This is a well made little product. When I use the word "little" I mean it literally in the sense that it is much smaller than a Star Wars™ light-saber that they use for props in the movies. Although I do have big hands . . . unless Alec Guinness and Mark Hamill have teensy-tiny hands, this is about an inch smaller than the ones they used to battle the empire.

The diameter is just a little bigger than a US Quarter coin and just over 1 inch. The ones in the movie are closer to over 2 inches by my estimation.

All that being said, this is still a fun little toy light-saber, if a little overpriced in my opinion. At the current price of $120, I'd say wait for a sale.

It is well made and the colors and sounds are well done. It has motion-sensing so the sounds will change when you "swing" it at a stormtrooper, for instance. (see video).

There are quite a few different modes that can be set by double-clicking on the power button once it's turned on.

It is very LOUD as well, so be aware. There is no volume control for the sound that I can tell -- nothing in the instructions about it. The instructions are just a 1-page printout, but they're fairly thorough, so I can't complain. The translation is not that bad -- average, but understandable-ish.

It recharges quickly and it can go at least an hour without the battery dying. I haven't messed with it enough to see exactly how long the battery will last, but it recharges pretty quickly.

The "saber" portion is just a piece of semi-opaque PVC tubing with a curved "nose-cone" on the end to give it a rounded look. It looks decent. It's covered in protective film that you can peel off for a nice look. I didn't peel it off all the way yet because I'm thinking of maybe mounting it on a wall mounted display box to nerd-out my office more.

This would be fun for a child/adult who's into anything Star Wars™ but I don't think it's an "officially" licensed Lucasfilm product. Does it matter? It doesn't actually claim to be anywhere on the box or labeling that I can see and I'm not sure that the term "light saber" is trademarked or copyrighted, so unless you care to have the "official".

If you are considering this for a child, be aware -- it's not sharp, but the "saber" part is not a soft piece of plastic. By that I mean . . . if you get hit with a good swing, it's going to leave a mark. Not as bad as getting hit with a Louisville Slugger™ . . . but still . . . probably not a good gift idea for the younger kiddos.

Overall, it's a neat product, but I had to take off a star because it's smaller than the movie version and the price is quite steep for a toy, even considering that it's a very nice quality toy.

And did I mention very fun? Now I must go and take care of that annoying Vader guy.
text_fidelity_b: Lorsaberus Light Saber, 10 Mode Sound RGB 12 Color Changeable Metal Hilt Light Sabers, Dueling Smooth Swing Light Saber Sword Toy for Men,Children's Day Gifts (1 inch Blade)-Grey

text_fidelity_a:
SHASHIBO Shape Shifting Box - Award-Winning, Patented Fidget Cube w/ 36 Rare Earth Magnets - Transforms Into Over 70 Shapes, Gift Box, Download Fun in Motion Toys Mobile App (Black & White, 4 Pack) This is much more fun than I thought it would be.

It's easy to get started, but gets really tough to figure out all the shapes when you know that there are *allegedly* over 70 shapes to make with it.

Right out of the box, it looks a lot like a weird little cube. It's maybe a little smaller than a standard Rubik's cube for comparison. But this cube is more complex, even though it doesn't have as many permutations as Rubik's.

The printed portions have nice patterns (on this cube, there are three different patterns depending on the configuration). Once you start playing with it, you can't put it down.

Even though it says in the instructions that you might have trouble getting it back to its cubic form, it's really not that hard and it also seems to be the default shape that you will keep returning to again and again, even when you're obsessing about discovering another shape.

I'd recommend this for anyone who enjoys puzzles and mind games. Even if they don't, this might get them thinking more spatially. There's a certain thrill of finding a new shape that you never knew was there. And the satisfying *click* sound when you get one. So far, I'm nowhere close to the 70+ that the box mentions. I can make a couple dozen, but then it's back to a cube. It's very weird even to try to duplicate the same shape you just had only a few seconds ago.

Nothing negative about this that I could find except maybe if the cube starts to wear out after a ton of usage. It seems to be made with vinyl stickers that will hopefully last a long time, though.

And one word of warning: I can imagine certain personality types getting frustrated with this and tearing it to a pile of tiny little plastic pyramids.

Overall, this gets a solid 5-stars. I'll probably get at least one more of these since they can be combined to create even more variations.
text_fidelity_b: SHASHIBO Shape Shifting Box - Award-Winning, Patented Fidget Cube w/ 36 Rare Earth Magnets - Transforms Into Over 70 Shapes, Gift Box, Download Fun in Motion Toys Mobile App (Black & White, 4 Pack)

text_fidelity_a:
HEXBUG nano Robotic Cat - Interactive Automated Toy, Stimulate Hunting Instinct of Your Feline and Create Exercising Opportunities - Ships Assorted When they hear it switch on, they will all jump down from the bed upstairs and come running downstairs to play with it. The downside is they will chase it under the stove, behind a cabinet, under the couch, and generally places that are a pain to retrieve it from. That has limited how often we get it out for them to play with it, but when we do, they are obsessed. Lots of reviews say the battery life is horrible, so I got the extra batteries, but we are still on the original. Granted, we don't leave it out all day for them (it isn't a loud toy, but when it goes underneath something and starts vibrating against it, that can be very loud).

Full disclosure: on the second or third day of having this toy, one of our cats bit down on it, causing one of the legs to come off. The legs are tiny and not a choking or digestive concern, but this made it unbalanced, causing it to go in tiny circles and not move in straight lines anymore. I was able to find Hexbugs made for kids in the toy section of a local big box store, but without the fluffy tail. This makes the bug even more likely to go underneath things, so stick with the fluffy tailed version!
text_fidelity_b: HEXBUG nano Robotic Cat - Interactive Automated Toy, Stimulate Hunting Instinct of Your Feline and Create Exercising Opportunities - Ships Assorted

Just turn on the Calm app on your phone, chill out, sip some wine, and put this puzzle together by yourself as you meditate on your breathing and enjoying the simple things in life, counting your blessings as you do. In fact, we loved this puzzle so much we ordered a second one in the series.

text_fidelity_a: Bicycle Nailed It - Games Party Games - Card Game We love having get togethers with friends, which is something we don't get to do a lot of in a pandemic. But there have been pretty days where we can do so safely on the patio and play a game, such as this new Bicycle game. Depending on who you have in attendance, this game can go from comical icebreaker to bawdy fun. The instructions are quite easy. The tough part is being creative enough on the fly to spin a story that will have the judge (and the competition) in stitches, which is pretty much the name of the game. Because you want to be original, fresh, and funny. The game progresses quickly, and you can play it in about 30 minutes, so it doesn't take up an entire evening in case you want to play something else or have dinner.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Nailed It - Games Party Games - Card Game

text_fidelity_a: Husaria European International Chess Wooden Game Set, King's Classic - 11.3-Inch Small Size Chess Set with Folding Board and Felt Bottom Chessmen When my grandfather died, the one thing I really wanted was his chess set. But when we went through his things, we discovered that someone else had taken it. So I never did get that game. This board, however, is also very well made, with hand carved playing pieces that are handsome and durable. I like that the board folds in half with ample storage inside to hold all of your game pieces. I also keep the box itself to store it in, so that things don't get scratched and it lasts even longer. But it is so well made and so attractive, you could very well make it a family heirloom to be handed down from one generation to the next if you so choose. If not, it is still a great game board to use and play chess with your family while we all stay at home.

text_fidelity_a: Snap Circuits Jr. SC-100 Electronics Exploration Kit, Over 100 Projects, Full Color Project Manual, 28 Snap Circuits Parts, STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8 + Poorly designed and clumsily made. The pieces are far too large and bulky to make anything a bit complicated. Kids are basically paying simple Lego games, although there are some sounds, a light and a turning fan. What it really is is mechanically buttoning pieces following some poorly explained charts. Not a good way to learn electronic circuits. Not even complete in basic electronic components. IC units are not clearly explained in terms of how they work and how to connect them. Some components like the photo resister are not very sensitive. The manual is wordy but does a poor job in explaining what is behind each circuit. Hence very poorly telling the kids what they are doing in terms of electronic circuitry.
text_fidelity_b: Snap Circuits Jr. SC-100 Electronics Exploration Kit, Over 100 Projects, Full Color Project Manual, 28 Snap Circuits Parts, STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8 +

Toysmith DLX Pocket Kite It is cute in a small package, especially for small kids. But it is not easy to fly, because its ratio of surface area to weight is low. That means it needs strong wind to fly. That is not very good for kids. In bullet points:

Positive:

3) Inexpensive.

Negative:

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Hi Ho! Cherry-O Board Game for 2 to 4 Players Kids Ages 3 and Up (Amazon Exclusive) At first glance my daughter seemed quite intrigued by the little fruity pieces. In the meantime, I was just wondering silently how long it would take for us to lose a few of the tiny things, whereas if we did, we'd have to throw the whole game away. Anyway, that was our first impression.

As we started the game, I found it very annoying to have to load all the little fruit pieces onto the board, 40 in all. 40 pieces tinier than a marble. And if you take your basket out of the hole, the little fruit pieces will roll into the hole where the basket was and to retrieve it you have to disrupt the entire board and put back all 40 pieces again. That is of course worst case, but it did (and WILL) happen, and was annoying.

You spin the spinner and if it lands on a number, you take that many fruits off your tree. If the spinner lands on the dog or bird you give back 2, and if it lands on the spilled basket, you give back everything in your basket.

There is a little over a 40% chance that the spinner will land you on one of the spaces where you need to give back your fruits. My poor daughter, through hard luck, kept landing on either the number 1, the dog, or the bird. So whatever little she got, she would have to keep putting it back.

This game bored me to tears and worst of all it made my daughter very sad. She did not have a fit but she just had a really sad face every time the spinner landed on the dog or bird. This game is pure luck, so there was no way to exercise her mind except for counting up to 4 fruits or taking away 2 of them.

Would not recommend. NOT FUN AT ALL. Lots of better games out there.
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Hi Ho! Cherry-O Board Game for 2 to 4 Players Kids Ages 3 and Up (Amazon Exclusive)

text_fidelity_a:
Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches First thing I noticed was how close this stuffed goose resembled the real thing. Second, the sound effect was so realistic. And third, there was no way for the batteries to be removed. All three demands of mine has been met. Now I purchase a lot of duck and geese related items for the baby shower of my niece, my brother finally got a girl who though he was decent and good looking enough to reproduce with. So while I was confused on what Auntie of the year was going to give to my first born niece, I remembered all the years growing up where my brother tormented and made fun of. Then it dawned on me! I was going to gift all duck and geese related things to my niece so she will grow up loving them. Why you ask? Well I will share a story. Long ago, back in the mid 90’s my grandmother took my brother and I to the local duck pond to let us feed the ducks bread. I, obviously the intelligent one, knew to throw the bread as far away as I could away from me. My brother, a few fries short of a happy meal, threw it at his feet. Before he knew it all these mystical, beautiful beasts of the pond surrounded him. I remember him mocking me, “ you aren’t cool the ducks don’t like you”. And I can remember clearly him saying “ I AM THEIR GOD.” Then karma happened. All my Sunday school teaching happened as I sat in the car with my grandmother waiting for this false duck god to finish his loaf of bread it happened. Our almighty creater from above, the real God, spoke “There is no true God but me” and just like that my brother ran out of bed. These geese, realized he had no bread and he was a false prophet started to chant their battle cry! Next thing I knew, my brother started to get attacked by a mob of geese. Now he’s banging at my grandmother’s car door to let him in but she still laughing so hard she couldn’t reach over to unlock the door. (We didn’t have power doors during this time) I could of easily reached over and unlocked the door, but I sat back and watched this biblical lesson unfold in front of my eyes. Did you know geese have teeth on their tongue? He found out that day Eventually my grandma let him in and they surrounded the car for a good 10 minutes before they left to stalk their new prey.
That day I almost became an only child and that day changed my brother forever.

So yes this stuffed geese and all the other geese and duck related items from this seller is worth the money. It was amazing seeing a grown mad cowering in fear as he unwrapped every single duck and goose at his baby shower. His child is going to befriend the very creatures that almost murdered him in cold blood over a loaf of bread.
10/10 will buy from again.
text_fidelity_b: Wild Republic Audubon Birds Canada Goose Plush with Authentic Bird Sound, Stuffed Animal, Bird Toys for Kids and Birders, 5 inches

text_fidelity_a:
Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual My child's science project last year was growing crystals. We had lots of fun using different temperature liquids, chemicals, etc. to see which would grow fastest, best, make the most solid of crystals and even made rock candy as a "take home" treat. I love the creativity of this kit. It allows for you to create UP TO 13 different experiments (but if you cheat you can get a couple more out of it). Some of the chemicals used are not safe for young kids so I'd highly suggest sticking to the recommended manufacturer's age. Not to mention the fact that some of the crystals will take longer than a week to fully form -- most kids don't have the patience to wait. Not waiting the proper amount of time to ensure the solidity of the crystals will result in disappointment as you can imagine something that isn't solid enough can break very easy. Following directions is paramount! Make sure you sit with your child and read through all of the instructions before beginning. I'd suggest sticking with the easiest project first to get their feet wet on experimenting then gradually go through the "harder" ones. I do like that the simple purchase of extra chemicals (or using sugar) can add a lot more fun to your kit. Thames & Kosmos is a good company. They even provide online printable instructions along side the greatly illustrated manual. http://www.thamesandkosmos.com/news/manualsamples/659127_glowingcrystals_manual_sample.pdf
The price of the kit is very fair. In fact, I'd say it would be an excellent science fair project to conduct with your child this spring. Start practicing now and wow the judges with modified versions. Just be sure to do your homework. Check out books from your local library on growing crystals and start taking notes. This could be a really fun learning experience for grade-schoolers and homeschoolers alike. The only thing I thought was slightly cheesy was the "treasure case" and the shapes (thus my four stars). But kids will get a kick out of them.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Crystal Growing Science Kit Grow Over A Dozen Crystals with 15 Experiments, Includes Storage Case & 32 Page Color Laboratory Manual

text_fidelity_a: Pass the Stache Board Game Watching a group of 13 year olds play Moustache Smash is like watching a Black Friday sale with everyone fighting for the same discounted towels. I couldn't help but laugh hysterically as each girl held the mustache up to her face then frantically tried to be the first to smash the card that either matched the color or the shape of their mustache. (Mind you they had to remember which mustache they chose and what it looked like because they have to keep it up on their face at all times when the game is in play - until it's time to snatch a card). The game comes with 6 mustaches on very solid plastic sticks. There is a suction cup at the end of the mustache that allows the playing card to be snatched up quite easily. It's best to play on a solid surface to make sure the card stays put. There are 32 mustache cards of various colors and shapes. Each player takes a turn being the dealer. The dealer flips the card over for all to see - but can't cheat by flipping the card facing them first. IF a player accidentally snatches up the wrong mustache, they have to return it plus two more mustaches (if they have them) from their stash. It goes into a pot for the next player who correctly snatches up a mustache to claim. When all 32 cards are dealt, the game is over. The player left standing with the most 'stashes wins. The cards are in perfect squares - keeping the field even for all players. The mustaches feel rubbery so are less likely to cause harm if accidentally smacked into another players hand. The one thing I suggest is you have the camera at the ready! I have some great video and excellent pictures that I was able to share with the players' parents. Unfortunately, without the parents' permissions, I cannot display any of the videos or photos. They weren't comfortable with their children being seen. The recommended age is 7 and up, but I can easily see a 5 year old handling this well. I would also be willing to play with a group of adults. For $15.99 with free prime shipping, it is a great birthday or Christmas gift without breaking the budget. Plus, there are no tiny pieces to lose or step on. (BONUS!)  Keep in mind, though, that there are only 6 mustaches... so a max of 6 players can play at one time.
text_fidelity_b: Pass the Stache Board Game

text_fidelity_a: LeapFrog Fridge Phonics Magnetic Letter Set, Pink I used LeapFrog Fridge Phonics when my children were little. Back then, it came with big chunky letters you'd press in to hear, "S says sss, S says sss. Every letter makes a sound. S says sss." (Or whatever letter you set in place). It also played the ABC song when you pressed the music note. We also had the Word Whammer that let you spell three letter words. The magnets were interchangeable and increased learning fun. Since then, I've always purchased LeapFrog products for the wee ones in the family. When I saw LeapFrog now had an adorable bus, I had to have it for my niece. It comes with the 26 letters of the alphabet and does everything the original LeapFrog did plus has some extra bonuses. Instead of just singing the ABC song, Leap sings two additional songs. He also uses the letters to create words and puts it in a sentence. (It's almost like having the Fridge Phonics and Word Whammer in one.) So not only is your child learning their alphabet, they are also learning how letter sounds work together to create words and complete sentences. The only downside of this darling phonics bus is the size of the letters. They used to be much larger.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog Fridge Phonics Magnetic Letter Set, Pink

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Glow Book Seeing commercials for the Glow Book, I've been interested in this toy for my 9 year old. Obviously commercials are made to show the absolute best of a product, so I expected it to be much less than what was advertised. I have to admit it's almost as cool as the advertisements. However, the best way to discover if a toy is really worth it is to test it out on more than just a few kids. I went with those who were interested in art. Thus, this is judging based on kids who are already fans of art.

Honest opinions from kids:

1. It came with pages you could trace for kids who can't draw too well.
2. If you make a mistake, it's easy to erase it, but it's hard to make it all clean. You really have to rub well to erase mistakes or it leaves smearing behind. They should have something to erase it better. At least you can use it more than one time.
3. It needs more pages. You have plastic pages you draw on and the lights come on to show each page. It makes everything look like it's moving when the lights flash. The pages also aren't very straight.
4. I really like to play with the glow book because it is fun. You just have to get used to using it.
5. It was just like a movie. I could color and draw it just how I pleased.
6. It would be nice if there could be just a little more colors because it shows purple in some of the tracings, but there is no purple. Maybe some black to show outlines, too. It just comes with six colors: tan, pink, yellow, blue, red and green.

From an adult's perspective - it definitely has keep the interest going with the kids. It's not a toy that ends up on the shelf - lost and forgotten. However, the price tag is a bit high for something that's so simple. I have seen Amazon have excellent deals on the Glow Book, however, and think if you are patient and give yourself time to find a great deal, you will. Anything less than $20 would be great. I agree with one of the children that it could use more colors. Especially when dealing with kids interested in art. For younger kids, the small amount of color choices is probably fine. Glass cleaner takes care of the smudges you'll find after repeated use by kids. After a few mistakes, the drawing takes on a foggy/dusty look - thus making it harder to see the pictures "move" clearly. Downside is it can't be cleaned until the child is entirely finished. Definitely stick with the manufacturer age recommendation of 6 years and up. This toy is not made well enough to handle rough use from younger kids.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Glow Book

Overall it will be ok. The kids love it. Good size, lamps are fun in that they light up. Will be using a lot of superglue to reinforce everything to try to get a longer life from the pieces. Probably wouldn't buy it again but for what it is it was an ok purchase.

text_fidelity_a:
LeapFrog Fridge DJ Magnetic Learning Radio Had a little bit of trouble figuring out how to get it off 'demo' mode. There was a tiny bit of hard plastic stuck into a tiny hole in the back of the unit which we had to dig out with tweezers (had broken off). Once we got that figured out, it was smooth sailing.

All of the positives that have been listed I agree with and endorse. Our two year old is loving this radio - she's been fascinated with the regular one, and finding something appropriate for her to handle was great. It's been on the road, in the bathroom, all over the place. There is a very nice variety of songs and the animations on the screen match up very well I think. I like that there are two different ABC songs on this.

We have not had it on the fridge hardly at all. When we did, it did slide down - magnets weren't strong enough to hold it up and steady. But, since we don't really want it to stay on the fridge, it's a non-issue.

Don't know if I would spend $30+ on this particular toy (ours was about $20), but then again - if the other reviewers are getting years of life out of it, perhaps it would be worth it in the long run.
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog Fridge DJ Magnetic Learning Radio

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola Super Tips Markers, Coloring Book Markers, 20 count I was fairly excited when I found these at my local 'more-than-a-dollar' store. I've been working on lettering with markers (Tombows and Copics all the way down to the standard Crayola markers). So here was something I'd never come across in person and I was more than willing to cough up a little cash to try these out.

Unfortunately, my enthusiasm petered out as soon as I opened them. They are definitely manufactured on the cheap and some corners were cut. (Plain white cheap-looking barrel, caps not as secure as any other Crayola marker I've tried.) Still, I hoped for the best and spent several minutes practicing with them.

Sadly, I cannot recommend these whatsoever for 'brush' lettering. I do not understand at all what makes these special, they seem flimsy to me and I'm afraid the tip of the marker will pop right off. I vastly prefer the chubby Crayola markers for lettering and coloring. Save yourself a little money if you're into lettering (or coloring) and move right along.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola Super Tips Markers, Coloring Book Markers, 20 count

text_fidelity_a:
The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe) This game is addicting and so much fun for ages 10+. The teenagers at the summer camp I run especially found it fun.

The short version of how it works: Everyone gets an identity (spy or resistance member). Spies get to see who the other spies are, resistance members are clueless. You take turns choosing people to go on missions hoping that you don't have a spy among your group. Everyone on that mission turns in a pass or fail card. The spies are trying to get missions to fail, and resistance members are trying to pass the missions. You have 5 mission rounds to battle it out.

The first round or two playing with new people is always pretty quiet and awkward, but once everyone catches on to how to play, and opens up the game becomes a blast! It's been a great ice breaker for us, and it's got the kids talking and making friends with each other. All while being deceitful, calling others out for being spies, but overall having fun!

It's definitely more fun the more people you have, but it's still playable with only 5.
text_fidelity_b: The Resistance (The Dystopian Universe)

text_fidelity_a:
Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays I bought two packs of these bubble guns for a birthday party. You receive 2 pink guns and 3 blue guns in each pack. They are clear and have noise and lights.

Of the 10 bubble guns I received, 2 were defective. There is a lever that moves up and down to produce the bubbles. The lever is supposed to move when the trigger is pressed. For one of the defective bubble guns the lever was so tight that it rarely moved hence no bubbles. For the second defective bubble gun the rubber tubing was run the wrong way down the front of the gun so the rubber tube is very short. It produces bubbles but only when immersed in liquid in the bottle. It also spills a large amount of bubble liquid because of the defective tubing. After a short while it stops working because the bubble solution is too low in the bottle. My hand was also covered in solution at this point.

For the remainder of the bubble guns the rubber tubing is too long and they will not produce bubbles. The tubing is pressed against the side of the bubble container and is unable to siphon up the bubble liquid. The solution is to either push the tubing back up into the gun to make it about 1/4 inch shorter or to snip the end of the tubing by about 1/8 inch. The remaining 8 guns worked after I pushed the tubing higher.

I recommend you test the guns before handing them to children. I bought them for a birthday party so I tested them ahead of time to prevent disappointment.

These are different than battery operated bubble guns. For one thing, the lever has to be pressed about three times each time to produce bubbles in most of the bubble guns. For a few of the bubble guns a slow steady press produced a steady stream of bubbles but most of the triggers are too loose to allow a slow press. So the quality is inconsistent.

I paid $15.99 per box so from a value perspective I wasted about $6.36 because of the defective guns. I'll probably return one box.

UPDATE: Amazon shipped two replacement boxes but 5 of the 10 replacement guns were defective. I could not get them to work no matter how hard or long I tried. I shipped the defective bubble guns back. I will repeat my advice. Test each gun if you are using them for a party or event. Buy early enough so you have time to have replacements shipped to you. The ones that did work, worked beautifully. The kids enjoyed them.
text_fidelity_b: Prextex Pack of 2 Wind up Bubble Machine Toy Gun Shooter LED Light up Bubbles Blower Indoor and Outdoor Toys for Kids and Toddler - no Batteries Needed | Great Gift Set for Birthdays

It also came with an extra complimentary bill to show off what else they had very nice and worth the same as what I paid for this one, so buy one get one free.  The second bill I think is a plain one million or hundred million bill, I kind of looked at it and slipped it behind Princess Diana bill and put it on my shelf.  The paper is not bill quality so don't be misled and using this for anything else but novelty decoration in a frame or sat on shelf as I did will probably be disappointing.  It's not cut perfect but is very very clear picture and writing.  It took forever to arrive so expect fourteen day delivery or so, sure it might be different by massive amounts so just saying.  Diana is one of the most beautiful woman on the planet and that smile is worth a million, I had such a crush on her at sixteen and now I'm fourty five and had to have it, I'm a collector of sorts though I don't see this cheap paper knock off every being worth anything more than a coversation piece.  It's worth two bucks and not much more than that in my eyes.  Just don't expect some amazing quality bill, but instead a plain paper print of a cool Princess Diana Bill.

text_fidelity_a: LEGO Star Wars: The Revenge of The Sith Droid Gunship 75233 Building Kit (329 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) For many years I've bought Legos and avoided any other imitation brand of because the quality of the materials was excellent. I used to think that the quality of the materials and how well the blocks came to together justified the costly price of the Lego sets. With this purchase and other Lego sets' I've noticed the quality has decreased and the blocks come undone easily and even break with the slight pressure when assembling. Worse was to see, missing steps in the printed instructions copy versus the digital instructions version. The figurine's size has become smaller and the price has gone up. Makes me wonder if manufacturer's think loyal customers won't notice? Well we do, and we expect better if you are going to be leading in the blocks industry.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Star Wars: The Revenge of The Sith Droid Gunship 75233 Building Kit (329 Pieces) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide The 3Doodler Create + is both a toy and an artist's tool. While trying it out the hours flew by, I felt like a little kid playing with new toys on Christmas morning. Despite the fact that it will take a lot of practice before I can make anything useful or artistic, I'm having a blast trying to learn how to make various shapes. The instructions are very basic, but the website has lots of hints, tips, projects, and stencils to download for free. There are quite a few YouTube videos as well.

As the packaging states, the tip gets incredibly hot. However, the pen's design makes holding it and using it comfortable without risk of a burn. There are 2 types of filaments in the kit; ABS and PLA.

PLA is made from sugarcane and cornstarch and is used for plastic cups, cutlery, and other food grade plasticware. It has a lower melting point and a slightly glossier finish but is not as strong as ABS.

ABS requires a higher melting point and has a chemical smell but it is stronger and less likely to break if dropped.

Cleaning it after use is easy. If there is still some of the plastic sticking out from the unheated end of the pen you simply tap one of the speed buttons twice and it goes in reverse. Once the filament clears the gear mechanism, which can be seen through a clear window, it's easy to pull out. If there is no plastic sticking out then simply use the rest of it up or the long tool can be used to push the remainder out once the tip is removed. The kit has tools to accomplish this and more. The website has good visual instruction for removing the plastic.

So far I wrote my dog's name. The second try was legible but more practice is needed. I then made a pyramid. Not too difficult but a bit rough...more practice needed. I have tried to make a long vertical spiral...haven't figured that out yet. I think it's best if I stick with 2 dimensional objects until I am better able to control the pen and it's flow. Once I master that - look out! I'd like to make a small lampshade, Christmas ornaments, and focal beads for jewelry.

Just what I need, another hobby!!
text_fidelity_b: 3Doodler Create+ 3D Printing Pen for Teens, Adults & Creators! - Black (2023 Model) - with Free Refill Filaments + Stencil Book + Getting Started Guide

Barbie Made to Move Doll, Orange Top Made to Move Teresa (blue top) can be posed almost like a real person. So it’s great for people who use her for photography, or in place of an artist wooden mannequin for drawing.

Her face and thick eyebrows seem to be modeled after 1980’s actress and model Brooke Shields. If you’re buying her for a child, the downside is the delicate and sparse hair plugs that will easily be yanked with any vigorous brushing like children tend to do.

The flash lightens up her skin tone in photos. In reality she has a very tanned orangey skin color. The deep orange tint is strange like a bad fake tan, but I got used to it.

I like the 2015 version of her face more than the 2019 version: she had softer eyes, two defined dimples, a more realistic natural-looking mouth, and less of an orange skin. If you want the 2015 version you can get one used on ebay.

Overall it’s a good doll for collectors, photographers, and artists.

Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red The Canopy and two seats (that can easily be used or not as your needs change) with seatbelts features take this from a standard utility cart to a multi-purpose cart that is good for both transporting stuff and transporting kids. Even when out in the sun. Also the end storage net is very nice because even if the kids take up a big chunk of the available space, you can still store a bag or two or three depending on how well you pack. On the other end the two drink holders mean you don’t have to carry your drinks. Handy if you have kids prone to tossing bottles around as they’ll be within easy reach of you, but not in eyesight of the little ones.

Although it is more useful in that sense than some other carts, it does have some faults. The Velcro that holds the handle against the cart when not in use is almost more trouble than it’s worth. It’s not very sturdy, so if you even lightly bump the handle, it pops the Velcro open and the handle falls. Also the seams at the bottoms are exposed instead of being finished properly, leaving it more open to fraying or damage. The wheels are much larger than most utility carts, so the turning radius isn’t as good as our other carts. Going down a hill, it almost wants to get away from you, though that is an issue with most carts. The canopy is useful but works almost like slap bracelets, so getting it to stay is tricky at first, I’d almost prefer straps that just hold it in place around the retractable poles.

Overall, this is not a perfect cart, but it still very nice despite its faults. The canopy is optional and takes up almost no storage space because the poles are retractable into the cart, so you only need to roll up the fabric and stick in the net storage. The seats are perfect for young kids. It can go back and forth between kiddie wagon and an ideal cart for things like flea markets.

I was torn on the star rating, and rounded up to 4. I’d actually put this at about a 3.5. Do keep in mind that it doesn’t come with any tools, so you’ll need your own (a hammer, a wrench, and a screwdriver).
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Kid & Cargo with Canopy, Folding Wagon with 2 Versatile Seats, (Amazon Exclusive) (3965Z), Red

text_fidelity_a:
Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack Okay first off -- you can just download the app for this product in your Apple or Android app store. It will be somewhat limited, including having some of the "backgrounds" aka digital coloring pages disabled. There are more than one DigiTools apps - I was able to unlock two of the currently available four with this set: Their paint app and their airbrush app. Other sets that include different tools can unlock the other two (including a 3D set). The App consists of the backgrounds and several solid colored canvases. Using the appropriate tool allows you to do things like paint, stamp included images onto your scene, roll paint or images along your painting. Staying true to the Crayola kid friendly tradition the app doesn't include any sort of advanced features (no layers, etc). Your tools, an eraser, and an undo button are all you will find here.

The tools (what you're really buying here) consists of a Stamper, a roller, a brush, and an airbrush. Basically all of these (except the brush) are just several stylus nubs embedded into plastic tools that are kid friendly. The brush looks just like a run of the mill cheap brush (I can see kids grabbing it to paint with for real so look out for that) but when you hold it properly it too works like a stylus.

If you or the kids graduate out of the app and decide that say they do want to use them on more advanced programs? Good news and bad news there... The good news is that since these are basically just kid friendly tablet tools, yes these work in others apps. The bad news is that if you plan to say drag the stamper across your screen to get three lines at once? That's not going to happen. The screen will see this same as if you are using two fingers at once. So, for example, when I used these tools in Sketchbook pro? The brush worked perfectly. The airbrush and roller tools worked IF I tilted them so that only one nub was touching the screen at a time (otherwise it thought I was trying to pinch in and out / zoom). The stamper tool, which has three nubs, was basically useless.

The brush (the most useful tool in the pack) is also what makes this overall a 4 not a 5 star tool. The bristles are very fragile, I used this set a couple of times, put them away in the included carrying case, went to draw again and hmm the bristles were all fanned out and bent back. I don't know that the brush will hold up long term, it's already the most finicky tool in the set. Still, a fun kid friendly set that adults will love too.
text_fidelity_b: Crayola DigiTools Paint Pack

Great for people who want to practice their drawing skills, encourage the kiddies to be creative, or just get the family away from the electronics (what better way to trick them into a family fun night than by using a board game of their favorite app?).

The official site doesn't list replacement parts for sale which is no big deal for crayons but could be for the game pads so if you're a prolific arteest you'll have to find the right sized paper pads or make your own.

KRE-O Battleship U.S.S. Missouri Set (38977)(Discontinued by manufacturer) Overall a nice set of blocks. There are some very small pieces so it's not a set for very small children or those with issues with their hands (I actually had to take frequent breaks while putting it together when I was working on some sections of it). At least one section of it was frustrating, at least for me -- two flat pieces that made a floor which you might be lifting often if you want to see /show off the room under it, connected together by another much smaller flat piece underneath the two. it kept falling off, knocking off everything I'd done on the two pieces off. I was (and still am) tempted to just glue them together. Other than that one little issue the instructions really do lead you to build a nice sturdy ship complete with working "weapons" (kids would really have to work hard to hurt someone with them but yes, you should be aware there are guns that shoot -- you make those too using the blocks / thin plastic bar pieces).

I do recommend having something like zippered plastic baggies or a plastic box with separate compartments handy as the pieces are not bagged in any logical order (except for some of the figures being with their own pieces) so having a way to sort the pieces ahead of time will save you a lot of effort as you go.
text_fidelity_b: KRE-O Battleship U.S.S. Missouri Set (38977)(Discontinued by manufacturer)

Of the several teddy bears I've bought on Amazon, they tend to be kind of smaller than they are supposed to be in my mind..  Another thing is that they compact the teddy bears in a box and need fluffing out and shaping the form.  This bear is nice, cuddly, and so soft, but after delivering it from the boxed constraints it doesn't seem to have sufficient stuffing for the size and cost.  When someone hugs a teddy bear, they usually want to feel the  bear's fullness and being fully stuffed to  make it feel better for cuddling and comfort.  On a 1 to 10, I'd give it a 8.6 or so.  It is wonderfully soft and cozy but it really could have used more stuffing to fill it out in the apendages (i.e. arms and legs).  It is a fairly good size and is soft!  Ah, yes!  He will come out of the box a little deformed so to speak, but with some care he/she will fill out somewhat better.  Of the bears I've bought on Amazon, I am most happy with this model.  If the manufacturer would use a slightly bigger box and fill the body up more than they do it would be great!  The nose on the teddy bear is rather stiff and not soft at all which is in a way kind of strange!  All in all I am pretty happy with my purchase.  Don't forget to name it and make it yours friend!
text_fidelity_b: JOON Big Teddy Bear, 30 Inches, Tan

1. It feels “ok well” made and feels like its probably worth around 50-60$ in techology and material.
2. The screen resolution looks good
3. It says there is over 36000+ game on it.

Now lets get into the negative aspects:

1. Graphics: This emulator is VERY weak / has low processing power which makes “heavier” games basically unplayable/unenjoyable. (Framerate Drop, Audio Stretching, Gamespeed dropping)
2. Audio: The included audio speaker sounds like it is broken on my device and Mono only, which is alright, the issue is the games have been so compressed that most audio just sounds terrible.
3. Price: This device is too expensive for how it performs, it should be aroun 70-80$ max.

Conclusion:

I would Not recommend this emulator - if you are looking for a handheld gaming experience, you may want to look into a nintendo Switch or a Steam Deck.
text_fidelity_b: Petforu POWKIDDY RGB10 MAX 2 Handheld Games Console 5-inch (17000 Games 128G Black)

It's our joy to be able to provide quality toys for our grandchildren now that we are older. This one definitely fills the bill. It is well made. I am 54 yrs. old and with a little time (4.5 - 5 hrs.) and elbow grease, I had it put together. Quite proud of myself, actually. :0) There are LOTS of pieces. But the reaction of my 3 yr. old grand daughter when she got it was priceless. Money can't buy that kind of thing. Anyhow...I'd definitely buy it again. It is just the kind of toy that sparks imagination in children and lets them be a kid.

Suggestion for whomever assembles it. Lay out all your parts & screws & count them to make sure they're all there. It would be a horrible dissappointment to get partially through and not be able to complete the project because of some missing parts. We did have one missing part, but it wasn't the worse thing. It was just the canopy over the bed, which my daughter ordered immediately and got with no problems, along with two of the roof pieces that had bent corners. This company is awesome to work with. They shipped it right away...no questions asked.

And the price was good too being it wasn't a used item. Much better than I could get at any local store.
text_fidelity_b: KidKraft Annabelle Wooden Dollhouse with Elevator, Balcony and 17 Accessories, Gift for Ages 3+

First off, the padding on the wheels wore down to the metal hy the 3rd use, which has damaged our barre, and increased the already loud noise of the motor, and barrel spinning, although because it is rubber the rocks didnt make a ton of loud sound like in metal or plastic ones. Also, the timing, and speed system no longer work, at all. No matter how many days I set it for, it goes until I manually shut it off, and no matter what speed i set it for, it automatically starts and stays on high. Also if you want stones that are actually polished, you will have to run them through at least a few times on the last step, otherwise they cone out all scratched up, looking dull and cloudy. I bought them just over a year ago, but they were Christmas gifts" so didnt get used for the first time until exactly a year from this month. My husband has only tumbled approximately 6 light batches of small jewelry stones for me over that time. Our friend has only used his to tumble the rocks that came with it, and his is still in good shape, as I would rightly expect.

text_fidelity_a:
Aerobie Pro Ring Outdoor Kids Toy for Boys and Girls, All Ages, Colors may Vary This is a great ring! Once you get your hands on the comfortable, flexible silicone body, you'll want to throw it. Children of all ages and even grown men cannot resist chucking it as far as they can. These big rings sail FAAAAR! And they are a tad prone to getting stuck in high and sometimes funny places. (Believe me, these will end up in the trees and on roofs but they are easy to get down with a broom stick because of their ring shape.)

A boy at cub scouts had one of these that everyone was playing with last week. My son decided to spend his hard earned allowance money on Amazon to order one, hoping it wouldn't be pink. :) He was thrilled when a yellow ring arrived. It has a VERY rice, silicone-like, soft rubbery grip and is fun to throw! Kids fight over these rings so I'm thinking of ordering several for birthday gifts and cousin Christmas gifts. You can't beat a gift for under ten that kids actually want to play outside with!

Consider spending a little more and buying the 13 inch ring. It flies farther and better than the 10 inch rings did. However, if you don't have a wide open play space, the 10 inch rings might be better because they play more like a Frisbee and don't get hung up in trees quite as easily.

UPDATE: I am now buying our THIRD ring! These make awesome gifts for boys in the 8 to 11 range, as my son is frequently swarmed by boys wanting to play with his. But be aware that if you throw it too far and loose sight of it, you won't get it back. It will be stolen by the first kid who comes across it. We had this happen at a party where the ring ended up sailing over a house and landing far behind it in an empty field right at dark. It was snatched before daylight. Hence me having to buy our third. (Since it was probably the roving neighborhood teenagers who picked it up late that night, I am going to say this is a good toy for fussy 16 and 17 year-olds, too!) It has been a favorite gift at birthday parties, followed by thank yous from the moms who are grateful for any toy that gets their video game addicted boys outside. I am thrilled to have found such a good gift for under $10. You can't go wrong with this ring!

Update March 2017: I have now ordered nearly 10 of these rings in the last 5 months for birthday gifts for 9 and 10 year old boys and without fail, it has been an instant hit. The boys are always eager to show how FAR they can throw the ring and then are shocked when it sails two hundred yards or more. They puff out their chests as their friends exclaim "WOOOAH!" while the ring whizzes one or two streets over and then the birthday boy swaggers off to fetch the ring with every other boy tagging along, begging for a turn to throw it next. Children now double check with my son to ensure that he's going to get them an Aerobie ring for their birthday. I keep at least one on-hand for last minute birthday party invites.

• COLORS •

Out of all the rings we have ordered, only 1 has been pink. We have received 2 orange, 1 pink and all the rest have been yellow. Trying to get a big pink ring for a girl's birthday party coming up in May is proving challenging since we keep getting shipped yellow!
text_fidelity_b: Aerobie Pro Ring Outdoor Kids Toy for Boys and Girls, All Ages, Colors may Vary

The foot pads are wide enough that you don't slip off and the padded handlebars are great in case you topple to one side and accidentally bonk yourself in the face. (Hey, it happens!)

This stick is for beginners that are just learning. It takes about 2 days for a child to learn to pogo, especially if they are tall or longer-legged. Start on a very flat surface (not a slanted driveway) and encourage them to be patient as they learn how to balance on it. And once you learn, you never forget! But don't try it, dad - this pogo smashes pretty flat if an adult tries to use it because it's only rated to 80 pounds! (Might handle 90 lbs okay.) Soon they'll be able to do several bounces in a row and, before you're completely comfortable with the idea, they'll be taking massive leaps on the thing, galloping down the cul-de-sac!

Incredibly fun outdoor toy in a bright color that helps you spot it so you don't run it over if it's left out in the driveway!

I was fortunate to receive this product at a slight discount (not free) so that I could try it, use it, abuse it and determine if it is worth spending your hard-earned money on. If it doesn’t work, I will tell you. I hope my honesty helps you to make the best buying decision for your family!

(And I mean things quickly deteriorated into a 5-cousin brawl of boys and girls ages 2-7 until the board was put away because everyone wanted it!)

Children LOOOOVE making rubber band designs and this 11x11 inch board allows for some cool ones. You can buy colored rubber bands on Amazon but I recommend grabbing a bag of neon bright bands for under five at an office supply store. The very few (like 12 total?) it came with were a rubber-eraser reddish-pink, dusty white and vintage spearmint green. They are fairly gross looking colors and except for the white, the rest reside permanently in the bottom of the rubber band bag.

When it arrived our board was yellow, which I liked MUCH better than the red shown but be aware you'll get a random color. The one we just ordered in October 2013 for a cousin christmas gift (since it was such a hit!) was also yellow. Every time my son pulls it out in church, children in the pews in front of us and behind us begin quietly peeking over his work to see what he's making with that contraption and everyone wants a turn! If you need a fun toy for kids of all ages that won't break the bank, doesn't require batteries or make any noise and builds brain cells while you play, this is it!
text_fidelity_b: Learning Resources Single-Sided Geoboard 11 x 11 Pin

text_fidelity_a:
VTech Sit-to-Stand Alphabet Train I don't know about a kid being strangled by the alphabet train. I suppose it's possible as there is a dip in between the two pieces of the train. My problems, however, are just of a different nature. I think this may be one of the most poorly designed toys I've ever purchased for my toddler..
I bought the train on a whim because it was on sale. It's colorful, makes noise, blah blah blah. After a couple of weeks of use, I started to notice the flaws in the design of the toy, and you know it seems like VTech has a bad habit of just putting out colorful, noisy crap that they know parents will buy regardless if it's good quality and design or not.
First of all, the thing is LOUD. There are two "choices" for volume, but the one that's supposed to be quieter can be heard across our 2500 square foot house. This is a common toy problem; I believe that the idiots coming up with kids' toys do not actually HAVE children, or they would put a quieter setting on these toys so that parents aren't stuck in the "LET'S RIDE THE ALPHABET TRAIN!" hell day after day.
Second, the train is too freaking narrow. It's too easy to topple over, so when my still-a-bit-unsteady 14-month-old would try to get on it to "ride", he often fell over. Now he's a lot better with balance at 18 months, but the thing is still too narrow.
Third, the train is not designed well for riding at all. Yes, it has handles and a seat, but the design of them is pretty unusable until the kid is way too old to be playing with an alphabet train. I watched my toddler today try to get on the toy and ride it; where his little butt goes is where the hump in the train car is, and if he sat back far enough to get off the hump, he couldn't reach the handles. What the crap? My child is not a chimp and he's not Stretch Armstrong. Why are the engine and car so far apart?
Ugh. We're keeping the dang thing because he does like to put the blocks into the train and watch them shoot out the engine. But as far as usability, the alphabet recognition is really the only thing that the toy has accomplished. If I could go back in time, I'd never buy this stupid train.
text_fidelity_b: VTech Sit-to-Stand Alphabet Train

text_fidelity_a:
SmartLab Toys Squishy Human Body with 21 Removable Body Parts with Anatomy Book This product has the potential to be an incredible teaching tool which is why I initially purchased it. However, it is evident after ordering this item (even after a replacement of the original product that was initially delivered--replacement is shown in pictures above), that there are reoccurring issues with this item that are extremely problematic.

You can see how there are pieces of this product that come lodged incorrectly including the skull which does not stay in its designated hole. The large intestine looks like it's already been pulled apart by a child passed its point of stretch as it is extremely thin at the connection area.

Also--I if I as a teacher could not even put this item in full back together, I can only imagine how difficult this would be for a child of any age to maneuver as well.

If this company would just give more effort into putting out a quality product it would be extremely useful across-the-board and save them so much money in returns if they would just take the small effort to fix these ongoing issues that so many purchasers report.

I was able to get a 25% refund on my initial purchase with being able to keep the item as I explained I do not want to do a third replacement bit instead that I would rather just find a innovative way to make the issues I've experienced usable for teaching my students.

If you get this product don't settle for a poor quality item...they used to be made so well and now this company has made cheaply made pieces of it the regular. Stick to your guns on insisting on either a working product and/or a refund.

Wish you all the best with this item.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys Squishy Human Body with 21 Removable Body Parts with Anatomy Book

You pull the plastic tab which activates the batteries which is good and then you shove it back into the hippopotamuses stomach with the button facing outwards and when you press the button he does what he does. It is sturdy and seems well made. You can change the color of the light, and there are 3 different sound modes.

The sounds it makes are neat but that they are a bit delayed. Also, hitting the blade of the lightsaber doesn't cause a reaction, the sounds are triggered by movement of the hilt.

It is also a bit of a pain to change settings, because there is only one button that controls everything. Pressing the button once turns it on, second press makes a blaster sound, three presses changes the color, long pressure turns it off, to change sound modes you have to turn it off and then long press the button.

Jurassic World Toys Camp Cretaceous Feeding Frenzy Indominus Rex Interactive Dinosaur, Bite Reflex, Toy Ribs, Lights & Sounds, Authentic Detail, Ages 4 Old & Up [Amazon Exclusive] [[VIDEOID:3d3135b328048c7b303338b7b5ea20ac]] This little guy is so cute. He growls, chomps and his eyes light up. However, there are a few issues with this toy.

Most importantly, there is no off switch. To turn him off, you'd have to take out the batteries.

Also, the button on his head is the only function that works correctly every time. To get him to chomp down on the ribs, you have to press them at the back of his tongue. To get him to make the chopping is also a bit difficult. You press the tail to open his mouth, but after doing it 3 or 4 times it doesn't work as well any more.

I think young children will like this toy, but they will break it quickly. And older children may get frustrated with the features not working all the time.

WowWee Grimlings - Unicorn - Interactive Animal Toy [[VIDEOID:6eeb2af37a62fc3f9f4a5dfcc0084b61]] This unicorn is a little crazy. It has several functions/interactions. Flipping it upside down or being in the dark will bring out it's from side. It laughs, sneezes and farts.

It does sometimes have a delay in it's reactions, and sometimes you have to do the interactions a couple of times before it responds.

Also, it will not fit on an adult finger and it doesn't want to stand because it's feet are uneven.

text_fidelity_a:
NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC Morphing Matter Dinosaur Kit – 3 Cups of Morphing Matter, 6 Dinosaur Figures, Package Converts Into Play Setting, Astounding Kinetic Sensory Activity for Kids [[VIDEOID:d3bb1c3c7f2743a41a3ab64b3b6628d4]] This kit is pretty neat. text_fidelity_a:
ClasseArt Watercolor Paint Set with Bonus 15 Paper Pads Includes 48+6 Premium Colors-3 Water Brush Pens-Storage Case with Palette-Swatch Sheet and Sponge This set has quickly become my favorite, go to solid pan watercolors.
The color selection is gorgeous & exceptional with rich pigment concentrations that are extremely versatile, providing both excellent transparency AND an almost gouache like boldness when activated with very little water. These paints offer clean, pure color effects, & with so many beautiful colors to choose from there’s little risk of ending up with muddy mixtures & inconsistent results.
The small box arrived neatly packed with a nice, fairly sturdy plastic case containing 48 pans of the most beautiful colors, a removable palate that fits perfectly inside the lid, 2 water brushes, a pad with 15 sheets of cold pressed watercolor paper, a do it yourself color chart with printed color names & helpful “tips & tricks” on the reverse side. text_fidelity_a: BARWA 41 Pack Doll Clothes and Accessories 5 PCS Fashion Dresses 5 Tops 5 Pants Outfits 10 PCS Mini Dresses 10shoes 6 Necklace 5 Glasses for 11.5 inch Doll In fact, I just ordered another set. As an adult fashion doll collector and semi-professional photographer, I appreciate the fact that the clothes are from a variety of dolls. Some of the clothes are standard, wide hip Barbie size, while others are slimmer in the hips and torso (more like Model Muse) and still more fit dolls who are short and petite (like Barbie's sisters Skipper and Stacey). The Skipper and Stacey size tops look cute as midriff baring tops on a regular Barbie. I read a complaint below about the pants not fitting, but that's the way Mattel has been making pants since about 1999 when they introduced the first wide hip Barbie doll (the doll that we know today as a regular Barbie). The jeans are meant to fit below the waist and you have to tug to get them on and close them completely because they are meant to fit snugly. It's true, the clothing seams aren't always perfectly straight, but I have the same issue with Mattel Barbie clothes that I buy in person. Plus, the fabrics for these fashions are - for the most part - nicer than what Mattel has been offering lately. At the end of the day, when you consider that SINGLE ITEM Barbie brand clothing packs currently sell for $2.44 - $5.00 each, and Barbie brand complete fashion sets with shoes retail for $5.00 - $35.00 each, spending just under $2.00 for complete outfit is a great deal.

The wand has a nice feel and weight to it and seems to be made of a strong resin plastic. The wand comes in a lovely window box with directions, customer support information and a bonus app for making your light paintings.

There is a tiny button on the wand’s handle for turning on the LED light which only stays on as long as you hold the button down. For those of you that look forward to some creative light painting, you will want to download the app. Light painting is just photographing a moving light at a longer exposure shutter speed, in the dark, with no flash. Putting the set together is easy with the enclosed directions. It's basically snapping plastic pieces together. There are a few stickers you put on first that give more detail and color to the set.

Once you get the set together, you will see that the set needs water. This means a water mess as the cars dive into the tanks to change colors. For inside play, I put down a cheap plastic tablecloth on the floor, with a towel nearby. This made indoor play a much more dry experience, keeping the water contained to the plastic cloth. But for the best experience, with no water to clean up- outdoors is best when weather permits it.

The Sharkport Set has 2 color change zones (cold and warm), along with a big mouth shark that chomps a car when the car hits the trigger. To release the car from the jaws of the shark, another car must come to the rescue, by hitting the shark. The boys ages 3 to about 7 find this set lots of fun. The other set- The Splash & Dash Set is simply a dunk tank for color changing the cars. It has a hidden trap door, so the car makes a splash.

You will find that having hot wheel tracks (NOT included) attached to this set, makes this set way more fun, as the boys love zooming around the tracks with the 5 included cars before getting eaten by the shark or getting the cars color changed. There are a couple tips I found, to make the experience better also. Don't over fill the water tanks. Also you will find the cold water gets warm quickly and the warm water cools down just as quick. This means you will have to constantly keep emptying and refilling the 3 water containers with warm and cold water, unless you do what I do.

I put some ice into the cold water tanks. The cold water stays good longer and the color changes instantly, as the ice does the trick. When the water is no longer icy cold, the colors do not change on the cars. As for the hot water, I also found out I can deal with that too, as I keep hot water in a thermos and let the kids add the water. NOT TOO HOT- just hot enough for children to handle. Between the thermos and ice- they are good to play for hours- and they do!

Sometimes the cars jam or get lint on the wheels, but these are minor fixes with a little push or cleaning the tire areas with a toothpick. Overall, if you use a thermos of warm water and ice in the cold water- they won't be running back and forth to the faucets making messes and will have lots of fun changing these 5 car's colors and of course they love those shark bites too. This is a fun, but messy set that the boys enjoy when you know how to set it up with your plastic cloth, ice and thermos.

We found that really flat combed hair, warm water and pulling the flat iron hard and slowly gave some great results on some of the tattoo patterns. Others just looked like color blobs.

This all really didn't even seem to matter, as the girls love this doll and especially when the tattoos came out looking pretty good in her hair. When they didn't look good, the tattoos just washed out in a minute. For the tattoos that didn't turn out on Barbie, the girls ended up putting the tattoos on themselves as bracelets on their wrists or ankles. They had fun no matter if the tattoos came out good or bad looking in Barbie's hair, so this Barbie Hair Tattoos is still worth 4 Stars, even though you have to experiment to get some of the tattoos to look great.

Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up In the 50's and 60's Board Games and Cards were very popular. I remember playing Yahtzee in the 60's mainly with older family than with friends. The older people in the 50's and 60's loved cards- my Mother's friends had Bridge Clubs and the men loved their Poker Nights. I always felt Yahtzee was a combination of a board type game using dice combined with the skill of cards.

The object of Yahtzee is to get the most points by figuring out the points the dice will give you with 3 of a kind, large straight, full house, aces and other card type combinations. You get three chances to roll the most points you can figure out. You really had to figure out which dice would get you more points on the upper section or the lower section of your score card to score high. They even included chips in the game, as you could get a chip for every 100 points you score.

When you roll the 5 dice all the same number, that was Yahtzee. It's nice to see Classic games coming around again to enjoy. For anyone who likes the strategy of playing cards, only with rolling 5 dice, Yahtzee brings that and more to this classic 50's game of both skill and chance.
text_fidelity_b: Classic Yahtzee, An Exciting Game Of Skill And Chance for age 8 and up

Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor My first introduction to the board game of Sorry was in the early 60's. Sorry was one of the more fast and fun games. The object of the game is to be the first player to move all 4 of your men around the board to get back home. You choose from 4 different colors of your men and your home- blue, green, yellow or red. There is a deck of cards that tell you how many spaces to move your man, and of course it isn't as easy as just moving your man as quickly as you can around the board to get home before anyone and win the game. There are obstacles along the way, should a player get to slide, he slides everyone in his way back to start, and no two men can occupy the same space, so someone has to go back to start- Sorry!

I remember when we played with 2 players, the game took about 15-20 minutes, but with 4 players, it took close to half an hour. It's very fast moving and even faster when hardly any players are sent back to start. I really love the look of this classic 1939 Sorry Game- it's a little different from the one we played on in the 60's. Regardless of the look you like, Sorry is a fast and fun game that brings back so many fun memories of when we had 15 minutes to kill before we went bike riding to a picnic on a lovely summer day in 1962. This early version of the game is really a nice one to own and it also comes with other game versions you can play including a Sorry For One, in case you have a few minutes to kill by yourself! Some Classic games never wear out their fast fun and this 5 Star Classic Sorry Board Game is one of them!
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Sorry Classic Edition Board Game, Multicolor

Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll Since the first Barbie doll was created in 1959, little girl's have always loved to style/color Barbie doll's hair, and this fun to color hair Barbie is no exception. (I took my 1960's ponytail down, so she could look like Sleeping Beauty back in the day!) This gorgeous Color Stylin' Hair Barbie is a huge favorite with the grandchildren now.

Barbie comes with a suction cupped chair, comb, applicator brush, bowl, seven color swatches in 3 colors-3 pink, 2 purple and 2 orange, clip on foiler holder and rubberbands. Barbie is dressed in a glittery pink dress with shoes, necklace and belt. The color application is easy- seat Barbie in her chair, which doesn't move due to an ingenious suction cup bottom, wet the hair section you want to color, place the color swatch in the foiler, then clip the foiler to the wet hair and pull through. When you want to remove the color or color again, you just wash and dry the hair and you are ready for more fun.

There are a couple things you should know before using this coloring set: don't color near carpet, furniture, walls or clothes you don't want to ruin, as these colors can be a permanent stain for certain fabrics or walls. I laid down a cheap plastic tablecloth from the dollar store, so the girls had a great area to play on with no worries. I called Mattel, and found they do not sell extra color swatches, so once these are used up, they are gone, and to replace the colors, you would have to buy another doll. This is a shame, as they always sell accessories and extra hair swatches for the dolls with hair swatches that can be cut, so why not some inexpensive color swatches too Mattel?

The girls just love coloring, braiding and styling the gorgeous streaked areas of this Barbie's hair, so of course they want more colors- and even different colors too. As for something interesting I noticed, I bought another one of these dolls, as I have 2 granddaughters, and we immediately noticed one set colored darkly and another set colored very faintly. I looked closely at the boxes and what did I find on the backs of the boxes, but an expiration date! It says Best Used By and then a date which you need a magnifying glass to read. Reading the back of our boxes showed that one of the boxes colors was expired! That explains the faint color! Being a wonderfully fun to play with Barbie gives this doll 5 Stars, but color that is expired and having no refills brings her down to limited playability with the color, making this gorgeous Barbie a 4 Star doll.
text_fidelity_b: Mattel Barbie Hairtastic Color Stylin Doll

Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari Hasbro's new Elefun's Snackin Safari Game for children 3 and up has a wonderful concept for fun, if your child has a lot of patience. The game is made for 1 or 2 players. There are two elephant heads with handles connected to a long slinky trunk with a suction cup on the end. Included are 2 home base cards and 13 snack cards. The object of the game is to pick up a snack card with the suction cup, and there are 3 different ways to play the game.

The first way to play is to find the Golden Tutti Fruit Cake and be the winner. The second way is to collect all your matching colors to win and the third way is to get the most pairs of matching snacks to win. It sounds easy enough, until you realize that it takes a lot of patience to bounce the elephant's slinky trunk quickly and hard enough to actually suction a card to it. It could take 6 times or 60 times, as the slinky is a weak plastic one and the small suction cup needs to be pushed on a card to pick it up.

Surprisingly enough, the little ones loved the concept, but after a dozen tries to pick up a card, became frustrated. If Hasbro can tweak this game to make a stronger slinky and stronger suction cup, so the little ones can pick up a card after a few tries, this game would be a big hit. I hope Hasbro reads these reviews and makes this cute game less frustrating, as the kids will really enjoy it!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari

The kitchen itself is made of a high grade, colorful and sturdy plastic that you have to put together with a screwdriver. You'll spend around a half hour screwing the walls and shelves together and to the base, and that's it. The batteries that make Dora talk to the little cook are already included and inserted in the compartment.

This colorful kitchen is very compact and everything gets conveniently stored inside the roomy refrigerator and oven. The sink is over the refrigerator and the burner and grill is over the oven. Above the sink/stove top is a window and a place to slide in the recipe card, and above this at the top is a shelf. Next to the recipe card is a cell phone holder. Dora stands behind the stove cooktop to the other side.

The recipe card is double sided, with 2 recipes on each side for a total of 4 recipes included. When you slide the card in, you can then press one of two flower buttons that speak to you with directions for your recipe. Sometimes the phone will ring as well and speak to you. One side of the card has 2 recipes for a Barbecue- hamburgers and ice cream and the other side of the card has 2 recipes for a Spring Picnic- huevos rancheros and tacos. Step by step, Dora tells the little cook exactly what to do.

All the ingredients and cooking utensils your little chef will need to create these 4 recipes are included. There are 20 play accessories, including: plate, spatula, pan, cup, fork, spoon, phone, salad dressing, milk, hash browns, egg, lettuce, hamburger patty, tortilla, chicken breast, buns, banana and ice creams. Your kids will have so much fun learning to create scrumptious dishes with Dora in this wonderful talking kitchen. I'm already looking for more recipe cards for this kitchen and I found a great Holiday Cookies one for this Christmas for them. We've had other play kitchens, but this talking one gets all the play time by both the girls and boys.
