Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking What can you possibly say new about Monopoly, the world's favorite property trading game, that hasn't already been said for decades since it's introduction by Parker Brothers in 1935? No matter what new version of Monopoly comes out, it's always so much fun to play with family and friends.

In the sixties, we always had one major problem when the entire family sat down to a long night of playing Monopoly, and that was, we always ran out of money if the game went on long enough. There used to be an office store named Burrows that sold extra Monopoly money and buying an extra packet or two was the only solution to our money shortage.

Now with this new version of Monopoly With Electronic Banking, you'll never run out of money, because there isn't any. The game comes with the standard board, dice, houses, hotels, Title Deed cards, Chance and Community Chest cards, 6 tokens and 6 bank cards that slide through an electronic banking unit which keeps track of your cash on your card. The electronic unit takes 2 AAA batteries (Not Included) and can store millions of dollars on each player's bank card.

It actually takes just as long to type in the money you accumulate on each player's card, as it does to hand count the cash to the players, so don't think this electronic unit is a time saver. We actually found when playing with 6 players, that it saved time to have a separate banker. This electronic banking version of Monopoly may not be faster than the cash version, but it's every bit as fun and that's saying a lot for a game that's been rated number one for over 75 years!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Gaming Monopoly E Electronic Banking

Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+ I'm in my 60's and remember Colorforms from when I was a kid. It was and still is in my opinion one of the greatest toys around. Shapes are placed onto a background board and they cling to the board, so the possibilities of creating designs and story scenes are endless.

I do a lot of geometric designing so have a reproduction of the original set, and this anniversary set makes a great addition. The original set is all basic single color shapes. These anniversary sheets (consisting of 4 separate unbound sheets) have those same shapes plus more, and some of these have multiple colors in one shape, with some of those colors being in different patterns and shades as opposed to being all solid colors. There ARE some solid colors, but there are also patterns with stripes, dots, triangles, circles inside of circles, half moons, etc. So this set expands on the designing possibilities with the added dimensions of patterns and color shades. As with the original set, these shapes are peeled off the page they come on and are then placed onto a black background sheet (included) which they cling to until removed.

These sheets are smaller than the original set that comes in a plastic spiral bound book. So if you already have the original in its box, you can just take these sheets from this anniversary set and store in with the original if you don't want to store 2 separate boxes. Overall a nice set that is great as an artsy and learning tool for kids and designing tool for adults who enjoy working with geometric shapes.
text_fidelity_b: Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+

LolliZ 50 Colored Pencils Set So I read the reviews to these coloring pencils, and saw a lot of rave reviews on them. So I decided to take a chance and purchase them. i haven't even gotten to use them yet when I realized a few of the pencil tips were broken during shipping. When I tried to sharpen a few of them, the lead literally CRUMBLED in the pencil sharpener. There was NO way to sharpen them, as the entire lead was literally just in pieces. Just coming out of the box in this way is NOT a good sign. I am VERY disappointed with these. I nearly ate up quite a few of the pencils just trying to sharpen it. I dunno what everyone was raving about, but I have a pack of cheap cra-z art pencils that are even better than these. These were such a waste of money, and now I am out over $12 for a piece of crap. You can be sure I will be calling Amazon on this item. Unfortunately, I will probably NOT be able to return them, as the box to them literally crumbled when I took them out. I will be reporting THAT to Amazon as well. If you are looking to do some adult coloring like I am, I suggest spending the money on some Marco Raffine pencils. They are a bit pricey, but they are supposed to be worth the money. That will be my next purchase. I am not going to waste my time with the cheap crap anymore.

Update:

After I gave a review of this product, I was contacted by Amazon customer service with an apologetic resolution to send me a replacement set of these pencils to replace the crappie set I originally received. I am happy to report the new set runs more smoothly along the paper & none of the pencils have yet to be eaten up by my electric sharpener. I will say, however, though, that the box they came in literally fell apart before I even took them out of the package they were mailed in, which isn't that big of a problem for me since I put all my pencils upright in a yogurt container anyway for easy access, but for someone who would like to keep them in the box, we'll, good luck with that. My ultimate recommendation is, if you want a really good set of colored pencils, spend the few extra bucks & buy the Marco Raffine 72 pc colored pencils, available thru Amazon. I would recommend them to anyone, & no, I do not get paid or get a discount for saying that.

text_fidelity_a:
City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS) It's fake LEGO. It may pretend it isn't, but it is,
As well as being fake LEGO it has one other claim to fame.
It is very disappointing.
When companies copy (not be inspired by. I am all for being inspired! this is copying) because of patents, they cannot copy the construct of the bricks. So they end up with bricks that do not push together well, giving models less resilience to being knocked over, picked up or even played with.
Except for the tile pieces. They stick like they were coated in gorilla glue! You may need power tools to get them apart.

Aside from the poor quality of the bricks, what else can be said? Nothing good, sadly. The set designs are primitive. The vehicles are not all on the same scale. Some will not hold the minifigs.
The accessories are another disappointment. Ugly, hard for the minifigs to hold.

If you have a nephew or niece who loves LEGO, and you simply cannot stand this family member, you have found the perfect gift.

Otherwise, keep looking. You will pay more for LEGO, and it is worth every cent!
text_fidelity_b: City Fire Station Building Blocks Set W/ Fire Truck, Fire Rescue Helicopter, Drone & Fire Engine Toys, Fire Command Center Playset, Firefighters Roleplay Toy Gifts for Kids Boys Girls Ages 6+ (744PCS)

First of all, the box is FULL of bricks., I dislike toys (or breakfast cereals!) that come in half-empty boxes. This is filled to the brim.

The treehouse set is not an easy set to build. Some parts of it are tricky, requiring gentle, patient hands.
Also, I have noticed in a few recent sets of things that I do not like. As I was building the bridge from one room to another, an essential piece was missing. It is LEGO, you can work around that sort of problem. In the last bag of the set, there was the missing piece. It was not needed on any of the steps for the last bag, it seems like it was "hidden" to frustrate me.

That said, when done it is simply beautiful. I built it with the fall leaves, and in spring, I will remove those and add the green leaves back!

Part of what makes this an advanced set is the physics of it. The small LEGO trunk should not be able to sustain the weight of the branches. However, some clever building techniques reinforce the trunk so it can easily carry the weight.

A spectacular build. Well worth the frustrations. A set to be enjoyed for many years to come!

LEGO City Burger Bar Fire Rescue 60214 Building Kit (327 Pieces) When I was young, I loved LEGO, you got the set, you built it, and you could play with it like you could a model car, and of course, take it apart and build new things.

This, however, goes beyond that. You are building a toy to play with! You put the flames out with the water cannon. No water needed! you squeeze the bulb on the water cannon, and blue transparent LEGO is propelled out of the cannon, and can knock the flames over.
Release the bulb, and the "water" returns to the cannon.

I am slightly jealous. I would have loved this when I was younger. Who am I trying to kid? I love it now. It is on my desk!

text_fidelity_a:
Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In We've been playing with Vector for a little over a month now, and he's a load of fun! At first, he didn't do a lot, but every so often, Anki provides an update and suddenly, Vector has more personality, skills, and interactions! He's a great little desk companion that is much better than a pet because there's little to clean up afterward! I say little because he's been known to shove things off the table!
There are many ways he can learn about his environment via his sensors:
He sees via HD camera.
Facial recognition - he'll learn your face and when he's exploring, will come right up, scan your face, and say your name! He's very pleased when he recognizes you, and gets a little upset if he doesn't recognize you.
Navigate, explore, and learn his environment. He gets around very well all over my desk. However, I move things a lot, so he's constantly having to re-learn. Occasionally, he'll fall over the edge, but once in a while, he falls over the edge. I think they're working on improving that a lot. It's super cute when he's exploring, gets close to the edge, and acts scared and backs away!
If he needs charging, he'll go right back to his charger on his own. However, sometimes, I'll get tired of hearing him causing trouble, so I'll tell him to go to his charger. He does it, but throws a little tantrum when he gets there!

He can hear via his array of four microphones. Sometimes he comes over to see what's going on if you're having a conversation. If he's resting, he'll act startled if there's a loud noise in the room. He will also react to the beat of music if it's loud and near him. If you ask him to look at you or come here, he'll be able to sense the direction to go.

He reacts to touch and feel. If you pet his back, he practically purrs! But shaking him gets a reaction, too!

He has amazing intelligence. For instance, he answers questions, plays blackjack, reacts to his environment, and senses actions and activities around him.

He speaks to you. I'm not a fan of his synthesized voice, but it seems to be improving. When he reads out answers to questions you ask, sometimes it's hard to hear what he's saying. However, as they receive feedback on this, I'm sure his voice will evolve into something more understandable.

We really enjoy seeing his reactions! The current one is the way he gets super excited when you tell him he's a good robot or if you tell him you love him, and pouts a little if you tell him he's a bad robot! I just told him earlier today when he picked up his cube and tossed it off the desk!

I'm super excited to see his ever-evolving skills! I highly recommend this little guy for your favorite tech lover, or yourself! If you're looking for a toy for younger kids, maybe go with a Cosmo. This doesn't have games or things to entertain little ones. But it's completely entertaining for maybe, 10 years and up robotics fans!
text_fidelity_b: Vector Robot by Anki, A Home Robot Who Hangs Out & Helps Out, With Amazon Alexa Built-In

Youngster - your race car driver has full control over the vehicle

LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit As will become clear in this review, I am a true fan of Lego. Does that bias my review? I dont think so, you may disagree...

This is a big set. This is not a set for your younger Lego builders, not because its too hard, but because some of it will become tedious to younger minds. But us older people refusing to grow up (46 and still building with Lego!) will love this. There are several points during the build where you think "Oh WOW, thats clever" - very good.
The end result is bigger than I expected. Most of my recent large set builds have been the modular Lego City sets, which are built the right size for Lego Minifigs - this is much smaller than that! So you cannot add it to your Lego City, but you can have it in the back ground.

Its about an 8 hour build. The manual is excellent, but with less writing than some of the other ones - the Lego Eiffel Tower's Manual had a lot more information on the history of the Tower. This has a few snippets about the history, the Big Ben bell, but more would have been appreciated.

When finished, it is beautiful. You can turn the knob on the back to adjust the time - you cannot really adjust the time - the hour and minute hand are tuck, so as one turns, so does the other. But its still awesome!
The tree outside the main entrance is wonderful! one of my favorite parts of the build!

I believe that Lego is the best toy ever made. This set only re-enforces that opinion. Some Legos, when complete can be played with (the Lego City ones, for instance) but others not so much. I dont see this being played with, just built, displayed, and maybe dismantled and rebuilt.

5 stars though. A wonderful Lego set. A must have for collectors big kids, and us huge kids!
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit I am a Lego fan, but I kept that in mind as I reviewed this, not wanting it to make my review unfair.
So, lets start with the kit. The pieces do not fit together as well as Lego pieces do. That’s not a huge thing, but it’s a little annoying with some of the steps.
I have to say that the instructions are much better than Lego ones –MegaBlox devised a very clear way to show what piece to put, and where to put it. That was nice. However, they lace the style Lego shows – if this were a Lego set, it would be hollow – allowing things to go inside it – this set is solid, no room inside for anything. The feet fall off easily, which gets old fast.

Plus there are many “special” bricks that will limit the owners ability to make other things out of the set. Although, that is moot if you have a sizable MegaBlox collection already.

The finished piece is nice – a little boxy – think Minions meets Minecraft.

My issue is the price though. If you look at Lego sets (aside from brand ones like Disney and some of the collectable ones) the cost is around 10c per brick.
This set works out at almost 30cents per brick. Three times the cost of a comparably sized Lego set.
The quality does not warrant that price. Despite the added value of the Despicable Me brand. If it was rounder, more interactive, or had stronger feet I would be inclines to give it a better score

If the shortcomings don’t bother you, and your life *needs* all things “Despicable Me” then you will enjoy this.
If someone else is paying for it, you will find it a bargain.

Otherwise I would recommend you get your Despicable Me and building set fix from a better product.
text_fidelity_b: Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Little Live Scruff-A-Luvs Cutie Cuts: Shave, Reveal and Style, Plush Rescue Pet - Pink Puppy I see a lot of reviews complaining, but I got this for my 6 year old's birthday and she loves it. No, the fur doesn't really "shave off" it's more like you comb it off and grab it. It takes parental involvement and it's messy, but it's meant to be an experience, which it fully delivers. My daughter did the unboxing and loved finding all the surprises. We "shaved" her pup and gave it a bath in a bowl at my kitchen table. We set up a "drying station" with my hair dryer and a towel. The entire experience was magical and bonding for my daughter and I. We giggled and guessed if we would get the Frenchie or Yorkie and wondered what color it's nails would turn. The bath was fun and a bit messy, and blow drying took a while (mostly mom, she got bored) but her favorite part was grooming the Frenchie (it was easy to tell) and adding the little accessories. The surprise factor was 100% on point. The whole time the suspense was palpable for her. She was guessing the whole time and we came up with names for it.
Don't buy this toy if you can't be bothered to spend an hour playing with your child.
Don't buy this toy expecting a 5-7 year old to do this independently.
This toy is clearly meant for interactive play with an adult.
This toy was a wonderful addition to our homeschooling dramatic play for kindergarten.

If you want a toy that allows you and your child to pretend to own a grooming salon, this toy is perfect. Have everything prepared ahead of time. We put a table cloth down and a bowl of warm water with shampoo, then in a separate area we had the drying and grooming station. Expect to spend at least 45-60 minutes on this adorable experience. It's wonderful for people who enjoy playing with their kids. Our whole family loves it.

Ravensburger Neuschwanstein Castle 2000 Piece Panorama XXL Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly For the last 15 years my extended family has been assembling puzzles during our beach vacation at the North Carolina Outer Banks. We now have a well established family tradition of puzzling with increasingly challenging puzzles. For the last few years, only Ravensburgers will do. These puzzles are well made, with thick, solid cardboard with a bright, spill resistant color.

The difficult part about this puzzle are the vast blue and cloudy blue areas at the top, and the large amounts of snow covered tree limbs. At 132 cm wide, this puzzle is 4' 4" across, much wider than most coffee tables. We set up a specific rectangular folding table for puzzles like this, or push two together. I would judge this puzzle as on the "difficult" end for puzzles with 2,000 pieces (to be precise, it has 2,040 pieces!). It took our family a full week to work through all the branches, blues, snow, etc.

A nice thing about this puzzle is that even though its 2,000 pieces, the pieces are all a "large" nice size, which makes it more fun, and easier to tell one from another, and spot tiny differences in color and shape.

The insert in the box comes in a wide variety of languages, the pieces come inside the sturdy box wrapped in a bag. Its quality throughout.

Have fun!
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Neuschwanstein Castle 2000 Piece Panorama XXL Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults – Softclick Technology Means Pieces Fit Together Perfectly

text_fidelity_a:
FurReal Friends Hop `N Cuddle Tan Bunny The Furreal Friends Hop 'N Cuddle Bunny (Tan color) is a nice toy for a young child. Rabbits are one of the more popular animals with little kids, and a stuffed animal like this that the child can control is a great idea, particular for a young girl like my niece who is completely bunny-crazy, and may be too young to own the real thing.

The bunny has a switch with three settings located on the bottom hidden by a velcro slot. "Try Me," for temporary activity, "Off," and "On." The "on" switch activates the one minute sequence of crawling in a circle approximately 3 feet in diameter (going clockwise), with occasional stops, sitting up, and various noises that I suppose to the right young person could be considered endearing. The sequence lasts long enough for the bunny do do a little more than one circular loop. It worked just fine on our carpet. I haven't tried it on the hardwood.

The "on" sequence will stop after about a minute, but if you gently brush a switch located on the bunny's lower back near the tail, the sequence starts again. My niece quickly figured out the mechanism, and sleeps with the bunny next to her, occasionally pushing the button if she wanted some motion or sounds. It stops after a short while if she does not.

The construction seems reasonable. The faux fur has been sewn over a hard shell animatronic body. There are pink pads on the bottom of the bunny feet. So this bunny is not squishable, and may not give the best hugs. I clicked four stars on the durable, but of course it hasn't been in action long enough to judge this.

However, I have noticed that she prefers her animals to make friends with each other and converse. After quickly learning the geometry of the pattern, she sits another animal where she expects the bunny to be at the end of its circular path, then begins narrating the important commands, statements, and then, when the bunny finally gets to the other stuffed animal, friendly greetings are exchanged between the two stuffed acquaintances. Adorable.
text_fidelity_b: FurReal Friends Hop `N Cuddle Tan Bunny

text_fidelity_a:
Sagrada - Board Game by Floodgate Games, 4 playres The game is fun, kind of like solving a sudoku puzzle where there's some limited interaction between players. Some people take too long to make decisions, don't play with someone like that in a group of more than 2 people as there's not much to do while waiting your turn. The game is pretty and well built, and the dice drafting mechanic is unique and fun.

I'm glad I bought the game and it's in our rotation, but it's not as good as games like Patchwork or Carcassonne because you're always trying to do the same thing- fill up your grid while maximizing your score. Patchwork has shifting objectives you need to play off against each other. Carcassonne has more interplay between people while building out the map and has more emergent complexity. We pull this game out mostly because we have 3 people and want the fun of the dice drafting game mechanic.
text_fidelity_b: Sagrada - Board Game by Floodgate Games, 4 playres

text_fidelity_a:
Westcott 6" Titanium Precision Scissors - Violet I’m a crafter and a super office supply freak. I confess this so you will understand that I have a LOT of scissors. It is a well known fact that you need different scissors for different types of project. It’s also fact that there is something slightly wrong with every pair. It’s one of those mysteries like when you put a pair of socks in the dryer only one comes out. Head scratcher.
Against all odds, and the rules of the crafting universe, these scissors are perfect.
The handle is big enough for any size fingers. The grip is so comfortable I have not had a case of the “scissor cramps” no matter how long I use them for.
The blades are super sharp, aaaaallll the way down to the tips. They allow me to snip into the most minute 'V' of a paper cut out. Even better they let me cut the most clean appliqués for quilting. No need to tear out that last little bit of paper you couldn’t get with your scissors. I’m so used to doing that it now feels like I’m missing a step. They cut cleanly through even my thickest macrame cord, which is why I bought them in the first place.
The anti-stick is no joke. These are now my exclusive washi tape cutting scissors. I don’t need to get out the rubbing alcohol or Goof-Off to wipe down the blades to get the adhesive off. It simply doesn’t stick to the blades at all. It’s a miracle!
When I was first looking at these to buy them I giggled a bit about the lanyard, like who would use that? The answer is me! I use the lanyard! Most of the time I have them hanging right next to my workspace where I can grab them easy peasy. But I find myself putting it around my neck when I’m moving around. It keeps the sharp point safe and they don’t get lost under the inevitable mess I make. And when I’m working on a large macrame project I don’t need to drop the cord to get the scissors.
Now don’t shake your head, I haven’t lost my mind entirely, I don’t use them for tape/paper AND fabric. That would be up there with drinking orange juice then brushing my teeth. No, instead I simply bought two pairs. The orange/grey for fabric and the purple/pink for everything else. I probably could’ve used the same pair but why upset the balance of the universe, amma right?
Will these replace all of your scissors? Nope. But they for sure will replace all your smaller pairs. I definitely recommend getting these, in all available colors!
text_fidelity_b: Westcott 6" Titanium Precision Scissors - Violet

HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 This is a great little plane, no question. But I ignored Hobbyzone's recommendation for 14 years old and up. I bought two: one for each of my 9-year-old twin sons, who were hot to fly RC model airplanes. One learned to fly quickly, but the other has been seriously disappointed. And I had to learn quickly how to use styrofoam glue to reattach broken wings, tail parts, motor mounts, etc.

It took me a while to understand how critical the trim really is: a beginner really can't fly a plane that isn't trimmed properly. You can get the trim in the ballpark with visual inspection of the control surfaces, but to get it right you have to fly the plane yourself. When I did that, and touched up the trim, flying became a lot of fun - for one boy. The other boy still can't fly more than a few seconds before landing his plane on its nose. He has just about given up in disgust.

I suspect that in a year or two both boys will have good flying skills. But in the meantime one boy is ready to move up while the other is ready to give up. Bummer!

One of our messages for young children is to never touch slugs or snails with bare hands, and we teach people of all ages to "jug the slug" by collecting slugs they find in their garden using tongs or chopsticks. We used these slugs as a tool to get kids "practicing" picking up slugs with chopsticks (chopsticks are a common household item in Hawaii). This is my second purchase of this item - the first bag lasted through probably 50+ events and being "jugged" 100s of times before they got so mangled it was time to get new ones. A great, inexpensive teaching tool!

text_fidelity_a: Rechargeable Laser Tag 360° Sensors + LCDs - Set of 4 - Gift Ideas for Kids Teens and Adults Boys & Girls Family Fun - Cool Teenage Christmas Lazer Group Activity - Teen Gifts Ages 8+ Year Old Boy I was concerned about this product at first because one of the vests came broken and I had read some poor reviews about the customer service here, but that was not my experience.  Once I contacted the company saying one came broken, they asked me to give them the number off the back and in less then two weeks we had a replacement and we did not have to bother sending the broken one back.  I still wasn't ready to write a review however because we hadn't tried the game yet, and we had used another brand before.  I wanted a comparison, and I was not disappointed.  Some of the things that make these guns better.  NO CABLE attached to the gun, you just shoot yourself to link.  We loved this feature.  NO BATTERIES, whew, most of these guns take 6 or more batteries per set, I think this alone will pay for it's slightly steeper cost than some of the others with similar features.  Four different gun types, each does different amounts of damage, super fun to switch around.  I like the "pew, pew" laser gun.  There is the ability to turn the sound off if you would like, and the ability to turn the lighting off for a "Stealth" mode that lasts about 30 seconds, so you can sneak up on someone if you are playing in the dark.  The quality of the guns feels very solid, no some flimsy light weight thing.  The chest receivers also have a sensor in the back which a lot of the other laser gun sets lack.  This is a very good laser set, highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs) We like the Lego brand, but sometimes we need a lot of bricks without paying an exorbitant amount of money. The 1,100 piece kit from Building Bricks was exactly what we were looking for. The Big Questions:
1. Do they really work well with Lego Brand Legos?
Yes - they work very well. It's difficult to tell the difference if you're not really trying hard.
2. How much cheaper are they? Is it really worth it?
It's hard to compare exact pricing here because this set does not include wheels, doors or special pieces. If I had to choose a product to compare it to, I'd probably compare it with Lego's XXL Classic Box (https://www.amazon.com/10697-Building-Large-Creator-Pieces/dp/B00XJ5C4FW). When pricing per piece, the Lego box is about 5¢ per piece. And yes, you read that right. You're dolling out a nickel for every piece of plastic with Lego's brand stamped on it. :) Building Bricks runs about 3¢ per piece. So the answer is: It's almost half the price - very worth it if you're just needing a lot of standard pieces.
As a side note: We really liked the color choices Building Bricks made. They're perfect for expanding your Lego creation palette.
text_fidelity_b: Brickyard Building Blocks 177 Pieces Large Building Block Toys for Children Ages 1.5-5, Bulk Block Set, Compatible with Duplo (177 pcs)

My niece washed a bunch of dishes for me, so in return I purchased a toy for her. She chose this one!

- The idea is F-ING CUTE AF. Especially for girly girls who love hair and makeup stuff.
- It came with a bunch of different accessories
- This is so affordable!
- It's similar to the very popular LOL dolls in that it's got a bunch of different compartments that you open separately for each accessory

RECOMMENDATION

Because we live on separate islands, I turned to Amazon so I could have the gift shipped to her house. I came upon this and was so stoked! 100 pieces for $30? YES PLEASE.

text_fidelity_a: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries I'm not much of a drone guy myself and if it were just for me, I'd have gotten bored with it a while ago, but my dogs LOVE it and for that alone it's worth the price. The drone is surprisingly durable, and has survived numerous bites and swats as the dogs chase it around the yard. It also came with spare rotors, which was a nice touch. I haven't needed them yet, but it's good to know they're there. Giving it 4 instead of 5 stars because it doesn't respond to controls like the instructions say it should. It luckily has a rudimentary collision detection system that helps it (sometimes) avoid obstacles, and it can ascend/descend well enough, but fine controls and steering are awkward at best. Still, for the price and for how well it stands up to abuse from the dogs, it's a winner!
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Drone with Camera 1080P HD FPV Cameras Remote Control Toys RC Quadcopter Helicopter Gifts for Boys Girls Adults Beginners with Altitude Hold, Headless Mode, One Key Start, 3D Flips 2 Batteries

text_fidelity_a: Little Tikes Cozy Truck Ride-On with removable floorboard I only give two stars rather than one because it looks cool. Putting this thing together is a royal pita. First of all you better have some tools because parts do NOT fit correctly. The left front wheel assembly slides up from the bottom and is attached with a pressed on fastener which was no problem for the right side however the left side did not have any metal sticking up past the bushing. I had to take a Dremel tool and cut the pinched metal that stops the washer so that I could get enough of the rod to attach a fastener. The steering wheel is locked in place with a clip that is inserted into the plastic rod that goes into the dash and is supposed to go through a plastic ring that you place on the rod from the other side of the dash. Well I pushed as hard as I could and there is no way this was going to connect. If it would have connected there is no way a child would be able to turn the steering wheel. I had to elongate the holes in the steering column in order to get this connected. Bottom line is this product is severely lacking in quality control. I would not buy another one because of this problem By the way, I'm not someone who usually has trouble putting things together and I have quite a large collection of tools that I know how to use otherwise I don't see anyway this thing gets put together.
text_fidelity_b: Little Tikes Cozy Truck Ride-On with removable floorboard

The reason I only gave this kit only 4 stars is that there is so little ink in the kit's stamp pad set. An enthusiastic stenciler is probably going to run out fairly quickly and need to buy a replacement. I would consider giving additional ink with the kit if I were giving it as a gift.

I highly recommend this kit for ages 11 and up (below that age, I think it could be frustrating for some children and enjoyable for others)

text_fidelity_a: HSP Nature Toys Root-Vue Farm Multicolor, 16 Inch Loved the idea of this - who doesn't want to get their kids excited about veggies? But this has been a disaster since it arrived. I also wasn't aware that it's an expensive piece of styrofoam.  Also, you need to keep a cover over the viewing area to help the veggies grow, so none of the roots are visible without an adult carefully removing and replacing the cover (which is a thin piece of plastic).  Our veggies sprouted quickly and well, and then promptly fizzled out.  You place 3 ropes through the dirt extending into the tray of water on the bottom, and these are supposed to wick all the needed water to the plants. At least here in Colorado, it is too dry and the plants couldn't get enough water.  They could however mold a little and then die.  The bottom holding tank of water turns into this muddy cistern that supports fruit flies amazingly well, and is easily knocked by an eager kid trying to see the plants.  The roots weren't particularly visible. This toy has been very disappointing overall, and now I have a hunk of styrofoam that I will have to pay to bring to our special recycling center.  Hoping that our garden reignites some excitement for growing things and the wonder of nature!
text_fidelity_b: HSP Nature Toys Root-Vue Farm Multicolor, 16 Inch

text_fidelity_a:
Castle Panic 2nd Edition | Family Board Game | Board Game for Adults and Family | Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ | for 1 to 6 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Fireside Games I purchased this game with the intention of playing with my 5 year old daughter, wife, and possibly my 4 year old son. This has proven to be a great game. I don't think most avid gamers would find it as fun, simply because the design is you play against random board mechanics. Some real bad draws and no matter how good you are, you just can't beat it. Other times, it's skill and other times it's just luck of the draw.

That said, this game is EXCELLENT! There's no heavy competition (unless you use some of the modified rules). Basically, everyone WINS or everyone LOSES. That means my daughter's not nagging her brother, etc, etc. It's a great family game for this reason where it is cooperative. The theme is also the fun part, while you're playing, you will have nail biting times, and easier times, etc. We just purchased it and have played it over 5 times in the last week. My nephews have come over and played multiple times too. It's also great because it can host up to 6 players, which is excellent!

The only downfall I've seen is this. Avid gamers might not like it as it's light in strategy, meaning it's easy to play (almost self guided at times). Also, this game can be harder to play at certain player numbers. For example: 2 players each player has 6 cards, and that's 12 total to look at. With 5 players, there's 5 x 5 hands meaning 25 cards making the odds alot better. Basically 2 and 3 player games can be rough. Lower player games aren't unwinnable, it's just higher difficulty (which again is mostly random). Out of 5 stars I definitely rate this a 4. i would give it a 5 if it wasn't so random (meaning hopeless on some games). By the way, out of 5 games played, we've won 4...so it's not 'that' hopless really...great game!!!
text_fidelity_b: Castle Panic 2nd Edition | Family Board Game | Board Game for Adults and Family | Cooperative Board Game | Ages 8+ | for 1 to 6 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Fireside Games

While flying at a local reservoir the drone lost signal and landed in the water instead of returning to the launch point as it should have.

DJI customer care used "their" data to duck responsibly of the malfunction. The problem is that their data conviently doesn't reflect the reality of what happened.

Their remedy was to sell me another drone without the controller for 15 percent discount over a full kit. Less $120. Nice deal... For them. The controllers are sold on eBay for $150 unused. It's a higher profit margin than selling a basic drone for $800.

DJI customer care is offshore despite their Los Angeles phone number. When I first called I spoke to a representative who barely spoke English and had such a thick accent that at times I thought he was speaking a different language.

The email support was protracted taking 3 days to receive a response from each email I sent. I will not buy another DJI drone based on my customer service experience.

Snap Circuits Classic SC-300 Electronics Exploration Kit | Over 300 Projects | Full Color Manual Parts | STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8+ 2.3 x 13.6 x 19.3 inches I got this kit for my 10 year old. We had been experimenting with kit electric motors, magnets and radios and everything ended up mixed in a box that he liked to play with, so there was interest in this type of toy.

The parts of this kit snap together on a clear plastic grid. The instruction book is a black and white center stapled pamphlet that can be challenging to decipher for builds that are more complex. My son liked building the simple circuit that included the motor with the fan. Many of the advanced plans are very similar.

The kit seems durable but not indestructable. My kids can be pretty rough on things so they have been using this kit with my supervision.

For most kids under 10, this is not the type of toy that they can play with on their own. I have my son use this toy at the dining room table. We check to make sure that all of the parts get back in their place when we are done.

This is an educational toy. My experience is that early exposure to learning experiences like this can shape interests later on in life.

text_fidelity_a: NATURALIFE 1byone Professional Bubble Machine with High Output, Automatic Blowing Mechanism for Outdoor or Indoor Use Started to buy one of the more expensive models but noticed this one didn't have any mention of foaming issues so decided for the price to give it a try. WOW! This thing is great! Thousands of bubbles most just under tennis ball size but some smaller. If you use the Gazillion Bubble solution you get beautiful iridescent bubbles that drift a long way before breaking. It works best and the bubble sdrift farther if you can get it up off the ground. A breeze helps too. I set it on the top step of a 3-step ladder and that was perfect. This machine is a bubble solution hog but it couldn't be any less and produce this volume of bubbles. Seems to run maybe 20 minutes or so on a fill and you get about 4 fills from a bottle of the 2 liter Gazillion Bubbles solution. It can make a but of a mess on the ground under the machine so be sure to place it somewhere that doesn't matter or is easy to clean. I didn't find the machine all that difficult to clean after using but you have to have a little patience. Hold it upside down and use the garden hose on low flow to wash out the solution tray being careful not to wet the motor or switch.. We ran this off and on over the 3 day July 4th weekend and it ran perfectly. Kids and adults both were amazed. If you want a bubble machine and don't want to spend a lot of money get this one.
text_fidelity_b: NATURALIFE 1byone Professional Bubble Machine with High Output, Automatic Blowing Mechanism for Outdoor or Indoor Use

text_fidelity_a: Greater Than Games Sentinels of The Multiverse Enhanced Card Game (2nd Edition) I played this game multiple times with friends hoping it would get better but I found this board game to not be very tactical and more independent than dependent on teammates compared to other great cooperative board games such as Ghost Stories and Pandemic. You just take turns playing a hero then choosing a low simple attack against the villain and then the villain does an overpowered attack against the heroes and you just repeat until someone runs out of health points. People I played with all found the game mechanics to be boring and never wanted to play the game again once they knew all the rules and how to play it. Even for some players new to board games, the game is too simple for my group of players. I would really like this board game to incorporate tile movement on a board, like a tactical turn based game then I would feel that this would be worth playing and feel more like a team than just taking turns reading their own cards and doing simple attacks. But if you are into that kind of gameplay disregard this review then.
text_fidelity_b: Greater Than Games Sentinels of The Multiverse Enhanced Card Game (2nd Edition)

Kanagawa Game The game itself is good, once you figure out the instructions. The rule book is written so poorly that you have to read it through a few times before you figure out how the game works.

The game is similar to Tokaido, if Tokaido were just about creating paintings and had slightly more complex game mechanics (not a bad thing, once you figure out the rules). This is a pretty low-key competitive game. For people willing to decipher the rule book, it's the kind of game you could play with people who aren't highly competitive gamers.

The art is really nice, as you can probably guess from the box.
text_fidelity_b: Kanagawa Game

text_fidelity_a:
Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder This version adds difficulty without making it more interesting. In this game, there are both railways and ship routes to build, which means you have to collect cards for each route in the correct color and mode of transportation. Effectively, this game adds twice the number of colors you have to collect to build things. In the original game, you always end up with a bunch of cards in your hand that aren't useful to you because they're not the colors you need to finish your tickets. This game is twice as bad in that regard. Furthermore, there are fewer ship cards, even though you're expected to build more ship routes than train routes. Many of the ship cards are actually worth 2 of that color, which theoretically allows you to collect fewer cards of that color before building, but what actually happens is that you can go through the entire stack of ship cards without getting what you need because the other players are unintentionally hoarding the few cards in the color and type you need.

I didn't hate this game, but I wouldn't play it again.
text_fidelity_b: Ticket to Ride Rails & Sails Board Game | Train Route-Building Strategy Game | Fun Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 10+ | 2-5 Players | Average Playtime 90-120 Minutes | Made by Days of Wonder

And to top it off, the Panda sleeves are 1mm narrower than the Delphia sleeves and so the fit, for games like Arkham Horror LCG, is even better! (see photo) Absolutely my favorite sleeves, by far! Balloon Arch Kit Adjustable for Different Table Sizes Birthday, Wedding, Christmas, and Graduation Party Update: Second time we used it, one of the plastic clamps broke. I have contacted the seller by phone and by email to purchase JUST the clamps... no response. None. I need to use it for a party next weekend, so I purchased a different one with metal clamps - and having major problems with the new one as well. I would say..... if you need it for a one time use, it's still worth it, but a huge a disappointment that it can't be used again. The balloon stands are still fine.

Original review: I used this arch for my niece's baby shower. I was seriously worried about the stability of the arch, setup, and tear down. But after giving it a test run at my house first, it was so simple to set up and use, and it was very stable. I received a bunch of clips with the set, but I found that putting the balloons around the pole was much easier than using the clips. We also purchased 2 sets of balloon poles, and those were easy to use as well, same method. I took these on a plane across the country, and they traveled well. The only negative, and it is minor, was that there were no instructions included in the boxes. I initially had a hard time getting the poles to stay together, until I YouTubed a Party Zealot setup video, then it became apparent what the glue dots are for! Trust me...you will want to use the glue dots to "glue" the poles together, or they WILL come apart. But using the glue dots made them much more stable. There are still some little blue clippy things that came in the boxes that we never did figure out how to use, and I couldn't find the information anywhere on their website or google searches. So they remain a mystery. But overall, for the money, this was a HUGE success and a fantastic buy. I have never had so many compliments. Highly recommend.
